```rust
// Named-pipe server and router for mayak-hook.
//
// `\\.\pipe\mayak-<sid>` — one instance per connection, one line of JSON per
// connection. `route()` decides what a line is for:
//   * Codex, any event → Observe: handed to the observer, never answered;
//   * Claude PermissionRequest → Approval: the legacy Allow/Deny card, the only
//     connection kept open — it waits for the island's decision and writes it
//     back on the same pipe;
//   * anything else → Ignore: for Claude the session observer is the source of
//     truth, not hooks.
//
// Claude Code is never blocked by us. Three things guarantee it:
//   * mayak-hook gives the connection 300 ms and exits cleanly if we are closed;
//   * we only wait for a human once the island has *confirmed* the card is on
//     screen, so a paused island or a webview that is not listening costs a few
//     hundred milliseconds, not two minutes;
//   * whatever happens we drop the connection after the decision timeout, and
//     the terminal takes over.
//
// What we write back is the bare word `allow` or `deny`. Turning that into the
// documented hookSpecificOutput JSON is mayak-hook's job, so the wire format
// Claude Code expects lives in exactly one place.
//
// The app is plugged in through `RouterSink` (lib.rs), so this file knows
// nothing about Tauri and its tests run a real pipe with a test sink.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use serde_json::{json, Value};
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::windows::named_pipe::{NamedPipeServer, ServerOptions};
use tokio::sync::mpsc;

use crate::observe::keys::SessionKey;

/// A line longer than this is dropped, never parsed.
pub const MAX_PAYLOAD: usize = 1 << 20;
/// How long the island gets to say "the card is up". Without it, an island
/// that is paused, hidden behind a crashed webview or simply not listening
/// would leave Claude Code staring at a prompt nobody can see.
const ACK_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(800);
/// Slightly under mayak-hook's own 110 s wait, so we always answer first.
const DECISION_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(108);

/// What the island can say about a permission request.
pub enum Reply {
    /// The card is on screen and a human can act on it.
    Ack,
    /// A human clicked: `allow` or `deny`.
    Decision(String),
    /// Nobody can act on it — paused, or another request already holds the card.
    Decline,
}

/// Permission requests the island has been told about.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Pending(pub Mutex<HashMap<String, mpsc::Sender<Reply>>>);

static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Route {
    Observe,
    Approval,
    Ignore,
}

/// `agent` is payload["agent"] ("claude" when absent: a Coucou-era relay only
/// ever relayed Claude).
pub fn route(agent: &str, event: &str) -> Route {
    match (agent, event) {
        ("codex", _) => Route::Observe,
        ("claude", "PermissionRequest") => Route::Approval,
        _ => Route::Ignore,
    }
}

/// What the island shows about the session behind an approval card.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ApprovalContext {
    pub session_key: Option<SessionKey>,
    pub project_name: Option<String>,
}

/// Sets `request_id`, `session_key` and `project_name` (string or null).
pub fn annotate_approval(payload: &mut Value, request_id: &str, ctx: &ApprovalContext) {
    if let Some(map) = payload.as_object_mut() {
        map.insert("request_id".into(), json!(request_id));
        map.insert("session_key".into(), json!(ctx.session_key));
        map.insert("project_name".into(), json!(ctx.project_name));
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum LineError {
    Oversize(usize),
    Invalid { len: usize, reason: String },
}

/// The line is everything before the first '\n' (or all of `buf`). The reason
/// of an Invalid line never quotes the line itself.
pub fn parse_line(buf: &[u8]) -> Result<Value, LineError> {
    let line = match buf.iter().position(|b| *b == b'\n') {
        Some(i) => &buf[..i],
        None => buf,
    };
    if line.len() > MAX_PAYLOAD {
        return Err(LineError::Oversize(line.len()));
    }
    match serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(line) {
        Ok(v) if v.is_object() => Ok(v),
        Ok(_) => Err(LineError::Invalid { len: line.len(), reason: "not a JSON object".into() }),
        Err(err) => Err(LineError::Invalid {
            len: line.len(),
            reason: format!("{:?} error at line {} column {}", err.classify(), err.line(), err.column()),
        }),
    }
}

/// "hook <agent> <Event> s=<first 8 chars of session_id or '-'>". No payload text.
pub fn log_line_for(agent: &str, event: &str, session_id: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let short: String = match session_id.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
        Some(s) => s.chars().take(8).collect(),
        None => "-".into(),
    };
    format!("hook {agent} {event} s={short}")
}

/// Where accepted lines go. lib.rs implements it on the app; tests on a fake.
pub trait RouterSink: Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn pending(&self) -> &Pending;
    /// Route::Observe. Must not block.
    fn observe(&self, payload: Value);
    /// Route::Approval: data for `annotate_approval`. May block (Win32 + file
    /// probes); `serve` always calls it through `spawn_blocking`.
    fn approval_context(&self, payload: &Value) -> ApprovalContext;
    /// Route::Approval: the annotated payload to show.
    fn show_approval(&self, payload: Value);
}

/// `\\.\pipe\mayak-<sid>` — must match mayak-hook's `pipe_path()` exactly.
pub fn pipe_name() -> String {
    let key = crate::win_user::current_user_sid()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| std::env::var("USERNAME").unwrap_or_else(|_| "user".into()));
    format!(r"\\.\pipe\{}{key}", crate::ident::PIPE_PREFIX)
}

/// The only place a pipe instance is created. `first` also means we refuse to
/// join a pipe somebody else already owns under our name.
pub fn create_instance(name: &str, first: bool) -> std::io::Result<NamedPipeServer> {
    ServerOptions::new().first_pipe_instance(first).create(name)
}

/// Accept loop: one task per connection. Err only if the first instance cannot
/// be created. Runs on whatever runtime polls it (Tauri's in the app, the
/// test's own in tests): every instance is created here, and connection tasks
/// are spawned with `tokio::spawn`.
pub async fn serve<S: RouterSink>(name: String, sink: Arc<S>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut server = create_instance(&name, true)?;
    loop {
        if let Err(err) = server.connect().await {
            note(format!("relay pipe connect failed: {err}"));
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
            continue;
        }
        // Hand the connected instance to a task and listen on a fresh one.
        let next = match create_instance(&name, false) {
            Ok(s) => s,
            Err(err) => {
                note(format!("cannot reopen the relay pipe: {err}"));
                return Ok(());
            }
        };
        let connected = std::mem::replace(&mut server, next);
        tokio::spawn(handle(connected, sink.clone()));
    }
}

async fn handle<S: RouterSink>(mut pipe: NamedPipeServer, sink: Arc<S>) {
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    let mut chunk = [0u8; 4096];
    loop {
        match pipe.read(&mut chunk).await {
            Ok(0) => break,
            Ok(n) => {
                buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);
                if chunk[..n].contains(&b'\n') || buf.len() > MAX_PAYLOAD {
                    break;
                }
            }
            Err(err) => {
                note(format!("relay read failed after {} bytes: {err}", buf.len()));
                return;
            }
        }
    }
    let payload = match parse_line(&buf) {
        Ok(v) => v,
        Err(LineError::Oversize(len)) => {
            note(format!("relay line dropped: oversize {len} bytes"));
            let _ = pipe.disconnect();
            return;
        }
        Err(LineError::Invalid { len, reason }) => {
            note(format!("relay line dropped: {len} bytes, {reason}"));
            let _ = pipe.disconnect();
            return;
        }
    };

    let agent = payload.get("agent").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("claude").to_string();
    let event = payload.get("hook_event_name").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
    note(log_line_for(&agent, &event, payload.get("session_id").and_then(Value::as_str)));

    match route(&agent, &event) {
        Route::Observe => {
            sink.observe(payload);
            let _ = pipe.disconnect();
        }
        Route::Ignore => {
            let _ = pipe.disconnect();
        }
        Route::Approval => approval(pipe, payload, sink).await,
    }
}

async fn approval<S: RouterSink>(mut pipe: NamedPipeServer, mut payload: Value, sink: Arc<S>) {
    let id = format!("{}-{}", std::process::id(), COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed));
    let ctx = {
        let sink = sink.clone();
        let payload = payload.clone();
        match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || sink.approval_context(&payload)).await {
            Ok(ctx) => ctx,
            Err(err) => {
                note(format!("approval context failed id={id}: {err}"));
                ApprovalContext::default()
            }
        }
    };
    let (tx, mut rx) = mpsc::channel::<Reply>(4);
    sink.pending().0.lock().unwrap().insert(id.clone(), tx);
    annotate_approval(&mut payload, &id, &ctx);
    note(format!("approval id={id}"));
    sink.show_approval(payload);

    let decision = wait_for_decision(&id, &mut rx).await;
    sink.pending().0.lock().unwrap().remove(&id);

    // No decision: say nothing at all. mayak-hook then writes nothing to stdout
    // and Claude Code asks in the terminal, exactly as if Mayak were closed.
    if let Some(d) = decision {
        let _ = pipe.write_all(format!("{d}\n").as_bytes()).await;
        let _ = pipe.flush().await;
    }
    let _ = pipe.disconnect();
}

/// Two waits: a short one for "the card is up", then the long one for a human.
async fn wait_for_decision(id: &str, rx: &mut mpsc::Receiver<Reply>) -> Option<String> {
    match tokio::time::timeout(ACK_TIMEOUT, rx.recv()).await {
        Ok(Some(Reply::Ack)) => {}
        // A click that beats the ack is still a click.
        Ok(Some(Reply::Decision(d))) => {
            note(format!("approval id={id} answered {d}"));
            return Some(d);
        }
        Ok(Some(Reply::Decline)) => {
            note(format!("approval id={id} not shown — terminal takes over"));
            return None;
        }
        Ok(None) => return None,
        Err(_) => {
            note(format!("approval id={id} island never acknowledged — terminal takes over"));
            return None;
        }
    }

    match tokio::time::timeout(DECISION_TIMEOUT, rx.recv()).await {
        Ok(Some(Reply::Decision(d))) => {
            note(format!("approval id={id} answered {d}"));
            Some(d)
        }
        Ok(Some(Reply::Decline)) => {
            note(format!("approval id={id} released without a decision"));
            None
        }
        _ => {
            note(format!("approval id={id} timed out — terminal takes over"));
            None
        }
    }
}

fn send(pending: &Pending, request_id: &str, reply: Reply, keep: bool) {
    let sender = {
        let mut map = pending.0.lock().unwrap();
        if keep { map.get(request_id).cloned() } else { map.remove(request_id) }
    };
    match sender {
        Some(tx) => {
            let _ = tx.try_send(reply);
        }
        None => note(format!("reply for id={request_id} — no pending request")),
    }
}

/// The island has the card on screen; the long wait may begin.
pub fn acknowledge(pending: &Pending, request_id: &str) {
    send(pending, request_id, Reply::Ack, true);
}

/// Nobody can act on this one — paused, or another card already holds the view.
pub fn decline(pending: &Pending, request_id: &str) {
    note(format!("decline id={request_id}"));
    send(pending, request_id, Reply::Decline, false);
}

/// Called by the island's Allow / Deny buttons. Only ever a bare word: turning
/// it into Claude Code's JSON is mayak-hook's job.
pub fn answer(pending: &Pending, request_id: &str, decision: &str) {
    let word = match decision {
        "allow" | "always" => "allow",
        _ => "deny",
    };
    note(format!("decision id={request_id} {word}"));
    send(pending, request_id, Reply::Decision(word.to_string()), false);
}

/// Log sink of this module: mayak.log in the app, a capture buffer in tests
/// (tests must not write to the user's log).
#[cfg(not(test))]
fn note(message: String) {
    crate::log::line(message);
}

#[cfg(test)]
fn note(message: String) {
    tests::NOTES.lock().unwrap().push(message);
}

```

Notes on choices inside this code (all within the contract): the reason of an invalid line is the
serde_json error category and position, never the text; `note()` sends this module's log lines to
`mayak.log` in the app and to a buffer in tests, so tests never write the user's log; an approval's
`approval_context` runs on `spawn_blocking` (D46) and its `JoinError` is logged and yields
`ApprovalContext::default()`.

```rust
/// Where the relay pipe delivers what `pipe::route` accepted.
struct AppSink {
    app: AppHandle,
    pending: Arc<Pending>,
}

impl pipe::RouterSink for AppSink {
    fn pending(&self) -> &Pending {
        &self.pending
    }

    fn observe(&self, _payload: serde_json::Value) {
        log::line("codex event dropped — observer not running");
    }

    fn approval_context(&self, _payload: &serde_json::Value) -> pipe::ApprovalContext {
        pipe::ApprovalContext::default()
    }

    fn show_approval(&self, payload: serde_json::Value) {
        let _ = self.app.emit_to(island::WINDOW_LABEL, "hook", payload);
    }
}

#[tauri::command]
fn approval_decision(pending: State<Arc<Pending>>, request_id: String, decision: String) {
    pipe::answer(&pending, &request_id, &decision);
}

/// The island has the card on screen, so the long wait for a human may begin.
/// Until this arrives the relay only waits a few hundred milliseconds, which is
/// what stops a paused or unresponsive island from freezing Claude Code.
#[tauri::command]
fn approval_ack(pending: State<Arc<Pending>>, request_id: String) {
    pipe::acknowledge(&pending, &request_id);
}

/// Nobody can act on this request — the island is paused, or another card is
/// already up. Claude Code falls back to asking in the terminal immediately.
#[tauri::command]
fn approval_decline(pending: State<Arc<Pending>>, request_id: String) {
    pipe::decline(&pending, &request_id);
}
```

```rust
impl JsonlTail {
    pub fn new(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self;
    pub fn start_at_eof(&mut self) -> io::Result<u64>;
    pub fn start_with_window(&mut self, bytes: u64) -> io::Result<()>;
    pub fn read_new(&mut self) -> io::Result<(Vec<(u64, String)>, u64)>;
    pub fn eof(&self) -> u64;

```

  Behaviour later tasks rely on (all pinned by this task's tests):
  - `normalize`: `display` keeps letter case except the drive letter (uppercased); `key = display.to_lowercase()` (Unicode-aware, so Cyrillic folds too). `c:/Users/x`, `C:\Users\x\`, `/c:/Users/x`, `file:///c:/Users/x`, `\\?\C:\Users\x` all give `display = C:\Users\x`, `key = c:\users\x`. A drive root is `C:\`; `""` stays `""`.
  - `project_of`: probes `<dir>\.git` from the path itself upwards, the drive root last (`C:\.git`); the first hit is the root; no hit → the normalized path itself. `ProjectRef.key = root.to_lowercase()`. Empty input → empty `ProjectRef`, no probe call.
  - `glob_match` patterns are lowercase; `**` = zero or more segments, `*` = one segment, `abc*` = one segment with that prefix.
  - `basename("C:\")` = `"C:"`; `parent_basename("C:\repo")` = `Some("C:")`; `parent_basename("C:\")` = `None`.
  - `JsonlTail` offsets are byte offsets of line starts in the file. `eof` = offset of the first byte not yet consumed, where consumed means read as a line (returned, or skipped as blank) or skipped as pre-existing bytes; the held incomplete last line is not consumed. It equals the end of the last complete line, except after `start_at_eof` or `start_with_window` has landed inside a line and until that line's `\n` is read: then it is the end of the bytes skipped so far, a mid-line offset (everything before it is old). `read_new` on a missing file returns `Ok((vec![], 0))` and restarts at 0 (a re-created file is read from its start). `start_at_eof` on a file that does not end with `\n` also discards the rest of that last line on the next read (it began before us). Lines are decoded with `String::from_utf8_lossy` (an invalid byte becomes U+FFFD, never an error); whitespace-only lines are skipped; a trailing `\r` is removed.

Contract amendments (contract §7 D71–D73; one removal, no other signature changes; T11 and T12 rely on them):
- **D71** `JsonlTail::path()` (`pub fn path(&self) -> &Path`) is not in contract §2.9. No task calls it (sections B and D–H were searched), so it would stay a permanent ``method `path` is never used`` warning in both the test and the non-test build, contradicting T19 Step 2 (`no warnings`). The private `path` field stays; callers keep their own copy of the path.
- **D72** `JsonlTail::start_at_eof` discards the remainder of a trailing partial line (the line began before us); `read_new` on `NotFound` returns `Ok((vec![], 0))` and restarts at offset 0.
- **D73** `eof` = the first byte not yet consumed, either as a returned line or as skipped pre-existing bytes; it equals the end of the last complete line except right after `start_at_eof` or `start_with_window` has landed inside a line, until that line's `\n` is read. Contract §2.9 states this on `JsonlTail::eof`.

Insert at the top of `paths.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]` (one blank line between):

```rust
// Path identity for sessions and projects (spec §5.7, §13 point 2).
//
// Pure: no environment variables and no file system access, except `git_probe`, which
// callers pass to `project_of` / `ProjectCache::get` and tests replace with a closure.

/// A normalized Windows path. `display` keeps the original letter case (drive letter
/// uppercased); `key` is its lowercase form, used for identity and comparisons.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct NormPath {
    pub display: String,
    pub key: String,
}

/// Spec §5.7 order: trim → strip "file:///" (ASCII case-insensitive) → "/c:/" → "c:/" →
/// '/' → '\' → strip "\\?\" → drive letter uppercase → collapse repeated '\' → resolve "."
/// and ".." lexically (".." at the root is dropped) → strip the trailing '\' except "X:\"
/// (bare "X:" → "X:\") → key = display.to_lowercase(). No percent-decoding, no UNC (D8).
pub fn normalize(raw: &str) -> NormPath {
    let mut s = raw.trim();
    if let Some(head) = s.get(..8) {
        if head.eq_ignore_ascii_case("file:///") {
            s = &s[8..];
        }
    }
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    if b.len() >= 3 && b[0] == b'/' && b[1].is_ascii_alphabetic() && b[2] == b':' {
        s = &s[1..];
    }
    let slashed = s.replace('/', "\\");
    let text = slashed.strip_prefix(r"\\?\").unwrap_or(&slashed);

    let (drive, rest) = match text.as_bytes() {
        [d, b':', ..] if d.is_ascii_alphabetic() => (Some(d.to_ascii_uppercase() as char), &text[2..]),
        _ => (None, text),
    };
    // A drive path is always absolute here: drive-relative "C:foo" does not occur in agent
    // working directories.
    let rooted = drive.is_some() || rest.starts_with('\\');
    let mut parts: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    for seg in rest.split('\\') {
        match seg {
            "" | "." => {}
            ".." => {
                if parts.last().is_some_and(|p| *p != "..") {
                    parts.pop();
                } else if !rooted {
                    parts.push("..");
                }
            }
            _ => parts.push(seg),
        }
    }
    let joined = parts.join("\\");
    let display = match drive {
        Some(d) => format!("{d}:\\{joined}"),
        None if rooted => format!("\\{joined}"),
        None => joined,
    };
    let key = display.to_lowercase();
    NormPath { display, key }
}
```

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
```

Insert directly above `#[cfg(test)]` (one blank line on each side):

```rust
/// A project: the git root found by walking up from a path, or the folder itself.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ProjectRef {
    pub key: String,
    /// `NormPath.display` of the root.
    pub root: String,
}

/// First of normalize(raw) and its ancestors (self included) where probe(dir\.git) is true;
/// none → normalize(raw) itself. The drive root "C:\" probes "C:\.git".
pub fn project_of(raw: &str, probe: impl Fn(&Path) -> bool) -> ProjectRef {
    let norm = normalize(raw);
    if norm.display.is_empty() {
        return ProjectRef { key: String::new(), root: String::new() };
    }
    let mut dir = norm.display.as_str();
    loop {
        let git = if dir.ends_with('\\') { format!("{dir}.git") } else { format!("{dir}\\.git") };
        if probe(Path::new(&git)) {
            return ProjectRef { key: dir.to_lowercase(), root: dir.to_string() };
        }
        match parent(dir) {
            Some(up) => dir = up,
            None => break,
        }
    }
    ProjectRef { key: norm.key, root: norm.display }
}

/// Real probe: `.git` exists as a folder (repository) or a file (worktree, submodule).
pub fn git_probe(p: &Path) -> bool {
    p.exists()
}

/// Lifetime cache owned by one source thread (spec §5.7): one probe walk per distinct path.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ProjectCache {
    by_key: HashMap<String, ProjectRef>,
}

impl ProjectCache {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn get(&mut self, raw: &str, probe: impl Fn(&Path) -> bool) -> ProjectRef {
        let key = normalize(raw).key;
        if let Some(found) = self.by_key.get(&key) {
            return found.clone();
        }
        let project = project_of(raw, probe);
        self.by_key.insert(key, project.clone());
        project
    }
}

/// Lexical parent of a normalized display path: "C:\a\b" → "C:\a", "C:\a" → "C:\",
/// "\a" → "\"; roots and single relative segments → None.
fn parent(display: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    if is_root(display) {
        return None;
    }
    let idx = display.rfind('\\')?;
    let head = &display[..idx];
    if head.is_empty() {
        return Some(&display[..1]);
    }
    let h = head.as_bytes();
    if h.len() == 2 && h[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() && h[1] == b':' {
        return Some(&display[..idx + 1]);
    }
    Some(head)
}

fn is_root(display: &str) -> bool {
    let b = display.as_bytes();
    display == "\\" || (b.len() == 3 && b[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() && b[1] == b':' && b[2] == b'\\')
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: Implement `glob_match`, `basename`, `parent_basename`**

Insert directly above `#[cfg(test)]` in `paths.rs` (one blank line on each side):

```rust
/// Segment glob over lowercase '\'-separated keys. Pattern segments: "**" = zero or more
/// segments, "*" = exactly one segment, "abc*" = one segment starting with "abc", else
/// literal. Empty segments (a trailing '\') are ignored on both sides.
pub fn glob_match(key: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool {
    let k: Vec<&str> = key.split('\\').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();
    let p: Vec<&str> = pattern.split('\\').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();
    match_segments(&k, &p)
}

fn match_segments(key: &[&str], pattern: &[&str]) -> bool {
    match pattern.split_first() {
        None => key.is_empty(),
        Some((&"**", rest)) => (0..=key.len()).any(|skip| match_segments(&key[skip..], rest)),
        Some((seg, rest)) => match key.split_first() {
            Some((k, key_rest)) => segment_matches(k, seg) && match_segments(key_rest, rest),
            None => false,
        },
    }
}

fn segment_matches(segment: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool {
    match pattern.strip_suffix('*') {
        Some(prefix) => segment.starts_with(prefix),
        None => segment == pattern,
    }
}

/// Last component of a display path; "C:\" → "C:".
pub fn basename(display: &str) -> String {
    let trimmed = display.trim_end_matches('\\');
    trimmed.rsplit('\\').next().unwrap_or("").to_string()
}

/// Basename of the parent; None for a drive root (or a path without a parent).
pub fn parent_basename(display: &str) -> Option<String> {
    parent(display).map(basename)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 16: Implement `JsonlTail`**

Insert at the top of `tail.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]` (one blank line between):

```rust
// Incremental reader of an append-only JSONL file (spec §5.7): Claude transcripts and Codex
// rollouts. Each read opens, reads and closes the file with full sharing, so the agent that
// writes it is never blocked and can rename or delete it at any time.

use std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};
use std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
use std::os::windows::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// First read of an existing transcript looks at its last 256 KiB only.
pub const WINDOW_BYTES: u64 = 256 * 1024;

/// FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE.
const SHARE_ALL: u32 = 0x1 | 0x2 | 0x4;

pub struct JsonlTail {
    path: PathBuf,
    /// Bytes of the file consumed so far (complete lines + `partial`).
    read_to: u64,
    /// The incomplete last line, held until its '\n' arrives.
    partial: Vec<u8>,
    /// Discard bytes up to and including the next '\n' (we started inside a line).
    skip_first: bool,
}

impl JsonlTail {
    /// Offset 0: the first `read_new` returns the whole file.
    pub fn new(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self { path: path.into(), read_to: 0, partial: Vec::new(), skip_first: false }
    }

    /// offset = current length. Missing file → offset 0, Ok(0). If the file does not end with
    /// '\n', the rest of that line (it started before us) is discarded by the next read.
    pub fn start_at_eof(&mut self) -> io::Result<u64> {
        self.restart();
        let Some(mut file) = open_shared(&self.path)? else { return Ok(0) };
        let len = file.metadata()?.len();
        if len > 0 {
            file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(len - 1))?;
            let mut last = [0u8; 1];
            file.read_exact(&mut last)?;
            self.skip_first = last[0] != b'\n';
        }
        self.read_to = len;
        Ok(len)
    }

    /// offset = max(0, len - bytes); if > 0 the bytes up to and including the first '\n' are
    /// discarded by the next read (spec §5.5: the window starts inside a line). Missing file →
    /// offset 0.
    pub fn start_with_window(&mut self, bytes: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.restart();
        let Some(file) = open_shared(&self.path)? else { return Ok(()) };
        let len = file.metadata()?.len();
        self.read_to = len.saturating_sub(bytes);
        self.skip_first = self.read_to > 0;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Complete new lines as (start offset of the line, text without the line ending); blank
    /// lines are skipped and the incomplete last line is kept for the next call. Second value =
    /// `eof()` after this read. A file shorter than what was consumed is read again from 0; a
    /// missing file gives no lines and restarts at 0 when it reappears.
    pub fn read_new(&mut self) -> io::Result<(Vec<(u64, String)>, u64)> {
        let Some(mut file) = open_shared(&self.path)? else {
            self.restart();
            return Ok((Vec::new(), 0));
        };
        let len = file.metadata()?.len();
        if len < self.read_to {
            self.restart();
        }
        if len == self.read_to {
            return Ok((Vec::new(), self.eof()));
        }
        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(self.read_to))?;
        let mut fresh = Vec::new();
        file.read_to_end(&mut fresh)?;
        drop(file);

        let fresh_at = self.read_to;
        self.read_to += fresh.len() as u64;
        let mut from = 0usize;
        if self.skip_first {
            match fresh.iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
                Some(nl) => {
                    from = nl + 1;
                    self.skip_first = false;
                }
                None => return Ok((Vec::new(), self.eof())),
            }
        }

        let mut data = std::mem::take(&mut self.partial);
        let data_at = fresh_at + from as u64 - data.len() as u64;
        data.extend_from_slice(&fresh[from..]);

        let mut lines = Vec::new();
        let mut start = 0usize;
        while let Some(rel) = data[start..].iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
            let end = start + rel;
            let mut line = &data[start..end];
            if let Some(stripped) = line.strip_suffix(b"\r") {
                line = stripped;
            }
            if !line.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_whitespace) {
                lines.push((data_at + start as u64, String::from_utf8_lossy(line).into_owned()));
            }
            start = end + 1;
        }
        self.partial = data[start..].to_vec();
        Ok((lines, self.eof()))
    }

    /// First byte not yet consumed (as a returned or blank line, or as skipped pre-existing
    /// bytes): the end of the last complete line, or a mid-line offset while the rest of a line
    /// that a start landed inside is being skipped.
    pub fn eof(&self) -> u64 {
        self.read_to - self.partial.len() as u64
    }

    fn restart(&mut self) {
        self.read_to = 0;
        self.partial.clear();
        self.skip_first = false;
    }
}

/// Opens for reading with full sharing; Ok(None) when the file does not exist.
fn open_shared(path: &Path) -> io::Result<Option<File>> {
    match OpenOptions::new().read(true).share_mode(SHARE_ALL).open(path) {
        Ok(file) => Ok(Some(file)),
        Err(err) if err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
        Err(err) => Err(err),
    }
}
```

  Behaviour T11/T12 rely on (pinned by this task's tests unless marked "design" or "observed"; checked on Windows 11 Pro 26200):
  - `DirWatcher::spawn` opens the directory synchronously: a missing directory is `Err` with `kind() == NotFound` (the caller reports `Health::Missing`). The directory is opened with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`; the watcher is still a blocking std thread, which keeps one overlapped `ReadDirectoryChangesW` request queued and blocks in `GetOverlappedResult(.., bWait = TRUE)` until it completes. `spawn` returns after the first `ReadDirectoryChangesW` request is queued. The kernel records changes from that request on, so an enumeration done after `spawn` returns cannot miss a change, and each watcher test writes only once.
  - Thread names (design): `dirwatch-<dir file name>` (`dirwatch-sessions`, `dirwatch-projects`) and `proc-exit-<pid>`.
  - `Changes` names are relative to the watched directory: `4242.json`, or `C--work-repo\abc.jsonl` from a recursive watcher. Deleting the watched directory ends in `Error` and the thread ends (the sink is dropped); observed: the files' `Removed` changes first, then `Error` with OS error 5. A `sink` that returns `false` ends the thread right after that call and drops the sink, so a closure like `tx.send(..).is_ok()` stops the watcher at the first notification after its receiver is gone.
  - `identify(0)` → `NotFound`; an exited process whose handle someone still holds → `Exited`; observed, not tested (it depends on elevation): pid 4 (System) from a non-elevated process → `AccessDenied`. `created_ft` is the creation FILETIME (100 ns ticks since 1601), the same number Claude writes as `procStart`.
  - `Registry::watch` returns `false` and drops the handle in two cases: `(pid, created_ft)` is already watched, or the waiter thread could not be started (`std::thread::Builder::spawn` failed; design, not tested). In the second case the entry is removed again and `proc-exit thread not started pid=…` is logged, so a later proof registers again; a caller needs nothing more for either `false`. The waiter removes the entry **before** calling `on_exit(pid, created_ft)`; a failed wait is logged (`proc-exit wait failed pid=…`) and does not call `on_exit`.

Contract amendments (contract §7 D74–D76 and the D38 amendment; no signature changes, one constant becomes test-only):
- **D74** `MASK_NAME_WRITE` is `#[cfg(test)]` in contract §2.10: only `masks_are_the_documented_bits` and the `#[ignore]` diagnostic use it, so in the non-test `mayak_lib` (which `cargo test -p mayak` also compiles for the `mayak` bin) it would stay a permanent ``constant `MASK_NAME_WRITE` is never used`` warning, contradicting T19 Step 2 (`no warnings`). It stays a plain `pub const` with the same value; no `#[allow]`.
- **D75** `Registry::watch` (contract §2.10) returns `false` (handle dropped) if already watched **or** if the waiter thread could not be started; in that case the entry is removed and the failure is logged (`proc-exit thread not started pid=…`), so a later proof registers again.
- **D76** `DirWatcher::spawn` (contract §2.10) runs a blocking thread and returns after the first request is queued; this replaces the earlier synchronous `ReadDirectoryChangesW` loop. The open adds `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` to `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`. Each request is an overlapped `ReadDirectoryChangesW` on a manual-reset event (`CreateEventW`) and is collected with `GetOverlappedResult(.., bWait = TRUE)`. The mapping in the contract §2.10 implementation notes is unchanged: `Ok` with 0 bytes or `ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR` → `Overflow`, any other error → `Error`. Reason: with a synchronous call, a change made between the handshake and the call was lost under load (reviewer stress run: 3 and 11 of 640 missed with 32 CPU hogs, 0 of 640 with this design).
- D38 amended: the Registry test child is `cmd /d /c "set /p _="` with piped stdin, held alive until stdin is dropped, so the second `watch()` deterministically sees the process running (a `cmd /c exit` child can exit before the second call, the first waiter then removes the entry and the second call returns `true`). Contract §7 D38 and the Windows integration-test bullet of contract §5 describe this child.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn record(action: u32, name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        let units: Vec<u16> = name.encode_utf16().collect();
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        out.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&action.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&((units.len() * 2) as u32).to_le_bytes());
        for u in units {
            out.extend_from_slice(&u.to_le_bytes());
        }
        while out.len() % 4 != 0 {
            out.push(0);
        }
        out
    }

    /// Chains records the way the kernel does: each NextEntryOffset = its own padded length.
    fn chain(records: Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> Vec<u8> {
        let last = records.len() - 1;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for (i, mut r) in records.into_iter().enumerate() {

                r[..4].copy_from_slice(&len.to_le_bytes());

            out.extend_from_slice(&r);

        assert_eq!(FileAction::from_raw(3), FileAction::Modified);
        assert_eq!(FileAction::from_raw(4), FileAction::RenamedOld);
    }

    #[test]
    fn masks_are_the_documented_bits() {
        // FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME 0x1, _SIZE 0x8, _LAST_WRITE 0x10.
        assert_eq!(MASK_NAME_WRITE_SIZE, 0x19);
        assert_eq!(MASK_NAME_WRITE, 0x11);
    }
}
```

```rust
// Win32 primitives for the observer (spec §5.8): a directory watcher and process proof.
//
// Blocking calls on plain std threads (spec §4). Every kernel handle is an `OwnedHandle`
// right after it is opened, so it can move into a thread (`HANDLE` is not `Send`) and is
// closed exactly once, by Drop.

use std::io;

use windows::Win32::Storage::FileSystem::{
    FILE_ACTION_ADDED, FILE_ACTION_MODIFIED, FILE_ACTION_REMOVED, FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_NEW_NAME,
    FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_OLD_NAME, FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME, FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_WRITE,
    FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_SIZE,
};

pub const WATCH_BUFFER: usize = 64 * 1024;
/// sessions\ and projects\ watchers (spec §5.5).
pub const MASK_NAME_WRITE_SIZE: u32 =
    FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME.0 | FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_WRITE.0 | FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_SIZE.0;
/// Only the mask test and the `#[ignore]` open-handle diagnostic use this one (spec §12),
/// so it exists in test builds only.
#[cfg(test)]
pub const MASK_NAME_WRITE: u32 = FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME.0 | FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_WRITE.0;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FileAction {
    Added,
    Removed,
    Modified,
    RenamedOld,
    RenamedNew,
    Other(u32),
}

impl FileAction {
    fn from_raw(code: u32) -> Self {
        match code {
            c if c == FILE_ACTION_ADDED.0 => Self::Added,
            c if c == FILE_ACTION_REMOVED.0 => Self::Removed,
            c if c == FILE_ACTION_MODIFIED.0 => Self::Modified,
            c if c == FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_OLD_NAME.0 => Self::RenamedOld,
            c if c == FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_NEW_NAME.0 => Self::RenamedNew,
            other => Self::Other(other),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum WatchEvent {
    /// Path relative to the watched directory, as reported (`sub\name.jsonl` when recursive).
    Changes(Vec<(FileAction, String)>),
    /// 0 bytes returned, or the call failed with ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR (1022): the buffer
    /// overflowed and the caller must re-enumerate.
    Overflow,
    /// Any other failure; the watcher thread ends after sending this.
    Error(io::Error),
}

/// Walks the FILE_NOTIFY_INFORMATION chain: NextEntryOffset u32, Action u32,
/// FileNameLength u32 (bytes), FileName UTF-16. Stops at a truncated record.
fn parse_notifications(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<(FileAction, String)> {
    let u32_at = |at: usize| u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[at], bytes[at + 1], bytes[at + 2], bytes[at + 3]]);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut at = 0usize;
    while at + 12 <= bytes.len() {
        let next = u32_at(at) as usize;
        let action = u32_at(at + 4);
        let name_len = u32_at(at + 8) as usize;
        let name_end = at + 12 + name_len;
        if name_end > bytes.len() {
            break;
        }
        let units: Vec<u16> = bytes[at + 12..name_end]
            .chunks_exact(2)
            .map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]]))
            .collect();
        out.push((FileAction::from_raw(action), String::from_utf16_lossy(&units)));
        if next == 0 {
            break;
        }
        at += next;
    }
    out
}
```

```rust
    /// Waits up to `limit` for an event matching `want`; other events are skipped.
    fn wait_for(
        rx: &mpsc::Receiver<WatchEvent>,
        limit: Duration,
        want: impl Fn(&WatchEvent) -> bool,
    ) -> Option<WatchEvent> {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + limit;
        loop {
            let left = deadline.checked_duration_since(Instant::now())?;
            match rx.recv_timeout(left) {
                Ok(event) if want(&event) => return Some(event),
                Ok(_) => continue,
                Err(_) => return None,
            }
        }
    }

            match rx.recv_timeout(left) {
                Ok(WatchEvent::Changes(c)) => count += c.iter().filter(|(_, n)| n == name).count(),
                Ok(_) => {}
                Err(_) => break,
            }
        }
```

```rust
use windows::Win32::Storage::FileSystem::{

    FILE_ACTION_REMOVED, FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_NEW_NAME, FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_OLD_NAME,

    FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME, FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_WRITE, FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_SIZE,
    FILE_SHARE_DELETE, FILE_SHARE_READ, FILE_SHARE_WRITE, OPEN_EXISTING,
```

Insert directly above the `#[cfg(test)]` line that opens `mod tests {` in `win.rs`, after `parse_notifications` (one blank line on each side; not above the `#[cfg(test)]` attribute of `MASK_NAME_WRITE`):

```rust
pub struct DirWatcher;

impl DirWatcher {
    /// Opens `dir` synchronously, so a missing directory is `Err(NotFound)` here (the caller
    /// reports `Missing`). Then thread "dirwatch-<dir file name>" keeps one overlapped
    /// ReadDirectoryChangesW request queued, blocks in GetOverlappedResult until it completes
    /// and hands every result to `sink`; `sink` returning false ends the thread. Returns after
    /// the first ReadDirectoryChangesW request is queued: the kernel records changes from that
    /// request on, so an enumeration done after `spawn` returns cannot miss a change.
    pub fn spawn(
        dir: &Path,
        recursive: bool,
        mask: u32,
        mut sink: impl FnMut(WatchEvent) -> bool + Send + 'static,
    ) -> io::Result<()> {
        let wide: Vec<u16> = dir.as_os_str().encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect();
        let raw = unsafe {
            CreateFileW(
                PCWSTR(wide.as_ptr()),
                FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY.0,
                FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE,
                None,
                OPEN_EXISTING,
                FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED,
                None,
            )
        }
        .map_err(io_error)?;
        let handle = unsafe { OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(raw.0) };
        // Manual-reset event that each request signals when it completes.
        let event = unsafe { CreateEventW(None, true, false, PCWSTR::null()) }.map_err(io_error)?;
        let done_event = unsafe { OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(event.0) };
        let name = format!(
            "dirwatch-{}",
            dir.file_name().map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default()
        );
        let (ready, started) = mpsc::sync_channel::<()>(1);
        std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name(name)
            .spawn(move || watch_loop(&handle, &done_event, recursive, mask, ready, &mut sink))?;
        started
            .recv()
            .map_err(|_| io::Error::other("dirwatch thread ended before its first request"))
    }
}

fn watch_loop(
    dir: &OwnedHandle,
    done_event: &OwnedHandle,
    recursive: bool,
    mask: u32,
    ready: mpsc::SyncSender<()>,
    sink: &mut impl FnMut(WatchEvent) -> bool,
) {
    // u32 storage keeps the FILE_NOTIFY_INFORMATION records DWORD-aligned.
    let mut buf = vec![0u32; WATCH_BUFFER / 4];
    let mut ready = Some(ready);
    loop {
        let mut ov = OVERLAPPED { hEvent: HANDLE(done_event.as_raw_handle()), ..Default::default() };
        let issued = unsafe {
            ReadDirectoryChangesW(
                HANDLE(dir.as_raw_handle()),
                buf.as_mut_ptr().cast(),
                WATCH_BUFFER as u32,
                recursive,
                FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE(mask),
                None,
                Some(&mut ov as *mut OVERLAPPED),
                None,
            )
        };
        // The first request is queued (or refused): from here on the kernel records changes.
        if let Some(ready) = ready.take() {
            // spawn() holds the receiver, blocked in recv(), so this send cannot fail. Never
            // return here: the kernel may still be writing into `buf` and `ov`.
            ready.send(()).ok();
        }
        // bWait = TRUE: returns only after the request has completed, so `buf` and `ov` are
        // never released while the kernel still owns them.
        let mut returned = 0u32;
        let result = issued.and_then(|()| unsafe {
            GetOverlappedResult(HANDLE(dir.as_raw_handle()), &ov, &mut returned, true)
        });
        let event = match result {
            Ok(()) if returned == 0 => WatchEvent::Overflow,
            Ok(()) => {
                let len = (returned as usize).min(WATCH_BUFFER);
                let bytes = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(buf.as_ptr().cast::<u8>(), len) };
                WatchEvent::Changes(parse_notifications(bytes))
            }
            Err(err) if err.code() == ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR.to_hresult() => WatchEvent::Overflow,
            Err(err) => {
                sink(WatchEvent::Error(io_error(err)));
                return;
            }
        };
        if !sink(event) {
            return;
        }
    }
}

/// windows-rs wraps a Win32 error in an HRESULT, and its `From` for io::Error keeps the
/// HRESULT, which hides `ErrorKind::NotFound` & co. Give std the plain Win32 code back.
fn io_error(err: windows::core::Error) -> io::Error {
    match WIN32_ERROR::from_error(&err) {
        Some(code) => io::Error::from_raw_os_error(code.0 as i32),
        None => io::Error::other(err),
    }
}
```

Insert directly above the `#[cfg(test)]` line that opens `mod tests {` in `win.rs`, after `io_error` (one blank line on each side):

```rust
pub mod proc {
    use std::io;
    use std::os::windows::io::{AsRawHandle, FromRawHandle, OwnedHandle};

    use windows::core::PWSTR;
    use windows::Win32::Foundation::{
        ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER, ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, FILETIME,
        HANDLE, WAIT_OBJECT_0, WAIT_TIMEOUT, WIN32_ERROR,
    };
    use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{
        GetProcessTimes, OpenProcess, QueryFullProcessImageNameW, WaitForSingleObject,
        PROCESS_NAME_WIN32, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE,
    };

    use super::io_error;
    use crate::observe::keys::ProcId;

    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum ProcError {
        NotFound,
        AccessDenied,
        Exited,
        Os(io::Error),
    }

    /// Proof that `pid` is a live process (spec §5.5 step 3): OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE |
    /// QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) → still running (a handle held elsewhere keeps an exited
    /// process object and its pid alive) → creation FILETIME → image path. The handle is
    /// returned for `Registry::watch`.
    pub fn identify(pid: u32) -> Result<(ProcId, OwnedHandle), ProcError> {
        let raw = unsafe {
            OpenProcess(PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, false, pid)
        }
        .map_err(|err| match WIN32_ERROR::from_error(&err) {
            Some(ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) => ProcError::NotFound,
            Some(ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED) => ProcError::AccessDenied,
            _ => ProcError::Os(io_error(err)),
        })?;
        let handle = unsafe { OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(raw.0) };
        let h = HANDLE(handle.as_raw_handle());

        let state = unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(h, 0) };
        if state == WAIT_OBJECT_0 {
            return Err(ProcError::Exited);
        }
        if state != WAIT_TIMEOUT {
            return Err(ProcError::Os(io::Error::last_os_error()));
        }

        let mut created = FILETIME::default();
        let mut exited = FILETIME::default();
        let mut kernel = FILETIME::default();
        let mut user = FILETIME::default();
        unsafe { GetProcessTimes(h, &mut created, &mut exited, &mut kernel, &mut user) }
            .map_err(|err| ProcError::Os(io_error(err)))?;
        let created_ft = (u64::from(created.dwHighDateTime) << 32) | u64::from(created.dwLowDateTime);

        let image = image_path(h).map_err(ProcError::Os)?;
        Ok((ProcId { pid, created_ft, image }, handle))
    }

    fn image_path(h: HANDLE) -> io::Result<String> {
        for capacity in [1024usize, 32_768] {
            let mut buf = vec![0u16; capacity];
            let mut len = capacity as u32;
            match unsafe { QueryFullProcessImageNameW(h, PROCESS_NAME_WIN32, PWSTR(buf.as_mut_ptr()), &mut len) } {
                Ok(()) => return Ok(String::from_utf16_lossy(&buf[..len as usize])),
                Err(err) if WIN32_ERROR::from_error(&err) == Some(ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER) => continue,
                Err(err) => return Err(io_error(err)),
            }
        }
        Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER.0 as i32))
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Windows integration tests of the exit-waiter registry (spec §12, D38).
#[cfg(all(test, windows))]
mod registry_tests {
    use super::proc::Registry;
    use crate::observe::keys::ProcId;
    use std::os::windows::io::AsHandle;
    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
    use std::sync::mpsc;
    use std::time::Duration;

    #[test]
    fn registry_fires_once_per_process_and_refuses_a_second_waiter() {
        // `set /p` keeps cmd alive until its stdin closes, so both watch calls see it running.
        let mut child = Command::new("cmd")
            .args(["/d", "/c", "set /p _="])
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .unwrap();
        // D38: duplicated child handles and a hand-built ProcId (identify could race the exit).
        let id = ProcId { pid: child.id(), created_ft: 1, image: String::new() };
        let registry = Registry::new();
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
        let dup = child.as_handle().try_clone_to_owned().unwrap();
        assert!(registry.watch(&id, dup, move |pid, ft| tx.send((pid, ft)).unwrap()));
        assert!(registry.is_watched(id.pid, 1));
        let dup2 = child.as_handle().try_clone_to_owned().unwrap();
        assert!(
            !registry.watch(&id, dup2, |_, _| panic!("a second waiter must not exist")),
            "the same (pid, created) must not get a second thread"
        );

        drop(child.stdin.take()); // EOF → `set /p` returns → cmd exits
        assert_eq!(rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).unwrap(), (id.pid, 1));
        assert!(!registry.is_watched(id.pid, 1), "the entry is removed before on_exit runs");
        child.wait().unwrap();
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// Exit waiters shared by claude-io and codex-io: at most one thread per (pid, created_ft).
    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
    pub struct Registry {
        watched: Arc<Mutex<HashSet<(u32, u64)>>>,
    }

    impl Registry {
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self::default()
        }

        /// Returns false (and drops `handle`) if this process is already watched, or if the
        /// waiter thread could not be started: then the entry is removed and the failure is
        /// logged, so a later proof registers again. Otherwise thread "proc-exit-<pid>" waits
        /// INFINITE on the given handle, removes the entry, then calls `on_exit(pid,
        /// created_ft)`. A failed wait is logged and does not call `on_exit` (the entry is
        /// removed, so the next proof registers again).
        pub fn watch(
            &self,
            id: &ProcId,
            handle: OwnedHandle,
            on_exit: impl FnOnce(u32, u64) + Send + 'static,
        ) -> bool {
            let key = (id.pid, id.created_ft);
            if !self.watched.lock().unwrap().insert(key) {
                return false;
            }
            let watched = Arc::clone(&self.watched);
            let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name(format!("proc-exit-{}", id.pid))
                .spawn(move || {
                    let state = unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(HANDLE(handle.as_raw_handle()), INFINITE) };
                    let failure = (state != WAIT_OBJECT_0).then(io::Error::last_os_error);
                    drop(handle);
                    watched.lock().unwrap().remove(&key);
                    match failure {
                        None => on_exit(key.0, key.1),
                        Some(err) => crate::log::line(format!("proc-exit wait failed pid={}: {err}", key.0)),
                    }
                });
            if let Err(err) = spawned {
                self.watched.lock().unwrap().remove(&key);
                crate::log::line(format!("proc-exit thread not started pid={}: {err}", key.0));
                return false;
            }
            true
        }

        pub fn is_watched(&self, pid: u32, created_ft: u64) -> bool {
            self.watched.lock().unwrap().contains(&(pid, created_ft))
        }
    }
```

Choices inside the contract's room (recorded so T9/T11 can rely on them):
- `fact_of` returns None for a title record whose title is missing or blank (it is no title); title text is `collapse(_, 160)`.
- `interrupted` looks at string content and `text` blocks only, never at `tool_result` content (tool output can quote the marker — seen in real transcripts), and only at a text that starts with the marker (D62 below).
- `parse_session_file` errors carry only serde_json's position text ("invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a string at line 1 column 93"), never file content, so T11 may log them.
- The 256 KiB window and "drop the bytes before the first '\n'" (spec §12 lists it under claude_transcript tests) belong to `JsonlTail::start_with_window` and are tested in T5, not here.
- Spec §12 "мусорный JSON у известного файла сохраняет состояние" is tested in T11 (claude-io), not here: T7 only checks that `parse_session_file` returns Err (`empty_truncated_and_non_object_files_are_errors`). `observe::claude::io_thread::tests::garbage_in_a_known_file_keeps_the_session_and_degrades_health` (T11) writes garbage bytes into the session file of a known pid and checks that no `ClaudeGone` is sent (the model keeps the last `ClaudeFile`) and that `SourceHealth{Claude, Degraded{unreadable: 1}}` is sent.

Contract amendment (contract §7 D62; the spec wins over the contract):
- **D62** `fact_of` sets `interrupted` only when the string content or a `text` block, after leading whitespace, starts with `INTERRUPT_MARKER` (`text.trim_start().starts_with(INTERRUPT_MARKER)`), not when it merely contains it (contract §2.12 states this on `fact_of`). Spec §7 rule 1 ("Последняя запись user — маркер `[Request interrupted by user`") and §3 ("запись user с текстом `[Request interrupted by user`") name a user record that *is* the marker. With "contains", a prompt that quotes the marker mid-sentence (a user discussing Mayak itself) is the last User fact of a turn without tool calls, so `terminal_outcome` returns Interrupted instead of Finished and the alert is lost. Local evidence (counts only, 1412 transcript files under `~/.claude/projects`; re-counted at review with 1429 files, same result): all 3 real markers in main-chain user text start their text block, none is mid-text (2 more quotes sit in tool_result content, which never counts). Contract §7 records this as D62, and the §2.12 comment on `fact_of` reads "`interrupted` = string content or a text block that starts (after leading whitespace) with INTERRUPT_MARKER (`text.trim_start().starts_with(INTERRUPT_MARKER)`); tool_result content never counts (D62)". No task step edits `contract.md`; T7's code and tests already follow D62, and T9's tests (leading marker) pass under both readings.

In `windows/src-tauri/src/observe/text.rs`, insert the following directly after the two header comment lines (before the blank line that precedes `#[cfg(test)]`):

```rust

use serde_json::Value;

/// Longest summary, label or title the observer keeps (spec §7: "первые 160 символов").
pub const SUMMARY_MAX: usize = 160;

/// Tool input fields that name what a tool acts on, most specific first (the order of the
/// island's approval card).
pub const TARGET_FIELDS: &[&str] = &["command", "file_path", "path", "url", "query", "pattern", "prompt"];

/// Whitespace runs (including newlines) become one space, the ends are trimmed, and the
/// first `max_chars` characters are kept. No ellipsis.
pub fn collapse(s: &str, max_chars: usize) -> String {
    let joined = s.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
    joined.chars().take(max_chars).collect()
}

/// Label of one tool call. `AskUserQuestion` → its first question; otherwise
/// `"<tool> · <target>"` with the first non-blank `TARGET_FIELDS` value (an array of strings
/// is joined with ' '), or `"<tool>"` without one. The result is `collapse(_, SUMMARY_MAX)`.
pub fn tool_label(tool: &str, input: Option<&Value>) -> String {
    if tool == "AskUserQuestion" {
        let question = input
            .and_then(|i| i.pointer("/questions/0/question"))
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .filter(|q| !q.trim().is_empty());
        if let Some(q) = question {
            return collapse(q, SUMMARY_MAX);
        }
    }
    let target = input.and_then(|i| TARGET_FIELDS.iter().find_map(|field| target_text(i.get(*field)?)));
    match target {
        Some(t) => collapse(&format!("{tool} · {t}"), SUMMARY_MAX),
        None => collapse(tool, SUMMARY_MAX),
    }
}

fn target_text(v: &Value) -> Option<String> {
    let text = match v {
        Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
        Value::Array(items) => items.iter().filter_map(Value::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" "),
        _ => return None,
    };
    if text.trim().is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(text)
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Implement session-file parsing, acceptance and host classification**

In `windows/src-tauri/src/observe/claude.rs`, insert the following directly after the three header comment lines (before the blank line that precedes `#[cfg(test)]`):

```rust

use std::path::Path;

use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use super::keys::HostKind;
use super::paths::{glob_match, normalize};

/// One `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`. Built field by field from a `serde_json::Value`: a
/// missing key or a value of the wrong JSON type gives None for that field only, and unknown
/// keys are ignored. The format is undocumented and changes with Claude Code (spec §15).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ClaudeSessionFile {
    pub pid: Option<u32>,
    pub session_id: Option<String>,
    pub cwd: Option<String>,
    /// Decimal creation FILETIME: a JSON string as is, or a JSON u64 number in decimal.
    pub proc_start: Option<String>,
    pub version: Option<String>,
    pub kind: Option<String>,
    pub entrypoint: Option<String>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub name_source: Option<String>,
    pub status: Option<String>,
    pub waiting_for: Option<String>,
    /// Milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
    pub status_updated_at: Option<i64>,
    pub updated_at: Option<i64>,
    pub spare: Option<bool>,
    pub parked_job_id: Option<String>,
    pub pid_domain: Option<String>,
}

/// `^[0-9]+\.json$` without a regex crate. The `<pid>.<hash>.key` files next to the session
/// files hold peer tokens and must never match.
pub fn is_session_file_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    match name.strip_suffix(".json") {
        Some(stem) => !stem.is_empty() && stem.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()),
        None => false,
    }
}

/// Empty or whitespace-only → Err("empty"); invalid JSON → Err("invalid JSON: …", position
/// only, never content); valid JSON that is not an object → Err("not an object"). Any JSON
/// object → Ok. Never panics.
pub fn parse_session_file(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<ClaudeSessionFile, String> {
    if bytes.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_whitespace) {
        return Err("empty".to_string());
    }
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(bytes).map_err(|e| format!("invalid JSON: {e}"))?;
    let Value::Object(o) = value else {
        return Err("not an object".to_string());
    };
    Ok(ClaudeSessionFile {
        pid: o.get("pid").and_then(Value::as_u64).and_then(|n| u32::try_from(n).ok()),
        session_id: text(&o, "sessionId"),
        cwd: text(&o, "cwd"),
        proc_start: match o.get("procStart") {
            Some(Value::String(s)) => Some(s.clone()),
            Some(Value::Number(n)) => n.as_u64().map(|n| n.to_string()),
            _ => None,
        },
        version: text(&o, "version"),
        kind: text(&o, "kind"),
        entrypoint: text(&o, "entrypoint"),
        name: text(&o, "name"),
        name_source: text(&o, "nameSource"),
        status: text(&o, "status"),
        waiting_for: text(&o, "waitingFor"),
        status_updated_at: o.get("statusUpdatedAt").and_then(Value::as_i64),
        updated_at: o.get("updatedAt").and_then(Value::as_i64),
        spare: o.get("spare").and_then(Value::as_bool),
        parked_job_id: text(&o, "parkedJobId"),
        pid_domain: text(&o, "pidDomain"),
    })
}

fn text(o: &Map<String, Value>, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    o.get(key).and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SkipReason {
    Spare,
    Parked,
    ForeignDomain,
    Incomplete,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Accept {
    Track { pid: u32, proc_start: u64 },
    Skip(SkipReason),
}

/// Spec §5.5 item 2, in order: spare → Spare; non-empty `parkedJobId` → Parked; `pidDomain`
/// present and not starting with "win32:" → ForeignDomain; pid missing, procStart missing or
/// not a u64, sessionId or cwd missing/empty → Incomplete (the source counts it as unreadable).
pub fn accept(f: &ClaudeSessionFile) -> Accept {
    if f.spare == Some(true) {
        return Accept::Skip(SkipReason::Spare);
    }
    if f.parked_job_id.as_deref().is_some_and(|j| !j.is_empty()) {
        return Accept::Skip(SkipReason::Parked);
    }
    if f.pid_domain.as_deref().is_some_and(|d| !d.starts_with("win32:")) {
        return Accept::Skip(SkipReason::ForeignDomain);
    }
    let filled = |s: &Option<String>| s.as_deref().is_some_and(|v| !v.is_empty());
    let proc_start = f.proc_start.as_deref().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok());
    match (f.pid, proc_start) {
        (Some(pid), Some(proc_start)) if filled(&f.session_id) && filled(&f.cwd) => {
            Accept::Track { pid, proc_start }
        }
        _ => Accept::Skip(SkipReason::Incomplete),
    }
}

/// Claude Desktop (MSIX) runs `claude.exe` from its package folder; virtualized views
/// (`Get-Process`) show the same file under `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude-code\<ver>\`.
const DESKTOP_MSIX: &str = r"**\packages\claude_*\localcache\roaming\claude\claude-code\*\claude.exe";
const CURSOR_EXTENSION: &str = r"**\.cursor\extensions\anthropic.claude-code-*\**\claude.exe";
const VSCODE_EXTENSION: &str = r"**\.vscode\extensions\anthropic.claude-code-*\**\claude.exe";

/// Host of a Claude process from its raw image path (QueryFullProcessImageNameW), compared as
/// `paths::normalize(image).key` (spec §5.5 item 5). A Desktop image counts as ClaudeDesktop
/// only together with `entrypoint == "claude-desktop"`, else Unknown. `appdata` is %APPDATA%,
/// passed in by the caller (no environment reads here).
pub fn classify_host(image: &str, entrypoint: Option<&str>, appdata: &Path) -> HostKind {
    let key = normalize(image).key;
    let roaming_desktop = !appdata.as_os_str().is_empty()
        && glob_match(
            &key,
            &format!(r"{}\claude\claude-code\*\claude.exe", normalize(&appdata.to_string_lossy()).key),
        );
    if glob_match(&key, DESKTOP_MSIX) || roaming_desktop {
        return if entrypoint == Some("claude-desktop") { HostKind::ClaudeDesktop } else { HostKind::Unknown };
    }
    if glob_match(&key, CURSOR_EXTENSION) {
        HostKind::Cursor
    } else if glob_match(&key, VSCODE_EXTENSION) {
        HostKind::VsCode
    } else {
        HostKind::Unknown
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 14: Write the failing transcript tests**

Create `windows/src-tauri/src/observe/claude_transcript.rs` with exactly this content:

```rust
// Facts from Claude Code transcript records (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl`,
// spec §5.5 "Транскрипт", §7 "Вычисление итога"). Pure: the model passes parsed records in;
// nothing here reads files or keeps state.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    const END_TURN: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/turn_end_turn.jsonl");
    const REFUSAL: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/turn_refusal.jsonl");
    const API_ERROR: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/turn_api_error.jsonl");
    const INTERRUPTED: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/turn_interrupted.jsonl");
    const TOOL_USE_AFTER_END: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/turn_tool_use_after_end.jsonl");
    const NO_ASSISTANT: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/turn_no_assistant.jsonl");
    const TOOLS_PAIRING: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/tools_pairing.jsonl");
    const TITLES: &str = include_str!("fixtures/claude/titles.jsonl");

    /// (byte offset of the line, fact) for every line that yields a fact — what the model
    /// gets from `ClaudeTranscript.records`. Works with LF and CRLF checkouts.
    fn facts(src: &str) -> Vec<(u64, Fact)> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut offset = 0u64;
        for line in src.split_inclusive('\n') {
            let text = line.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
            if !text.is_empty() {
                let v: Value = serde_json::from_str(text).expect("fixture lines are JSON");
                if let Some(fact) = fact_of(&v) {
                    out.push((offset, fact));
                }
            }
            offset += line.len() as u64;
        }
        out
    }

    fn plain(list: &[(u64, Fact)]) -> Vec<Fact> {
        list.iter().map(|(_, fact)| fact.clone()).collect()
    }

    fn user(tool_results: &[&str]) -> Fact {
        Fact::User { interrupted: false, tool_results: tool_results.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect() }
    }

    fn assistant(stop_reason: Option<&str>, text: &str, tool_uses: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Fact {
        Fact::Assistant {
            stop_reason: stop_reason.map(str::to_owned),
            api_error: None,
            text: text.to_owned(),
            tool_uses: tool_uses.iter().map(|(id, label)| ToolUse { id: id.to_string(), label: label.to_string() }).collect(),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn main_chain_is_user_and_assistant_outside_sidechains() {
        assert!(is_main_chain(&json!({ "type": "user", "isSidechain": false })));
        assert!(is_main_chain(&json!({ "type": "assistant" })));
        assert!(!is_main_chain(&json!({ "type": "assistant", "isSidechain": true })));
        for other in ["system", "attachment", "last-prompt", "queue-operation", "file-history-snapshot", "ai-title"] {
            assert!(!is_main_chain(&json!({ "type": other, "isSidechain": false })), "{other}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn records_outside_the_conversation_give_no_fact() {
        let records: Vec<Value> = END_TURN.lines().map(|l| serde_json::from_str(l).unwrap()).collect();
        assert_eq!(records.len(), 8);
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&records[6]), None, "system stop_hook_summary");
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&records[7]), None, "last-prompt");
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&json!({ "type": "attachment", "isSidechain": false })), None);
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&json!([1, 2])), None);
        assert_eq!(facts(END_TURN).len(), 6);
    }

    #[test]
    fn end_turn_fixture_yields_user_and_assistant_facts() {
        let list = plain(&facts(END_TURN));
        assert_eq!(list[0], user(&[]));
        assert_eq!(list[1], assistant(Some("tool_use"), "", &[]), "thinking-only record");
        assert_eq!(list[2], assistant(Some("tool_use"), "", &[("toolu_01", "Bash · cargo test")]));
        assert_eq!(list[3], user(&["toolu_01"]));
        assert_eq!(list[5], assistant(Some("end_turn"), "All 12 tests pass. Nothing else changed.", &[]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn labels_follow_the_target_field_order() {
        let labels: Vec<String> = plain(&facts(TOOLS_PAIRING))
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|fact| match fact {
                Fact::Assistant { tool_uses, .. } => tool_uses.into_iter().map(|t| t.label).collect(),
                _ => Vec::new(),
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            labels,
            [
                "Bash · git status",
                r"Read · C:\Users\dev\src\demo\README.md",
                "Grep · src",
                "Which database should the demo use?",
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn pairing_ignores_sidechain_records() {
        let list = facts(TOOLS_PAIRING);
        assert_eq!(list.len(), 7, "the two sidechain records give no fact");
        let pending = pair_tools(list.iter().map(|(_, fact)| fact));
        assert_eq!(
            pending,
            vec![
                ("toolu_B".to_string(), r"Read · C:\Users\dev\src\demo\README.md".to_string()),
                ("toolu_D".to_string(), "Which database should the demo use?".to_string()),
            ],
            "toolu_B stays open: only a sidechain record answered it"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn apply_tools_step_by_step_matches_pair_tools() {
        let list = facts(TOOLS_PAIRING);
        let mut pending = Vec::new();
        let mut sizes = Vec::new();
        for (_, fact) in &list {
            apply_tools(&mut pending, fact);
            sizes.push(pending.len());
        }
        assert_eq!(sizes, [0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(pending, pair_tools(list.iter().map(|(_, fact)| fact)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn last_tool_label_is_the_latest_call() {
        let list = facts(TOOLS_PAIRING);
        assert_eq!(last_tool_label(list.iter().map(|(_, fact)| fact)).as_deref(), Some("Which database should the demo use?"));
        let none = facts(NO_ASSISTANT);
        assert_eq!(last_tool_label(none.iter().map(|(_, fact)| fact)), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_interrupt_marker_counts_in_text_not_in_tool_output() {
        let string_content = json!({ "type": "user", "message": { "role": "user", "content": "[Request interrupted by user]" } });
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&string_content), Some(Fact::User { interrupted: true, tool_results: vec![] }));
        let last = facts(INTERRUPTED).pop().unwrap().1;
        assert_eq!(last, Fact::User { interrupted: true, tool_results: vec![] });
        // tools_pairing line 6: a tool_result whose output quotes the marker.
        assert_eq!(facts(TOOLS_PAIRING)[5].1, user(&["toolu_C"]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_prompt_quoting_the_marker_mid_sentence_is_no_interrupt() {
        // D62: the interrupt record starts with the marker; a prompt that mentions it is a prompt.
        let quoted = "Why is the turn lost? see the [Request interrupted by user marker in the log";
        let as_string = json!({ "type": "user", "message": { "role": "user", "content": quoted } });
        let as_block = json!({ "type": "user", "message": { "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": quoted }] } });
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&as_string), Some(user(&[])));
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&as_block), Some(user(&[])));
        let indented = json!({ "type": "user", "message": { "role": "user", "content": "\n [Request interrupted by user]" } });
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&indented), Some(Fact::User { interrupted: true, tool_results: vec![] }));
        let list = vec![(0, fact_of(&as_string).unwrap()), (10, assistant(Some("end_turn"), "Only a leading marker counts.", &[]))];
        assert_eq!(
            terminal_outcome(&list, 0),
            (TurnOutcome::Finished { summary: "Only a leading marker counts.".into() }, Some(10))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn titles_come_from_title_records() {
        assert_eq!(
            plain(&facts(TITLES)),
            vec![
                Fact::Title { kind: TitleKind::Ai, text: "Investigate flaky test".into() },
                Fact::Title { kind: TitleKind::Custom, text: "Release prep".into() },

            ],
            "a blank custom title and the mode record give nothing"
        );
        let sidechain_title = json!({ "type": "ai-title", "aiTitle": "Side", "isSidechain": true });
        assert_eq!(fact_of(&sidechain_title), Some(Fact::Title { kind: TitleKind::Ai, text: "Side".into() }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn end_turn_finishes_with_the_collapsed_text() {
        let list = facts(END_TURN);
        let deciding = list.last().unwrap().0;
        assert_eq!(
            terminal_outcome(&list, 0),
            (TurnOutcome::Finished { summary: "All 12 tests pass. Nothing else changed.".into() }, Some(deciding))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn refusal_finishes() {
        let list = facts(REFUSAL);
        let deciding = list.last().unwrap().0;
        assert_eq!(
            terminal_outcome(&list, 0),
            (TurnOutcome::Finished { summary: "I can't help with that request.".into() }, Some(deciding))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_api_error_record_is_an_error() {
        let list = facts(API_ERROR);
        let deciding = list.last().unwrap().0;
        let expected = ApiError {
            code: Some("rate_limit".into()),
            status: Some(429),
            text: "API Error: Rate limit reached. Try again later.".into(),

    #[test]
    fn a_successful_retry_after_an_api_error_finishes() {
        let mut list = facts(API_ERROR);

    #[test]

        let result_after_end = vec![(0, assistant(Some("end_turn"), "Done.", &[])), (10, user(&["toolu_9"]))];

    #[test]

        let list = vec![

    #[test]
    fn only_facts_from_the_turn_start_count() {
        let both = format!("{END_TURN}{NO_ASSISTANT}");

        let one = facts(END_TURN);
        let after_final = one.last().unwrap().0 + 1;
        assert_eq!(terminal_outcome(&one, after_final), (TurnOutcome::Pending, None));
```
