In `windows/src-tauri/src/observe/claude_transcript.rs`, insert the following directly after the three header comment lines (before the blank line that precedes `#[cfg(test)]`):

```rust

use serde_json::Value;

use super::text::{collapse, tool_label, SUMMARY_MAX};

/// Prefix of the user record Claude Code writes when the user interrupts a turn
/// ("…by user]" or "…by user for tool use]").
pub const INTERRUPT_MARKER: &str = "[Request interrupted by user";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ToolUse {
    pub id: String,
    /// `text::tool_label(name, input)`.
    pub label: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ApiError {
    /// The record's `error`, e.g. "rate_limit".
    pub code: Option<String>,
    /// The record's `apiErrorStatus`, e.g. 429.
    pub status: Option<u16>,
    /// Collapsed message text.
    pub text: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TitleKind {
    /// `custom-title` / `customTitle`
    Custom,
    /// `agent-name` / `agentName`
    Agent,
    /// `ai-title` / `aiTitle`
    Ai,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Fact {
    /// Main-chain `type: user`.
    User { interrupted: bool, tool_results: Vec<String> },
    /// Main-chain `type: assistant`.
    Assistant { stop_reason: Option<String>, api_error: Option<ApiError>, text: String, tool_uses: Vec<ToolUse> },
    /// `custom-title` / `agent-name` / `ai-title` (any chain).
    Title { kind: TitleKind, text: String },
}

/// `isSidechain != true` and `type` ∈ {user, assistant}. Subagent records carry
/// `isSidechain: true`.
pub fn is_main_chain(v: &Value) -> bool {
    v.get("isSidechain").and_then(Value::as_bool) != Some(true)
        && matches!(v.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str), Some("user" | "assistant"))
}

/// The fact a record contributes, or None for records that are neither main-chain
/// user/assistant nor title records (system, attachment, last-prompt, …). A title record
/// whose title is missing or blank is no title (None). Title text is `collapse(_, 160)`.
pub fn fact_of(v: &Value) -> Option<Fact> {
    match v.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str)? {
        "custom-title" => title_fact(v, TitleKind::Custom, "customTitle"),
        "agent-name" => title_fact(v, TitleKind::Agent, "agentName"),
        "ai-title" => title_fact(v, TitleKind::Ai, "aiTitle"),
        "user" if is_main_chain(v) => Some(user_fact(v.pointer("/message/content"))),
        "assistant" if is_main_chain(v) => Some(assistant_fact(v)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn title_fact(v: &Value, kind: TitleKind, field: &str) -> Option<Fact> {
    let text = collapse(v.get(field)?.as_str()?, SUMMARY_MAX);
    (!text.is_empty()).then_some(Fact::Title { kind, text })
}

/// `interrupted`: the string content or a text block is the interrupt record, i.e. starts with
/// INTERRUPT_MARKER after leading whitespace (D62: a prompt quoting the marker mid-sentence is
/// not an interrupt). tool_result content does not count: tool output may quote the marker.
fn user_fact(content: Option<&Value>) -> Fact {
    let mut interrupted = false;
    let mut tool_results = Vec::new();
    match content {
        Some(Value::String(s)) => interrupted = is_interrupt(s),
        Some(Value::Array(blocks)) => {
            for block in blocks {
                match block.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                    Some("text") => {
                        let text = block.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                        interrupted |= is_interrupt(text);
                    }
                    Some("tool_result") => {
                        if let Some(id) = block.get("tool_use_id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                            tool_results.push(id.to_owned());
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    Fact::User { interrupted, tool_results }
}

fn is_interrupt(text: &str) -> bool {
    text.trim_start().starts_with(INTERRUPT_MARKER)
}

/// Text blocks joined by ' ' and collapsed to SUMMARY_MAX; thinking blocks are ignored.
/// `isApiErrorMessage: true` → ApiError { error, apiErrorStatus, the same text }.
fn assistant_fact(v: &Value) -> Fact {
    let mut texts: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    let mut tool_uses = Vec::new();
    match v.pointer("/message/content") {
        Some(Value::String(s)) => texts.push(s),
        Some(Value::Array(blocks)) => {
            for block in blocks {
                match block.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                    Some("text") => texts.extend(block.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str)),
                    Some("tool_use") => {
                        if let Some(id) = block.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                            let name = block.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                            tool_uses.push(ToolUse { id: id.to_owned(), label: tool_label(name, block.get("input")) });
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    let text = collapse(&texts.join(" "), SUMMARY_MAX);
    let api_error = (v.get("isApiErrorMessage").and_then(Value::as_bool) == Some(true)).then(|| ApiError {
        code: v.get("error").and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned),
        status: v.get("apiErrorStatus").and_then(Value::as_u64).and_then(|s| u16::try_from(s).ok()),
        text: text.clone(),
    });
    Fact::Assistant {
        stop_reason: v.pointer("/message/stop_reason").and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned),
        api_error,
        text,
        tool_uses,
    }
}

/// Tool pairing, one fact at a time: an Assistant fact adds its tool_uses as (id, label);
/// a User fact removes the ids in its tool_results. Title facts change nothing.
pub fn apply_tools(pending: &mut Vec<(String, String)>, fact: &Fact) {
    match fact {
        Fact::Assistant { tool_uses, .. } => {
            pending.extend(tool_uses.iter().map(|t| (t.id.clone(), t.label.clone())));
        }
        Fact::User { tool_results, .. } => pending.retain(|(id, _)| !tool_results.contains(id)),
        Fact::Title { .. } => {}
    }
}

/// Unresolved tool calls (id, label) in call order, computed from scratch.
pub fn pair_tools<'a>(facts: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a Fact>) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut pending = Vec::new();
    for fact in facts {
        apply_tools(&mut pending, fact);
    }
    pending
}

/// Label of the last tool_use among `facts` (the session's `activity`).
pub fn last_tool_label<'a>(facts: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a Fact>) -> Option<String> {
    facts
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|fact| match fact {
            Fact::Assistant { tool_uses, .. } => tool_uses.last(),
            _ => None,
        })
        .last()
        .map(|t| t.label.clone())
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TurnOutcome {
    Pending,
    Interrupted,
    Error(ApiError),
    Finished { summary: String },
}

/// Outcome of the turn made of the facts with offset >= `after` (spec §7). Assistant records
/// without a stop_reason (streaming fragments) are skipped, so a later successful retry beats
/// an earlier API error:
/// 1. the last User fact is `interrupted` → Interrupted;
/// 2. A = the last Assistant fact with a stop_reason or an API error; A has an API error → Error;
/// 3. A.stop_reason != "tool_use" and no later fact has tool_uses or tool_results →
///    Finished { A.text, or, when empty, the text of the nearest earlier Assistant fact in range
///    with non-empty text, else "" };
/// 4. otherwise Pending (also when there is no such Assistant fact).
/// The second value is the offset of the deciding fact (the User fact for Interrupted, A for
/// Error/Finished), None for Pending; the model uses it so that a final record read after the
/// session went idle is not read again by the next turn.
pub fn terminal_outcome(facts: &[(u64, Fact)], after: u64) -> (TurnOutcome, Option<u64>) {
    let turn: Vec<&(u64, Fact)> = facts.iter().filter(|(offset, _)| *offset >= after).collect();

    let last_user = turn.iter().rev().find_map(|(offset, fact)| match fact {
        Fact::User { interrupted, .. } => Some((*offset, *interrupted)),
        _ => None,
    });
    if let Some((offset, true)) = last_user {
        return (TurnOutcome::Interrupted, Some(offset));
    }

    let decisive = turn.iter().enumerate().rev().find_map(|(index, (offset, fact))| match fact {
        Fact::Assistant { stop_reason, api_error, text, .. } if stop_reason.is_some() || api_error.is_some() => {
            Some((index, *offset, stop_reason, api_error, text))
        }
        _ => None,
    });
    let Some((index, offset, stop_reason, api_error, text)) = decisive else {
        return (TurnOutcome::Pending, None);
    };
    if let Some(error) = api_error {
        return (TurnOutcome::Error(error.clone()), Some(offset));
    }

    let tool_activity_after = turn[index + 1..].iter().any(|(_, fact)| match fact {
        Fact::Assistant { tool_uses, .. } => !tool_uses.is_empty(),
        Fact::User { tool_results, .. } => !tool_results.is_empty(),
        Fact::Title { .. } => false,
    });
    if stop_reason.as_deref() == Some("tool_use") || tool_activity_after {
        return (TurnOutcome::Pending, None);
    }
    let summary = if text.is_empty() {
        turn[..index]
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .find_map(|(_, fact)| match fact {
                Fact::Assistant { text, .. } if !text.is_empty() => Some(text.clone()),
                _ => None,
            })
            .unwrap_or_default()
    } else {
        text.clone()
    };
    (TurnOutcome::Finished { summary }, Some(offset))
}
```

- Used later by: T9 (`HookEvent` in `Signal::CodexHook`, re-exported by `model.rs`), T10 (`parse_rollout_line`, `RolloutRecord`), T12 (`parse_hook`, `classify_host`, `index_title`, `is_readable_rollout`, `parse_rollout_line`, `Unknown` → health), T15 (rule updates after S2/S3).
- There is no `is_subagent_meta` (D67 below; contract §2.13 does not list it). `RolloutRecord::Meta` still carries `parent_thread_id` and `agent_role`.

Choices inside the contract's room:
- `parse_hook` errors keep only the text before the first ':' of serde_json's message ("missing field `session_id`", "invalid type", "invalid value"), so no payload value can reach `mayak.log` when T12 logs "length + reason".
- `Unknown` (not legacy-shaped) also covers: `event_msg`/`response_item` without a string `payload.type`, `session_meta` without a string `payload.id`, `function_call`/`custom_tool_call` without `name`. A missing `call_id` gives `""` (Codex declares it optional on `local_shell_call`).
- `index_title` returns `collapse(thread_name, 160)` (one line, like Claude titles).
- `Meta.parent_thread_id` and `Meta.agent_role` come from the top-level string keys of `session_meta.payload`; when a top-level key is absent or not a string, that field comes from `payload.source.subagent.thread_spawn.<key>` instead. That nested object is the serde form of Codex `SessionSource::SubAgent(SubAgentSource::ThreadSpawn { parent_thread_id, depth, agent_path, agent_nickname, agent_role })` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs` on main; the installed `openai.chatgpt-26.721.30844` codex.exe contains the serde text "struct variant SubAgentSource::ThreadSpawn with 5 elements"). Neither form is observed locally (all 68 local `session_meta` payloads are main threads with a string `source`), so the fixture carries both and S3 (T15) confirms which one 0.146/0.158 write.
- Spec §12 "неизвестная запись → Degraded" is tested in T12 (codex-io), not here: T8 only checks that such lines parse to `RolloutRecord::Unknown` (`records_that_are_not_legacy_shaped_are_unknown`). `observe::codex::io_thread::tests::unknown_records_degrade_health_until_untracked` (T12) appends an unknown record to a tracked rollout and checks `SourceHealth{Codex, Degraded{unreadable: 1}}` (back to `Ok` after `UntrackRollout`); `health_counts_rollouts_with_unknown_records` (T12) checks the count.

Contract amendment (contract §7 D67, orchestrator decision; the spec wins over the contract):
- **D67** `codex::is_subagent_meta` is removed from production code: no production code calls it, so it would leave a permanent `dead_code` warning in the non-test build (T19 Step 2 expects no warnings). `RolloutRecord::Meta` keeps `parent_thread_id` and `agent_role`, parsed as described above, and `subagent_meta_fields_are_parsed` asserts both fields for every line of `rollout_subagent_meta.jsonl`. Spec §5.6 ("сессией он не становится") and §12 ("`session_meta` субагента игнорируется") hold by construction: Codex sessions are created only from hooks keyed by the root `session_id` (subagents share it), and rollout tails start at EOF (T12), so a subagent `Meta` never creates a session; T10 maps `Meta` to a no-op. T15's S3 script also spawns one Codex subagent and reports where `parent_thread_id`, `agent_role` and `source.subagent` appear (keys only). If they are not where T8 parses them, a T15 sub-step updates the `RolloutRecord::Meta` extraction in `observe/codex.rs`, with a fixture and a test. Contract §7 records this as D67, and contract §2.13 has no `is_subagent_meta`. No task step edits `contract.md`.

Observed and reproduced: each line is `{timestamp, type, payload}`; top-level types `session_meta` (repeated many times in one file with the same `id`, and `id == session_id`), `event_msg`, `response_item`, `turn_context`, `world_state`, `compacted`; `task_started{turn_id, started_at, …}`; `task_complete{turn_id, last_agent_message: string|null, completed_at, duration_ms, …}`; `function_call{name, arguments: JSON text, call_id}`; `custom_tool_call{name, input, call_id, status}`. Not present locally, so shaped after spec §3/§5.6 and D11 and to be confirmed by S3 (T15): `turn_aborted{turn_id?, reason}`, `task_complete.error` (string and object forms), `local_shell_call.action`, subagent `session_meta` with top-level `parent_thread_id`/`agent_role` (lines 1–3 of `rollout_subagent_meta.jsonl`) or with them only under `source.subagent.thread_spawn` (line 4, the Codex main serde shape of `SubAgentSource::ThreadSpawn`). Hook payloads follow spec §3 (Codex fields) plus the relay fields of spec §5.2. All values are generic. Create each file under `windows/src-tauri/src/observe/fixtures/codex/` with exactly the shown content and a final newline.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing Codex parsing tests**

Create `windows/src-tauri/src/observe/codex.rs` with exactly this content:

```rust
// Codex source (spec §5.6): hook events forwarded by the relay, rollout records (legacy
// mode), subagent meta, host classification and session_index titles. These functions are
// pure: payloads, lines, paths and %LOCALAPPDATA% come in as arguments.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    const LEGACY: &str = include_str!("fixtures/codex/rollout_legacy.jsonl");
    const SUBAGENT_META: &str = include_str!("fixtures/codex/rollout_subagent_meta.jsonl");
    const UNKNOWN: &str = include_str!("fixtures/codex/rollout_unknown.jsonl");
    const HOOK_PERMISSION: &str = include_str!("fixtures/codex/hook_permission_request.json");
    const HOOK_STOP: &str = include_str!("fixtures/codex/hook_stop.json");
    const SESSION_INDEX: &str = include_str!("fixtures/codex/session_index.jsonl");

    const SESSION: &str = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222";
    const LOCALAPPDATA: &str = r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local";

    fn records(src: &str) -> Vec<RolloutRecord> {
        src.lines()
            .filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
            .map(|line| parse_rollout_line(&serde_json::from_str(line).expect("fixture lines are JSON")))
            .collect()
    }

    fn turn(n: u32) -> Option<String> {
        Some(format!("33333333-3333-4333-8333-33333333333{n}"))
    }

    fn error_of(r: RolloutRecord) -> Option<String> {
        match r {
            RolloutRecord::TaskComplete { error, .. } => error,
            other => panic!("not a task_complete: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_a_permission_request_hook() {
        let event = parse_hook(serde_json::from_str(HOOK_PERMISSION).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let expected = HookEvent {
            hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest".into(),
            session_id: SESSION.into(),
            turn_id: turn(1),
            cwd: r"C:\Users\dev\src\demo".into(),
            transcript_path: Some(
                r"C:\Users\dev\.codex\sessions\2026\10\01\rollout-2026-10-01T10-00-00-22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222.jsonl".into(),
            ),
            tool_name: Some("Bash".into()),
            tool_input: Some(json!({ "command": "cargo test --offline" })),
            last_assistant_message: None,
            agent_id: None,
            agent_type: None,
            relay_ts: 1_790_000_001_000,
            agent_pid: Some(5150),
            agent_created: Some(134_040_000_000_005_150),
            agent_image: Some(r"c:\Users\dev\.cursor\extensions\openai.chatgpt-0.146.0-win32-x64\bin\windows-x86_64\codex.exe".into()),
        };
        assert_eq!(event, expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_a_stop_hook_with_null_fields() {
        let event = parse_hook(serde_json::from_str(HOOK_STOP).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(event.hook_event_name, "Stop");
        assert_eq!(event.turn_id, turn(1));
        assert_eq!(event.last_assistant_message.as_deref(), Some("Tests pass.\nNothing else changed."));
        assert_eq!(event.transcript_path, None);
        assert_eq!((event.agent_pid, event.agent_created, event.agent_image), (None, None, None));
        assert_eq!(event.relay_ts, 1_790_000_009_000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn absent_optional_fields_are_none() {
        let event = parse_hook(json!({
            "hook_event_name": "SessionEnd", "session_id": SESSION, "cwd": r"C:\x", "relay_ts": 5,
            "agent_id": "agent-1", "agent_type": "explorer"
        }))
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(event.turn_id, None);
        assert_eq!(event.transcript_path, None);
        assert_eq!(event.tool_name, None);
        assert_eq!(event.tool_input, None);
        assert_eq!(event.agent_pid, None);
        assert_eq!(event.agent_id.as_deref(), Some("agent-1"));
        assert_eq!(event.agent_type.as_deref(), Some("explorer"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hook_errors_name_the_problem_without_payload_values() {
        assert_eq!(parse_hook(json!([1])), Err("not an object".to_string()));
        let missing = parse_hook(json!({ "hook_event_name": "Stop", "cwd": r"C:\x", "relay_ts": 5 }));
        assert_eq!(missing, Err("missing field `session_id`".to_string()));
        let wrong = parse_hook(json!({ "hook_event_name": "Stop", "session_id": "s", "cwd": r"C:\x", "relay_ts": "secret-value" }));
        assert_eq!(wrong, Err("invalid type".to_string()));
        let negative = parse_hook(json!({ "hook_event_name": "Stop", "session_id": "s", "cwd": r"C:\x", "relay_ts": 5, "agent_pid": -1 }));
        assert_eq!(negative, Err("invalid value".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn legacy_rollout_records() {
        use RolloutRecord::*;
        let call = |id: &str, label: &str| Call { call_id: id.into(), label: label.into() };
        assert_eq!(
            records(LEGACY),
            vec![
                Meta { id: SESSION.into(), cwd: Some(r"C:\Users\dev\src\demo".into()), parent_thread_id: None, agent_role: None },
                TaskStarted { turn_id: turn(1) },
                Other, // turn_context
                Other, // event_msg user_message
                Other, // response_item message
                Other, // response_item reasoning
                call("call_1", "shell · cargo test"),
                Other, // function_call_output
                call("call_2", "exec"),
                Other, // custom_tool_call_output
                call("call_3", "shell · git status"),
                call("call_4", "update_plan"),
                Other, // agent_message
                Other, // token_count
                TaskComplete { turn_id: turn(1), last_agent_message: Some("Tests pass.".into()), error: None },
                TaskStarted { turn_id: turn(2) },
                TurnAborted { turn_id: turn(2) },
                TaskStarted { turn_id: turn(3) },
                TaskComplete { turn_id: turn(3), last_agent_message: None, error: Some("stream disconnected before completion".into()) },
                TaskStarted { turn_id: turn(4) },
                TaskComplete { turn_id: turn(4), last_agent_message: None, error: Some("Usage limit reached".into()) },
                TurnAborted { turn_id: None },
                Other, // world_state
                Other, // compacted
                Other, // event_msg context_compacted
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn task_complete_error_forms() {
        let complete = |error: Value| {
            parse_rollout_line(&json!({ "type": "event_msg", "payload": { "type": "task_complete", "turn_id": "t", "error": error } }))
        };
        assert_eq!(error_of(complete(json!("boom"))), Some("boom".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(error_of(complete(json!({ "message": "Usage limit reached", "code": "x" }))), Some("Usage limit reached".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(error_of(complete(json!({ "code": "x" }))), Some(r#"{"code":"x"}"#.to_string()));
        assert_eq!(error_of(complete(json!(42))), Some("42".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(error_of(complete(Value::Null)), None);
        let absent = json!({ "type": "event_msg", "payload": { "type": "task_complete" } });
        assert_eq!(error_of(parse_rollout_line(&absent)), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn subagent_meta_fields_are_parsed() {
        let meta = |n: u32, parent_thread_id: Option<&str>, agent_role: Option<&str>| RolloutRecord::Meta {
            id: format!("44444444-4444-4444-8444-44444444444{n}"),
            cwd: Some(r"C:\Users\dev\src\demo".into()),
            parent_thread_id: parent_thread_id.map(str::to_owned),
            agent_role: agent_role.map(str::to_owned),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            records(SUBAGENT_META),
            vec![
                meta(1, Some(SESSION), Some("explorer")), // top-level keys
                meta(2, None, Some("worker")), // agent_role only
                meta(3, Some(SESSION), None), // agent_role null
                meta(4, Some(SESSION), Some("explorer")), // only under source.subagent.thread_spawn
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn records_that_are_not_legacy_shaped_are_unknown() {
        assert_eq!(records(UNKNOWN), vec![RolloutRecord::Unknown; 6]);
        assert_eq!(parse_rollout_line(&json!("text")), RolloutRecord::Unknown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn codex_hosts_come_from_the_agent_image() {
        let local = Path::new(LOCALAPPDATA);
        let cases = [
            (r"c:\Users\dev\.cursor\extensions\openai.chatgpt-0.146.0-win32-x64\bin\windows-x86_64\codex.exe", HostKind::Cursor),
            (r"C:\Users\dev\.vscode\extensions\openai.chatgpt-0.155.0-win32-x64\bin\windows-x86_64\codex.exe", HostKind::VsCode),
            (r"C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_26.924.0.0_x64__0000000000000\app\resources\codex.exe", HostKind::CodexDesktop),
            (r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\bin\0.158.0\codex.exe", HostKind::CodexDesktop),
            (r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe", HostKind::Unknown),
            (r"C:\tools\codex.exe", HostKind::Unknown),
        ];
        for (image, host) in cases {
            assert_eq!(classify_host(Some(image), local), host, "{image}");
        }
        assert_eq!(classify_host(None, local), HostKind::Unknown);
        let copy = r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\bin\0.158.0\codex.exe";
        assert_eq!(classify_host(Some(copy), Path::new("")), HostKind::Unknown, "without %LOCALAPPDATA%");
    }

        assert_eq!(index_title(SESSION_INDEX, "66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666"), None, "blank name");
        assert_eq!(index_title(SESSION_INDEX, "77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777"), None, "unknown id");

    #[test]
    fn only_plain_rollout_paths_are_read() {
        assert!(is_readable_rollout(r"C:\Users\dev\.codex\sessions\2026\10\01\rollout-a.jsonl"));
        assert!(!is_readable_rollout(r"C:\Users\dev\.codex\sessions\2026\10\01\rollout-a.jsonl.zst"));

        assert!(!is_readable_rollout("   "));
    }
}
```

```rust
use std::path::Path;

use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use super::keys::HostKind;
use super::paths::{glob_match, normalize};
use super::text::{collapse, tool_label, SUMMARY_MAX};

/// A Codex hook payload as the relay forwards it (spec §5.4 `HookEvent`, §5.2). Keys are
/// snake_case as Codex and the relay write them; unknown keys (`model`, `permission_mode`,
/// `agent`, `relay`, …) are ignored; a missing or null optional field is None.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize)]
pub struct HookEvent {
    pub hook_event_name: String,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub turn_id: Option<String>,
    pub cwd: String,
    pub transcript_path: Option<String>,
    pub tool_name: Option<String>,
    pub tool_input: Option<Value>,
    pub last_assistant_message: Option<String>,
    pub agent_id: Option<String>,
    pub agent_type: Option<String>,
    /// Relay clock, ms since the Unix epoch (UTC).
    pub relay_ts: i64,
    pub agent_pid: Option<u32>,
    /// Creation FILETIME of `agent_pid`.
    pub agent_created: Option<u64>,
    pub agent_image: Option<String>,
}

/// The relay payload as a HookEvent. The error names the problem ("not an object",
/// "missing field `cwd`", "invalid type", …) and never repeats a payload value, so codex-io
/// can log it (logs carry no payload content).
pub fn parse_hook(payload: Value) -> Result<HookEvent, String> {
    if !payload.is_object() {
        return Err("not an object".to_string());
    }
    serde_json::from_value(payload).map_err(|e| {
        let message = e.to_string();
        message.split(':').next().unwrap_or_default().trim().to_string()
    })
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RolloutRecord {
    Meta { id: String, cwd: Option<String>, parent_thread_id: Option<String>, agent_role: Option<String> },
    TaskStarted { turn_id: Option<String> },
    TaskComplete { turn_id: Option<String>, last_agent_message: Option<String>, error: Option<String> },
    TurnAborted { turn_id: Option<String> },
    Call { call_id: String, label: String },
    /// A legacy-shaped record that is not interesting.
    Other,
    /// Not legacy-shaped → source health Degraded.
    Unknown,
}

/// One rollout line, legacy mode only (spec §5.6). Top level `{timestamp, type, payload}`:
/// - `session_meta` with a string `payload.id` → Meta (cwd, parent_thread_id, agent_role);
///   parent_thread_id/agent_role from the top-level payload keys, else from
///   `payload.source.subagent.thread_spawn` (Codex `SubAgentSource::ThreadSpawn`);
/// - `event_msg` + `payload.type` task_started | task_complete | turn_aborted → the variants;
///   `task_complete.error`: string → itself; object → its "message" string, else compact JSON;
///   null or absent → None; any other JSON → compact JSON;
/// - `response_item` + `payload.type` function_call (label `tool_label(name, arguments parsed
///   as JSON)`), custom_tool_call (label `tool_label(name, None)`, i.e. the name), local_shell_call
///   (label `tool_label("shell", payload.action)`) → Call; `call_id` "" when absent;
/// - other `payload.type` values of event_msg/response_item, and top-level turn_context |
///   world_state | compacted → Other;
/// - anything else → Unknown: unknown or missing top-level type, non-object, event_msg or
///   response_item without a string `payload.type`, session_meta without `payload.id`,
///   function_call or custom_tool_call without `name`.
pub fn parse_rollout_line(v: &Value) -> RolloutRecord {
    let Some(kind) = v.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) else {
        return RolloutRecord::Unknown;
    };
    let payload = v.get("payload").and_then(Value::as_object);
    let payload_type = payload.and_then(|p| p.get("type")).and_then(Value::as_str);
    match (kind, payload, payload_type) {
        ("session_meta", Some(p), _) => match string(p, "id") {
            Some(id) => RolloutRecord::Meta {
                id,
                cwd: string(p, "cwd"),
                parent_thread_id: string(p, "parent_thread_id").or_else(|| thread_spawn(v, "parent_thread_id")),
                agent_role: string(p, "agent_role").or_else(|| thread_spawn(v, "agent_role")),
            },
            None => RolloutRecord::Unknown,
        },
        ("event_msg", Some(p), Some("task_started")) => RolloutRecord::TaskStarted { turn_id: string(p, "turn_id") },
        ("event_msg", Some(p), Some("task_complete")) => RolloutRecord::TaskComplete {
            turn_id: string(p, "turn_id"),
            last_agent_message: string(p, "last_agent_message"),
            error: error_text(p.get("error")),
        },
        ("event_msg", Some(p), Some("turn_aborted")) => RolloutRecord::TurnAborted { turn_id: string(p, "turn_id") },
        ("response_item", Some(p), Some("function_call")) => match string(p, "name") {
            Some(name) => RolloutRecord::Call { call_id: call_id(p), label: tool_label(&name, call_arguments(p).as_ref()) },
            None => RolloutRecord::Unknown,
        },
        ("response_item", Some(p), Some("custom_tool_call")) => match string(p, "name") {
            Some(name) => RolloutRecord::Call { call_id: call_id(p), label: tool_label(&name, None) },
            None => RolloutRecord::Unknown,
        },
        ("response_item", Some(p), Some("local_shell_call")) => {
            RolloutRecord::Call { call_id: call_id(p), label: tool_label("shell", p.get("action")) }
        }
        ("event_msg" | "response_item", Some(_), Some(_)) => RolloutRecord::Other,
        ("turn_context" | "world_state" | "compacted", _, _) => RolloutRecord::Other,
        _ => RolloutRecord::Unknown,
    }
}

fn string(o: &Map<String, Value>, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    o.get(key).and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned)
}

/// A string field of `payload.source.subagent.thread_spawn`: where Codex serializes
/// `SessionSource::SubAgent(SubAgentSource::ThreadSpawn { .. })`.
fn thread_spawn(v: &Value, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    v.pointer(&format!("/payload/source/subagent/thread_spawn/{key}")).and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned)
}

fn call_id(p: &Map<String, Value>) -> String {
    string(p, "call_id").unwrap_or_default()
}

/// `function_call.arguments` is a JSON document in a string; an object is taken as is.
fn call_arguments(p: &Map<String, Value>) -> Option<Value> {
    match p.get("arguments") {
        Some(Value::String(s)) => serde_json::from_str(s).ok(),
        Some(object @ Value::Object(_)) => Some(object.clone()),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn error_text(v: Option<&Value>) -> Option<String> {
    let v = v?;
    match v {
        Value::Null => None,
        Value::String(s) => Some(s.clone()),
        Value::Object(o) => Some(o.get("message").and_then(Value::as_str).map_or_else(|| v.to_string(), str::to_owned)),
        other => Some(other.to_string()),
    }
}

const CURSOR_EXTENSION: &str = r"**\.cursor\extensions\openai.chatgpt-*\**";
const VSCODE_EXTENSION: &str = r"**\.vscode\extensions\openai.chatgpt-*\**";
const DESKTOP_MSIX: &str = r"**\windowsapps\openai.codex_*\**";

/// Host of a Codex process from the relay's `agent_image`, compared as
/// `paths::normalize(image).key` (spec §5.6). Desktop: the MSIX package folder or a copy under
/// `<localappdata>\OpenAI\Codex\bin\<ver>\codex.exe`. None or anything else → Unknown.
pub fn classify_host(agent_image: Option<&str>, localappdata: &Path) -> HostKind {
    let Some(image) = agent_image else {
        return HostKind::Unknown;
    };
    let key = normalize(image).key;
    let local_copy = !localappdata.as_os_str().is_empty()
        && glob_match(
            &key,
            &format!(r"{}\openai\codex\bin\*\codex.exe", normalize(&localappdata.to_string_lossy()).key),
        );
    if glob_match(&key, CURSOR_EXTENSION) {
        HostKind::Cursor
    } else if glob_match(&key, VSCODE_EXTENSION) {
        HostKind::VsCode
    } else if glob_match(&key, DESKTOP_MSIX) || local_copy {
        HostKind::CodexDesktop
    } else {
        HostKind::Unknown
    }
}

/// Title from `~/.codex/session_index.jsonl` text: the `thread_name` of the last line whose
/// `id` equals `session_id` and whose name is not blank, as `collapse(_, 160)`. Lines that are
/// not JSON are skipped.
pub fn index_title(index_text: &str, session_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    index_text
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line).ok())
        .filter(|v| v.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some(session_id))
        .filter_map(|v| v.get("thread_name").and_then(Value::as_str).map(|name| collapse(name, SUMMARY_MAX)))
        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
        .last()
}

/// A rollout path codex-io may tail: not blank and not compressed (".zst", ASCII
/// case-insensitive).
pub fn is_readable_rollout(path: &str) -> bool {
    !path.trim().is_empty() && !path.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".zst")
}
```

**Notes (choices inside the contract, so the implementer does not re-decide them):**
- Transitions push a private `Raised { key, kind, body, since }`; `apply` turns them into `Alert`s after the transition, filtered by `AlertPrefs` (D18), with `Alert.project` = display name of the new state (D40). `Alert.detail` is the alert body (tool label or question for permission/input, summary for finished, `error_summary` for error); `Alert.since` is the episode start (Waiting `since_ms`, outcome `at_ms`).
- `rev`: `Store` keeps the last computed view (every snapshot field except `rev`/`now`) and bumps `rev` when it differs after `apply`. `snapshot()` always recomputes from the state.
- Claude `since_ms` changes only when the phase changes or a new waiting episode starts, always `max(prev, statusUpdatedAt or now_ms)`; D19 uses `max(prev + 1, statusUpdatedAt)`. «Источник фазы — status, since — statusUpdatedAt, не меньше предыдущего».
- The spec §7 cell «Idle / Unknown → idle: … иначе —» rules out only the collapsed-turn evaluation; the phase still follows `status` («Источник фазы — status»). Without a new `statusUpdatedAt` an `Idle` session is unchanged, and an `Unknown` session becomes `Idle` (`since = max(prev, ts)`, `idle_eof = transcript_eof` when given, outcome untouched, no evaluation, no alert). This is also what lets an `Unknown` session whose file has no or a mistyped `statusUpdatedAt` (D56 → None, so never a "new" one) return to `Idle` (table row "unknown → idle, same statusUpdatedAt").
- `Signal::ClaudeTranscript.eof` is not used by the model: offsets come only from `rebind_at` and `ClaudeFile.transcript_eof`. Title facts update `titles` at any offset; every other fact is kept only when its offset ≥ `turn_start_offset`.
- `cargo build` (non-test) prints dead-code warnings for the model until T13 wires the store thread; `cargo test` compiles cleanly apart from warnings about the Codex items that T10 uses.

Contract amendment (contract §7 D68, orchestrator decision; the spec wins over the contract):
- **D68** `Store::session`, `Store::projects`, `Store::rev` and `Project` are `#[cfg(test)]` (Steps 2 and 16). Only tests call them (`model_tests.rs`, T9 and T10); production code reads the store only through `apply` and `snapshot`, and no later task calls them. Without the mark, the non-test build of `mayak_lib` would keep a permanent `dead_code` warning for them, and T19 Step 2 expects no warnings. `model_tests.rs` is a child module of `model` that is compiled only under `cfg(test)`, so every test that calls them still compiles. Contract §7 records this as D68, and contract §2.15 marks the three accessors and `Project` `#[cfg(test)]`. No task step edits `contract.md`.

```rust
// The session model (spec §5.4, §6, §7, §10). Pure: no I/O, no clock, no threads.
// Every state decision of the observer is made by `Store::apply`; source threads send facts as
// `Signal`s and execute the `Effect`s it returns. Time always comes in as `now_ms`.

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};

use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::Value;

pub use super::claude::ClaudeSessionFile;
pub use super::codex::HookEvent;
#[allow(unused_imports)] // spec §5.4 names them model::claude_key / model::codex_key; callers use observe::keys
pub use super::keys::{claude_key, codex_key};
pub use super::keys::{HostKind, ProcId, SessionKey};
pub use super::paths::ProjectRef;

use super::claude_transcript::Fact;
use super::paths;

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "model_tests.rs"]
mod tests;

/// Where a session comes from.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] // "claude" | "codex"
pub enum Source {
    Claude,
    Codex,
}

/// Health of one source (spec §10 `Health`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] // "ok" | "missing" | {"error":s} | {"degraded":{"unreadable":n}}
pub enum Health {
    Ok,
    Missing,
    Error(String),
    Degraded { unreadable: u32 },
}

/// Facts sent by the source threads (spec §5.4). One signal = one `Store::apply`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Signal {
    /// claude-io sends it before the `ClaudeFile` of the same session. `rebind_at = Some(o)` when
    /// the transcript is (re)bound: o = 0 for a new file, o = EOF for an existing file found by search.
    ClaudeTranscript { key: SessionKey, rebind_at: Option<u64>, records: Vec<(u64, Value)>, eof: u64 },
    ClaudeFile {
        key: SessionKey,
        proc: ProcId,
        host: HostKind,
        project: ProjectRef,
        file: ClaudeSessionFile,
        transcript_eof: Option<u64>,
    },
    /// Session file deleted, or procStart changed.
    ClaudeGone { key: SessionKey },
    /// codex-io sends it before the `CodexHook` of the same session.
    CodexRollout { key: SessionKey, path: String, records: Vec<(u64, Value)>, eof: u64 },
    CodexHook {
        key: SessionKey,
        event: HookEvent,
        proc: Option<ProcId>,
        host: HostKind,
        project: ProjectRef,
        rollout_eof: Option<u64>,
        /// session_index.jsonl title, filled on the first hook of a key in this run (D12).
        title: Option<String>,
    },
    CodexHooksInstalled(bool),
    ProcExit { pid: u32, created_ft: u64 },
    Ack(SessionKey),
    Visible(bool),
    AlertPrefs { waiting: bool, finished: bool, error: bool },
    SourceHealth { source: Source, health: Health },
}

/// Work for the source threads, returned by `Store::apply`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Effect {
    /// claude-io: find or wait for `<session_id>.jsonl`.
    TrackTranscript { key: SessionKey, session_id: String },
    UntrackTranscript { key: SessionKey },
    /// Emitted for every removed Codex session (D13).
    UntrackRollout { key: SessionKey },
    /// codex-io: 1 Hz rollout ticker on/off; emitted only when the wanted state changes.
    CodexTicker(bool),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Applied {
    pub alerts: Vec<Alert>,
    pub effects: Vec<Effect>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Outcome {

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AlertPrefs {
    pub waiting: bool,
    pub finished: bool,
    pub error: bool,
}

impl Default for AlertPrefs {
    fn default() -> Self {
        AlertPrefs { waiting: true, finished: true, error: true }
    }
}

pub struct Session {

    // Claude
    pub file_status_ts: i64,
    pub turn_start_offset: u64,
    pub idle_eof: u64,
    pub transcript_bound: bool,
    pub pending_tools: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Last `waitingFor` of the session file (waiting → waiting rule).
    pub waiting_for: Option<String>,
    /// Session file `name` (title fallback, D20).
    pub file_name: Option<String>,
    pub titles: TranscriptTitles,
    /// Facts with offset >= turn_start_offset, at most the last MAX_FACTS (D14).
    pub facts: Vec<(u64, Fact)>,
    // Codex
    pub current_turn: Option<String>,
    pub turn_started_ts: i64,
    /// At most MAX_CLOSED_TURNS, oldest dropped.
    pub closed_turns: VecDeque<String>,
    /// (turn, tool, fnv1a64(canonical_json(tool_input))).
    pub wait_key: Option<(String, String, u64)>,
}
```

```rust
// ── pure helpers ──

/// Object keys sorted recursively, compact. Input of the Codex `wait_key` hash (spec §7).
pub fn canonical_json(v: &Value) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    write_canonical(v, &mut out);
    out
}

fn write_canonical(v: &Value, out: &mut String) {
    match v {
        Value::Object(map) => {
            let mut keys: Vec<&String> = map.keys().collect();
            keys.sort();
            out.push('{');
            for (i, k) in keys.into_iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                out.push_str(&Value::String(k.clone()).to_string());
                out.push(':');
                write_canonical(&map[k.as_str()], out);
            }
            out.push('}');
        }
        Value::Array(items) => {
            out.push('[');
            for (i, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_canonical(item, out);
            }
            out.push(']');
        }
        other => out.push_str(&other.to_string()),
    }
}

/// FNV-1a, 64 bit.
pub fn fnv1a64(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    let mut hash: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for b in bytes {
        hash ^= u64::from(*b);
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
    }
    hash
}

/// Display name per project key (spec §6): basename of the root; when the basenames of different
/// keys collide (case-insensitive) → "<parent basename>\<basename>" (a drive root keeps its basename).
pub fn display_names(projects: &[(String, String)]) -> HashMap<String, String> {
    let mut keys_by_base: HashMap<String, Vec<&str>> = HashMap::new();
    for (key, root) in projects {
        let keys = keys_by_base.entry(paths::basename(root).to_lowercase()).or_default();
        if !keys.contains(&key.as_str()) {
            keys.push(key);
        }
    }
    projects
        .iter()
        .map(|(key, root)| {
            let base = paths::basename(root);
            let collides = keys_by_base.get(&base.to_lowercase()).is_some_and(|keys| keys.len() > 1);
            let name = match paths::parent_basename(root) {
                Some(parent) if collides => format!("{parent}\\{base}"),
                _ => base,
            };
            (key.clone(), name)
        })
        .collect()
}
```

```rust
// ── alert texts (spec §10 "Alert.text", T9) ──

/// "Claude" | "Codex".
pub fn agent_label(a: super::model::Source) -> &'static str {
    match a {
        super::model::Source::Claude => "Claude",
        super::model::Source::Codex => "Codex",
    }
}

/// Host caption used in alert texts; None for Unknown (the host part is then omitted).
pub fn host_label(h: super::keys::HostKind) -> Option<&'static str> {
    use super::keys::HostKind;
    match h {
        HostKind::ClaudeDesktop => Some("Desktop"),
        HostKind::Cursor => Some("Cursor"),
        HostKind::VsCode => Some("VS Code"),
        HostKind::CodexDesktop => Some("Codex app"),
        HostKind::Unknown => None,
    }
}

/// "<code>: <text>" or "<text>" (no code, or an empty one).
pub fn error_summary(code: Option<&str>, text: &str) -> String {
    match code {
        Some(code) if !code.is_empty() => format!("{code}: {text}"),
        _ => text.to_string(),
    }
}

/// "<Agent> · <project>[ (<host>)] needs permission[: <body>]" | "… asks[: <body>]" |
/// "… finished[: <body>]" | "… error[: <body>]"; whole string collapse(_, SUMMARY_MAX).
pub fn alert_text(
    agent: super::model::Source,
    project: &str,
    host: super::keys::HostKind,
    kind: super::model::AttentionKind,
    body: Option<&str>,
) -> String {
    use super::model::AttentionKind;
    let mut text = format!("{} · {}", agent_label(agent), project);
    if let Some(h) = host_label(host) {
        text.push_str(&format!(" ({h})"));
    }
    text.push_str(match kind {
        AttentionKind::Permission => " needs permission",
        AttentionKind::Input => " asks",
        AttentionKind::Finished => " finished",
        AttentionKind::Error => " error",
    });
    if let Some(body) = body.filter(|b| !b.trim().is_empty()) {
        text.push_str(": ");
        text.push_str(body);
    }
    collapse(&text, SUMMARY_MAX)
}
```

```rust
// ── fixtures shared by the store tests ──

/// Store clock used by every `apply` unless a test needs another one.
const NOW: i64 = 9_000;

fn project(name: &str) -> ProjectRef {
    ProjectRef { key: format!(r"c:\users\dev\{}", name.to_lowercase()), root: format!(r"C:\Users\dev\{name}") }
}

/// A session for snapshot-rule tests, inserted directly (no transition involved).
fn put(store: &mut Store, key: &str, project: ProjectRef, phase: Phase, since: i64, outcome: Outcome, acked_at: Option<i64>) {
    let mut s = Session::blank(
        key.to_string(),
        Source::Claude,
        HostKind::ClaudeDesktop,
        None,
        project,
        "s".into(),
        r"C:\Users\dev".into(),
        since,
    );
    s.phase = phase;
    s.outcome = outcome;
    s.acked_at = acked_at;
    store.sessions.insert(key.to_string(), s);
}

fn waiting(kind: WaitKind) -> Phase {
    Phase::Waiting { kind }
}

fn finished(at_ms: i64) -> Outcome {
    Outcome::Finished { summary: "done".into(), at_ms }
}

fn failed(at_ms: i64) -> Outcome {
    Outcome::Error { code: Some("rate_limit".into()), status: Some(429), text: "limit".into(), at_ms }
}

// ── snapshot rules (spec §6, §10) ──

    put(&mut st, "k-m", project("P"), waiting(WaitKind::Permission), 100, Outcome::None, None); // tie with k-b → key
    put(&mut st, "k-c", project("P"), waiting(WaitKind::Input), 50, Outcome::None, None);
    put(&mut st, "k-d", project("P"), waiting(WaitKind::Other("plan approval".into())), 60, Outcome::None, None);
    put(&mut st, "k-e", project("P"), Phase::Idle, 10, failed(500), None);
    put(&mut st, "k-f", project("P"), Phase::Idle, 10, failed(700), None);
    put(&mut st, "k-g", project("P"), Phase::Idle, 10, finished(800), None);

    put(&mut st, "k-i", project("P"), Phase::Working, 5, Outcome::None, None);
    put(&mut st, "k-j", project("P"), Phase::Idle, 900, Outcome::None, None);

    assert_eq!(order, ["k-b", "k-m", "k-a", "k-c", "k-d", "k-f", "k-e", "k-g", "k-i", "k-h", "k-k", "k-j", "k-l"]);
    let attention: Vec<Option<AttentionKind>> = snap.projects[0].sessions.iter().map(|s| s.attention).collect();
    use AttentionKind::*;
    assert_eq!(
        attention,
        [Some(Permission), Some(Permission), Some(Permission), Some(Input), Some(Input), Some(Error), Some(Error),
         Some(Finished), None, None, None, None, None]
    );
}

#[test]
fn projects_sort_by_best_rank_then_latest_activity_then_key() {
    let mut st = Store::new();
    put(&mut st, "a1", project("Alpha"), Phase::Idle, 100, finished(2_000), None); // rank 3, latest 2000
    put(&mut st, "b1", project("Beta"), waiting(WaitKind::Input), 50, Outcome::None, None); // rank 1
    put(&mut st, "b2", project("Beta"), Phase::Working, 10, Outcome::None, None);
    put(&mut st, "c1", project("Gamma"), Phase::Idle, 100, finished(3_000), None); // rank 3, latest 3000
    put(&mut st, "d1", project("Delta"), Phase::Idle, 4_000, Outcome::None, None); // rank 5
    put(&mut st, "e1", project("Epsilon"), Phase::Idle, 100, finished(2_000), None); // ties Alpha → key asc

    let snap = st.snapshot(NOW);
    let names: Vec<&str> = snap.projects.iter().map(|p| p.name.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(names, ["Beta", "Gamma", "Alpha", "Epsilon", "Delta"]);
    let projects = st.projects();
    let keys: Vec<&str> = projects.iter().map(|p| p.key.as_str()).collect();
    let snap_keys: Vec<&str> = snap.projects.iter().map(|p| p.key.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(keys, snap_keys);
    assert_eq!(projects[0].sessions, ["b1", "b2"]);
    assert_eq!(projects[0].root, r"C:\Users\dev\Beta");
}

#[test]
fn snapshot_names_colliding_projects_with_their_parent() {
    let mut st = Store::new();
    let work_app = ProjectRef { key: r"c:\work\app".into(), root: r"C:\work\app".into() };
    let other_app = ProjectRef { key: r"d:\other\app".into(), root: r"D:\other\App".into() };
    put(&mut st, "x1", work_app, Phase::Working, 10, Outcome::None, None);
    put(&mut st, "x2", other_app, Phase::Working, 20, Outcome::None, None);
    put(&mut st, "x3", project("Solo"), Phase::Working, 30, Outcome::None, None);

    let snap = st.snapshot(NOW);
    let names: HashMap<&str, &str> = snap.projects.iter().map(|p| (p.key.as_str(), p.name.as_str())).collect();
    assert_eq!(names[r"c:\work\app"], r"work\app");
    assert_eq!(names[r"d:\other\app"], r"other\App");
    assert_eq!(names[r"c:\users\dev\solo"], "Solo");
}

#[test]
fn counts_hold_and_aggregate_use_unacked_episodes_only() {
    struct Case {
        name: &'static str,
        sessions: Vec<(Phase, Outcome, Option<i64>)>,
        counts: Counts,
        hold: bool,
        aggregate: BotState,
    }
    let counts = |waiting, error, finished, working| Counts { waiting, error, finished, working };
    let cases = vec![
        Case { name: "empty", sessions: vec![], counts: counts(0, 0, 0, 0), hold: false, aggregate: BotState::Idle },
        Case {
            name: "unacked permission",
            sessions: vec![(waiting(WaitKind::Permission), Outcome::None, None)],
            counts: counts(1, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: true,
            aggregate: BotState::Approval,
        },
        Case {
            name: "acked permission",
            sessions: vec![(waiting(WaitKind::Permission), Outcome::None, Some(100))],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Idle,
        },
        Case {
            name: "unacked input is a question",
            sessions: vec![(waiting(WaitKind::Input), Outcome::None, None)],
            counts: counts(1, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: true,
            aggregate: BotState::Question,
        },
        Case {
            name: "unacked other wait is a question",
            sessions: vec![(waiting(WaitKind::Other("plan approval".into())), Outcome::None, None)],
            counts: counts(1, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: true,
            aggregate: BotState::Question,
        },
        Case {
            name: "permission beats question",
            sessions: vec![
                (waiting(WaitKind::Input), Outcome::None, None),
                (waiting(WaitKind::Permission), Outcome::None, None),
            ],
            counts: counts(2, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: true,
            aggregate: BotState::Approval,
        },
        Case {
            name: "error beats working",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Idle, failed(200), None), (Phase::Working, Outcome::None, None)],
            counts: counts(0, 1, 0, 1),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Error,
        },
        Case {
            name: "working beats finished",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Idle, finished(200), None), (Phase::Working, Outcome::None, None)],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 1, 1),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Working,
        },
        Case {
            name: "unacked finished",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Idle, finished(200), None)],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 1, 0),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Finished,
        },
        Case {
            name: "acked finished",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Idle, finished(200), Some(200))],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Idle,
        },
        Case {
            name: "acked error",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Idle, failed(200), Some(250))],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Idle,
        },
        Case {
            name: "an ack older than the episode does not count",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Idle, finished(200), Some(150))],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 1, 0),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Finished,
        },
        Case {
            name: "working counts even when acked (no episode)",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Working, Outcome::None, Some(100))],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 0, 1),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Working,
        },
        Case {
            name: "interrupted is not an episode",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Idle, Outcome::Interrupted { at_ms: 200 }, None)],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Idle,
        },
        Case {
            name: "finished outside Idle is not an episode",
            sessions: vec![(Phase::Unknown("compacting".into()), finished(200), None)],
            counts: counts(0, 0, 0, 0),
            hold: false,
            aggregate: BotState::Idle,
        },
    ];
    for case in cases {
        let mut st = Store::new();
        for (i, (phase, outcome, acked)) in case.sessions.into_iter().enumerate() {
            put(&mut st, &format!("s{i}"), project("P"), phase, 100, outcome, acked);
        }
        let snap = st.snapshot(NOW);
        assert_eq!(snap.counts, case.counts, "{}: counts", case.name);
        assert_eq!(snap.hold, case.hold, "{}: hold", case.name);
        assert_eq!(snap.aggregate, case.aggregate, "{}: aggregate", case.name);
    }
}

#[test]
fn hold_needs_alert_waiting_on() {
    let mut st = Store::new();
    put(&mut st, "w", project("Alpha"), waiting(WaitKind::Permission), 100, Outcome::None, None);
    assert!(st.snapshot(NOW).hold);
    st.apply(Signal::AlertPrefs { waiting: false, finished: true, error: true }, NOW);
    let snap = st.snapshot(NOW);
    assert!(!snap.hold);
    assert_eq!(snap.counts.waiting, 1);
    assert_eq!(snap.aggregate, BotState::Approval);
    assert_eq!(snap.attention, ["w"]);
}

#[test]
fn ack_marks_the_current_episode_and_never_changes_the_phase() {
    let mut st = Store::new();
    put(&mut st, "w", project("Alpha"), waiting(WaitKind::Permission), 5_000, Outcome::None, None);
    // store clock behind the episode start: acked_at = max(now, start) (D49)
    st.apply(Signal::Ack("w".into()), 4_000);
    let s = st.session("w").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(s.acked_at, Some(5_000));
    assert_eq!(s.phase, waiting(WaitKind::Permission));
    let snap = st.snapshot(NOW);
    assert!(snap.attention.is_empty());
    assert!(snap.projects[0].sessions[0].acked);
    assert_eq!(snap.projects[0].sessions[0].attention, None);
    assert_eq!(snap.projects[0].sessions[0].phase, PhaseView::Waiting { wait: WaitView::Permission, label: "permission".into() });

    // no episode: acked_at = now
    put(&mut st, "busy", project("Alpha"), Phase::Working, 10, Outcome::None, None);
    st.apply(Signal::Ack("busy".into()), 7_000);
    assert_eq!(st.session("busy").unwrap().acked_at, Some(7_000));
    assert_eq!(st.session("busy").unwrap().phase, Phase::Working);

    // unknown key: nothing at all
    let rev = st.rev();
    assert_eq!(st.apply(Signal::Ack("nope".into()), NOW), Applied::default());
    assert_eq!(st.rev(), rev);
}

#[test]
fn source_health_is_published_and_bumps_rev_on_change_only() {
    let mut st = Store::new();
    assert_eq!(st.rev(), 0);
    assert_eq!(
        st.snapshot(NOW).sources,
        Sources { claude: Health::Ok, codex: Health::Ok, codex_hooks: CodexHooksView::NotInstalled }
    );
    st.apply(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health: Health::Degraded { unreadable: 2 } }, NOW);
    assert_eq!(st.rev(), 1);
    st.apply(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Codex, health: Health::Missing }, NOW);
    assert_eq!(st.rev(), 2);
    st.apply(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Codex, health: Health::Missing }, NOW);
    assert_eq!(st.rev(), 2);
    let snap = st.snapshot(NOW + 1);
    assert_eq!(snap.sources.claude, Health::Degraded { unreadable: 2 });
    assert_eq!(snap.sources.codex, Health::Missing);
    assert_eq!((snap.rev, snap.now), (2, NOW + 1));
}

#[test]
fn visible_and_unchanged_prefs_change_nothing() {
    let mut st = Store::new();
    assert_eq!(st.apply(Signal::Visible(true), NOW), Applied::default());
    assert_eq!(st.apply(Signal::AlertPrefs { waiting: true, finished: true, error: true }, NOW), Applied::default());
    assert_eq!(st.rev(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn phase_and_outcome_views() {
    let phases = [
        (Phase::Working, PhaseView::Working),
        (waiting(WaitKind::Permission), PhaseView::Waiting { wait: WaitView::Permission, label: "permission".into() }),
        (waiting(WaitKind::Input), PhaseView::Waiting { wait: WaitView::Input, label: "input".into() }),
        (
            waiting(WaitKind::Other("plan approval".into())),
            PhaseView::Waiting { wait: WaitView::Other, label: "plan approval".into() },
        ),
        (Phase::Idle, PhaseView::Idle),
        (Phase::Unknown("compacting".into()), PhaseView::Unknown { label: "compacting".into() }),
    ];
    for (phase, view) in phases {
        assert_eq!(phase_view(&phase), view);
    }
    let outcomes = [
        (Outcome::None, None),
        (Outcome::Pending, None),
        (finished(5), Some(OutcomeView { kind: OutcomeKind::Finished, summary: "done".into(), at: 5 })),
        (failed(6), Some(OutcomeView { kind: OutcomeKind::Error, summary: "rate_limit: limit".into(), at: 6 })),
        (
            Outcome::Error { code: None, status: None, text: "stream disconnected".into(), at_ms: 7 },
            Some(OutcomeView { kind: OutcomeKind::Error, summary: "stream disconnected".into(), at: 7 }),
        ),
        (Outcome::Interrupted { at_ms: 8 }, Some(OutcomeView { kind: OutcomeKind::Interrupted, summary: String::new(), at: 8 })),
    ];
    for (outcome, view) in outcomes {
        assert_eq!(outcome_view(&outcome), view);
    }
}

#[test]
fn health_and_codex_hooks_serialize_externally_tagged() {
    fn wire<T: Serialize>(v: T) -> Value {
        serde_json::to_value(v).unwrap()
    }
    assert_eq!(wire(Health::Ok), json!("ok"));
    assert_eq!(wire(Health::Missing), json!("missing"));
    assert_eq!(wire(Health::Error("access denied".into())), json!({ "error": "access denied" }));
    assert_eq!(wire(Health::Degraded { unreadable: 3 }), json!({ "degraded": { "unreadable": 3 } }));
    assert_eq!(wire(CodexHooksView::NotInstalled), json!("not_installed"));
    assert_eq!(wire(CodexHooksView::InstalledUnseen), json!("installed_unseen"));
    assert_eq!(
        wire(CodexHooksView::Receiving { hosts: vec![HostKind::Cursor, HostKind::CodexDesktop], since: 5 }),
        json!({ "receiving": { "hosts": ["cursor", "codexDesktop"], "since": 5 } })
    );
    assert_eq!(wire(BotState::Question), json!("question"));
    assert_eq!(wire(AttentionKind::Finished), json!("finished"));
    assert_eq!(wire(Source::Codex), json!("codex"));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 16: Implement the store core (snapshot, ranks, ack, removal)**

Append to the end of `windows/src-tauri/src/observe/model.rs`. `apply` dispatches every signal; the two Claude transitions stay no-ops until Step 23 wires the Claude state machine:

```rust
// ── store ──

/// An alert raised by a transition; completed into an `Alert` at the end of `apply`, when the
/// project display names of the new state are known.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Raised {
    key: SessionKey,
    kind: AttentionKind,
    body: Option<String>,
    since: i64,
}

/// Every snapshot field except `rev` and `now`; a change after `apply` bumps `rev`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
struct View {
    projects: Vec<ProjectView>,
    attention: Vec<String>,
    counts: Counts,
    hold: bool,
    aggregate: BotState,
    sources: Sources,
}

/// Sessions of one project, in display order.
struct Group<'a> {
    key: String,
    root: String,
    sessions: Vec<&'a Session>,
}

pub struct Store {
    sessions: BTreeMap<SessionKey, Session>,
    rev: u64,
    prefs: AlertPrefs,
    claude_health: Health,
    codex_health: Health,
    codex_hooks: CodexHooksView,
    /// View after the last `apply` (rev bookkeeping only).
    last_view: Option<View>,
}

impl Default for Store {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Store {
    /// rev 0, prefs all true, both healths Ok, Codex hooks NotInstalled.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let mut store = Store {
            sessions: BTreeMap::new(),
            rev: 0,
            prefs: AlertPrefs::default(),
            claude_health: Health::Ok,
            codex_health: Health::Ok,
            codex_hooks: CodexHooksView::NotInstalled,
            last_view: None,
        };
        store.last_view = Some(store.view());
        store
    }

    pub fn apply(&mut self, s: Signal, now_ms: i64) -> Applied {
        let mut fx: Vec<Effect> = Vec::new();
        let raised: Vec<Raised> = Vec::new(); // filled by the state machines once they exist
        match s {
            Signal::ClaudeTranscript { .. } | Signal::ClaudeFile { .. } => {} // Claude transitions: next commit
            Signal::ClaudeGone { key } => self.remove_session(&key, &mut fx),
            Signal::CodexRollout { .. } | Signal::CodexHook { .. } | Signal::CodexHooksInstalled(_) => {} // Codex transitions: T10
            Signal::ProcExit { pid, created_ft } => self.proc_exit(pid, created_ft, &mut fx),
            Signal::Ack(key) => self.ack(&key, now_ms),
            Signal::Visible(_) => {} // read only by the Codex ticker (T10)
            Signal::AlertPrefs { waiting, finished, error } => self.prefs = AlertPrefs { waiting, finished, error },
            Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health } => self.claude_health = health,
            Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Codex, health } => self.codex_health = health,
        }
        let alerts = self.complete_alerts(raised);
        let view = self.view();
        if self.last_view.as_ref() != Some(&view) {
            self.rev += 1;
            self.last_view = Some(view);
        }
        Applied { alerts, effects: fx }
    }

    pub fn snapshot(&self, now_ms: i64) -> SessionsSnapshot {
        let v = self.view();
        SessionsSnapshot {
            rev: self.rev,
            now: now_ms,
            projects: v.projects,
            attention: v.attention,
            counts: v.counts,
            hold: v.hold,
            aggregate: v.aggregate,
            sources: v.sources,
        }
    }

    /// Test-only accessors (D68): production code reads the store through `apply` and `snapshot`.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn session(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Session> {
        self.sessions.get(key)
    }

    /// Projects in snapshot order, sessions in snapshot order.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn projects(&self) -> Vec<Project> {
        self.groups()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|g| Project { key: g.key, root: g.root, sessions: g.sessions.iter().map(|s| s.key.clone()).collect() })
            .collect()
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn rev(&self) -> u64 {
        self.rev
    }

    /// Ack sets `acked_at` and never changes the phase (spec §6, D49).
    fn ack(&mut self, key: &str, now_ms: i64) {
        if let Some(s) = self.sessions.get_mut(key) {
            s.acked_at = Some(episode_start(s).map_or(now_ms, |start| now_ms.max(start)));
        }
    }

    fn remove_session(&mut self, key: &str, fx: &mut Vec<Effect>) {
        if let Some(s) = self.sessions.remove(key) {
            if s.agent == Source::Claude {
                fx.push(Effect::UntrackTranscript { key: s.key });
            }
        }
    }

    /// Removes every session of the exited process (spec §7).
    fn proc_exit(&mut self, pid: u32, created_ft: u64, fx: &mut Vec<Effect>) {
        let gone: Vec<SessionKey> = self
            .sessions
            .values()
            .filter(|s| s.proc.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| p.pid == pid && p.created_ft == created_ft))
            .map(|s| s.key.clone())
            .collect();
        for key in gone {
            self.remove_session(&key, fx);
        }
    }

    fn complete_alerts(&self, raised: Vec<Raised>) -> Vec<Alert> {
        if raised.is_empty() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let names = display_names(&self.project_pairs());
        raised
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|r| self.prefs.allows(r.kind))
            .filter_map(|r| {
                let s = self.sessions.get(&r.key)?;
                let project = names.get(&s.project.key).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
                Some(Alert {
                    text: text::alert_text(s.agent, &project, s.host, r.kind, r.body.as_deref()),
                    key: r.key,
                    kind: r.kind,
                    rank: attention_rank(r.kind),
                    agent: s.agent,
                    host: s.host,
                    project,
                    title: s.title.clone(),
                    detail: r.body,
                    since: r.since,
                })
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// (project key, root) per project; the root of the first session in key order wins.
    fn project_pairs(&self) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
        let mut pairs: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
        for s in self.sessions.values() {
            if !pairs.iter().any(|(k, _)| *k == s.project.key) {
                pairs.push((s.project.key.clone(), s.project.root.clone()));
            }
        }
        pairs
    }

    fn groups(&self) -> Vec<Group<'_>> {
        let mut by_key: BTreeMap<&str, Group<'_>> = BTreeMap::new();
        for s in self.sessions.values() {
            by_key
                .entry(s.project.key.as_str())
                .or_insert_with(|| Group { key: s.project.key.clone(), root: s.project.root.clone(), sessions: Vec::new() })
                .sessions
                .push(s);
        }
        let mut groups: Vec<Group<'_>> = by_key.into_values().collect();
        for g in &mut groups {
            g.sessions.sort_by(|a, b| cmp_sessions(a, b));
        }
        // best rank asc, then most recent activity desc, then key asc (spec §6)
        groups.sort_by(|a, b| {
            let best = |g: &Group<'_>| g.sessions.iter().map(|s| rank_of(s)).min().unwrap_or(5);
            let latest = |g: &Group<'_>| g.sessions.iter().map(|s| last_activity(s)).max().unwrap_or(i64::MIN);
            best(a).cmp(&best(b)).then_with(|| latest(b).cmp(&latest(a))).then_with(|| a.key.cmp(&b.key))
        });
        groups
    }

    fn view(&self) -> View {
        let groups = self.groups();
        let names = display_names(&self.project_pairs());
        let projects = groups
            .iter()
            .map(|g| ProjectView {
                key: g.key.clone(),
                name: names.get(&g.key).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
                root: g.root.clone(),
                sessions: g.sessions.iter().map(|s| session_view(s)).collect(),
            })
            .collect();
        let mut flagged: Vec<&Session> = self.sessions.values().filter(|s| attention_of(s).is_some()).collect();
        flagged.sort_by(|a, b| cmp_sessions(a, b));
        let attention = flagged.iter().map(|s| s.key.clone()).collect();
        let mut counts = Counts::default();
        let (mut approval, mut question) = (false, false);
        for s in self.sessions.values() {
            match attention_of(s) {
                Some(AttentionKind::Permission) => {
                    counts.waiting += 1;
                    approval = true;
                }
                Some(AttentionKind::Input) => {
                    counts.waiting += 1;
                    question = true;
                }
                Some(AttentionKind::Error) => counts.error += 1,
                Some(AttentionKind::Finished) => counts.finished += 1,
                None => {}
            }
            if s.phase == Phase::Working {
                counts.working += 1;
            }
        }
        let hold = counts.waiting > 0 && self.prefs.waiting;
        let aggregate = if approval {
            BotState::Approval
        } else if question {
            BotState::Question
        } else if counts.error > 0 {
            BotState::Error
        } else if counts.working > 0 {
            BotState::Working
        } else if counts.finished > 0 {
            BotState::Finished
        } else {
            BotState::Idle
        };
        View {
            projects,
            attention,
            counts,
            hold,
            aggregate,
            sources: Sources {
                claude: self.claude_health.clone(),
                codex: self.codex_health.clone(),
                codex_hooks: self.codex_hooks.clone(),
            },
        }
    }
}

impl AlertPrefs {
    fn allows(&self, kind: AttentionKind) -> bool {
        match kind {
            AttentionKind::Permission | AttentionKind::Input => self.waiting,
            AttentionKind::Finished => self.finished,
            AttentionKind::Error => self.error,
        }
    }
}

impl Session {
    /// A session with no phase information yet (`Unknown("")`, outcome None, nothing acked).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn blank(
        key: SessionKey,
        agent: Source,
        host: HostKind,
        proc: Option<ProcId>,
        project: ProjectRef,
        logical_id: String,
        cwd: String,
        since_ms: i64,
    ) -> Session {
        Session {
            key,
            agent,
            host,
            proc,
            logical_id,
            cwd,
            project,
            title: None,
            phase: Phase::Unknown(String::new()),
            since_ms,
            activity: None,
            detail: None,
            outcome: Outcome::None,
            acked_at: None,
            file_status_ts: since_ms,
            turn_start_offset: 0,
            idle_eof: 0,
            transcript_bound: false,
            pending_tools: Vec::new(),
            waiting_for: None,
            file_name: None,
            titles: TranscriptTitles::default(),
            facts: Vec::new(),
            current_turn: None,
            turn_started_ts: 0,
            closed_turns: VecDeque::new(),
            wait_key: None,
        }
    }
}

// ── episodes, attention, ranks (spec §6) ──

/// Waiting → since_ms; Idle with Finished/Error → at_ms; otherwise no episode.
fn episode_start(s: &Session) -> Option<i64> {
    match (&s.phase, &s.outcome) {
        (Phase::Waiting { .. }, _) => Some(s.since_ms),
        (Phase::Idle, Outcome::Finished { at_ms, .. }) | (Phase::Idle, Outcome::Error { at_ms, .. }) => Some(*at_ms),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn unacked(s: &Session) -> bool {
    episode_start(s).is_some_and(|start| s.acked_at.is_none_or(|acked| acked < start))
}

fn attention_of(s: &Session) -> Option<AttentionKind> {
    if !unacked(s) {
        return None;
    }
    match (&s.phase, &s.outcome) {
        (Phase::Waiting { kind: WaitKind::Permission }, _) => Some(AttentionKind::Permission),
        (Phase::Waiting { .. }, _) => Some(AttentionKind::Input),
        (Phase::Idle, Outcome::Error { .. }) => Some(AttentionKind::Error),
        (Phase::Idle, Outcome::Finished { .. }) => Some(AttentionKind::Finished),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn attention_rank(kind: AttentionKind) -> u8 {
    match kind {
        AttentionKind::Permission => 0,
        AttentionKind::Input => 1,
        AttentionKind::Error => 2,
        AttentionKind::Finished => 3,
    }
}

/// 0..3 unacked episodes, 4 Working, 5 everything else.
fn rank_of(s: &Session) -> u8 {
    match attention_of(s) {
        Some(kind) => attention_rank(kind),
        None if s.phase == Phase::Working => 4,
        None => 5,
    }
}

fn outcome_at(s: &Session) -> Option<i64> {
    match &s.outcome {
        Outcome::Finished { at_ms, .. } | Outcome::Error { at_ms, .. } | Outcome::Interrupted { at_ms } => Some(*at_ms),
        Outcome::None | Outcome::Pending => None,
    }
}

fn last_activity(s: &Session) -> i64 {
    s.since_ms.max(outcome_at(s).unwrap_or(i64::MIN))
}

/// Rank asc; within rank 0,1,4 `since` asc; 2,3 `at_ms` desc; 5 `since` desc; ties by key asc.
fn cmp_sessions(a: &Session, b: &Session) -> Ordering {
    let (ra, rb) = (rank_of(a), rank_of(b));
    ra.cmp(&rb)
        .then_with(|| match ra {
            0 | 1 | 4 => a.since_ms.cmp(&b.since_ms),
            2 | 3 => outcome_at(b).cmp(&outcome_at(a)),
            _ => b.since_ms.cmp(&a.since_ms),
        })
        .then_with(|| a.key.cmp(&b.key))
}

fn phase_view(p: &Phase) -> PhaseView {
    match p {
        Phase::Working => PhaseView::Working,
        Phase::Waiting { kind: WaitKind::Permission } => {
            PhaseView::Waiting { wait: WaitView::Permission, label: "permission".into() }
        }
        Phase::Waiting { kind: WaitKind::Input } => PhaseView::Waiting { wait: WaitView::Input, label: "input".into() },
        Phase::Waiting { kind: WaitKind::Other(raw) } => PhaseView::Waiting { wait: WaitView::Other, label: raw.clone() },
        Phase::Idle => PhaseView::Idle,
        Phase::Unknown(raw) => PhaseView::Unknown { label: raw.clone() },
    }
}

fn outcome_view(o: &Outcome) -> Option<OutcomeView> {
    match o {
        Outcome::None | Outcome::Pending => None,
        Outcome::Finished { summary, at_ms } => {
            Some(OutcomeView { kind: OutcomeKind::Finished, summary: summary.clone(), at: *at_ms })
        }
        Outcome::Error { code, text, at_ms, .. } => Some(OutcomeView {
            kind: OutcomeKind::Error,
            summary: text::error_summary(code.as_deref(), text),
            at: *at_ms,
        }),
        Outcome::Interrupted { at_ms } => {
            Some(OutcomeView { kind: OutcomeKind::Interrupted, summary: String::new(), at: *at_ms })
        }
    }
}

fn session_view(s: &Session) -> SessionView {
    SessionView {
        key: s.key.clone(),
        agent: s.agent,
        host: s.host,
        title: s.title.clone(),
        phase: phase_view(&s.phase),
        since: s.since_ms,
        activity: s.activity.clone(),
        detail: s.detail.clone(),
        outcome: outcome_view(&s.outcome),
        attention: attention_of(s),
        acked: !unacked(s),
    }
}
```

```rust
/// A session file as claude-io parses it (status, waitingFor, statusUpdatedAt vary).
fn sfile(status: &str, waiting_for: Option<&str>, ts: i64) -> ClaudeSessionFile {

fn cfile_at(pid: u32, project_ref: ProjectRef, file: ClaudeSessionFile, transcript_eof: Option<u64>) -> Signal {

fn ctr(rebind_at: Option<u64>, records: Vec<(u64, Value)>, eof: u64) -> Signal {
    Signal::ClaudeTranscript { key: key(), rebind_at, records, eof }
}

/// Applies the signals in order at `NOW` and collects alerts and effects.
fn run(st: &mut Store, signals: Vec<Signal>) -> Applied {
    let mut all = Applied::default();
    for s in signals {
        let a = st.apply(s, NOW);
        all.alerts.extend(a.alerts);
        all.effects.extend(a.effects);
    }
    all
}

fn kinds(a: &Applied) -> Vec<AttentionKind> {
    a.alerts.iter().map(|x| x.kind).collect()
}

// Claude Code transcript records (JSONL shape).
fn user(text: &str) -> Value {
    json!({ "type": "user", "isSidechain": false, "message": { "role": "user", "content": text } })
}
fn result(tool_use_id: &str) -> Value {
    json!({ "type": "user", "isSidechain": false, "message": { "role": "user",
        "content": [{ "type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": tool_use_id, "content": "ok" }] } })
}
fn tool(id: &str, name: &str, input: Value) -> Value {
    json!({ "type": "assistant", "isSidechain": false, "message": { "role": "assistant",
        "content": [{ "type": "tool_use", "id": id, "name": name, "input": input }], "stop_reason": "tool_use" } })
}
fn reply(text: &str, stop_reason: &str) -> Value {
    json!({ "type": "assistant", "isSidechain": false, "message": { "role": "assistant",
        "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": text }], "stop_reason": stop_reason } })
}
fn api_error(code: &str, status: u16, text: &str) -> Value {
    json!({ "type": "assistant", "isSidechain": false, "isApiErrorMessage": true, "error": code, "apiErrorStatus": status,
        "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": text }], "stop_reason": "stop_sequence" } })
}
fn interrupted() -> Value {
    json!({ "type": "user", "isSidechain": false, "message": { "role": "user",
        "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "[Request interrupted by user]" }] } })
}
fn title_record(kind: &str, field: &str, text: &str) -> Value {
    let mut m = serde_json::Map::new();
    m.insert("type".into(), kind.into());
    m.insert(field.into(), text.into());
    Value::Object(m)
}

/// The state a table row starts from.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum Start {
    Fresh,
    Working,
    Waiting,
    Idle,
    Unknown,
}

fn prelude(start: Start) -> Vec<Signal> {
    match start {
        Start::Fresh => vec![],
        // Working since 1000; transcript bound at 0; the turn already ended with "Build finished."
        Start::Working => vec![
            cfile(sfile("busy", None, 1_000), None),
            ctr(
                Some(0),
                vec![
                    (0, user("build it")),
                    (100, tool("t1", "Bash", json!({ "command": "cargo build" }))),
                    (200, result("t1")),
                    (300, reply("Build finished.", "end_turn")),
                ],
                400,
            ),
        ],
        // Waiting(Permission) since 2000 on an unresolved `rm -rf build`
        Start::Waiting => vec![
            cfile(sfile("busy", None, 1_000), None),
            ctr(Some(0), vec![(0, user("clean up")), (100, tool("t1", "Bash", json!({ "command": "rm -rf build" })))], 200),
            cfile(sfile("waiting", Some("permission prompt"), 2_000), Some(200)),
        ],
        // Idle since 1000; existing transcript bound at its EOF 200 (history not replayed)
        Start::Idle => vec![
            cfile(sfile("idle", None, 1_000), None),
            ctr(Some(200), vec![(0, user("old question")), (100, reply("Old answer.", "end_turn"))], 200),
        ],
        Start::Unknown => vec![
            cfile(sfile("compacting", None, 1_000), None),
            ctr(Some(200), vec![(0, user("old question")), (100, reply("Old answer.", "end_turn"))], 200),
        ],
    }
}

struct Row {
    cell: &'static str,
    start: Start,
    step: Vec<Signal>,
    phase: Phase,
    since: i64,
    alerts: Vec<AttentionKind>,
    outcome: Outcome,
    /// (turn_start_offset, idle_eof)
    offsets: (u64, u64),
    detail: Option<&'static str>,
}

fn done(summary: &str) -> Outcome {
    Outcome::Finished { summary: summary.into(), at_ms: NOW }
}
```
