Replace the whole content of `windows/src-tauri/src/log.rs` (as T1 left it: the Coucou file with line 1 and line 20 renamed) with:

```rust
// Small append-only log at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak\mayak.log — the Windows
// equivalent of nbLog() in HookServer.swift. Nothing leaves the machine.
// Unit tests never write it: under cfg(test) a line goes to the running test's
// captured stderr instead (tests must not write to the user's log).

#[cfg(not(test))]
use std::io::Write;

#[cfg(not(test))]
use windows::Win32::System::SystemInformation::GetLocalTime;

#[cfg(not(test))]
use crate::settings;

#[cfg(not(test))]
pub fn line(message: impl AsRef<str>) {
    let t = unsafe { GetLocalTime() };
    let stamp = format!(
        "{:04}-{:02}-{:02} {:02}:{:02}:{:02}",
        t.wYear, t.wMonth, t.wDay, t.wHour, t.wMinute, t.wSecond
    );
    let dir = settings::local_dir();
    if std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).is_err() {
        return;
    }
    let path = dir.join(format!("{}.log", crate::ident::APP_SLUG));
    // Keep it from growing forever: start fresh past ~1 MB.
    if std::fs::metadata(&path).map(|m| m.len() > 1_000_000).unwrap_or(false) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
    }
    if let Ok(mut file) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(path) {
        let _ = writeln!(file, "{stamp} {}", message.as_ref());
    }
}

/// Unit tests: the line goes to the captured stderr of the running test (shown only when
/// that test fails, or with `-- --nocapture`), never to the user's mayak.log.
#[cfg(test)]
pub fn line(message: impl AsRef<str>) {
    eprintln!("{}", message.as_ref());
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Add the helper functions**

Insert inside `mod io_thread`, directly above the `    #[cfg(test)]` line:

```rust
    /// D9 precedence: Error > Missing > Degraded > Ok.
    fn claude_health(error: Option<String>, missing: bool, unreadable: usize) -> Health {
        if let Some(msg) = error {
            Health::Error(msg)
        } else if missing {
            Health::Missing
        } else if unreadable > 0 {
            Health::Degraded { unreadable: u32::try_from(unreadable).unwrap_or(u32::MAX) }
        } else {
            Health::Ok
        }
    }

    /// D47: distinct session file names of a batch in first-seen order. Actions are ignored.
    fn session_names(changes: &[(FileAction, String)]) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut names: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for (_, rel) in changes {
            let name = rel.rsplit(['\\', '/']).next().unwrap_or(rel);
            if is_session_file_name(name) && !names.iter().any(|n| n == name) {
                names.push(name.to_string());
            }
        }
        names
    }

    /// Last component of a watcher-relative path, lowercase (NTFS compares names ignoring case).
    fn file_name_lower(rel: &str) -> String {
        rel.rsplit(['\\', '/']).next().unwrap_or(rel).to_lowercase()
    }

    fn transcript_name(session_id: &str) -> String {
        format!("{session_id}.jsonl").to_lowercase()
    }

    /// A session id names one file under `projects\*\`: a separator, a drive colon or `..`
    /// would reach outside it (spec §8: nothing but the transcripts is opened).
    fn is_plain_session_id(session_id: &str) -> bool {
        !session_id.contains(['\\', '/', ':']) && !session_id.contains("..")
    }

    /// One JSON value per line; unparsable lines are skipped (D26).
    fn parse_records(lines: Vec<(u64, String)>) -> Vec<(u64, Value)> {
        lines
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|(offset, text)| serde_json::from_str(&text).ok().map(|v| (offset, v)))
            .collect()
    }
```

```rust
        const SID: &str = "0f6c2a51-0000-4000-8000-00000000c1a0";
        const SLUG: &str = "C--work-app";

            proc::identify(std::process::id()).expect("the test process identifies itself").0
        }

        fn session_json(pid: u32, proc_start: u64, cwd: &str, status: &str, at: i64) -> String {
            serde_json::json!({
                "pid": pid, "sessionId": SID, "cwd": cwd, "procStart": proc_start.to_string(),
                "version": "2.1.286", "kind": "interactive", "entrypoint": "claude-vscode",
                "status": status, "statusUpdatedAt": at, "updatedAt": at
            })
            .to_string()
        }

        struct Rig {
            dir: TempDir,
            io: ClaudeIo,
            rx: Receiver<Signal>,
            me: ProcId,
        }

        fn rig(tag: &str) -> Rig {
            let dir = TempDir::new(tag);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path.join("sessions")).unwrap();
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path.join("projects").join(SLUG)).unwrap();
            // The project root must not depend on a `.git` above %TEMP% (git_probe walks up).
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path.join("work").join(".git")).unwrap();
            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
            let cfg = ClaudeConfig { base: dir.path.clone(), appdata: dir.path.join("appdata"), watch: false };
            let io = ClaudeIo::new(cfg, tx, proc::Registry::new(), None);
            Rig { dir, io, rx, me: me() }
        }

        impl Rig {
            fn name(&self) -> String {
                format!("{}.json", self.me.pid)
            }
            fn key(&self) -> SessionKey {
                claude_key(self.me.pid, self.me.created_ft)
            }
            fn cwd(&self) -> String {
                self.dir.path.join("work").to_string_lossy().into_owned()
            }
            fn write_session(&self, status: &str, at: i64) {
                let text = session_json(self.me.pid, self.me.created_ft, &self.cwd(), status, at);
                std::fs::write(self.dir.path.join("sessions").join(self.name()), text).unwrap();
            }
            fn signals(&self) -> Vec<Signal> {
                self.rx.try_iter().collect()
            }
            fn session_changed(&mut self, actions: &[FileAction]) {
                let name = self.name();
                let changes = actions.iter().map(|a| (*a, name.clone())).collect();
                self.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Sessions(WatchEvent::Changes(changes)));
            }
            /// Start with the live session file written and the first ClaudeFile consumed.

                rig.write_session("idle", 100);

                let first = rig.signals();
                assert_eq!(names(&first), ["ClaudeFile"], "{first:?}");
                rig
            }

            signals

                .map(|s| match s {
                    Signal::ClaudeFile { .. } => "ClaudeFile",
                    Signal::ClaudeGone { .. } => "ClaudeGone",
                    Signal::ClaudeTranscript { .. } => "ClaudeTranscript",
                    Signal::SourceHealth { .. } => "SourceHealth",
                    Signal::ProcExit { .. } => "ProcExit",
                    _ => "other",

                .collect()

            let cwd = rig.cwd();
            // Same live pid but another procStart: a stale file of a reused pid.
            std::fs::write(sessions.join("999999.json"), session_json(rig.me.pid, rig.me.created_ft + 1, &cwd, "busy", 1)).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(sessions.join("4.json"), r#"{"pid":4,"spare":true}"#).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(sessions.join("5.json"), r#"{"pid":5,"sessionId":"x","cwd":"C:\\w"}"#).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(sessions.join("30584.abc.key"), "secret").unwrap();

            match &signals[0] {

                    assert_eq!(key, &rig.key());
                    assert_eq!(proc, &rig.me);
                    assert_eq!(project.root, paths::normalize(&cwd).display);
                    assert_eq!(file.status.as_deref(), Some("busy"));
                    assert_eq!(*transcript_eof, None);

            );
            // Deleted while notifications overflowed: only the rescan sees it (D9).
            std::fs::remove_file(&incomplete).unwrap();
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Sessions(WatchEvent::Overflow));
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), [Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health: Health::Ok }]);
        }

        #[test]
        fn a_watcher_error_reports_source_health_error() {
            let mut rig = rig("cio-error");
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Error(io::Error::other("gone"))));
            assert_eq!(
                rig.signals(),
                [Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health: Health::Error("projects watcher: gone".into()) }]
            );
        }

        #[test]
        fn missing_dirs_report_missing() {
            let dir = TempDir::new("cio-missing");
            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
            let cfg = ClaudeConfig { base: dir.path.join("absent"), appdata: dir.path.clone(), watch: false };
            let mut io = ClaudeIo::new(cfg, tx, proc::Registry::new(), None);
            io.start();
            assert_eq!(
                rx.try_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                [Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health: Health::Missing }]
            );
        }

        #[test]
        fn retry_without_watchers_rescans() {
            let mut rig = rig("cio-retry");
            rig.io.start();
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
            rig.write_session("busy", 100);
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Retry);
            assert_eq!(names(&rig.signals()), ["ClaudeFile"]);
        }

        #[test]
        fn an_exited_process_gets_proc_exit_after_its_file_and_is_not_sent_again() {
            let mut rig = rig("cio-exit");
            let mut child = std::process::Command::new("cmd")
                .args(["/c", "ping -n 3 127.0.0.1 >nul"])
                .spawn()
                .expect("cmd starts");
            let id = proc::identify(child.id()).expect("child is running").0;
            let name = format!("{}.json", id.pid);
            let text = session_json(id.pid, id.created_ft, &rig.cwd(), "busy", 100);
            std::fs::write(rig.dir.path.join("sessions").join(&name), text).unwrap();
            rig.io.start();
            assert_eq!(names(&rig.signals()), ["ClaudeFile"]);
            child.wait().unwrap();
            let exit = rig.rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).expect("ProcExit");
            assert_eq!(exit, Signal::ProcExit { pid: id.pid, created_ft: id.created_ft });
            // The file is still there (a crash leaves it): it must not bring the session back.
            let text = session_json(id.pid, id.created_ft, &rig.cwd(), "idle", 200);
            std::fs::write(rig.dir.path.join("sessions").join(&name), text).unwrap();
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Sessions(WatchEvent::Changes(vec![(FileAction::Modified, name)])));
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
        }
```

```rust
    pub struct ClaudeConfig {
        /// The .claude dir (`sessions\` and `projects\` under it).
        pub base: PathBuf,
        /// %APPDATA%, for host classification.
        pub appdata: PathBuf,
        /// false in tests: no DirWatcher, inputs are fed manually.
        pub watch: bool,
    }

    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum ClaudeInput {
        Sessions(WatchEvent),
        Projects(WatchEvent),
        Effect(Effect),
        Retry,
    }

    /// State of one directory watcher.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    enum Watch {
        /// Not started (watch: false, or before `start`).
        Off,
        Running,
        Missing,
        Failed(String),
    }

    /// A session file that produced a ClaudeFile.
    struct Known {
        key: SessionKey,
        proc: ProcId,
        /// Last file sent (D25: unchanged files are not sent again).
        last: ClaudeSessionFile,
    }

    /// A TrackTranscript binding. `tail == None`: not bound yet. `existed == false` means the
    /// name is expected: the file did not exist and binds at offset 0 once it appears (D48).
    /// `existed == true` means the file existed but could not be opened: it binds with the
    /// window at its EOF once it opens, never at 0 (the history is not replayed).
    struct Track {
        /// `<sessionId>.jsonl`, lowercase.
        name: String,
        tail: Option<JsonlTail>,
        existed: bool,
    }

    struct ClaudeIo {
        cfg: ClaudeConfig,
        signals: Sender<Signal>,
        send_failed: bool,
        registry: proc::Registry,
        watcher_tx: Option<Sender<ClaudeInput>>,
        sessions_watch: Watch,
        projects_watch: Watch,
        /// By session file name.
        known: HashMap<String, Known>,
        /// Session file names currently unreadable (D9): unparsable known file, Incomplete file,
        /// process that denies access.
        unreadable: BTreeSet<String>,
        tracks: HashMap<SessionKey, Track>,
        cache: ProjectCache,
        /// Last health sent; the store starts at Ok.
        health: Health,
    }

    impl ClaudeIo {
        fn new(
            cfg: ClaudeConfig,
            signals: Sender<Signal>,
            registry: proc::Registry,
            watcher_tx: Option<Sender<ClaudeInput>>,
        ) -> Self {
            ClaudeIo {
                cfg,
                signals,
                send_failed: false,
                registry,
                watcher_tx,
                sessions_watch: Watch::Off,
                projects_watch: Watch::Off,
                known: HashMap::new(),
                unreadable: BTreeSet::new(),
                tracks: HashMap::new(),
                cache: ProjectCache::new(),
                health: Health::Ok,
            }
        }

        fn sessions_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
            self.cfg.base.join("sessions")
        }

        fn projects_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
            self.cfg.base.join("projects")
        }

        /// Never blocks; the first failed send (store gone) is logged once.
        fn emit(&mut self, signal: Signal) {
            if self.signals.send(signal).is_err() && !self.send_failed {
                self.send_failed = true;
                log::line("claude-io: store is gone, signals are dropped");
            }
        }

        fn start(&mut self) {
            self.ensure_watchers();
            self.rescan();
            self.report_health();
        }

        fn handle(&mut self, input: ClaudeInput) {
            match input {
                ClaudeInput::Sessions(WatchEvent::Changes(changes)) => {
                    for name in session_names(&changes) {
                        self.look_at(&name);
                    }
                }
                ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Changes(_)) => {}
                ClaudeInput::Sessions(WatchEvent::Overflow)
                | ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Overflow) => {
                    log::line("claude-io: watcher overflow, rescanning");
                    self.rescan();
                }
                ClaudeInput::Sessions(WatchEvent::Error(err)) => {
                    log::line(format!("claude-io: sessions watcher stopped: {err}"));
                    self.sessions_watch = Watch::Failed(format!("sessions watcher: {err}"));
                }
                ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Error(err)) => {
                    log::line(format!("claude-io: projects watcher stopped: {err}"));
                    self.projects_watch = Watch::Failed(format!("projects watcher: {err}"));
                }
                ClaudeInput::Effect(effect) => log::line(format!("claude-io: ignored effect {effect:?}")),
                ClaudeInput::Retry => self.retry(),
            }
            self.report_health();
        }

        /// Starts every watcher that is not running. True if at least one started now.
        fn ensure_watchers(&mut self) -> bool {
            let Some(tx) = self.watcher_tx.clone() else { return false };
            let mut started = false;
            if self.sessions_watch != Watch::Running {
                self.sessions_watch =
                    start_watcher(&self.sessions_dir(), false, "sessions", tx.clone(), ClaudeInput::Sessions);
                started |= self.sessions_watch == Watch::Running;
            }
            if self.projects_watch != Watch::Running {
                self.projects_watch =
                    start_watcher(&self.projects_dir(), true, "projects", tx, ClaudeInput::Projects);
                started |= self.projects_watch == Watch::Running;
            }
            started
        }

        /// Visible(true): restart missing/failed watchers; on success behave as Overflow. Without
        /// watchers (tests) there is nothing to restart, so Retry always rescans.
        fn retry(&mut self) {
            if self.watcher_tx.is_none() || self.ensure_watchers() {
                self.rescan();
            }
        }

        /// Sent on change only. Precedence Error > Missing > Degraded > Ok (D9).
        fn report_health(&mut self) {
            let error = [&self.sessions_watch, &self.projects_watch]
                .into_iter()
                .find_map(|w| match w {
                    Watch::Failed(msg) => Some(msg.clone()),
                    _ => None,
                });
            let missing = dir_missing(&self.sessions_watch, &self.sessions_dir())
                || dir_missing(&self.projects_watch, &self.projects_dir());
            let health = claude_health(error, missing, self.unreadable.len());
            if health != self.health {
                log::line(format!("claude-io: health {health:?}"));
                self.health = health.clone();
                self.emit(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health });
            }
        }
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 13: Add session-file handling (D47, D25, process proof, re-watch)**

Insert inside `mod io_thread`, directly above the `    #[cfg(test)]` line:

```rust
    impl ClaudeIo {
        /// D47: the file system decides what a name means, never the action code.
        fn look_at(&mut self, name: &str) {
            let path = self.sessions_dir().join(name);
            match std::fs::read(&path) {
                Ok(bytes) => self.process(name, &bytes),
                Err(err) if err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => self.gone(name),
                Err(err) => self.unreadable_file(name, &format!("read failed: {:?}", err.kind())),
            }
        }

        fn gone(&mut self, name: &str) {
            self.unreadable.remove(name);
            if let Some(known) = self.known.remove(name) {
                log::line(format!("claude {name} removed: {}", known.key));
                self.emit(Signal::ClaudeGone { key: known.key });
            }
        }

        /// A known file keeps its last state and counts as unreadable; a new file is skipped
        /// (spec §5.5 step 1).
        fn unreadable_file(&mut self, name: &str, reason: &str) {
            log::line(format!("claude {name} unreadable: {reason}"));
            if self.known.contains_key(name) {
                self.unreadable.insert(name.to_string());
            }
        }

        fn process(&mut self, name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) {
            let file = match parse_session_file(bytes) {
                Ok(file) => file,
                Err(reason) => return self.unreadable_file(name, &reason),
            };
            let (pid, proc_start) = match accept(&file) {
                Accept::Track { pid, proc_start } => (pid, proc_start),
                Accept::Skip(SkipReason::Incomplete) => {
                    log::line(format!("claude {name} skipped: incomplete"));
                    self.unreadable.insert(name.to_string());
                    return;
                }
                Accept::Skip(reason) => {
                    // Spare / parked / foreign domain: not a session to show (spec §5.5 step 2).
                    log::line(format!("claude {name} skipped: {reason:?}"));
                    self.unreadable.remove(name);
                    if let Some(known) = self.known.remove(name) {
                        self.emit(Signal::ClaudeGone { key: known.key });
                    }
                    return;
                }
            };
            self.unreadable.remove(name);
            if let Some(known) = self.known.get(name) {
                let same = known.proc.pid == pid && known.proc.created_ft == proc_start;
                if !same {
                    // procStart changed for this pid: the old session is gone (spec §5.5 step 3).
                    let known = self.known.remove(name).expect("entry checked above");
                    self.emit(Signal::ClaudeGone { key: known.key });
                } else if !self.registry.is_watched(pid, proc_start) && !self.rewatch(name, pid, proc_start) {
                    // The process exited (its waiter fired; ProcExit removes the session in the
                    // model): the file is proved again below, and that proof fails.
                    self.known.remove(name);
                }
            }
            if let Some(known) = self.known.get_mut(name) {
                if known.last == file {
                    return; // D25
                }
                let status_changed = known.last.status != file.status
                    || known.last.status_updated_at != file.status_updated_at;
                known.last = file.clone();
                let (key, proc) = (known.key.clone(), known.proc.clone());
                self.send_file(key, proc, file, status_changed);
                return;
            }
            self.prove_new(name, pid, proc_start, file);
        }

        /// Process proof of a new session file (spec §5.5 steps 3–4).
        fn prove_new(&mut self, name: &str, pid: u32, proc_start: u64, file: ClaudeSessionFile) {
            match proc::identify(pid) {
                Ok((id, handle)) => {
                    if id.created_ft != proc_start {
                        // A file left behind by a dead process whose pid was reused.
                        log::line(format!("claude {name} skipped: procStart does not match pid {pid}"));
                        return;
                    }
                    let key = claude_key(id.pid, id.created_ft);
                    log::line(format!("claude {name} tracked as {key}"));
                    self.known.insert(
                        name.to_string(),
                        Known { key: key.clone(), proc: id.clone(), last: file.clone() },
                    );
                    self.send_file(key, id.clone(), file, false);
                    // Registered only after ClaudeFile went out, so ProcExit always follows it in
                    // the FIFO channel.
                    self.watch_exit(&id, handle);
                }
                Err(ProcError::NotFound) | Err(ProcError::Exited) => {
                    log::line(format!("claude {name} skipped: process {pid} is not running"));
                }
                Err(ProcError::AccessDenied) => {
                    log::line(format!("claude {name}: process {pid} denies access"));
                    self.unreadable.insert(name.to_string());
                }
                Err(ProcError::Os(err)) => {
                    log::line(format!("claude {name}: process {pid} not identified: {err}"));
                    self.unreadable.insert(name.to_string());
                }
            }
        }

        /// A known process missing from the Registry: its exit waiter fired, or the waiter
        /// thread did not start or its wait failed (the Registry drops the entry then). Still
        /// the same process → watched again and the session stays (true); gone → false.
        fn rewatch(&mut self, name: &str, pid: u32, created_ft: u64) -> bool {
            match proc::identify(pid) {
                Ok((id, handle)) if id.created_ft == created_ft => {
                    log::line(format!("claude {name}: process {pid} watched again"));
                    self.watch_exit(&id, handle);
                    true
                }
                _ => false,
            }
        }

        /// ProcExit when the process ends. `false` from the Registry needs nothing more here:
        /// the process is already watched, or its waiter thread could not be started, and then
        /// the Registry has removed the entry and logged it, so the next change of the file
        /// watches it again (`rewatch`).
        fn watch_exit(&self, id: &ProcId, handle: OwnedHandle) {
            let signals = self.signals.clone();
            let _ = self.registry.watch(id, handle, move |pid, created_ft| {
                if signals.send(Signal::ProcExit { pid, created_ft }).is_err() {
                    log::line(format!("proc-exit {pid}: store is gone"));
                }
            });
        }

        /// ClaudeFile, preceded by the transcript records it depends on (spec §5.5 step 6): an
        /// unbound transcript is searched again first (D48), and a status change drains the
        /// bound one and reports its EOF.
        fn send_file(
            &mut self,
            key: SessionKey,
            proc: ProcId,
            file: ClaudeSessionFile,
            status_changed: bool,
        ) {
            self.search_unbound(&key);
            let transcript_eof = if status_changed { self.drain(&key) } else { None };
            let host = classify_host(&proc.image, file.entrypoint.as_deref(), &self.cfg.appdata);
            let project = self.cache.get(file.cwd.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(), paths::git_probe);
            self.emit(Signal::ClaudeFile { key, proc, host, project, file, transcript_eof });
        }

        /// Start, Overflow, successful Retry: every session file plus every name that vanished
        /// unseen (a known file gives ClaudeGone, an unreadable one leaves the D9 count), then
        /// every unbound transcript name, then every bound tail.
        fn rescan(&mut self) {
            let mut names = list_session_files(&self.sessions_dir());
            let mut vanished: Vec<String> = self
                .known
                .keys()
                .chain(self.unreadable.iter())
                .filter(|name| !names.contains(*name))
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            vanished.sort();
            vanished.dedup();
            names.extend(vanished);
            for name in names {
                self.look_at(&name);
            }
            let mut keys: Vec<SessionKey> = self.tracks.keys().cloned().collect();
            keys.sort();
            for key in &keys {
                self.search_unbound(key);
            }
            for key in &keys {
                self.drain(key);
            }
        }
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 14: Add the transcript binding that `send_file` and `rescan` use, and the file helpers**

Insert inside `mod io_thread`, directly above the `    #[cfg(test)]` line:

```rust
    impl ClaudeIo {
        /// Reads a bound transcript; new records go out as ClaudeTranscript{rebind_at: None}.
        /// Returns the tail's EOF, or None when no transcript is bound for `key`.
        fn drain(&mut self, key: &str) -> Option<u64> {
            let (records, eof) = {
                let tail = self.tracks.get_mut(key)?.tail.as_mut()?;
                read_records(tail)
            };
            if !records.is_empty() {
                self.emit(Signal::ClaudeTranscript { key: key.to_string(), rebind_at: None, records, eof });
            }
            Some(eof)
        }

        /// D48: a tracked session whose transcript is not bound looks for it again.
        fn search_unbound(&mut self, key: &str) {
            let name = match self.tracks.get(key) {
                Some(track) if track.tail.is_none() => track.name.clone(),
                _ => return,
            };
            if let Some(path) = find_transcript(&self.projects_dir(), &name) {
                self.bind(key, path);
            }
        }

        /// Binds an unbound name: from offset 0 when its file did not exist at TrackTranscript
        /// (D48), else with the window at its EOF.
        fn bind(&mut self, key: &str, path: PathBuf) {
            match self.tracks.get(key) {
                Some(Track { tail: None, existed: false, .. }) => self.bind_from_start(key, path),
                Some(Track { tail: None, existed: true, .. }) => self.bind_at_eof(key, path),
                _ => {}
            }
        }

        fn bind_from_start(&mut self, key: &str, path: PathBuf) {
            let mut tail = JsonlTail::new(path);
            let (records, eof) = read_records(&mut tail);
            match self.tracks.get_mut(key) {
                Some(track) => track.tail = Some(tail),
                None => return,
            }
            log::line(format!("claude transcript bound for {key} at 0"));
            self.emit(Signal::ClaudeTranscript { key: key.to_string(), rebind_at: Some(0), records, eof });
        }

        /// An existing transcript: the last WINDOW_BYTES are read and the binding starts at its
        /// EOF. A file that cannot be opened stays unbound, never bound at offset 0 (that would
        /// replay its whole history): the next search, notification or rescan tries again.
        fn bind_at_eof(&mut self, key: &str, path: PathBuf) {
            let mut tail = JsonlTail::new(path);
            if let Err(err) = tail.start_with_window(WINDOW_BYTES) {
                log::line(format!("claude transcript window failed for {key}: {:?}", err.kind()));
                return;
            }
            let (records, eof) = read_records(&mut tail);
            match self.tracks.get_mut(key) {
                Some(track) => track.tail = Some(tail),
                None => return,
            }
            log::line(format!("claude transcript bound for {key} at {eof}"));
            self.emit(Signal::ClaudeTranscript { key: key.to_string(), rebind_at: Some(eof), records, eof });
        }
    }

    fn start_watcher(
        dir: &Path,
        recursive: bool,
        label: &str,
        tx: Sender<ClaudeInput>,
        wrap: fn(WatchEvent) -> ClaudeInput,
    ) -> Watch {
        match DirWatcher::spawn(dir, recursive, MASK_NAME_WRITE_SIZE, move |event| tx.send(wrap(event)).is_ok()) {
            Ok(()) => Watch::Running,
            Err(err) if err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Watch::Missing,
            Err(err) => {
                log::line(format!("claude-io: {label} watcher failed: {err}"));
                Watch::Failed(format!("{label} watcher: {err}"))
            }
        }
    }

    fn dir_missing(watch: &Watch, dir: &Path) -> bool {
        match watch {
            Watch::Missing => true,
            Watch::Off => !dir.is_dir(),
            Watch::Running | Watch::Failed(_) => false,
        }
    }

    fn list_session_files(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
            Ok(entries) => entries,
            Err(err) => {
                if err.kind() != io::ErrorKind::NotFound {
                    log::line(format!("claude-io: sessions dir unreadable: {:?}", err.kind()));
                }
                return Vec::new();
            }
        };
        let mut names: Vec<String> = entries
            .flatten()
            .filter_map(|entry| entry.file_name().into_string().ok())
            .filter(|name| is_session_file_name(name))
            .collect();
        names.sort();
        names
    }

    /// `projects\*\<name>`: the slug rule is not documented, the session UUID is unique.
    fn find_transcript(projects: &Path, name: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        let entries = std::fs::read_dir(projects).ok()?;
        entries
            .flatten()
            .filter(|entry| entry.file_type().map(|t| t.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false))
            .map(|entry| entry.path().join(name))
            .find(|candidate| candidate.is_file())
    }

    fn read_records(tail: &mut JsonlTail) -> (Vec<(u64, Value)>, u64) {
        match tail.read_new() {
            Ok((lines, eof)) => (parse_records(lines), eof),
            Err(err) => {
                log::line(format!("claude transcript read failed: {:?}", err.kind()));
                (Vec::new(), tail.eof())
            }
        }
    }
```

```rust
        const REPLY_STALE: &str = r#"{"type":"assistant","isSidechain":false,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Stale answer."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"}}"#;
        const USER_QUICK: &str = r#"{"type":"user","isSidechain":false,"message":{"role":"user","content":"quick one"}}"#;
        const REPLY_QUICK: &str = r#"{"type":"assistant","isSidechain":false,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Quick answer."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"}}"#;
        const TITLE: &str = r#"{"type":"custom-title","customTitle":"Release prep"}"#;
        const TOOL_PUSH: &str = r#"{"type":"assistant","isSidechain":false,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"git push"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use"}}"#;
        const CLEARED_SID: &str = "0f6c2a51-0000-4000-8000-00000000c1a1";

        /// claude-io's signals go to a real Store and the Store's effects back to claude-io until
        /// both are quiet (the store thread's job, T13). Returns every alert raised.
        fn pump(rig: &mut Rig, store: &mut Store) -> Vec<Alert> {
            let mut alerts = Vec::new();
            loop {
                let signals = rig.signals();
                if signals.is_empty() {
                    return alerts;
                }
                for signal in signals {
                    let applied = store.apply(signal, 9_000);
                    alerts.extend(applied.alerts);
                    for effect in applied.effects {
                        rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Effect(effect));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        fn texts(alerts: &[Alert]) -> Vec<(AttentionKind, &str)> {
            alerts.iter().map(|a| (a.kind, a.text.as_str())).collect()
        }

        impl Rig {
            /// Rewrites the session file with `edit` applied to its JSON.
            fn edit_session(&self, edit: impl FnOnce(&mut Value)) {
                let path = self.dir.path.join("sessions").join(self.name());
                let mut file: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(&path).unwrap()).unwrap();
                edit(&mut file);
                std::fs::write(path, file.to_string()).unwrap();
            }
            fn cleared_transcript(&self) -> PathBuf {
                self.dir.path.join("projects").join(SLUG).join(format!("{CLEARED_SID}.jsonl"))
            }
        }

        #[test]
        fn sessions_already_waiting_at_start_are_listed_and_held_without_alerts() {
            // Mayak starts (or restarts) while a session waits on a permission prompt.
            let mut rig = rig("cio-boot");
            rig.append(&[TITLE, USER_OLD, TOOL_PUSH]);
            rig.write_session("waiting", 100);
            rig.edit_session(|f| f["waitingFor"] = "permission prompt".into());
            rig.io.start();
            let mut store = Store::new();
            assert_eq!(texts(&pump(&mut rig, &mut store)), [], "first sight never alerts");
            let snap = store.snapshot(9_000);
            assert_eq!(snap.attention, [rig.key()]);
            assert_eq!((snap.counts.waiting, snap.hold, snap.aggregate), (1, true, BotState::Approval));
            let row = &snap.projects[0].sessions[0];
            assert_eq!(row.title.as_deref(), Some("Release prep"), "the start window's title is read");
            assert_eq!(row.since, 100);
            // Claude Code rewrites the file within the same episode: still no alert, still held.
            rig.edit_session(|f| f["updatedAt"] = 5_000.into());
            rig.session_changed(&[FileAction::Modified]);
            assert_eq!(texts(&pump(&mut rig, &mut store)), []);
            let snap = store.snapshot(9_000);
            assert_eq!((snap.attention.len(), snap.hold, snap.projects[0].sessions[0].since), (1, true, 100));
        }

        #[test]
        fn a_collapsed_turn_is_read_before_its_file_and_alerts_once() {
            // busy → idle between two reads (a quick answer, an API error at once): claude-io sees
            // only idle → idle with a new statusUpdatedAt (spec §7 collapsed turn).
            let mut rig = rig("cio-collapsed");
            rig.append(&[USER_OLD, REPLY_OLD]);
            rig.write_session("idle", 100);
            rig.io.start();
            let mut store = Store::new();
            assert_eq!(texts(&pump(&mut rig, &mut store)), []);
            rig.append(&[USER_QUICK, REPLY_QUICK]);
            rig.write_session("idle", 200);
            rig.session_changed(&[FileAction::Modified, FileAction::Modified]);
            let alerts = pump(&mut rig, &mut store);
            assert_eq!(texts(&alerts), [(AttentionKind::Finished, "Claude · work finished: Quick answer.")]);
            // The same writes reported again, the transcript's too: nothing more.
            rig.session_changed(&[FileAction::Modified]);
            let rel = rig.transcript_rel();
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Changes(vec![(FileAction::Modified, rel)])));
            assert_eq!(texts(&pump(&mut rig, &mut store)), []);
            let snap = store.snapshot(9_000);
            let outcome = snap.projects[0].sessions[0].outcome.as_ref().map(|o| o.summary.as_str());
            assert_eq!(outcome, Some("Quick answer."));
        }

        #[test]
        fn a_cleared_session_lets_the_old_transcript_go_and_counts_only_the_new_one() {
            // /clear: same process, new sessionId; the new transcript appears with the first prompt.
            let mut rig = rig("cio-clear");
            rig.append(&[USER_OLD, REPLY_OLD]);
            rig.write_session("idle", 100);
            rig.io.start();
            let mut store = Store::new();
            assert_eq!(texts(&pump(&mut rig, &mut store)), []);
            rig.edit_session(|f| f["sessionId"] = CLEARED_SID.into());
            rig.session_changed(&[FileAction::Modified]);
            assert_eq!(texts(&pump(&mut rig, &mut store)), []);
            // The old transcript is written once more, then removed: claude-io no longer reads it.
            rig.append(&[REPLY_STALE]);
            let old = rig.transcript_rel();
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Changes(vec![(FileAction::Modified, old.clone())])));
            std::fs::remove_file(rig.transcript()).unwrap();
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Changes(vec![(FileAction::Removed, old)])));
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
            // First prompt of the cleared session: its file is created, the turn runs and ends.
            std::fs::write(rig.cleared_transcript(), format!("{USER_QUICK}\n")).unwrap();
            let new = format!("{SLUG}\\{CLEARED_SID}.jsonl");
            rig.io.handle(ClaudeInput::Projects(WatchEvent::Changes(vec![(FileAction::Added, new)])));
            rig.edit_session(|f| {
                f["status"] = "busy".into();
                f["statusUpdatedAt"] = 200.into();
            });
            rig.session_changed(&[FileAction::Modified]);
            assert_eq!(texts(&pump(&mut rig, &mut store)), []);
            let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open(rig.cleared_transcript()).unwrap();
            std::io::Write::write_all(&mut file, format!("{REPLY_QUICK}\n").as_bytes()).unwrap();
            drop(file);
            rig.edit_session(|f| {
                f["status"] = "idle".into();
                f["statusUpdatedAt"] = 300.into();
            });
            rig.session_changed(&[FileAction::Modified]);
            let alerts = pump(&mut rig, &mut store);
            assert_eq!(texts(&alerts), [(AttentionKind::Finished, "Claude · work finished: Quick answer.")]);
        }
```

The last three tests are the plan's Review Focus for claude-io: they run claude-io against a real `model::Store` (T9), the way the store thread will (T13), so a regression in either half shows. `sessions_already_waiting_at_start_are_listed_and_held_without_alerts` is Mayak starting or restarting while a session waits: listed with the title from the start window, counted, `hold`, and no alert, not even when Claude Code rewrites the file within the same episode. `a_collapsed_turn_is_read_before_its_file_and_alerts_once` is a turn whose `busy` write claude-io never read (a quick answer or an immediate API error coalesced into one notification batch, D47): the file goes idle → idle with only a new `statusUpdatedAt`, so this is the one test of the second half of `status_changed` (without it the transcript is not drained first and the turn ends Pending, no alert); a repeated notification gives no second alert. `a_cleared_session_lets_the_old_transcript_go_and_counts_only_the_new_one` is `/clear`: the model's Untrack + Track(new id) reach claude-io, a later write and the removal of the old transcript produce no signal, the new file binds at 0 and only its turn becomes the outcome.

- [ ] **Step 20: Add transcript tracking (TrackTranscript / UntrackTranscript, D48 notifications)**

Insert inside `mod io_thread`, directly above the `    #[cfg(test)]` line:

```rust
    impl ClaudeIo {
        fn effect(&mut self, effect: Effect) {
            match effect {
                Effect::TrackTranscript { key, session_id } => self.track(key, &session_id),
                Effect::UntrackTranscript { key } => {
                    if self.tracks.remove(&key).is_some() {
                        log::line(format!("claude transcript untracked for {key}"));
                    }
                }
                other => log::line(format!("claude-io: ignored effect {other:?}")),
            }
        }

        /// An existing transcript binds with the window at its EOF; a missing one becomes an
        /// expected name that binds at 0 once it appears (spec §5.5 "Транскрипт", D48). A
        /// session id that is not a plain file name is never tracked.
        fn track(&mut self, key: SessionKey, session_id: &str) {
            if !is_plain_session_id(session_id) {
                log::line(format!("claude transcript not tracked for {key}: the session id is not a file name"));
                return;
            }
            let name = transcript_name(session_id);
            let path = find_transcript(&self.projects_dir(), &name);
            self.tracks.insert(key.clone(), Track { name, tail: None, existed: path.is_some() });
            match path {
                Some(path) => self.bind_at_eof(&key, path),
                None => log::line(format!("claude transcript for {key} not created yet")),
            }
        }

        /// Files are matched by name only (spec §5.5): an unbound name binds on
        /// Added/Modified/RenamedNew (at 0 when it was expected, D48); a bound name is read on
        /// Modified.
        fn projects_changed(&mut self, changes: &[(FileAction, String)]) {
            for (action, rel) in changes {
                let name = file_name_lower(rel);
                if !name.ends_with(".jsonl") {
                    continue;
                }
                let discovered =
                    matches!(action, FileAction::Added | FileAction::Modified | FileAction::RenamedNew);
                let mut keys: Vec<SessionKey> = self
                    .tracks
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|(_, track)| track.name == name)
                    .map(|(key, _)| key.clone())
                    .collect();
                keys.sort();
                for key in keys {
                    let bound = self.tracks.get(&key).is_some_and(|track| track.tail.is_some());
                    if bound && *action == FileAction::Modified {
                        self.drain(&key);
                    } else if !bound && discovered {
                        let path = self.projects_dir().join(rel);
                        self.bind(&key, path);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
```

```rust
    /// Thread "claude-io". With `watch` it starts DirWatcher(sessions\, non-recursive) and
    /// DirWatcher(projects\, recursive), both MASK_NAME_WRITE_SIZE. The initial enumeration of
    /// sessions\ treats every file as new (the model gives no alerts for first sight).
    pub fn spawn(
        cfg: ClaudeConfig,
        signals: Sender<Signal>,
        registry: proc::Registry,
    ) -> io::Result<Sender<ClaudeInput>> {
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
        // Watchers need a sender of their own. Without watchers (tests) the thread keeps none,
        // so it ends as soon as the caller drops the returned sender.
        let watcher_tx = cfg.watch.then(|| tx.clone());
        std::thread::Builder::new().name("claude-io".into()).spawn(move || {
            let mut io = ClaudeIo::new(cfg, signals, registry, watcher_tx);
            io.start();
            for input in rx {
                io.handle(input);
            }
        })?;
        Ok(tx)
    }
```

  - T4 `observe::keys::codex_key(session_id: &str) -> SessionKey`; T6 `ProcId`.
  - T9/T10 `observe::model::{Signal::{CodexRollout { key, path: String, records: Vec<(u64, Value)>, eof: u64 }, CodexHook { key, event: HookEvent, proc: Option<ProcId>, host: HostKind, project: ProjectRef, rollout_eof: Option<u64>, title: Option<String> }, ProcExit { pid, created_ft }, SourceHealth { source, health }}, Effect::{UntrackRollout { key }, CodexTicker(bool)}, Health, Source::Codex}`.
  - T4 `lib.rs`: `struct AppSink { app: AppHandle, pending: Arc<Pending> }` implementing `pipe::RouterSink { fn pending(&self) -> &Pending; fn observe(&self, payload: Value); fn approval_context(&self, payload: &Value) -> ApprovalContext; fn show_approval(&self, payload: Value) }`; `pipe::serve<S: RouterSink>(name: String, sink: Arc<S>) -> io::Result<()>` (async); `pipe::pipe_name() -> String`; `Arc<Pending>` managed as Tauri state; `island::WINDOW_LABEL`.
- Produces (contract §2.17, §3):
  ```rust
  pub const TICK: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
  pub struct CodexConfig { pub codex_home: PathBuf, pub localappdata: PathBuf }
  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub enum CodexInput { Hook(Value), Effect(Effect) }
  pub fn spawn(cfg: CodexConfig, signals: Sender<Signal>, registry: proc::Registry)
      -> io::Result<Sender<CodexInput>>;
  // lib.rs (private)
  struct AppPaths { claude_dir: PathBuf, codex_home: PathBuf, appdata: PathBuf, localappdata: PathBuf }
  fn app_paths() -> AppPaths;
  fn app_paths_from(var: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<std::ffi::OsString>) -> AppPaths;
  struct AppSink { app, pending, codex: Sender<CodexInput>, codex_closed: AtomicBool }   // T13 replaces
  fn start_codex_io(paths: &AppPaths) -> Sender<CodexInput>;                           // T13 removes
  ```

**Behaviour fixed here** (contract §2.17 plus):
1. `registry.watch` for a proved agent runs after its `CodexHook` was sent (ProcExit never overtakes the hook that created the session).
2. A rollout that produced an `Unknown` record stays counted in `Degraded{unreadable}` until it is untracked (D9 "tracked rollouts that yielded Unknown").
3. Records drained from one path go to every session whose main rollout it is (in key order); a hook from a subagent (`agent_id` present) never chooses the main rollout but still drains the one its session has.
4. `app_paths_from` treats an empty environment value as unset; a missing `USERPROFILE`/`APPDATA`/`LOCALAPPDATA` falls back to `.` like `settings::config_dir()` does.
5. A `transcript_path` becomes a main rollout only when the base name of `normalize(path).key` is `rollout-*.jsonl`, the name Codex gives its rollouts (the pattern the S3 spike lists; T15 owns rule updates from S3). Any other path (for example `~/.codex/auth.json` or `config.toml`, never opened per spec §8) logs `codex rollout path rejected` and is not opened; the session keeps the main rollout it had.
6. A rollout that cannot be opened at its EOF (`start_at_eof` fails) is not tracked and is never read from offset 0, which would replay its history (spec §5.6 "история не воспроизводится"). That event changes nothing (`rollout_eof` stays `None` for a session without a main rollout), and the session's next hook tries again.

Insert inside `mod io_thread`, directly above the `    #[cfg(test)]` line:

```rust
    /// D9: tracked rollouts that produced an Unknown record.
    fn codex_health(unknown_rollouts: usize) -> Health {
        if unknown_rollouts == 0 {
            Health::Ok
        } else {
            Health::Degraded { unreadable: u32::try_from(unknown_rollouts).unwrap_or(u32::MAX) }
        }
    }

    /// Codex names its rollouts `rollout-<time>-<id>.jsonl`. Any other file a hook names (for
    /// example `auth.json` or `config.toml`, spec §8) is never opened. `path_key` is a
    /// `NormPath.key` (lowercase).
    fn is_rollout_name(path_key: &str) -> bool {
        let name = path_key.rsplit('\\').next().unwrap_or(path_key);
        name.starts_with("rollout-") && name.ends_with(".jsonl")
    }

    /// First 8 characters of a session id for the log, "-" when empty.
    fn short(session_id: &str) -> String {
        if session_id.is_empty() {
            "-".into()
        } else {
            session_id.chars().take(8).collect()
        }
    }

    /// One JSON value per line; unparsable lines are skipped.
    fn parse_records(lines: Vec<(u64, String)>) -> Vec<(u64, Value)> {
        lines
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|(offset, text)| serde_json::from_str(&text).ok().map(|v| (offset, v)))
            .collect()
    }
```

```rust
        const SID: &str = "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-00000000c0de";
        const TASK_STARTED: &str = r#"{"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"task_started","turn_id":"t2"}}"#;
        const TASK_COMPLETE: &str = r#"{"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"task_complete","turn_id":"t2","last_agent_message":"done"}}"#;
        const MYSTERY: &str = r#"{"type":"mystery","payload":{}}"#;

        fn me() -> ProcId {
            proc::identify(std::process::id()).expect("the test process identifies itself").0
        }

        struct Rig {
            dir: TempDir,
            io: CodexIo,
            rx: Receiver<Signal>,
            me: ProcId,
        }

        fn rig(tag: &str) -> Rig {
            let dir = TempDir::new(tag);
            let home = dir.path.join("codex");
            std::fs::create_dir_all(home.join("sessions")).unwrap();
            // The project root must not depend on a `.git` above %TEMP% (git_probe walks up).
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path.join("work").join(".git")).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(
                home.join("session_index.jsonl"),
                format!("{{\"id\":\"{SID}\",\"thread_name\":\"Fix the login page\"}}\n"),
            )
            .unwrap();
            let rollout = home.join("sessions").join("rollout-a.jsonl");
            std::fs::write(&rollout, format!("{TASK_STARTED}\n")).unwrap();
            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
            let cfg = CodexConfig { codex_home: home, localappdata: dir.path.join("local") };
            let io = CodexIo::new(cfg, tx, proc::Registry::new());
            Rig { dir, io, rx, me: me() }
        }

        impl Rig {
            fn rollout(&self) -> PathBuf {
                self.dir.path.join("codex").join("sessions").join("rollout-a.jsonl")
            }
            fn cwd(&self) -> String {
                self.dir.path.join("work").to_string_lossy().into_owned()
            }
            fn payload(&self, event: &str, transcript: Option<&Path>) -> Value {
                serde_json::json!({
                    "hook_event_name": event, "session_id": SID, "turn_id": "t2",
                    "cwd": self.cwd(), "model": "gpt-5-codex",
                    "transcript_path": transcript.map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
                    "agent": "codex", "relay": 2, "relay_ts": 1_000,
                    "agent_pid": self.me.pid, "agent_created": self.me.created_ft,
                    "agent_image": self.me.image,
                })
            }
            fn hook(&mut self, payload: Value) {
                self.io.handle(CodexInput::Hook(payload));
            }
            fn append(&self, lines: &[&str]) {
                use std::io::Write;
                let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open(self.rollout()).unwrap();
                for line in lines {
                    writeln!(f, "{line}").unwrap();
                }
            }
            fn len(&self) -> u64 {
                std::fs::metadata(self.rollout()).unwrap().len()
            }
            fn signals(&self) -> Vec<Signal> {
                self.rx.try_iter().collect()
            }
        }

        fn hook_of(signals: &[Signal]) -> (Option<ProcId>, Option<u64>, Option<String>) {
            match signals.last() {
                Some(Signal::CodexHook { proc, rollout_eof, title, .. }) => (proc.clone(), *rollout_eof, title.clone()),
                other => panic!("{other:?}"),
            }
        }

        #[test]
        fn an_invalid_payload_is_dropped() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-invalid");
            rig.hook(serde_json::json!({ "hook_event_name": "Stop" }));
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
        }

        #[test]
        fn first_hook_proves_reads_the_title_and_starts_the_rollout_at_eof() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-first");
            let rollout = rig.rollout();
            rig.hook(rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", Some(&rollout)));
            let signals = rig.signals();
            assert_eq!(signals.len(), 1, "history is not replayed: {signals:?}");
            match &signals[0] {
                Signal::CodexHook { key, event, proc, project, rollout_eof, title, .. } => {
                    assert_eq!(key, &codex_key(SID));
                    assert_eq!(event.hook_event_name, "UserPromptSubmit");
                    assert_eq!(proc.as_ref(), Some(&rig.me));
                    assert_eq!(project.root, paths::normalize(&rig.cwd()).display);
                    assert_eq!(*rollout_eof, Some(rig.len()));
                    assert_eq!(title.as_deref(), Some("Fix the login page"));
                }
                other => panic!("{other:?}"),
            }
            rig.hook(rig.payload("Stop", Some(&rollout)));
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).2, None, "the title is read on first sight only");
        }

            let rollout = rig.rollout();
            let mut sub = rig.payload("PermissionRequest", Some(&rollout));
            sub["agent_id"] = "a-1".into();
            sub["agent_type"] = "explorer".into();
            rig.hook(sub);
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).1, None);
            let zst = rig.dir.path.join("codex").join("sessions").join("rollout-b.jsonl.zst");
            rig.hook(rig.payload("Stop", Some(&zst)));
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).1, None);
            rig.append(&[TASK_COMPLETE]);
            rig.io.tick();
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
        }

        #[test]
        fn a_transcript_path_that_is_not_a_rollout_file_is_never_opened() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-reject");
            let auth = rig.dir.path.join("codex").join("auth.json");
            std::fs::write(&auth, "{}\n").unwrap();
            rig.hook(rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", Some(&auth)));
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).1, None);
            std::fs::write(&auth, "{}\n{}\n").unwrap();
            rig.io.tick();
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
        }

        #[test]
        fn a_rollout_that_cannot_be_opened_is_never_read_from_offset_zero() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-unopened");
            // A directory cannot be opened as a file, so start_at_eof fails.
            let later = rig.dir.path.join("codex").join("sessions").join("rollout-later.jsonl");
            std::fs::create_dir(&later).unwrap();
            rig.hook(rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", Some(&later)));
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).1, None);
            std::fs::remove_dir(&later).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(&later, format!("{TASK_STARTED}\n")).unwrap();
            rig.hook(rig.payload("Stop", Some(&later)));
            let signals = rig.signals();
            assert_eq!(signals.len(), 1, "the history is not replayed: {signals:?}");
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&signals).1, Some(std::fs::metadata(&later).unwrap().len()));
        }

        #[test]
        fn a_different_creation_time_gives_no_proc() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-proof");
            let mut payload = rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", None);
            payload["agent_created"] = (rig.me.created_ft + 1).into();
            rig.hook(payload);
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).0, None);
            let mut payload = rig.payload("Stop", None);
            payload["agent_pid"] = Value::Null;
            rig.hook(payload);
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).0, None);
        }

        #[test]
        fn an_exited_agent_gets_proc_exit_after_its_hook() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-exit");
            let mut child = std::process::Command::new("cmd")
                .args(["/c", "ping -n 3 127.0.0.1 >nul"])
                .spawn()
                .expect("cmd starts");
            let id = proc::identify(child.id()).expect("child is running").0;
            let mut payload = rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", None);
            payload["agent_pid"] = id.pid.into();
            payload["agent_created"] = id.created_ft.into();
            rig.hook(payload);
            assert_eq!(hook_of(&rig.signals()).0, Some(id.clone()), "the hook comes first");
            child.wait().unwrap();
            let exit = rig.rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).expect("ProcExit");
            assert_eq!(exit, Signal::ProcExit { pid: id.pid, created_ft: id.created_ft });
        }

        #[test]
        fn tick_reads_every_tracked_rollout() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-tick");
            let rollout = rig.rollout();
            rig.hook(rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", Some(&rollout)));
            rig.signals();
            rig.io.tick();
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
            rig.append(&[TASK_COMPLETE]);
            rig.io.tick();
            match rig.signals().as_slice() {
                [Signal::CodexRollout { key, records, .. }] => {
                    assert_eq!(key, &codex_key(SID));
                    assert_eq!(records.len(), 1);
                }
                other => panic!("{other:?}"),
            }
        }

        #[test]
        fn untrack_drops_the_tail_and_the_seen_mark() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-untrack");
            let rollout = rig.rollout();
            rig.hook(rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", Some(&rollout)));
            rig.signals();
            rig.io.handle(CodexInput::Effect(Effect::UntrackRollout { key: codex_key(SID) }));
            rig.append(&[TASK_COMPLETE]);
            rig.io.tick();
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), []);
            rig.hook(rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", Some(&rollout)));
            let signals = rig.signals();
            assert_eq!(signals.len(), 1, "restarted at EOF: {signals:?}");
            let (_, eof, title) = hook_of(&signals);
            assert_eq!(eof, Some(rig.len()));
            assert_eq!(title.as_deref(), Some("Fix the login page"));
        }

        #[test]
        fn unknown_records_degrade_health_until_untracked() {
            let mut rig = rig("xio-health");
            let rollout = rig.rollout();
            rig.hook(rig.payload("UserPromptSubmit", Some(&rollout)));
            rig.signals();
            rig.append(&[MYSTERY]);
            rig.io.tick();
            let signals = rig.signals();
            assert_eq!(signals.len(), 2, "{signals:?}");
            assert_eq!(signals[1], Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Codex, health: Health::Degraded { unreadable: 1 } });
            rig.io.handle(CodexInput::Effect(Effect::UntrackRollout { key: codex_key(SID) }));
            assert_eq!(rig.signals(), [Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Codex, health: Health::Ok }]);
        }
```

```rust
    pub struct CodexConfig {
        pub codex_home: PathBuf,
        pub localappdata: PathBuf,
    }

    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum CodexInput {
        Hook(Value),
        Effect(Effect),
    }

    /// Tail state of one rollout file, shared by every session whose main rollout it is.
    struct Rollout {
        tail: JsonlTail,
        /// NormPath.display, sent as CodexRollout.path.
        display: String,
        /// Produced an `Unknown` record while tracked (health, D9).
        unknown: bool,
    }

    struct CodexIo {
        cfg: CodexConfig,
        signals: Sender<Signal>,
        send_failed: bool,
        registry: proc::Registry,
        cache: ProjectCache,
        /// By normalized path key (spec §5.6: tail state is kept per path).
        rollouts: HashMap<String, Rollout>,
        /// Session → its main rollout's path key.
        main_rollout: HashMap<SessionKey, String>,
        /// Keys whose title was looked up in this run.
        seen: HashSet<SessionKey>,
        /// Last health sent; the store starts at Ok.
        health: Health,
    }

    impl CodexIo {
        fn new(cfg: CodexConfig, signals: Sender<Signal>, registry: proc::Registry) -> Self {
            CodexIo {
                cfg,
                signals,
                send_failed: false,
                registry,
                cache: ProjectCache::new(),
                rollouts: HashMap::new(),
                main_rollout: HashMap::new(),
                seen: HashSet::new(),
                health: Health::Ok,
            }
        }

        /// Never blocks; the first failed send (store gone) is logged once.
        fn emit(&mut self, signal: Signal) {
            if self.signals.send(signal).is_err() && !self.send_failed {
                self.send_failed = true;
                log::line("codex-io: store is gone, signals are dropped");
            }
        }

        fn handle(&mut self, input: CodexInput) {
            match input {
                CodexInput::Hook(payload) => self.hook(payload),
                CodexInput::Effect(Effect::UntrackRollout { key }) => self.untrack(&key),
                CodexInput::Effect(other) => log::line(format!("codex-io: ignored effect {other:?}")),
            }
            self.report_health();
        }

        fn hook(&mut self, payload: Value) {
            let len = payload.to_string().len();
            let event = match parse_hook(payload) {
                Ok(event) => event,
                Err(reason) => {
                    log::line(format!("codex hook dropped: len={len} reason={reason}"));
                    return;
                }
            };
            let key = codex_key(&event.session_id);
            let proven = self.prove(&event);
            let host = classify_host(event.agent_image.as_deref(), &self.cfg.localappdata);
            let project = self.cache.get(&event.cwd, paths::git_probe);
            let title = if self.seen.insert(key.clone()) { self.read_title(&event.session_id) } else { None };
            let rollout_eof = self.main_rollout_eof(&key, &event);
            log::line(format!(
                "codex {} s={} host={host:?} proc={}",
                event.hook_event_name,
                short(&event.session_id),
                if proven.is_some() { "yes" } else { "no" }
            ));
            let proc = proven.as_ref().map(|(id, _)| id.clone());
            self.emit(Signal::CodexHook { key, event, proc, host, project, rollout_eof, title });
            if let Some((id, handle)) = proven {
                // Registered after CodexHook, so ProcExit can never overtake the hook that created
                // the session. `false` needs nothing more: the process is already watched, or its
                // waiter thread could not be started, and then the Registry has removed the entry
                // and logged it, so the next proven hook registers it again.
                let signals = self.signals.clone();
                let _ = self.registry.watch(&id, handle, move |pid, created_ft| {
                    if signals.send(Signal::ProcExit { pid, created_ft }).is_err() {
                        log::line(format!("proc-exit {pid}: store is gone"));
                    }
                });
            }
        }

        /// identify(agent_pid) with a creation time equal to agent_created (spec §5.6).
        fn prove(&self, event: &HookEvent) -> Option<(ProcId, OwnedHandle)> {
            let (pid, created) = (event.agent_pid?, event.agent_created?);
            match proc::identify(pid) {
                Ok((id, handle)) if id.created_ft == created => Some((id, handle)),
                Ok(_) => {
                    log::line(format!("codex agent {pid}: creation time differs, not proved"));
                    None
                }
                Err(err) => {
                    log::line(format!("codex agent {pid} not identified: {err:?}"));
                    None
                }
            }
        }

        fn read_title(&self, session_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
            let path = self.cfg.codex_home.join("session_index.jsonl");
            match std::fs::read(&path) {
                Ok(bytes) => index_title(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes), session_id),
                Err(err) if err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => None,
                Err(err) => {
                    log::line(format!("codex session index unreadable: {:?}", err.kind()));
                    None
                }
            }
        }
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Add rollout tails, the tick, untracking and health**

Insert inside `mod io_thread`, directly above the `    #[cfg(test)]` line:

```rust
    impl CodexIo {
        /// Main rollout = transcript_path of events without agent_id (spec §5.6). Drains it
        /// (CodexRollout first) and returns its EOF for CodexHook; None when the session has no
        /// main rollout.
        fn main_rollout_eof(&mut self, key: &SessionKey, event: &HookEvent) -> Option<u64> {
            if event.agent_id.is_none() {
                if let Some(path_key) = event.transcript_path.as_deref().and_then(|raw| self.open_rollout(raw)) {
                    if self.main_rollout.insert(key.clone(), path_key).is_some() {
                        self.drop_unused_rollouts();
                    }
                }
            }
            let path_key = self.main_rollout.get(key)?.clone();
            self.drain_path(&path_key);
            self.rollouts.get(&path_key).map(|r| r.tail.eof())
        }

        /// Path key of a usable rollout: a readable `rollout-*.jsonl` (else the path is not used
        /// at all), whose tail starts at its EOF on first sight (history is not replayed). A
        /// file that cannot be opened at its EOF is not tracked and never read from offset 0:
        /// the session's next hook tries again.
        fn open_rollout(&mut self, raw: &str) -> Option<String> {
            if !is_readable_rollout(raw) {
                return None;
            }
            let norm = paths::normalize(raw);
            if !is_rollout_name(&norm.key) {
                log::line("codex rollout path rejected");
                return None;
            }
            if !self.rollouts.contains_key(&norm.key) {
                let mut tail = JsonlTail::new(&norm.display);
                if let Err(err) = tail.start_at_eof() {
                    log::line(format!("codex rollout start failed: {:?}", err.kind()));
                    return None;
                }
                self.rollouts.insert(norm.key.clone(), Rollout { tail, display: norm.display, unknown: false });
            }
            Some(norm.key)
        }

        /// New records of one rollout, sent to every session that uses it as main rollout.
        fn drain_path(&mut self, path_key: &str) {
            let Some(rollout) = self.rollouts.get_mut(path_key) else { return };
            let (records, eof) = match rollout.tail.read_new() {
                Ok((lines, eof)) => (parse_records(lines), eof),
                Err(err) => {
                    log::line(format!("codex rollout read failed: {:?}", err.kind()));
                    return;
                }
            };
            if records.is_empty() {
                return;
            }
            let unknown = records.iter().any(|(_, v)| matches!(parse_rollout_line(v), RolloutRecord::Unknown));
            if unknown && !rollout.unknown {
                log::line("codex rollout has records of an unknown shape");
                rollout.unknown = true;
            }
            let path = rollout.display.clone();
            let mut keys: Vec<SessionKey> = self
                .main_rollout
                .iter()
                .filter(|(_, p)| p.as_str() == path_key)
                .map(|(k, _)| k.clone())
                .collect();
            keys.sort();
            for key in keys {
                self.emit(Signal::CodexRollout { key, path: path.clone(), records: records.clone(), eof });
            }
        }

        fn tick(&mut self) {
            let mut path_keys: Vec<String> = self.rollouts.keys().cloned().collect();
            path_keys.sort();
            for path_key in path_keys {
                self.drain_path(&path_key);
            }
            self.report_health();
        }

        /// Drops the key → path mapping, the tail when no other session uses it, and the "seen"
        /// mark (a re-created session reads its title again).
        fn untrack(&mut self, key: &str) {
            self.seen.remove(key);
            if self.main_rollout.remove(key).is_some() {
                self.drop_unused_rollouts();
            }
        }

        fn drop_unused_rollouts(&mut self) {
            let used: HashSet<&String> = self.main_rollout.values().collect();
            self.rollouts.retain(|path_key, _| used.contains(path_key));
        }

        /// Sent on change only.
        fn report_health(&mut self) {
            let health = codex_health(self.rollouts.values().filter(|r| r.unknown).count());
            if health != self.health {
                log::line(format!("codex-io: health {health:?}"));
                self.health = health.clone();
                self.emit(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Codex, health });
            }
        }
    }
```

```rust
    pub const TICK: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);

    /// Thread "codex-io". The ticker is a recv_timeout against a 1 s deadline while
    /// CodexTicker(true) is in force; a plain recv otherwise (no extra thread, D27).
    pub fn spawn(
        cfg: CodexConfig,
        signals: Sender<Signal>,
        registry: proc::Registry,
    ) -> io::Result<Sender<CodexInput>> {
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
        std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("codex-io".into())
            .spawn(move || run(rx, CodexIo::new(cfg, signals, registry)))?;
        Ok(tx)
    }

    fn run(rx: Receiver<CodexInput>, mut io: CodexIo) {
        let mut deadline = Instant::now();
        loop {
            let input = if io.ticker {
                let now = Instant::now();
                if now >= deadline {
                    io.tick();
                    deadline = now + TICK;
                    continue;
                }
                match rx.recv_timeout(deadline - now) {
                    Ok(input) => input,
                    Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => continue,
                    Err(RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => return,
                }
            } else {
                match rx.recv() {
                    Ok(input) => input,
                    Err(_) => return,
                }
            };
            let was_on = io.ticker;
            io.handle(input);
            if io.ticker && !was_on {
                deadline = Instant::now() + TICK;
            }
        }
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 22: Add `AppPaths`**

In `windows/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, insert directly below the closing brace of `fn find_on_path(stem: &str) -> Option<std::path::PathBuf>` (the PATH/PATHEXT walker used by `open_in_vscode`):

```rust
/// Base paths of the observer and the installer. `app_paths()` is the only reader of these
/// environment variables for them (spec §5.5 "Пути", §8 "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR и CODEX_HOME").
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct AppPaths {
    claude_dir: std::path::PathBuf,
    codex_home: std::path::PathBuf,
    appdata: std::path::PathBuf,
    localappdata: std::path::PathBuf,
}

fn app_paths() -> AppPaths {
    app_paths_from(|name| std::env::var_os(name))
}

/// `var` reads one environment variable; an empty value counts as unset.
fn app_paths_from(var: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<std::ffi::OsString>) -> AppPaths {
    use std::path::PathBuf;
    let get = |name: &str| var(name).filter(|v| !v.is_empty()).map(PathBuf::from);
    let home = get("USERPROFILE").unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
    AppPaths {
        claude_dir: get("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR").unwrap_or_else(|| home.join(".claude")),
        codex_home: get("CODEX_HOME").unwrap_or_else(|| home.join(".codex")),
        appdata: get("APPDATA").unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(".")),
        localappdata: get("LOCALAPPDATA").unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(".")),
    }
}
```

In `windows/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, replace T4's `struct AppSink { … }` definition together with the `///` doc line directly above it (``/// Where the relay pipe delivers what `pipe::route` accepted.``), and the whole `impl pipe::RouterSink for AppSink { … }` block that T4 added (T4's `observe` logs `codex event dropped — observer not running`), with:

```rust
/// The router's view of the app (spec §5.3). From T12 on, Codex events go to codex-io.
struct AppSink {
    app: AppHandle,
    pending: Arc<Pending>,
    codex: std::sync::mpsc::Sender<observe::codex::CodexInput>,
    codex_closed: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
}

impl pipe::RouterSink for AppSink {
    fn pending(&self) -> &Pending {
        &self.pending
    }

    /// Never blocks: the channel is unbounded.
    fn observe(&self, payload: serde_json::Value) {
        let input = observe::codex::CodexInput::Hook(payload);
        if self.codex.send(input).is_err() && !self.codex_closed.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
            log::line("codex event dropped — codex-io not running");
        }
    }

    fn approval_context(&self, _payload: &serde_json::Value) -> pipe::ApprovalContext {
        pipe::ApprovalContext::default()
    }

    fn show_approval(&self, payload: serde_json::Value) {
        if let Err(err) = self.app.emit_to(island::WINDOW_LABEL, "hook", payload) {
            log::line(format!("hook emit failed: {err}"));
        }
    }
}

/// T12 only (T13 replaces it with the observer): codex-io runs, and the signals it sends are
/// drained by thread "signals-drain" because there is no store thread yet.
fn start_codex_io(paths: &AppPaths) -> std::sync::mpsc::Sender<observe::codex::CodexInput> {
    use observe::codex::CodexConfig;
    use observe::model::Signal;
    let (signals, drained) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<Signal>();
    let drain = std::thread::Builder::new().name("signals-drain".into()).spawn(move || for _ in drained {});
    if let Err(err) = drain {
        log::line(format!("signals-drain failed to start: {err}"));
    }
    let cfg = CodexConfig { codex_home: paths.codex_home.clone(), localappdata: paths.localappdata.clone() };
    match observe::codex::spawn(cfg, signals, observe::win::proc::Registry::new()) {
        Ok(tx) => tx,
        Err(err) => {
            log::line(format!("codex-io failed to start: {err}"));
            std::sync::mpsc::channel().0
        }
    }
}
```

**Behaviour fixed here** (contract §2.6 plus):
1. `should_emit`'s `prev` is the last snapshot *emitted*, so hidden-mode comparisons are against what the island actually has.
2. `became_visible` = the batch contained `Visible(true)` (always a full snapshot, spec §9), and each `Visible(true)` forwards `ClaudeInput::Retry`.
3. `AlertPrefs` needs no store-specific handling: it is applied by the model like any signal; T14 sends it (startup and `save_settings`).
4. `start` builds the initial shared snapshot from `Store::new().snapshot(now_ms())` (rev 0), so `sessions_snapshot` answers before the first batch.

```rust
// Session observer (spec §4, §9). Three std threads: "claude-io" and "codex-io" turn file
// notifications and Codex hooks into Signals; "store" applies them to the pure model
// (model::Store), dispatches the returned effects back to the sources and publishes snapshots.
// Nothing here runs on the tokio runtime.

pub mod claude;
pub mod claude_transcript;
pub mod codex;
pub mod keys;
pub mod model;
pub mod paths;
pub mod tail;
pub mod text;
pub mod win;

use model::{SessionsSnapshot, Store};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn should_emit_follows_the_publication_rules() {
        let base = Store::new().snapshot(0);
        let mut rev = base.clone();
        rev.rev += 1;
        let mut counts = rev.clone();
        counts.counts.waiting = 1;
        let mut hold = rev.clone();
        hold.hold = true;
        let mut attention = rev.clone();
        attention.attention = vec!["claude:1:2".into()];
        let mut aggregate = rev.clone();
        aggregate.aggregate = model::BotState::Working;

        assert!(should_emit(None, &base, false, false, false), "first snapshot");
        assert!(should_emit(Some(&base), &base, true, true, false), "Visible(true) always");
        assert!(should_emit(Some(&base), &rev, true, false, false), "visible: rev changed");
        assert!(!should_emit(Some(&base), &base, true, false, true), "visible: same rev");
        assert!(!should_emit(Some(&base), &rev, false, false, false), "hidden: only rev changed");
        assert!(should_emit(Some(&base), &rev, false, false, true), "hidden: alerts");
        for changed in [&counts, &hold, &attention, &aggregate] {
            assert!(should_emit(Some(&base), changed, false, false, false), "hidden: {changed:?}");
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Spec §9. `prev` is the last snapshot emitted. Visible: every rev change; hidden: only when
/// counts, attention, hold or aggregate change, or the batch had alerts; Visible(true) always.
pub(crate) fn should_emit(
    prev: Option<&SessionsSnapshot>,
    next: &SessionsSnapshot,
    visible: bool,
    became_visible: bool,
    had_alerts: bool,
) -> bool {
    let Some(prev) = prev else { return true };
    if became_visible {
        return true;
    }
    if visible {
        return next.rev != prev.rev;
    }
    had_alerts
        || next.counts != prev.counts
        || next.attention != prev.attention
        || next.hold != prev.hold
        || next.aggregate != prev.aggregate
}
```
