```rust
    const WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
    enum Published {
        Alerts(Vec<String>),
        Snapshot(SessionsSnapshot),
    }

    struct FakePublisher(Sender<Published>);

    impl Publisher for FakePublisher {
        fn alerts(&self, alerts: &[Alert]) {
            let keys = alerts.iter().map(|a| a.key.clone()).collect();
            self.0.send(Published::Alerts(keys)).expect("test receiver alive");
        }
        fn snapshot(&self, snapshot: &SessionsSnapshot) {
            self.0.send(Published::Snapshot(snapshot.clone())).expect("test receiver alive");
        }
    }

    fn fixed_now() -> i64 {
        1_000
    }

    struct StoreRig {
        signals: Sender<Signal>,
        published: Receiver<Published>,
        claude: Receiver<ClaudeInput>,
        codex: Receiver<CodexInput>,
        shared: Arc<Mutex<SessionsSnapshot>>,
        thread: JoinHandle<()>,
    }

    fn store_rig() -> StoreRig {
        let (signals, rx) = mpsc::channel();
        let (publish_tx, published) = mpsc::channel();
        let (claude_tx, claude) = mpsc::channel();
        let (codex_tx, codex) = mpsc::channel();
        let shared = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Store::new().snapshot(0)));
        let store_shared = shared.clone();
        let thread = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            run_store(rx, Box::new(FakePublisher(publish_tx)), claude_tx, codex_tx, store_shared, fixed_now)
        });
        StoreRig { signals, published, claude, codex, shared, thread }
    }

    impl StoreRig {
        fn send(&self, s: Signal) {
            self.signals.send(s).unwrap();
        }
        fn next(&self) -> Published {
            self.published.recv_timeout(WAIT).expect("a publication")
        }
        fn next_snapshot(&self) -> SessionsSnapshot {
            match self.next() {
                Published::Snapshot(s) => s,
                other => panic!("expected a snapshot, got {other:?}"),
            }
        }
        /// Ends the store loop and returns whatever was published after the last `next`.
        fn finish(self) -> (Vec<Published>, SessionsSnapshot) {
            let StoreRig { signals, published, shared, thread, .. } = self;
            drop(signals);
            thread.join().expect("store loop ends when the senders are gone");
            let rest = published.try_iter().collect();
            let last = shared.lock().unwrap().clone();
            (rest, last)
        }
    }

    fn claude_file(status: &str, at: i64) -> Signal {
        let file = ClaudeSessionFile {
            pid: Some(42),
            session_id: Some("s-1".into()),
            cwd: Some(r"C:\work\app".into()),
            proc_start: Some("7".into()),
            status: Some(status.into()),
            waiting_for: (status == "waiting").then(|| "permission prompt".to_string()),
            status_updated_at: Some(at),
            ..ClaudeSessionFile::default()
        };
        Signal::ClaudeFile {
            key: keys::claude_key(42, 7),
            proc: ProcId { pid: 42, created_ft: 7, image: r"C:\bin\claude.exe".into() },
            host: HostKind::Unknown,
            project: ProjectRef { key: r"c:\work\app".into(), root: r"C:\work\app".into() },
            file,
            transcript_eof: None,
        }
    }

    fn codex_prompt() -> Signal {
        let event = HookEvent {
            hook_event_name: "UserPromptSubmit".into(),
            session_id: "t-1".into(),
            turn_id: Some("u1".into()),
            cwd: r"C:\work\app".into(),
            transcript_path: None,
            tool_name: None,
            tool_input: None,
            last_assistant_message: None,
            agent_id: None,
            agent_type: None,
            relay_ts: 500,
            agent_pid: None,
            agent_created: None,
            agent_image: None,
        };
        Signal::CodexHook {
            key: keys::codex_key("t-1"),
            event,
            proc: None,
            host: HostKind::Unknown,
            project: ProjectRef { key: r"c:\work\app".into(), root: r"C:\work\app".into() },
            rollout_eof: None,
            title: None,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn hidden_changes_wait_for_counts_or_visibility() {
        let rig = store_rig();
        rig.send(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health: Health::Missing });
        assert_eq!(rig.next_snapshot().sources.claude, Health::Missing, "first batch is published");
        // Hidden, counts unchanged: not published on its own…
        rig.send(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Codex, health: Health::Degraded { unreadable: 1 } });
        // …but Visible(true) always publishes the full snapshot.
        rig.send(Signal::Visible(true));
        let shown = rig.next_snapshot();
        assert_eq!(shown.sources.codex, Health::Degraded { unreadable: 1 });
        assert!(matches!(rig.claude.recv_timeout(WAIT), Ok(ClaudeInput::Retry)));
        // Visible: every rev change.
        rig.send(Signal::SourceHealth { source: Source::Claude, health: Health::Ok });
        let after = rig.next_snapshot();
        assert_eq!(after.sources.claude, Health::Ok);
        assert!(after.rev > shown.rev);
        let (rest, last) = rig.finish();
        assert_eq!(rest, []);
        assert_eq!(last, after, "shared holds the last snapshot");
    }

    #[test]
    fn effects_go_to_their_source_and_alerts_precede_their_snapshot() {
        let rig = store_rig();
        let key = keys::claude_key(42, 7);
        rig.send(claude_file("busy", 100));
        rig.next_snapshot();
        match rig.claude.recv_timeout(WAIT) {
            Ok(ClaudeInput::Effect(Effect::TrackTranscript { key: k, session_id })) => {
                assert_eq!(k, key);
                assert_eq!(session_id, "s-1");
            }
            other => panic!("{other:?}"),
        }
        rig.send(claude_file("waiting", 200));
        assert_eq!(rig.next(), Published::Alerts(vec![key.clone()]));
        let waiting = rig.next_snapshot();
        assert_eq!(waiting.attention, [key.clone()]);
        assert!(waiting.hold);
        rig.send(Signal::ProcExit { pid: 42, created_ft: 7 });
        assert_eq!(rig.next_snapshot().counts.waiting, 0, "hidden, but counts changed");
        assert!(matches!(
            rig.claude.recv_timeout(WAIT),
            Ok(ClaudeInput::Effect(Effect::UntrackTranscript { key: k })) if k == key
        ));
        let (rest, _) = rig.finish();
        assert_eq!(rest, []);
    }

    #[test]
    fn alert_prefs_reach_the_model_through_the_store() {
        let rig = store_rig();
        rig.send(Signal::AlertPrefs { waiting: false, finished: true, error: true });
        rig.next_snapshot();
        rig.send(claude_file("busy", 100));
        rig.next_snapshot();
        rig.send(claude_file("waiting", 200));
        // No alert (D18), but the row and the counters still change: published while hidden.
        let waiting = rig.next_snapshot();
        assert_eq!(waiting.counts.waiting, 1);
        assert!(!waiting.hold, "hold needs alertWaiting");
        let (rest, _) = rig.finish();
        assert_eq!(rest, []);
    }

    #[test]
    fn codex_ticker_effects_go_to_codex_io() {
        let rig = store_rig();
        rig.send(Signal::Visible(true));
        rig.next_snapshot();
        rig.send(codex_prompt());
        assert!(matches!(rig.codex.recv_timeout(WAIT), Ok(CodexInput::Effect(Effect::CodexTicker(true)))));
        rig.send(Signal::Visible(false));
        assert!(matches!(rig.codex.recv_timeout(WAIT), Ok(CodexInput::Effect(Effect::CodexTicker(false)))));
        rig.finish();
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Add the publisher seam and the store loop**

```rust
/// Where the store thread publishes. The app emits to the island window; tests record.
pub trait Publisher: Send + 'static {
    /// "session-alert"
    fn alerts(&self, alerts: &[Alert]);
    /// "sessions"
    fn snapshot(&self, snapshot: &SessionsSnapshot);
}

/// Never blocks; the first failure (receiver gone) is logged, later ones are silent.
fn send_logged<T>(tx: &Sender<T>, value: T, to: &str, closed: &AtomicBool) {
    if tx.send(value).is_err() && !closed.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
        log::line(format!("observe: {to} is not running, messages are dropped"));
    }
}

/// Store loop body. Blocks on `rx`; each batch = first message + everything already queued.
/// Per batch: apply each signal with `now()`, dispatch its effects (TrackTranscript /
/// UntrackTranscript → claude-io, UntrackRollout / CodexTicker → codex-io), forward Retry to
/// claude-io on Visible(true); then write `shared`, emit alerts (if any) before the snapshot,
/// and the snapshot per `should_emit`. Returns when every sender of `rx` is gone.
pub(crate) fn run_store(
    rx: Receiver<Signal>,
    publisher: Box<dyn Publisher>,
    claude: Sender<ClaudeInput>,
    codex: Sender<CodexInput>,
    shared: Arc<Mutex<SessionsSnapshot>>,
    now: fn() -> i64,
) {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let mut visible = false;
    let mut published: Option<SessionsSnapshot> = None;
    let claude_closed = AtomicBool::new(false);
    let codex_closed = AtomicBool::new(false);
    while let Ok(first) = rx.recv() {
        let mut batch = vec![first];
        batch.extend(rx.try_iter());
        let mut alerts: Vec<Alert> = Vec::new();
        let mut became_visible = false;
        for signal in batch {
            let shown = if let Signal::Visible(on) = &signal { Some(*on) } else { None };
            let applied = store.apply(signal, now());
            if let Some(on) = shown {
                visible = on;
                if on {
                    became_visible = true;
                    send_logged(&claude, ClaudeInput::Retry, "claude-io", &claude_closed);
                }
            }
            alerts.extend(applied.alerts);
            for effect in applied.effects {
                match effect {
                    Effect::TrackTranscript { .. } | Effect::UntrackTranscript { .. } => {
                        send_logged(&claude, ClaudeInput::Effect(effect), "claude-io", &claude_closed)
                    }
                    Effect::UntrackRollout { .. } | Effect::CodexTicker(_) => {
                        send_logged(&codex, CodexInput::Effect(effect), "codex-io", &codex_closed)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        let snapshot = store.snapshot(now());
        *shared.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner) = snapshot.clone();
        if !alerts.is_empty() {
            publisher.alerts(&alerts);
        }
        if should_emit(published.as_ref(), &snapshot, visible, became_visible, !alerts.is_empty()) {
            publisher.snapshot(&snapshot);
            published = Some(snapshot);
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
pub struct ObserveConfig {
    /// $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or %USERPROFILE%\.claude
    pub claude_dir: PathBuf,
    /// $CODEX_HOME or %USERPROFILE%\.codex
    pub codex_home: PathBuf,
    /// %APPDATA% (host classification)
    pub appdata: PathBuf,
    /// %LOCALAPPDATA% (host classification)
    pub localappdata: PathBuf,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Handle {
    signals: Sender<Signal>,
    codex: Sender<CodexInput>,
    shared: Arc<Mutex<SessionsSnapshot>>,
    signals_closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    codex_closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl Handle {
    /// Never blocks (unbounded channel); a failed send is logged once.
    pub fn send(&self, s: Signal) {
        send_logged(&self.signals, s, "store", &self.signals_closed);
    }

    /// Router intake (Route::Observe) → codex-io.
    pub fn codex_hook(&self, payload: Value) {
        send_logged(&self.codex, CodexInput::Hook(payload), "codex-io", &self.codex_closed);
    }

    /// Clone of the last snapshot the store thread wrote.
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> SessionsSnapshot {
        self.shared.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner).clone()
    }
}

/// Spawns threads "store", "claude-io", "codex-io" with one shared proc::Registry. A source that
/// fails to spawn reports SourceHealth Error and the others still run.
pub fn start(cfg: ObserveConfig, publisher: Box<dyn Publisher>) -> Handle {
    let (signals, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Signal>();
    let registry = proc::Registry::new();
    let shared = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Store::new().snapshot(now_ms())));

    let claude_cfg = ClaudeConfig { base: cfg.claude_dir, appdata: cfg.appdata, watch: true };
    let claude = match claude::spawn(claude_cfg, signals.clone(), registry.clone()) {
        Ok(tx) => tx,
        Err(err) => {
            source_failed(&signals, Source::Claude, &err);
            mpsc::channel().0
        }
    };
    let codex_cfg = CodexConfig { codex_home: cfg.codex_home, localappdata: cfg.localappdata };
    let codex = match codex::spawn(codex_cfg, signals.clone(), registry) {
        Ok(tx) => tx,
        Err(err) => {
            source_failed(&signals, Source::Codex, &err);
            mpsc::channel().0
        }
    };

    let store_shared = shared.clone();
    let store_codex = codex.clone();
    let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("store".into())
        .spawn(move || run_store(rx, publisher, claude, store_codex, store_shared, now_ms));
    if let Err(err) = spawned {
        log::line(format!("observe: store thread failed to start: {err}"));
    }

    Handle {
        signals,
        codex,
        shared,
        signals_closed: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
        codex_closed: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
    }
}

fn source_failed(signals: &Sender<Signal>, source: Source, err: &std::io::Error) {
    log::line(format!("observe: {source:?} source failed to start: {err}"));
    let health = Health::Error(format!("thread failed to start: {err}"));
    // `start` still owns the receiver at this point, so this send cannot fail.
    let _ = signals.send(Signal::SourceHealth { source, health });
}

/// Milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC); 0 if the clock is before 1970.
pub(crate) fn now_ms() -> i64 {
    SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| i64::try_from(d.as_millis()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX))
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// Router annotations for a Claude PermissionRequest (spec §5.3): payload["agent_pid"] →
/// proc::identify → claude_key(pid, created_ft); payload["cwd"] → project root basename (D39,
/// D40). Each part None on failure. Blocking (Win32 + .git probes): the router calls it on
/// spawn_blocking (D46).
pub fn approval_context(payload: &Value) -> ApprovalContext {
    let session_key = payload
        .get("agent_pid")
        .and_then(Value::as_u64)
        .and_then(|pid| u32::try_from(pid).ok())
        .and_then(|pid| proc::identify(pid).ok())
        .map(|(id, _handle)| keys::claude_key(id.pid, id.created_ft));
    let project_name = payload
        .get("cwd")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .filter(|cwd| !cwd.trim().is_empty())
        .map(|cwd| paths::basename(&paths::project_of(cwd, paths::git_probe).root));
    ApprovalContext { session_key, project_name }
}
```

```rust
/// Publishes the observer's output to the island window (spec §9).
struct IslandPublisher {
    app: AppHandle,
}

impl observe::Publisher for IslandPublisher {
    fn alerts(&self, alerts: &[Alert]) {
        if let Err(err) = self.app.emit_to(island::WINDOW_LABEL, "session-alert", alerts) {
            log::line(format!("session-alert emit failed: {err}"));
        }
    }

    fn snapshot(&self, snapshot: &SessionsSnapshot) {
        if let Err(err) = self.app.emit_to(island::WINDOW_LABEL, "sessions", snapshot) {
            log::line(format!("sessions emit failed: {err}"));
        }
    }
}

/// The router's view of the app (spec §5.3): Codex events feed the observer, Claude approvals
/// get their session key and project name from it.
struct AppSink {
    app: AppHandle,
    pending: Arc<Pending>,
    observe: observe::Handle,
}

impl pipe::RouterSink for AppSink {
    fn pending(&self) -> &Pending {
        &self.pending
    }

    /// Never blocks: the channel is unbounded.
    fn observe(&self, payload: serde_json::Value) {
        self.observe.codex_hook(payload);
    }

    fn approval_context(&self, payload: &serde_json::Value) -> pipe::ApprovalContext {
        observe::approval_context(payload)
    }

    fn show_approval(&self, payload: serde_json::Value) {
        if let Err(err) = self.app.emit_to(island::WINDOW_LABEL, "hook", payload) {
            log::line(format!("hook emit failed: {err}"));
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
// ── Sessions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[tauri::command]
fn sessions_snapshot(observe: State<observe::Handle>) -> SessionsSnapshot {
    observe.snapshot()
}

/// Row click / "OK": marks the session's current episode as seen; never changes its phase.
#[tauri::command]
fn session_ack(observe: State<observe::Handle>, key: String) {
    observe.send(Signal::Ack(key));
}

/// "↗ Open" (D32): a Cursor / VS Code session opens its project root in that editor — launcher
/// found on PATH, the root passed as one argument, no shell; any other host, or no launcher,
/// opens Explorer. True only when an editor was launched; an unknown key is false.
#[tauri::command]
fn session_open(observe: State<observe::Handle>, key: String) -> bool {
    let Some((host, root)) = session_target(&observe.snapshot(), &key) else { return false };
    if let Some(launcher) = launcher_for(host).and_then(find_on_path) {
        match Command::new(launcher).arg(&root).creation_flags(CREATE_NO_WINDOW).spawn() {
            Ok(_) => return true,
            Err(err) => log::line(format!("session_open: editor did not start: {err}")),
        }
    }
    if let Err(err) = Command::new("explorer").arg(&root).spawn() {
        log::line(format!("session_open: explorer did not start: {err}"));
    }
    false
}

/// Launcher stem for a host (D32).
fn launcher_for(host: HostKind) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match host {
        HostKind::Cursor => Some("cursor"),
        HostKind::VsCode => Some("code"),
        HostKind::ClaudeDesktop | HostKind::CodexDesktop | HostKind::Unknown => None,
    }
}

/// Host and project root of a session in a snapshot.
fn session_target(snapshot: &SessionsSnapshot, key: &str) -> Option<(HostKind, String)> {
    snapshot.projects.iter().find_map(|project| {
        project.sessions.iter().find(|s| s.key == key).map(|s| (s.host, project.root.clone()))
    })
}
```

```rust
/// Hidden island → shrink the window to the invisible wake strip and park the
/// cursor poll; anything else → full panel and 60 Hz polling. The observer
/// publishes every change only while the island is visible (spec §9).
#[tauri::command]
fn set_collapsed(app: AppHandle, shared: State<Shared>, observe: State<observe::Handle>, collapsed: bool) {
    let pref = shared.settings.lock().unwrap().screen.clone();
    shared.gate.collapsed.store(collapsed, Ordering::Relaxed);
    island::apply_geometry(&app, &pref, collapsed);
    // The wake strip must always take the mouse, and a resize invalidates the flag.
    island::set_ignore_cursor(&app, false);
    shared.gate.forget_ignore_state();
    shared.gate.set_active(!collapsed);
    observe.send(Signal::Visible(!collapsed));
}
```

```rust
            observe.send(Signal::Visible(true));
            handle.manage(observe.clone());
            let sink = Arc::new(AppSink {
                app: handle.clone(),
                pending: handle.state::<Arc<Pending>>().inner().clone(),
                observe,
            });
            tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
                if let Err(err) = pipe::serve(pipe::pipe_name(), sink).await {
                    log::line(format!("cannot open the relay pipe: {err}"));
                }
            });
```

**Decisions recorded by Section F** (contract §7 D77–D81):
- **D77** T11 (log.rs, owned by T1 in contract §1): under `cfg(test)` `crate::log::line` writes to stderr, so no unit test writes the user's `mayak.log`; the signature is unchanged.
- **D78** T11/T12: liveness of a known session is checked with `Registry::is_watched`, and exit waiters are registered only after the session's first signal was sent (prevents ghost sessions after `ProcExit` and `ProcExit` overtaking creation). T11: a known process that is not watched but still identifies with the same creation time is watched again and keeps its session.
- **D79** T11: `Spare`/`Parked`/`ForeignDomain` on a known file → `ClaudeGone`; `ProcError::Os` → unreadable; transcript re-search before `ClaudeFile`; `Retry` with `watch: false` always rescans; `Missing` with `watch: false` via `is_dir()`; a transcript that exists but cannot be opened stays unbound (`Track.existed`) and is bound with the window at its EOF later, never at 0; session ids with `\`, `/`, `:` or `..` are not tracked; a rescan re-checks vanished unreadable names.
- **D80** T12: `Unknown` rollouts stay counted until untracked; drained records go to every session sharing the path; only `rollout-*.jsonl` paths become main rollouts; a rollout whose `start_at_eof` fails is not tracked (the next hook tries again).
- **D81** T13: `prev` in `should_emit` is the last emitted snapshot; `Handle` carries two private "closed" flags for log-once.

Behaviour notes fixed by this task (the reasons are in the code comments; all are inside the contract's room; the one marked "Contract decision" is D82 in contract §7):
- `write_plan` creates the backup with `create_new`: an existing backup file is an error, never overwritten. The new bytes go to a temp file that is flushed (`sync_all`) before the rename, so a power loss cannot leave an empty or partial config in place.
- `detect_format` of a file with no line ending (one-line JSON, empty file) is LF without final newline, so a one-line file stays without a final newline.
- Legacy `merged` keeps the `PermissionRequest` key where it was; `without_ours` drops `"hooks"` with `shift_remove`, so the user's other keys keep their order (serde_json's `remove` with `preserve_order` is `swap_remove`). `strip_ours` drops only an event list it emptied, and `without_ours` drops `"hooks"` only when it emptied every list: an empty list or an empty `"hooks": {}` the user left there stays, on install and on removal.
- Codex removal without a usable relay (`our_command` fails) matches by the marker only, which finds long-name commands only: on a volume with 8.3 names the installer writes `…\MAYAK-~1.EXE --agent codex`, which has no marker. In that case `status` (Codex) and the Codex Remove preview carry the note "Mayak's relay isn't available, so entries written with its short (8.3) path can't be recognised. Restart Mayak to restore the relay, then Remove." (`is_ours` never matches an empty `our_command` by equality.)
- Contract decision D82 (contract §3 `hooks_apply`, §7): for target `codex`, `CodexHooksInstalled` is sent after every `hooks_apply` call that got past `Target::parse` — also when `Plans::take` refuses — always from a fresh `installed_at` read of the file, as spec §8 says («после каждого hooks_apply»). An extra send after a refused take reports the file as it is on disk; when the file did not change, the model state does not change either (contract §2.15: `(false)` → NotInstalled, `(true)` → InstalledUnseen unless Receiving).
- D58: the settings window is created with `.focused(false)`, because Tauri focuses a new webview by default (`focus: true`) and wry then calls `MoveFocus` on the hidden webview; the first DOM `focus` must come from `show_settings_window`. `hooks_status` logs `hooks_status target=<name>` (the target name only), which Step 34 uses to check when the Claude config is read.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testutil::TempDir;
    use serde_json::json;

    const WHERE: &str = "settings.json";
    const STAMP: &str = "20261001-120000";

    #[test]
    fn a_utf8_bom_is_stripped_not_treated_as_corruption() {
        // PowerShell 5's `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` produces exactly this.
        let mut bytes = vec![0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF];
        bytes.extend_from_slice(br#"{"model":"opus","hooks":{}}"#);
        let parsed = parse_object(&bytes, WHERE).expect("a BOM must not defeat the parser");
        assert_eq!(parsed["model"], "opus");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unreadable_content_is_an_error_never_an_empty_object() {
        // Returning {} here would let a merge produce a file holding nothing but
        // our hooks, and the write would replace everything the user had.
        for bad in [&b"{ not json"[..], &b"[1,2,3]"[..], &b"\"a string\""[..]] {
            assert!(
                parse_object(bad, WHERE).is_err(),
                "content we cannot use must refuse, not come back empty"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_and_whitespace_files_start_from_nothing() {
        assert_eq!(parse_object(b"", WHERE).unwrap(), json!({}));
        assert_eq!(parse_object(b"  \n\t ", WHERE).unwrap(), json!({}));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_fingerprint_notices_any_change() {
        assert_eq!(fingerprint(b"{}"), fingerprint(b"{}"));
        assert_ne!(fingerprint(b"{}"), fingerprint(b"{ }"));
        assert_ne!(fingerprint(b""), fingerprint(b"{}"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn targets_parse_with_claude_as_the_default() {
        assert_eq!(Target::parse(None), Ok(Target::Claude));
        assert_eq!(Target::parse(Some("claude")), Ok(Target::Claude));
        assert_eq!(Target::parse(Some("codex")), Ok(Target::Codex));
        let err = Target::parse(Some("cursor")).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.starts_with("unknown target"), "got: {err}");
        assert_eq!(Target::Codex.as_str(), "codex");
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(Target::Claude).unwrap(), json!("claude"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_format_of_an_existing_file_is_detected() {
        let f = detect_format(b"\xEF\xBB\xBF{\r\n  \"a\": 1\r\n}\r\n");
        assert_eq!(f, TextFormat { bom: true, crlf: true, final_newline: true, mixed_eol: false });

        let f = detect_format(b"{\n  \"a\": 1\n}");
        assert_eq!(f, TextFormat { bom: false, crlf: false, final_newline: false, mixed_eol: false });

        // First line ending decides the style; both kinds present → mixed.
        let f = detect_format(b"{\r\n  \"a\": 1\n}\r\n");
        assert_eq!(f, TextFormat { bom: false, crlf: true, final_newline: true, mixed_eol: true });

        let f = detect_format(br#"{"a":1}"#);
        assert_eq!(f, TextFormat { bom: false, crlf: false, final_newline: false, mixed_eol: false });
    }

    #[test]
    fn rendering_keeps_bom_crlf_and_the_final_newline() {
        let v = json!({ "b": 1, "a": "x\ny" });
        let crlf = TextFormat { bom: true, crlf: true, final_newline: true, mixed_eol: false };
        assert_eq!(render(&v, crlf), b"\xEF\xBB\xBF{\r\n  \"b\": 1,\r\n  \"a\": \"x\\ny\"\r\n}\r\n".to_vec());

        let bare = TextFormat { bom: false, crlf: false, final_newline: false, mixed_eol: false };
        assert_eq!(render(&v, bare), b"{\n  \"b\": 1,\n  \"a\": \"x\\ny\"\n}".to_vec());

        assert_eq!(render(&json!({}), TextFormat::NEW_FILE), b"{}\n".to_vec());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_file_is_shown_whole_and_created_in_the_new_file_format() {
        let next = json!({ "hooks": { "Stop": [] } });

        let (plan, diff, notes) = make_plan(Target::Codex, true, path, None, &next, STAMP);

        assert_eq!(plan.bytes, b"{\n  \"hooks\": {\n    \"Stop\": []\n  }\n}\n".to_vec());
        assert_eq!(diff, "+ {\n+   \"hooks\": {\n+     \"Stop\": []\n+   }\n+ }\n");
        assert!(notes.is_empty());
        assert!(!plan.unchanged);
        assert_eq!(plan.fingerprint, fingerprint(b""));
        assert_eq!(plan.path, path);
        assert_eq!(plan.backup_path, PathBuf::from(r"C:\Users\dev\.codex\hooks.json.mayak-backup-20261001-120000"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_diff_is_made_from_the_bytes_that_will_be_written() {
        let current = b"\xEF\xBB\xBF{\r\n    \"model\": \"x\"\r\n}\r\n".to_vec();
        let next = json!({ "model": "x", "hooks": {} });
        let (plan, diff, _) =
            make_plan(Target::Claude, true, Path::new("settings.json"), Some(&current), &next, STAMP);

        // The new file keeps BOM, CRLF and the final newline...
        assert_eq!(plan.bytes, b"\xEF\xBB\xBF{\r\n  \"model\": \"x\",\r\n  \"hooks\": {}\r\n}\r\n".to_vec());
        // ...and the context and "+" lines of the diff are exactly its lines.
        let after: Vec<&str> = diff
            .lines()
            .filter(|l| !l.starts_with('-'))
            .map(|l| &l[2..])
            .collect();
        let written = String::from_utf8_lossy(strip_bom(&plan.bytes)).into_owned();
        assert_eq!(after, written.lines().collect::<Vec<_>>());
        assert!(diff.contains("-     \"model\": \"x\""), "the old 4-space line must show as removed: {diff}");
        assert_eq!(plan.fingerprint, fingerprint(&current));

    #[test]
    fn an_identical_entry_in_another_layout_is_unchanged_and_never_written() {

        let tmp = TempDir::new("hookfile-same");
        let dir = tmp.path.join("cfg");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("hooks.json");
        let current = b"{\r\n    \"hooks\": {\r\n        \"Stop\": [ { \"hooks\": [] } ]\r\n    },\r\n    \"description\": \"d\"\r\n}\r\n".to_vec();
        std::fs::write(&path, &current).unwrap();
        let next = json!({ "description": "d", "hooks": { "Stop": [ { "hooks": [] } ] } });

        let (plan, diff, notes) = make_plan(Target::Codex, true, &path, Some(&current), &next, STAMP);
        assert!(plan.unchanged);
        assert_eq!(diff, "No change.");
        assert!(notes.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(plan.bytes, current);

        let err = write_plan(&plan).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.starts_with("No change:"), "got: {err}");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), current);
        assert!(!plan.backup_path.exists(), "no backup for a write that did not happen");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&dir).unwrap().count(), 1, "no temp file left behind");

        let current = b"{\r\n  \"a\": 1\n}\r\n".to_vec();
        let (plan, _, notes) =
            make_plan(Target::Claude, true, Path::new("settings.json"), Some(&current), &json!({ "a": 2 }), STAMP);
        assert_eq!(notes, vec!["Line endings will be normalised to CRLF.".to_string()]);
        assert_eq!(plan.bytes, b"{\r\n  \"a\": 2\r\n}\r\n".to_vec());

        let current = b"{\n  \"a\": 1\r\n}\n".to_vec();
        let (_, _, notes) =
            make_plan(Target::Claude, true, Path::new("settings.json"), Some(&current), &json!({ "a": 2 }), STAMP);
        assert_eq!(notes, vec!["Line endings will be normalised to LF.".to_string()]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn local_stamp_is_date_dash_time() {
        let s = local_stamp();
        assert_eq!(s.len(), 15, "got: {s}");
        assert_eq!(&s[8..9], "-");
        assert!(s.chars().enumerate().all(|(i, c)| i == 8 || c.is_ascii_digit()), "got: {s}");
    }

    fn plan_for(target: Target, install: bool, fp: &str) -> PendingPlan {
        PendingPlan {
            target,
            install,
            path: PathBuf::from("x.json"),
            fingerprint: fp.into(),
            bytes: b"{}\n".to_vec(),
            backup_path: PathBuf::from("x.json.mayak-backup-1"),
            unchanged: false,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn plans_are_taken_once_and_only_with_matching_install_and_fingerprint() {
        let plans = Plans::default();
        assert!(plans.take(Target::Codex, true, "aa").is_err(), "nothing previewed yet");

        plans.store(plan_for(Target::Codex, true, "aa"));
        plans.store(plan_for(Target::Claude, false, "bb"));
        assert!(plans.take(Target::Codex, true, "zz").is_err(), "unknown fingerprint");
        assert!(plans.take(Target::Codex, false, "aa").is_err(), "install flag differs");
        // A refused take leaves the plan in place.
        assert_eq!(plans.take(Target::Codex, true, "aa").unwrap(), plan_for(Target::Codex, true, "aa"));
        assert!(plans.take(Target::Codex, true, "aa").is_err(), "a plan is applied once");
        // Targets do not share plans.
        assert_eq!(plans.take(Target::Claude, false, "bb").unwrap(), plan_for(Target::Claude, false, "bb"));

        // A newer preview replaces the older one of the same target.
        plans.store(plan_for(Target::Codex, true, "aa"));
        plans.store(plan_for(Target::Codex, true, "cc"));
        assert!(plans.take(Target::Codex, true, "aa").is_err());
        assert!(plans.take(Target::Codex, true, "cc").is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_plan_backs_up_byte_for_byte_and_replaces_the_file() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("hookfile-write");
        let dir = tmp.path.join("cfg");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("settings.json");
        let original = b"\xEF\xBB\xBF{\r\n  \"model\": \"x\"\r\n}\r\n".to_vec();
        std::fs::write(&path, &original).unwrap();

        let next = json!({ "model": "x", "hooks": {} });
        let (plan, _, _) = make_plan(Target::Claude, true, &path, Some(&original), &next, STAMP);
        let backup = write_plan(&plan).expect("the write should succeed");

        assert_eq!(backup, dir.join("settings.json.mayak-backup-20261001-120000").to_string_lossy());
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&backup).unwrap(), original, "the backup is the exact old bytes");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), plan.bytes, "the file is the exact previewed bytes");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&dir).unwrap().count(), 2, "file + backup, no temp file left");

        // The same backup path is never overwritten.
        let (again, _, _) = make_plan(Target::Claude, false, &path, Some(&plan.bytes), &json!({}), STAMP);
        let err = write_plan(&again).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("Backup to"), "got: {err}");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), plan.bytes, "a failed backup writes nothing");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&backup).unwrap(), original);
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_plan_refuses_a_file_that_changed_since_the_preview() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("hookfile-stale");
        let dir = tmp.path.join("cfg");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("hooks.json");
        std::fs::write(&path, b"{}").unwrap();
        let (plan, _, _) = make_plan(Target::Codex, true, &path, Some(b"{}"), &json!({ "hooks": {} }), STAMP);

        std::fs::write(&path, br#"{"description":"edited by hand"}"#).unwrap();
        let err = write_plan(&plan).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("changed since the preview"), "got: {err}");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), br#"{"description":"edited by hand"}"#.to_vec());
        assert!(!plan.backup_path.exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_plan_with_no_previous_file_returns_an_empty_backup() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("hookfile-new");
        let path = tmp.path.join("not-yet").join("hooks.json");
        let (plan, _, _) = make_plan(Target::Codex, true, &path, None, &json!({ "hooks": {} }), STAMP);

        assert_eq!(write_plan(&plan), Ok(String::new()));
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), b"{\n  \"hooks\": {}\n}\n".to_vec());
        assert!(!plan.backup_path.exists());
    }
}
```

```rust
// Write protection shared by every tool config Mayak may edit (spec §8):
// ~/.codex/hooks.json (the optional Codex integration) and ~/.claude/settings.json
// (the legacy Allow/Deny relay under Advanced).
//
// The rules, for both targets:
// - the diff is computed between the current raw bytes and the exact bytes that
//   will be written; a missing file is shown whole;
// - the preview's plan (those bytes, the fingerprint of the file they were made
//   from, the backup path) stays here in Rust; the webview hands back only a
//   target and a fingerprint, never a path or content;
// - the file's own format is kept: BOM, CRLF/LF, final newline;
// - right before writing, the file is read again and must still match the
//   fingerprint; then a byte-exact backup, a flushed temp file next to the
//   target, and a rename over it, so a crash leaves the original intact.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};

use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::{Map, Value};
use windows::Win32::System::SystemInformation::GetLocalTime;

use crate::ident;

const BOM: [u8; 3] = [0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF];

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Target {
    Claude,
    Codex,
}

impl Target {
    /// No target means "claude": that is what the commands did before targets existed.
    pub fn parse(raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Target, String> {
        match raw {
            None | Some("claude") => Ok(Target::Claude),
            Some("codex") => Ok(Target::Codex),
            Some(other) => Err(format!(
                "unknown target \"{other}\" (expected \"claude\" or \"codex\")"
            )),
        }
    }

    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Target::Claude => "claude",
            Target::Codex => "codex",
        }
    }
}

/// How an existing file is laid out, so a rewrite keeps it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TextFormat {
    pub bom: bool,
    /// Line endings to write: the style of the file's first line ending.
    pub crlf: bool,
    pub final_newline: bool,
    /// The file has both "\r\n" and bare "\n"; the rewrite uses `crlf` everywhere.
    pub mixed_eol: bool,
}

impl TextFormat {
    /// A file created from scratch: no BOM, LF, final newline (D28).
    pub const NEW_FILE: TextFormat =
        TextFormat { bom: false, crlf: false, final_newline: true, mixed_eol: false };
}

pub fn detect_format(bytes: &[u8]) -> TextFormat {
    let bom = bytes.starts_with(&BOM);
    let body = strip_bom(bytes);
    let mut crlf = None;
    let (mut has_crlf, mut has_lf) = (false, false);
    for (i, &b) in body.iter().enumerate() {
        if b != b'\n' {
            continue;
        }
        let is_crlf = i > 0 && body[i - 1] == b'\r';
        crlf.get_or_insert(is_crlf);
        if is_crlf {
            has_crlf = true;
        } else {
            has_lf = true;
        }
    }
    TextFormat {
        bom,
        crlf: crlf.unwrap_or(false),
        final_newline: body.ends_with(b"\n"),
        mixed_eol: has_crlf && has_lf,
    }
}

/// One leading UTF-8 BOM, which PowerShell's `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` writes
/// and serde_json refuses.
pub fn strip_bom(bytes: &[u8]) -> &[u8] {
    bytes.strip_prefix(&BOM).unwrap_or(bytes)
}

/// The config as a JSON object. Empty or whitespace-only means "start from
/// nothing"; anything else that is not a JSON object is refused, because
/// treating somebody's unreadable config as empty and writing that back over
/// it would destroy it.
pub fn parse_object(bytes: &[u8], path: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let text = strip_bom(bytes);
    if text.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_whitespace) {
        return Ok(Value::Object(Map::new()));
    }
    match serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(text) {
        Ok(v) if v.is_object() => Ok(v),
        Ok(_) => Err(format!("{path} isn't a JSON object — {} won't touch it.", ident::APP_NAME)),
        Err(err) => Err(format!(
            "{path} isn't valid JSON ({err}). Fix or move it, then try again — {} won't overwrite it.",
            ident::APP_NAME
        )),
    }
}

/// Pretty JSON (2 spaces, key order kept) in the given format.
pub fn render(value: &Value, fmt: TextFormat) -> Vec<u8> {
    // serde_json escapes newlines inside strings, so every '\n' it emits is a
    // line break and can be rewritten as one.
    let pretty = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(value).expect("serializing a serde_json::Value cannot fail");
    let eol: &[u8] = if fmt.crlf { b"\r\n" } else { b"\n" };
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(pretty.len() + pretty.len() / 16 + 8);
    if fmt.bom {
        out.extend_from_slice(&BOM);
    }
    for &b in &pretty {
        if b == b'\n' {
            out.extend_from_slice(eol);
        } else {
            out.push(b);
        }
    }
    if fmt.final_newline {
        out.extend_from_slice(eol);
    }
    out
}

/// Identifies the exact bytes a preview was computed from. FNV-1a is plenty:
/// the question is only "is this still the file I showed the user?". A missing
/// file has the fingerprint of no bytes.
pub fn fingerprint(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut hash: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for b in bytes {
        hash ^= *b as u64;
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x1000_0000_01b3);
    }
    format!("{hash:016x}")
}

/// Configs are short, so a plain O(n·m) LCS is the simplest honest diff.
pub fn unified_diff(before: &str, after: &str) -> String {
    let a: Vec<&str> = before.lines().collect();
    let b: Vec<&str> = after.lines().collect();
    let (n, m) = (a.len(), b.len());

    let mut lcs = vec![vec![0usize; m + 1]; n + 1];
    for i in (0..n).rev() {
        for j in (0..m).rev() {
            lcs[i][j] = if a[i] == b[j] {
                lcs[i + 1][j + 1] + 1
            } else {
                lcs[i + 1][j].max(lcs[i][j + 1])
            };
        }
    }

    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let (mut i, mut j) = (0usize, 0usize);
    while i < n && j < m {
        if a[i] == b[j] {
            out.push(format!("  {}", a[i]));
            i += 1;
            j += 1;
        } else if lcs[i + 1][j] >= lcs[i][j + 1] {
            out.push(format!("- {}", a[i]));
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(format!("+ {}", b[j]));
            j += 1;
        }
    }
    while i < n {
        out.push(format!("- {}", a[i]));
        i += 1;
    }
    while j < m {
        out.push(format!("+ {}", b[j]));
        j += 1;
    }

    // Keep three lines of context around each change so the panel stays readable.
    let changed: Vec<usize> = out
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, l)| l.starts_with('+') || l.starts_with('-'))
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .collect();
    if changed.is_empty() {
        return "No change.".into();
    }
    let mut keep = vec![false; out.len()];
    for idx in changed {
        let lo = idx.saturating_sub(3);
        let hi = (idx + 4).min(out.len());
        for k in lo..hi {
            keep[k] = true;
        }
    }
    let mut result = String::new();
    let mut gap = false;
    for (idx, line) in out.iter().enumerate() {
        if keep[idx] {
            result.push_str(line);
            result.push('\n');
            gap = false;
        } else if !gap {
            result.push_str("  …\n");
            gap = true;
        }
    }
    result
}

/// The raw bytes, or None when the file does not exist. Any other failure — a
/// lock, a permission problem — is an error: not knowing is not the same as empty.
pub fn read_config(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, String> {
    match std::fs::read(path) {
        Ok(bytes) => Ok(Some(bytes)),
        Err(err) if err.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
        Err(err) => Err(format!("Can't read {}: {err}", path.display())),
    }
}

/// `<config>.mayak-backup-<stamp>`, next to the config.
pub fn backup_path(config: &Path, stamp: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let mut name = config.as_os_str().to_os_string();
    name.push(format!(".{}-backup-{stamp}", ident::APP_SLUG));
    PathBuf::from(name)
}

/// Local time down to the second, "YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS".
pub fn local_stamp() -> String {
    let t = unsafe { GetLocalTime() };
    format!(
        "{:04}{:02}{:02}-{:02}{:02}{:02}",
        t.wYear, t.wMonth, t.wDay, t.wHour, t.wMinute, t.wSecond
    )
}

/// `<config>.<ext>.mayak-<pid>`: next to the target, so the rename stays on one volume.
fn temp_path(config: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let ext = config.extension().map(|e| e.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();
    let suffix = format!("{}-{}", ident::APP_SLUG, std::process::id());
    if ext.is_empty() {
        config.with_extension(suffix)
    } else {
        config.with_extension(format!("{ext}.{suffix}"))
    }
}

/// What `hooks_preview` showed, kept in Rust until `hooks_apply`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PendingPlan {
    pub target: Target,
    pub install: bool,
    pub path: PathBuf,
    /// Of the bytes the plan was computed from (`fingerprint(b"")` for a missing file).
    pub fingerprint: String,
    /// Exactly what will be written.
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
    pub backup_path: PathBuf,
    /// The file already holds `next`: nothing will be written.
    pub unchanged: bool,
}

/// Plan, diff text and notes for writing `next` over `current` (D53, D54).
pub fn make_plan(
    target: Target,
    install: bool,
    path: &Path,
    current: Option<&[u8]>,
    next: &Value,
    stamp: &str,
) -> (PendingPlan, String, Vec<String>) {
    let before = current.unwrap_or_default();
    // Structural: serde_json maps compare without key order and arrays by
    // position (which is what Codex trust follows), so the same entry in a file
    // with other indentation or line endings is not a write.
    let unchanged = match current {
        Some(bytes) => parse_object(bytes, "").map_or(false, |v| v == *next),
        None => next.as_object().map_or(false, |o| o.is_empty()),
    };
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    let (bytes, diff) = if unchanged {
        (before.to_vec(), "No change.".to_string())
    } else {
        let fmt = current.map(detect_format).unwrap_or(TextFormat::NEW_FILE);
        if fmt.mixed_eol {
            // BOM and final newline are kept, so this is the one byte change the
            // line diff cannot show.
            let style = if fmt.crlf { "CRLF" } else { "LF" };
            notes.push(format!("Line endings will be normalised to {style}."));
        }
        let bytes = render(next, fmt);
        let diff = unified_diff(
            &String::from_utf8_lossy(strip_bom(before)),
            &String::from_utf8_lossy(strip_bom(&bytes)),
        );
        (bytes, diff)
    };
    let plan = PendingPlan {
        target,
        install,
        path: path.to_path_buf(),
        fingerprint: fingerprint(before),
        bytes,
        backup_path: backup_path(path, stamp),
        unchanged,
    };
    (plan, diff, notes)
}

/// One pending plan per target, between preview and apply.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Plans(Mutex<HashMap<Target, PendingPlan>>);

impl Plans {
    /// Replaces the plan of that target.
    pub fn store(&self, plan: PendingPlan) {
        self.lock().insert(plan.target, plan);
    }

    /// Removes and returns the plan only if target, install and fingerprint all
    /// match what the user previewed; otherwise the stored plan stays and
    /// nothing is returned.
    pub fn take(&self, target: Target, install: bool, fingerprint: &str) -> Result<PendingPlan, String> {
        let mut plans = self.lock();
        let matches = match plans.get(&target) {
            None => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "There is no {} preview to apply. Open the preview again.",
                    target.as_str()
                ))
            }
            Some(plan) => plan.install == install && plan.fingerprint == fingerprint,
        };
        if !matches {
            return Err(format!(
                "This doesn't match the last {} preview. Nothing was written — open the preview again.",
                target.as_str()
            ));
        }
        plans
            .remove(&target)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("There is no {} preview to apply.", target.as_str()))
    }

    fn lock(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, HashMap<Target, PendingPlan>> {
        // Every operation under this lock is one insert or one remove, so a
        // poisoned lock cannot hold a half-updated map.
        self.0.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())
    }
}

/// Writes a previewed plan. Ok(backup path), or Ok("") only when there was no
/// previous file (so nothing to back up).
pub fn write_plan(plan: &PendingPlan) -> Result<String, String> {
    let path = &plan.path;
    // Read again: what is on disk now is what must match the preview and what
    // the backup must hold.
    let current = read_config(path)?;
    if fingerprint(current.as_deref().unwrap_or_default()) != plan.fingerprint {
        return Err(format!(
            "{} changed since the preview. Nothing was written — review the new diff.",
            path.display()
        ));
    }
    if plan.unchanged {
        return Err(format!(
            "No change: {} already has this entry; nothing was written.",
            path.display()
        ));
    }
    if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(|e| format!("Can't create {}: {e}", dir.display()))?;
    }
    let backup = match &current {
        Some(bytes) => {
            write_new(&plan.backup_path, bytes).map_err(|e| {
                format!(
                    "Backup to {} failed ({e}). Nothing was written.",
                    plan.backup_path.display()
                )
            })?;
            plan.backup_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
        }
        None => String::new(),
    };
    // Write beside the target, flush, and rename over it: a crash, a power loss
    // or a full disk leaves the original intact rather than half a file.
    let temp = temp_path(path);
    if let Err(err) = write_synced(&temp, &plan.bytes) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&temp);
        return Err(format!("write failed: {err}"));
    }
    if let Err(err) = std::fs::rename(&temp, path) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&temp);
        return Err(format!("write failed: {err}"));
    }
    Ok(backup)
}

/// Creates `path` and writes `bytes`. An existing file is an error, never
/// overwritten: a second backup in the same second must not replace the first.
fn write_new(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(path)?;
    file.write_all(bytes)?;
    file.sync_all()
}

/// Creates or truncates `path`, writes `bytes` and flushes them to disk before
/// returning, so the rename that follows can never put a file whose data is
/// not on disk yet in place of the config.
fn write_synced(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create(true).truncate(true).open(path)?;
    file.write_all(bytes)?;
    file.sync_all()
}
```

```rust
            (r"C:x\y", "absolute path"),
            (r"C:\", "empty folder name"),
            (r"C:\a\\b", "empty folder name"),
            (r"C:\a\", "empty folder name"),
        ] {
            let err = check_command_path(bad).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains(why), "{bad}: expected {why} in: {err}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_file_becomes_one_group_per_event() {
        let next = merge_install(&json!({}), OUR).unwrap();
        let events = next["hooks"].as_object().unwrap();
        let names: Vec<&str> = events.keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["UserPromptSubmit", "PermissionRequest", "Stop", "Interrupt", "SessionEnd"]);
        for (name, timeout) in CODEX_EVENTS {
            assert_eq!(event(&next, name), &vec![our_group(OUR, *timeout)]);
        }
        assert_eq!(
            our_group(OUR, 2),
            json!({ "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": OUR, "timeout": 2 } ] })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_string(&our_group("c", 10)).unwrap(),
            r#"{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"c","timeout":10}]}"#,
            "key order is part of what the user reviews"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn install_appends_after_foreign_groups_and_keeps_their_indices() {
        let current = json!({
            "description": "mine",
            "hooks": {
                "Stop": [ foreign("a.exe"), foreign("b.exe") ],
                "PreToolUse": [ foreign("c.exe") ]
            }
        });
        let next = merge_install(&current, OUR).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(next["description"], "mine");
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "Stop"), &vec![foreign("a.exe"), foreign("b.exe"), our_group(OUR, 10)]);
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "PreToolUse"), &vec![foreign("c.exe")]);
        // Existing event keys keep their place; new ones follow.
        let names: Vec<&str> = next["hooks"].as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["Stop", "PreToolUse", "UserPromptSubmit", "PermissionRequest", "Interrupt", "SessionEnd"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn reinstall_replaces_our_group_in_place_and_placeholders_duplicates() {
        let old = r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local\Mayak\bin\mayak-hook.exe --agent codex --old";
        let current = json!({ "hooks": { "Stop": [
            foreign("a.exe"),
            json!({ "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": old, "timeout": 99 } ] }),
            foreign("b.exe"),
            json!({ "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": old } ] }),
            foreign("c.exe")
        ] } });
        let next = merge_install(&current, OUR).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            event(&next, "Stop"),
            &vec![foreign("a.exe"), our_group(OUR, 10), foreign("b.exe"), json!({ "hooks": [] }), foreign("c.exe")]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reinstalling_the_same_command_changes_nothing() {
        let once = merge_install(&json!({ "hooks": { "Stop": [ foreign("a.exe") ] } }), OUR).unwrap();
        let twice = merge_install(&once, OUR).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(twice, once);
        assert!(installed(&once, OUR));
    }

    #[test]
    fn our_groups_outside_the_event_set_are_cleaned_on_install() {
        // D55: a group of ours under an event Mayak no longer installs.
        let installed_now = merge_install(&json!({}), OUR).unwrap();
        let mut current = installed_now.clone();
        current["hooks"]["PreToolUse"] = json!([ foreign("a.exe"), our_group(OUR, 10) ]);
        current["hooks"]["PostToolUse"] = json!([ our_group(OUR, 10), foreign("b.exe") ]);
        current["hooks"]["SubagentStop"] = json!([ our_group(OUR, 10) ]);

        let next = merge_install(&current, OUR).unwrap();
        assert_ne!(next, current, "so status reports outdated");
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "PreToolUse"), &vec![foreign("a.exe")]);
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "PostToolUse"), &vec![json!({ "hooks": [] }), foreign("b.exe")]);
        assert!(next["hooks"].get("SubagentStop").is_none());
        assert_eq!(merge_install(&next, OUR).unwrap(), next);
    }

    #[test]
    fn uninstall_removes_a_last_group_and_placeholders_the_others() {
        let current = json!({ "description": "d", "hooks": {
            "Stop": [ foreign("a.exe"), our_group(OUR, 10) ],
            "UserPromptSubmit": [ our_group(OUR, 10), foreign("b.exe") ],
            "SessionEnd": [ our_group(OUR, 2) ],
            "Interrupt": [ foreign("c.exe"), our_group(OUR, 2), our_group(OUR, 2) ],
            "PreCompact": []
        } });
        let next = merge_uninstall(&current, OUR).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "Stop"), &vec![foreign("a.exe")]);
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "UserPromptSubmit"), &vec![json!({ "hooks": [] }), foreign("b.exe")]);
        assert!(next["hooks"].get("SessionEnd").is_none(), "an array we emptied goes");
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "Interrupt"), &vec![foreign("c.exe")]);
        assert_eq!(event(&next, "PreCompact"), &Vec::<Value>::new(), "an array we did not touch stays");
        assert!(!installed(&next, OUR));

        let only_ours = merge_install(&json!({}), OUR).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(merge_uninstall(&only_ours, OUR).unwrap(), json!({ "hooks": {} }), "\"hooks\" is kept");
        assert_eq!(merge_uninstall(&json!({}), OUR).unwrap(), json!({}));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_top_level_keys_and_wrong_shapes_are_refused() {
        let unknown = json!({ "hooks": {}, "state": {} });
        let err = merge_install(&unknown, OUR).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("\"state\""), "got: {err}");
        assert!(merge_uninstall(&unknown, OUR).is_err());

        assert!(merge_install(&json!({ "hooks": [] }), OUR).unwrap_err().contains("\"hooks\" isn't an object"));
        assert!(merge_install(&json!({ "hooks": { "Stop": {} } }), OUR).unwrap_err().contains("\"Stop\""));
        assert!(check_shape(&json!([])).is_err());
        assert_eq!(check_shape(&json!({ "description": "x" })), Ok(()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn ours_is_the_marker_or_the_exact_short_command() {
        assert!(is_ours(r"C:\X\MAYAK-HOOK.EXE --agent codex", OUR));
        let short = r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local\Mayak\bin\MAYAK-~1.EXE --agent codex";
        assert!(is_ours(&short.to_lowercase(), short), "8.3 name: equal ignoring ASCII case");
        assert!(!is_ours(r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local\Mayak\bin\MAYAK-~2.EXE --agent codex", short));
        assert!(!is_ours("someone-elses-tool.exe", OUR));
        assert!(!is_ours("", ""), "an empty command is never ours by equality");
        assert!(!group_is_ours(&json!({ "hooks": [] }), OUR), "a placeholder is not ours");
    }

    fn place_relay(tmp: &TempDir) -> PathBuf {
        let bin = tmp.path.join("bin");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin).unwrap();
        let exe = bin.join(ident::HOOK_EXE);
        std::fs::write(&exe, b"relay").unwrap();
        exe
    }

    #[test]
    fn short_path_resolves_an_existing_file_and_fails_on_a_missing_one() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("codex-short");

        assert!(Path::new(&short).is_file(), "{short} must name the same file");
        assert!(short_path(&tmp.path.join("bin").join("missing.exe")).is_err());
    }

        assert_eq!(check_command_path(path), Ok(()));

        assert!(our_command(&tmp.path.join("nope.exe")).is_err());

    #[test]
    fn installed_at_reads_the_file_and_treats_problems_as_not_installed() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("codex-installed");
        let home = tmp.path.join(".codex");
        assert!(!installed_at(&home, Some(OUR)), "no folder, no file");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&home).unwrap();
        let path = hooks_json_path(&home);
        assert_eq!(path, home.join("hooks.json"));

        std::fs::write(&path, b"{ broken").unwrap();
        assert!(!installed_at(&home, Some(OUR)));

        let with_ours = merge_install(&json!({}), OUR).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&with_ours).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(installed_at(&home, Some(OUR)));
        assert!(installed_at(&home, None), "the marker alone is enough");

        let short = r"C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local\Mayak\bin\MAYAK-~1.EXE --agent codex";
        std::fs::write(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&merge_install(&json!({}), short).unwrap()).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(installed_at(&home, Some(short)));
        assert!(!installed_at(&home, None), "an 8.3 command needs the current command to be recognised");
    }
}
```

Insert this at the top of `windows/src-tauri/src/codex_hooks.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]` (one blank line between them):

```rust
// Optional Codex integration: Mayak's groups in ~/.codex/hooks.json (spec §8).
//
// Codex trusts user hooks by position (<file>:<event>:<group index>:<handler
// index>) and by a hash of command/timeout/matcher/statusMessage, so the merge
// never moves anybody else's group: install appends at the end of the event's
// array, reinstall replaces our group in place, uninstall removes our group only
// when it is last and otherwise leaves the placeholder {"hooks":[]}. Our group
// carries only type/command/timeout, and the command never changes between
// Mayak versions, so a reinstall keeps the user's Trust.
//
// The command is the relay's absolute path without quotes plus "--agent codex".
// Codex runs it through `powershell -Command` or `cmd /C`, so the path must mean
// the same to both: it is shortened with GetShortPathNameW and then checked
// against an allow-list. Codex 0.144/0.146 reject unknown top-level keys
// (deny_unknown_fields), so a file with anything but "description" and "hooks"
// at the top is refused rather than "fixed".

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde_json::{json, Map, Value};
use windows::core::PCWSTR;
use windows::Win32::Storage::FileSystem::GetShortPathNameW;

use crate::hookfile;
use crate::ident;

/// Events Mayak installs, with the hook timeout in seconds.
pub const CODEX_EVENTS: &[(&str, u64)] = &[
    ("UserPromptSubmit", 10),
    ("PermissionRequest", 10),
    ("Stop", 10),
    ("Interrupt", 2),
    ("SessionEnd", 2),
];

const TOP_LEVEL_KEYS: &[&str] = &["description", "hooks"];

pub fn hooks_json_path(codex_home: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    codex_home.join("hooks.json")
}

/// GetShortPathNameW. Fails when the file does not exist.
pub fn short_path(long: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;

    let wide: Vec<u16> = long.as_os_str().encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect();
    let mut buf = vec![0u16; 260];
    loop {
        // SAFETY: `wide` is NUL-terminated and outlives the call; the output
        // slice is passed with its own length.
        let n = unsafe { GetShortPathNameW(PCWSTR(wide.as_ptr()), Some(&mut buf)) } as usize;
        if n == 0 {
            return Err(format!(
                "Can't resolve the short path of {}: {}",
                long.display(),
                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
            ));
        }
        if n < buf.len() {
            // Success: n characters, without the terminating NUL.
            buf.truncate(n);
            return String::from_utf16(&buf)
                .map_err(|_| format!("The short path of {} isn't valid UTF-16.", long.display()));
        }
        // Too small: n is the size needed, NUL included.
        buf.resize(n, 0);
    }
}

/// `^[A-Za-z]:(\\[\p{L}\p{N}._~-]+)+$`, with `char::is_alphabetic` for \p{L} and
/// `char::is_numeric` for \p{N} (D29).
pub fn check_command_path(path: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let refuse = |why: String| -> Result<(), String> {
        Err(format!(
            "{path} can't be used as a Codex hook command: {why}. The relay path must be a drive \
             letter followed by folder names made only of letters, digits, '.', '_', '~' and '-'."
        ))
    };
    let mut chars = path.chars();
    match (chars.next(), chars.next()) {
        (Some(drive), Some(':')) if drive.is_ascii_alphabetic() => {}
        _ => return refuse("it doesn't start with a drive letter".into()),
    }
    let Some(rest) = chars.as_str().strip_prefix('\\') else {
        return refuse("it isn't an absolute path".into());
    };
    for segment in rest.split('\\') {
        if segment.is_empty() {
            return refuse("it has an empty folder name".into());
        }
        let bad = segment
            .chars()
            .find(|c| !(c.is_alphabetic() || c.is_numeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '_' | '~' | '-')));
        if let Some(c) = bad {
            let shown = if c == ' ' { "a space".to_string() } else { format!("'{c}'") };
            return refuse(format!("it contains {shown}"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The command written into hooks.json: "<short relay path> --agent codex".
pub fn our_command(hook_exe: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let short = short_path(hook_exe)?;
    check_command_path(&short)?;
    Ok(format!("{short} --agent codex"))
}

/// One group per event; no matcher, statusMessage, commandWindows or async, so
/// the trust hash covers as little as possible.
pub fn our_group(command: &str, timeout: u64) -> Value {
    json!({ "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": command, "timeout": timeout } ] })
}

fn placeholder() -> Value {
    json!({ "hooks": [] })
}

/// Top level holds only "description" and "hooks"; "hooks" is an object whose
/// values are arrays.
pub fn check_shape(v: &Value) -> Result<(), String> {
    let Some(root) = v.as_object() else {
        return Err(format!("hooks.json isn't a JSON object — {} won't touch it.", ident::APP_NAME));
    };
    if let Some(key) = root.keys().find(|k| !TOP_LEVEL_KEYS.contains(&k.as_str())) {
        return Err(format!(
            "hooks.json has the top-level key \"{key}\". Codex only accepts \"description\" and \
             \"hooks\" there, so {} won't touch it.",
            ident::APP_NAME
        ));
    }
    match root.get("hooks") {
        None => Ok(()),
        Some(Value::Object(events)) => match events.iter().find(|(_, list)| !list.is_array()) {
            Some((event, _)) => Err(format!(
                "hooks.json: \"{event}\" isn't a list of hook groups — {} won't touch it.",
                ident::APP_NAME
            )),
            None => Ok(()),
        },
        Some(_) => Err(format!(
            "hooks.json: \"hooks\" isn't an object — {} won't touch it.",
            ident::APP_NAME
        )),
    }
}

/// Ours: the marker anywhere in the command (case-insensitive), or exactly our
/// current command ignoring ASCII case — GetShortPathNameW may have turned
/// "mayak-hook.exe" into an 8.3 name (D30). An empty `our_command` matches by
/// marker only.
pub fn is_ours(command: &str, our_command: &str) -> bool {
    command.to_lowercase().contains(ident::MARKER)
        || (!our_command.is_empty() && command.eq_ignore_ascii_case(our_command))
}

pub fn group_is_ours(group: &Value, our_command: &str) -> bool {
    group.get("hooks").and_then(Value::as_array).map_or(false, |handlers| {
        handlers.iter().any(|h| {
            h.get("command")
                .and_then(Value::as_str)
                .map_or(false, |c| is_ours(c, our_command))
        })
    })
}

pub fn installed(v: &Value, our_command: &str) -> bool {
    v.get("hooks").and_then(Value::as_object).map_or(false, |events| {
        events
            .values()
            .filter_map(Value::as_array)
            .flatten()
            .any(|g| group_is_ours(g, our_command))
    })
}

fn is_codex_event(event: &str) -> bool {
    CODEX_EVENTS.iter().any(|(name, _)| *name == event)
}

/// Uninstall rule for one event list: trailing groups of ours are removed, any
/// other group of ours becomes a placeholder, so no foreign group changes index.
fn remove_ours(list: &mut Vec<Value>, our_command: &str) -> bool {
    let mut changed = false;
    while list.last().map_or(false, |g| group_is_ours(g, our_command)) {
        list.pop();
        changed = true;
    }
    for group in list.iter_mut() {
        if group_is_ours(group, our_command) {
            *group = placeholder();
            changed = true;
        }
    }
    changed
}

/// Applies `remove_ours` to one event; a list it leaves empty takes its key
/// with it (key order of the other events kept).
fn uninstall_event(events: &mut Map<String, Value>, event: &str, our_command: &str) {
    let Some(Value::Array(list)) = events.get_mut(event) else { return };
    if remove_ours(list, our_command) && list.is_empty() {
        events.shift_remove(event);
    }
}

/// Install / reinstall. Missing file → call with `{}`.
pub fn merge_install(current: &Value, our_command: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    check_shape(current)?;
    let mut root = current.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let mut events = root.get("hooks").and_then(Value::as_object).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    for (event, timeout) in CODEX_EVENTS {
        let mut list = match events.get(*event) {
            Some(Value::Array(list)) => list.clone(),
            _ => Vec::new(),
        };
        // First group of ours is replaced in place; any further one becomes a
        // placeholder; none → append. Placeholders are never reused (D31).
        let mut placed = false;
        for group in list.iter_mut() {
            if group_is_ours(group, our_command) {
                *group = if placed { placeholder() } else { our_group(our_command, *timeout) };
                placed = true;
            }
        }
        if !placed {
            list.push(our_group(our_command, *timeout));
        }
        events.insert((*event).to_string(), Value::Array(list));
    }
    // Groups of ours under events Mayak no longer installs (e.g. after the
    // default set shrinks) get the uninstall rule (D55).
    let stale: Vec<String> = events.keys().filter(|k| !is_codex_event(k)).cloned().collect();
    for event in stale {
        uninstall_event(&mut events, &event, our_command);
    }
    root.insert("hooks".into(), Value::Object(events));
    Ok(Value::Object(root))
}

/// Uninstall. "hooks" stays even when it ends up empty (D31).
pub fn merge_uninstall(current: &Value, our_command: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    check_shape(current)?;
    let mut root = current.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    if let Some(Value::Object(events)) = root.get_mut("hooks") {
        let names: Vec<String> = events.keys().cloned().collect();
        for event in names {
            uninstall_event(events, &event, our_command);
        }
    }
    Ok(Value::Object(root))
}

/// Read-only status for `Signal::CodexHooksInstalled`. A missing, unreadable or
/// invalid file counts as not installed.
pub fn installed_at(codex_home: &Path, our_command: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    let path = hooks_json_path(codex_home);
    match hookfile::read_config(&path) {
        Ok(Some(bytes)) => hookfile::parse_object(&bytes, &path.display().to_string())
            .map_or(false, |v| installed(&v, our_command.unwrap_or(""))),
        Ok(None) | Err(_) => false,
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// The old filesystem test, now on a HookCtx in a temp dir instead of a
    /// process-wide USERPROFILE.
    #[test]
    fn writing_backs_up_preserves_and_refuses_a_changed_file() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("hooks-claude");
        let ctx = ctx_in(&tmp);
        place_relay(&ctx);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&ctx.claude_dir).unwrap();
        let path = ctx.claude_dir.join("settings.json");

        // A real-shaped file, written the way PowerShell 5 would: UTF-8 with BOM,
        // on one line, without a final newline.
        let original = r#"{"model":"claude-opus-5","theme":"dark","tui":{"x":1},"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"other-tool.exe"}]}]}}"#;
        let mut bytes = vec![0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF];
        bytes.extend_from_slice(original.as_bytes());
        std::fs::write(&path, &bytes).unwrap();

        // Install.
        let plan = preview(&ctx, Target::Claude, true, STAMP).expect("a BOM must not stop the preview");
        assert!(plan.diff.contains(ident::MARKER), "the diff must show what changes");
        assert!(!plan.unchanged);
        let backup = apply(&ctx, Target::Claude, true, &plan.fingerprint).expect("install should succeed");

        // The backup holds the original bytes, BOM and all, next to the file.
        assert_eq!(backup, ctx.claude_dir.join("settings.json.mayak-backup-20261001-120000").to_string_lossy());
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&backup).unwrap(), bytes);

        // The format survived: BOM kept, no CRLF invented, still no final newline.
        let written = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        assert!(written.starts_with(&[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF]));
        assert!(!written.windows(2).any(|w| w == b"\r\n"));
        assert!(!written.ends_with(b"\n"));

        // Everything else survived, and so did the other tool's hook.
        let after = hookfile::parse_object(&written, "settings.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(after["model"], "claude-opus-5");
        assert_eq!(after["theme"], "dark");
        assert_eq!(after["tui"]["x"], 1);
        let pre = after["hooks"]["PreToolUse"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert!(pre.iter().any(|e| serde_json::to_string(e).unwrap().contains("other-tool.exe")));
        let st = status(&ctx, Target::Claude);
        assert!(st.installed && !st.outdated && st.hook_ready);
        assert_eq!(st.settings_path, path.to_string_lossy());

        // A file that moved since the preview is refused, and left alone.
        let stale = preview(&ctx, Target::Claude, false, "20261001-120001").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(&path, br#"{"model":"someone-else-edited-this"}"#).unwrap();
        let err = apply(&ctx, Target::Claude, false, &stale.fingerprint).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("changed since the preview"), "got: {err}");
        let untouched = hookfile::parse_object(&std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), "s").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(untouched["model"], "someone-else-edited-this");

        // Content we cannot parse is refused before anything is written.
        std::fs::write(&path, b"{ broken").unwrap();
        assert!(preview(&ctx, Target::Claude, true, STAMP).is_err());
        assert!(apply(&ctx, Target::Claude, true, "whatever").is_err());
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), b"{ broken");
        let st = status(&ctx, Target::Claude);
        assert!(!st.installed && st.notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("isn't valid JSON")));
    }

    fn codex_install_reinstall_and_remove_through_the_plan() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("hooks-codex");

        let path = codex_hooks::hooks_json_path(&ctx.codex_home);
        let our = codex_hooks::our_command(&ctx.hook_exe).unwrap();

        let st = status(&ctx, Target::Codex);
        assert!(!st.installed && !st.outdated && st.hook_ready, "{st:?}");
        assert!(st.notes.is_empty(), "{:?}", st.notes);
        assert_eq!(st.settings_path, path.to_string_lossy());

        // No file yet: shown whole, written in the new-file format, no backup.
        let install = preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, STAMP).unwrap();
        assert!(!install.unchanged);
        assert!(install.diff.lines().all(|l| l.starts_with("+ ")), "{}", install.diff);
        assert_eq!(apply(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, &install.fingerprint), Ok(String::new()));
        let written = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        let expected = codex_hooks::merge_install(&json!({}), &our).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(written, hookfile::render(&expected, hookfile::TextFormat::NEW_FILE));
        let shown: Vec<&str> = install.diff.lines().map(|l| &l[2..]).collect();
        assert_eq!(shown, String::from_utf8_lossy(&written).lines().collect::<Vec<_>>(), "diff = written bytes");
        assert!(codex_hooks::installed_at(&ctx.codex_home, Some(&our)));
        let st = status(&ctx, Target::Codex);
        assert!(st.installed && !st.outdated);

        // Reinstall of the identical entry: nothing to write (D53).
        let again = preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, "20261001-120001").unwrap();
        assert!(again.unchanged);
        assert_eq!(again.diff, "No change.");
        let err = apply(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, &again.fingerprint).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.starts_with("No change:"), "got: {err}");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), written);

        // Remove: backup of the exact bytes; "hooks" stays as an empty object.
        let removal = preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, false, "20261001-120002").unwrap();
        let backup = apply(&ctx, Target::Codex, false, &removal.fingerprint).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&backup).unwrap(), written);
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), b"{\n  \"hooks\": {}\n}\n".to_vec());
        assert!(!codex_hooks::installed_at(&ctx.codex_home, Some(&our)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn codex_refuses_bad_files_and_a_missing_relay() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("hooks-codex-bad");
        let ctx = ctx_in(&tmp);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&ctx.codex_home).unwrap();
        let path = codex_hooks::hooks_json_path(&ctx.codex_home);

        // No relay: install is refused, status explains, and removal finds a
        // long-name command by the marker alone.
        let st = status(&ctx, Target::Codex);
        assert!(!st.hook_ready && st.notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("not in place")), "{st:?}");
        assert!(preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, STAMP).is_err());
        let ours = json!({ "hooks": { "Stop": [codex_hooks::our_group(r"C:\x\mayak-hook.exe --agent codex", 10)] } });
        std::fs::write(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&ours).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let removal = preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, false, STAMP).unwrap();
        assert!(removal.diff.contains("mayak-hook.exe"));

        // An 8.3 command has no marker: without the relay it can't be recognised,
        // and status and the Remove preview say so instead of a bare "No change.".
        let short = json!({ "hooks": { "Stop": [codex_hooks::our_group(r"C:\x\MAYAK-~1.EXE --agent codex", 10)] } });
        std::fs::write(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&short).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let blind = preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, false, STAMP).unwrap();
        assert!(blind.unchanged, "{}", blind.diff);
        assert!(blind.notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("short (8.3) path")), "{:?}", blind.notes);
        let st = status(&ctx, Target::Codex);
        assert!(!st.installed && st.notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("short (8.3) path")), "{st:?}");

        place_relay(&ctx);
        std::fs::write(&path, br#"{"hooks":{},"state":{}}"#).unwrap();
        let err = preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, STAMP).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("\"state\""), "got: {err}");
        assert!(status(&ctx, Target::Codex).notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("\"state\"")));

        std::fs::write(&path, b"{ nope").unwrap();
        assert!(preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, STAMP).unwrap_err().contains("isn't valid JSON"));
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), b"{ nope");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_target_and_unknown_fingerprint_are_refused() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("hooks-refuse");
        let ctx = ctx_in(&tmp);
        place_relay(&ctx);
        assert!(Target::parse(Some("vscode")).is_err());
        assert!(apply(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, "0000000000000000").is_err(), "nothing previewed");

        let p = preview(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, STAMP).unwrap();
        assert!(apply(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, "0000000000000000").is_err(), "wrong fingerprint");
        assert!(apply(&ctx, Target::Claude, true, &p.fingerprint).is_err(), "other target");
        assert!(apply(&ctx, Target::Codex, false, &p.fingerprint).is_err(), "other direction");
        assert!(!codex_hooks::hooks_json_path(&ctx.codex_home).exists(), "nothing was written");
        assert!(apply(&ctx, Target::Codex, true, &p.fingerprint).is_ok(), "the matching plan still applies");
    }
}
```
