- [ ] **Step 19: Rewrite the implementation**

In `windows/src-tauri/src/hooks.rs`, replace everything above `#[cfg(test)]` (the old header comment, `HOOK_EVENTS`, `MARKER`, `HookStatus`, `HookPreview`, `home`, `settings_path`, `read_settings*`, `parse_settings`, `hook_command`, `entry_is_ours`, `merged`, `without_ours`, `pretty`, `stamp`, `backup_path`, `fingerprint`, `current_fingerprint`, `status`, `preview`, `write`, `ensure_hook_exe`, `unified_diff`) with:

```rust
// Hook installers (spec §8), one per target, both on the write protection in
// hookfile.rs:
// - "codex": Mayak's groups in ~/.codex/hooks.json (codex_hooks.rs), optional;
// - "claude": the legacy Allow/Deny relay in ~/.claude/settings.json, under
//   Advanced and off by default. It installs PermissionRequest only; status and
//   removal also recognise what an old Coucou install left there.
//
// Nothing here runs at app start: a tool config is read only when the settings
// window asks for a status, a preview or an apply. Writes happen only from an
// explicit click on a diff the user has seen.
//
// The Claude command is only the quoted exe path in forward slashes plus the
// event name: on Windows Claude Code runs hook commands through Git Bash, and
// anything with PowerShell or cmd in it breaks.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::{json, Map, Value};
use tauri::{AppHandle, Manager};

use crate::codex_hooks;
use crate::hookfile::{self, Plans, Target};
use crate::ident;
use crate::settings;

/// Legacy Claude target. PermissionRequest waits for a human, so it gets the
/// island's decision timeout + 10 s.
pub const CLAUDE_EVENTS: &[(&str, u64)] = &[("PermissionRequest", 120)];

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct HookStatus {
    pub target: Target,
    pub installed: bool,
    /// Installed, but an install now would change the file.
    pub outdated: bool,
    /// Config path of the target (settings.json or hooks.json); the name is kept
    /// from the single-target days.
    pub settings_path: String,
    pub hook_path: String,
    pub hook_ready: bool,
    pub notes: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct HookPreview {
    pub diff: String,
    pub backup: String,
    pub settings_path: String,
    /// Handed back to apply, so only the reviewed bytes are ever written.
    pub fingerprint: String,
    pub notes: Vec<String>,
    /// The file already holds exactly this; Apply has nothing to write (D53).
    pub unchanged: bool,
}

/// What the installer works on. Built once in lib.rs from `app_paths()`; tests
/// point it at a temp directory.
pub struct HookCtx {
    pub claude_dir: PathBuf,
    pub codex_home: PathBuf,
    pub hook_exe: PathBuf,
    pub plans: Plans,
}

fn config_path(ctx: &HookCtx, target: Target) -> PathBuf {
    match target {
        Target::Claude => ctx.claude_dir.join("settings.json"),
        Target::Codex => codex_hooks::hooks_json_path(&ctx.codex_home),
    }
}

// ── Legacy Claude target ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn hook_command(exe: &Path, event: &str) -> String {
    let exe = exe.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
    format!("\"{exe}\" {event}")
}

fn entry_has_command(entry: &Value, pred: impl Fn(&str) -> bool) -> bool {
    entry
        .get("hooks")
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .map_or(false, |hooks| {
            hooks
                .iter()
                .any(|h| h.get("command").and_then(Value::as_str).map_or(false, &pred))
        })
}

/// Ours: Mayak's marker, or the marker an older build of this app wrote.
fn entry_is_ours(entry: &Value) -> bool {
    entry_has_command(entry, |c| {
        c.contains(ident::MARKER) || ident::LEGACY_MARKERS.iter().any(|m| c.contains(m))
    })
}

fn entry_is_legacy(entry: &Value) -> bool {
    entry_has_command(entry, |c| ident::LEGACY_MARKERS.iter().any(|m| c.contains(m)))
}

fn any_entry(settings: &Value, pred: fn(&Value) -> bool) -> bool {
    settings
        .get("hooks")
        .and_then(Value::as_object)
        .map_or(false, |hooks| hooks.values().filter_map(Value::as_array).flatten().any(pred))
}

fn is_claude_event(event: &str) -> bool {
    CLAUDE_EVENTS.iter().any(|(name, _)| *name == event)
}

/// Every event list without our (or Coucou's) entries. A list we emptied goes,
/// unless `keep_empty(event)`: install keeps its own events' keys in place. A
/// list that was empty already is the user's and stays.
fn strip_ours(hooks: &Map<String, Value>, keep_empty: fn(&str) -> bool) -> Map<String, Value> {
    let mut out = Map::new();
    for (event, value) in hooks {
        match value.as_array() {
            Some(list) => {
                let kept: Vec<Value> = list.iter().filter(|e| !entry_is_ours(e)).cloned().collect();
                let emptied_by_us = kept.is_empty() && !list.is_empty();
                if !emptied_by_us || keep_empty(event) {
                    out.insert(event.clone(), Value::Array(kept));
                }
            }
            None => {
                out.insert(event.clone(), value.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Settings with only Mayak's PermissionRequest entry: every older entry of ours
/// (any event, Mayak or Coucou) is removed first; everything else is untouched.
fn merged(existing: &Value, exe: &Path) -> Value {
    let mut root = existing.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let current = root.get("hooks").and_then(Value::as_object).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let mut hooks = strip_ours(&current, is_claude_event);
    for (event, timeout) in CLAUDE_EVENTS {
        let mut list = hooks.get(*event).and_then(Value::as_array).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        list.push(json!({
            "hooks": [{
                "type": "command",
                "command": hook_command(exe, event),
                "timeout": timeout,
            }]
        }));
        hooks.insert((*event).to_string(), Value::Array(list));
    }
    root.insert("hooks".into(), Value::Object(hooks));
    Value::Object(root)
}

/// Settings with every entry of ours (Mayak or Coucou) removed, and nothing else changed.
fn without_ours(existing: &Value) -> Value {
    let mut root = existing.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let Some(hooks) = root.get("hooks").and_then(Value::as_object) else {
        return Value::Object(root);
    };
    let out = strip_ours(hooks, |_| false);
    if out.is_empty() && !hooks.is_empty() {
        // We emptied every event list, so "hooks" goes too; a "hooks": {} that
        // was empty already stays. shift_remove keeps the order of the user's
        // other keys.
        root.shift_remove("hooks");
    } else {
        root.insert("hooks".into(), Value::Object(out));
    }
    Value::Object(root)
}

// ── Shared ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// The config as an object (`{}` when the file is missing), or None with the
/// reason in `notes`.
fn read_value(path: &Path, notes: &mut Vec<String>) -> Option<Value> {
    match hookfile::read_config(path) {
        Ok(None) => Some(json!({})),
        Ok(Some(bytes)) => match hookfile::parse_object(&bytes, &path.display().to_string()) {
            Ok(v) => Some(v),
            Err(err) => {
                notes.push(err);
                None
            }
        },
        Err(err) => {
            notes.push(err);
            None
        }
    }
}

fn claude_state(ctx: &HookCtx, path: &Path, notes: &mut Vec<String>) -> (bool, bool) {
    let Some(current) = read_value(path, notes) else { return (false, false) };
    if any_entry(&current, entry_is_legacy) {
        notes.push(format!(
            "{} still has hook entries from Coucou. Reinstall replaces them; Remove deletes them.",
            path.display()
        ));
    }
    let installed = any_entry(&current, entry_is_ours);
    let outdated = installed && merged(&current, &ctx.hook_exe) != current;
    (installed, outdated)
}

/// Without a usable relay there is no current command, and the marker alone
/// does not match a command GetShortPathNameW turned into an 8.3 name.
fn relay_unusable_note() -> String {
    format!(
        "{0}'s relay isn't available, so entries written with its short (8.3) path can't be \
         recognised. Restart {0} to restore the relay, then Remove.",
        ident::APP_NAME
    )
}

fn codex_state(ctx: &HookCtx, path: &Path, hook_ready: bool, notes: &mut Vec<String>) -> (bool, bool) {
    // Without the relay there is no short path to compute; the missing-relay
    // note is already there.
    let our = if hook_ready {
        match codex_hooks::our_command(&ctx.hook_exe) {
            Ok(cmd) => Some(cmd),
            Err(err) => {
                notes.push(err);
                None
            }
        }
    } else {
        None
    };
    if our.is_none() {
        notes.push(relay_unusable_note());
    }
    let Some(current) = read_value(path, notes) else { return (false, false) };
    if let Err(err) = codex_hooks::check_shape(&current) {
        notes.push(err);
    }
    let installed = codex_hooks::installed(&current, our.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
    let outdated = match &our {
        Some(cmd) if installed => {
            codex_hooks::merge_install(&current, cmd).map_or(false, |next| next != current)
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    (installed, outdated)
}

// ── Public API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Read-only. Never fails: problems become `notes`.
pub fn status(ctx: &HookCtx, target: Target) -> HookStatus {
    let path = config_path(ctx, target);
    let hook_ready = ctx.hook_exe.exists();
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    if !hook_ready {
        notes.push(format!(
            "The relay {} is not in place yet. Restart {}.",
            ctx.hook_exe.display(),
            ident::APP_NAME
        ));
    }
    let (installed, outdated) = match target {
        Target::Claude => claude_state(ctx, &path, &mut notes),
        Target::Codex => codex_state(ctx, &path, hook_ready, &mut notes),
    };
    HookStatus {
        target,
        installed,
        outdated,
        settings_path: path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        hook_path: ctx.hook_exe.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        hook_ready,
        notes,
    }
}

/// Computes the exact bytes an install (or removal) would write, keeps the plan
/// for `apply` and returns the diff to show. `stamp` names the backup.
pub fn preview(ctx: &HookCtx, target: Target, install: bool, stamp: &str) -> Result<HookPreview, String> {
    let path = config_path(ctx, target);
    let shown = path.display().to_string();
    let current_bytes = hookfile::read_config(&path)?;
    let current = match &current_bytes {
        Some(bytes) => hookfile::parse_object(bytes, &shown)?,
        None => json!({}),
    };
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    let next = match target {
        Target::Claude => {
            if any_entry(&current, entry_is_legacy) {
                notes.push("Hook entries from Coucou are removed too.".to_string());
            }
            if install {
                merged(&current, &ctx.hook_exe)
            } else {
                without_ours(&current)
            }
        }
        Target::Codex => {
            if install {
                codex_hooks::merge_install(&current, &codex_hooks::our_command(&ctx.hook_exe)?)?
            } else {
                // Without a usable relay the marker alone finds our groups,
                // which works for long-name commands only; the notes say so.
                let our = match codex_hooks::our_command(&ctx.hook_exe) {
                    Ok(cmd) => cmd,
                    Err(err) => {
                        notes.push(err);
                        notes.push(relay_unusable_note());
                        String::new()
                    }
                };
                codex_hooks::merge_uninstall(&current, &our)?
            }
        }
    };
    let (plan, diff, plan_notes) =
        hookfile::make_plan(target, install, &path, current_bytes.as_deref(), &next, stamp);
    notes.extend(plan_notes);
    let out = HookPreview {
        diff,
        backup: plan.backup_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        settings_path: shown,
        fingerprint: plan.fingerprint.clone(),
        notes,
        unchanged: plan.unchanged,
    };
    ctx.plans.store(plan);
    Ok(out)
}

/// Writes the plan the last preview of `target` stored, if `install` and
/// `fingerprint` match it. Ok(backup path), or Ok("") when there was no file.
pub fn apply(ctx: &HookCtx, target: Target, install: bool, fingerprint: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let plan = ctx.plans.take(target, install, fingerprint)?;
    hookfile::write_plan(&plan)
}

/// Copies the relay into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak\bin on launch.
/// In a bundled install it comes from the app resources; in `tauri dev` it sits
/// next to the app exe in the workspace target directory.
///
/// Every candidate is tried rather than just the first, because getting this
/// wrong is silent and fatal: `resources` used to be a glob, which made NSIS
/// mirror the source path into `_up_\target\release\`, no candidate matched, and
/// the relay was simply never installed. It only looked healthy on a developer
/// machine, where a leftover copy from `tauri dev` was already sitting in bin/.
pub fn ensure_hook_exe(app: &AppHandle) {
    let dest = settings::hook_exe_path();
    let Some(dir) = dest.parent() else { return };
    if std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).is_err() {
        return;
    }

    let mut candidates: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(p) = app.path().resolve(ident::HOOK_EXE, tauri::path::BaseDirectory::Resource) {
        candidates.push(p);
    }
    if let Ok(exe) = std::env::current_exe() {
        if let Some(parent) = exe.parent() {
            // Installed build, then `tauri dev` (target/debug) next to the
            // release hook the pre-build step produces.
            candidates.push(parent.join(ident::HOOK_EXE));
            candidates.push(parent.join("../release").join(ident::HOOK_EXE));
            // Belt and braces: where the old glob form used to land it.
            candidates.push(parent.join("_up_/target/release").join(ident::HOOK_EXE));
        }
    }

    let tried: Vec<String> = candidates.iter().map(|p| p.display().to_string()).collect();
    let Some(src) = candidates.into_iter().find(|p| p.exists()) else {
        crate::log::line(format!(
            "{} not found — hooks cannot work. Looked in: {}",
            ident::HOOK_EXE,
            tried.join(", ")
        ));
        return;
    };

    let same = match (std::fs::metadata(&src), std::fs::metadata(&dest)) {
        (Ok(a), Ok(b)) => a.len() == b.len() && a.modified().ok() == b.modified().ok(),
        _ => false,
    };
    if same {
        return;
    }
    // A hook may be running right now and hold the file open; keeping the old
    // copy is fine, it is the same relay.
    if let Err(err) = std::fs::copy(&src, &dest) {
        if !dest.exists() {
            crate::log::line(format!("could not install {}: {err}", ident::HOOK_EXE));
        }
    }
}
```

`ensure_hook_exe` keeps T1's behaviour: the resource, the exe's folder, `../release/` and `_up_/target/release/` candidates and both log messages are built from `ident::HOOK_EXE`. `unified_diff`, `fingerprint` and the BOM-tolerant parsing moved unchanged to `hookfile.rs`.

```rust
// ── Hook installers (spec §8) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// What the installer works on. `app_paths()` is the only reader of
/// CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME / USERPROFILE for it.
fn hook_ctx() -> HookCtx {
    let paths = app_paths();
    HookCtx {
        claude_dir: paths.claude_dir,
        codex_home: paths.codex_home,
        hook_exe: settings::hook_exe_path(),
        plans: hookfile::Plans::default(),
    }
}

/// A fresh read of ~/.codex/hooks.json, for `Signal::CodexHooksInstalled`.
fn codex_hooks_installed(ctx: &HookCtx) -> bool {
    let our = codex_hooks::our_command(&ctx.hook_exe).ok();
    codex_hooks::installed_at(&ctx.codex_home, our.as_deref())
}

/// Read-only status of one target's config. `target` defaults to "claude".
#[tauri::command]
fn hooks_status(ctx: State<HookCtx>, target: Option<String>) -> Result<HookStatus, String> {
    let target = Target::parse(target.as_deref())?;
    // Only the target name: shows when a tool config was read (spec §8, D58).
    log::line(format!("hooks_status target={}", target.as_str()));
    Ok(hooks::status(&ctx, target))
}

/// The diff the user has to look at before anything is written. The plan
/// behind it stays in Rust; apply writes exactly those bytes or nothing.
#[tauri::command]
fn hooks_preview(
    ctx: State<HookCtx>,
    target: Option<String>,
    install: bool,
) -> Result<HookPreview, String> {
    let target = Target::parse(target.as_deref())?;
    hooks::preview(&ctx, target, install, &hookfile::local_stamp())
}

/// Only ever called from an explicit click in the settings window. No path
/// comes from the webview: the plan is found by target, install and the
/// fingerprint of the preview the user looked at.
#[tauri::command]
fn hooks_apply(
    ctx: State<HookCtx>,
    observe: State<observe::Handle>,
    target: Option<String>,
    install: bool,
    fingerprint: String,
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let target = Target::parse(target.as_deref())?;
    let result = hooks::apply(&ctx, target, install, &fingerprint);
    if target == Target::Codex {
        // After every Codex apply (spec §8), on success and failure alike, also
        // when no plan matched: read back from disk, never from `install`.
        observe.send(observe::model::Signal::CodexHooksInstalled(codex_hooks_installed(&ctx)));
    }
    result
}
```

- [ ] **Step 27: Build the Claude section on the first focus**

In `windows/src/settings/main.ts`, replace everything from the line `// ── Boot ──────…` to the end of the file (pre-T1 lines 420–459: `async function main()` that awaited `Bridge.hooksStatus()` at boot, and `void main();`) with:

```ts
// ── Boot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * The window is created hidden at app start, and spec §8 rules out reading
 * ~/.claude/settings.json at start-up, so the Claude Code section is built the
 * first time the window gets focus (`show_settings_window` focuses it).
 */
async function fillClaudeSection(slot: HTMLElement) {
  const status = (await Bridge.hooksStatus()) ?? {
    installed: false, settingsPath: "", hookPath: "", hookReady: false,
  };
  clear(slot);
  slot.append(claudeSection(status));
}

async function main() {
  // Registered before anything is awaited, so the first focus is never missed.
  // `display:contents` keeps the section a direct flex item of the root.
  const claudeSlot = h("div", { style: "display:contents" });
  window.addEventListener("focus", () => void fillClaudeSection(claudeSlot), { once: true });

  const boot = await Bridge.boot();
  if (boot) {
    settings = { ...settings, ...boot.settings };
    version = boot.version;
  }

  const hasKey = (await Bridge.secretPresent("anthropic-api-key")) ?? false;

  const keys = [
    "stripe-api-key", "github-token", "vercel-token",
    "n8n-url", "n8n-api-key", "resend-api-key", "notion-api-key", "calcom-api-key",
  ];
  const present: Record<string, boolean> = {};
  for (const k of keys) present[k] = (await Bridge.secretPresent(k)) ?? false;

  clear(root);
  root.append(
    h("h1", {}, h("span", { text: "Mayak" }), h("span", { class: "version", text: version })),
    claudeSlot,
    apiSection(hasKey),
    integrationsSection(present),
    generalSection(),
    h("div", {
      class: "hint",
      text: "No telemetry. Network requests only go to the services you configure yourself.",
    }),
  );

  void onEvent<Settings>("settings-changed", (s) => {
    settings = { ...settings, ...s };
  });
}

void main();
```

#### Part F — uninstaller hint

- [ ] **Step 30: Replace the NSIS uninstall hook**

Replace the whole content of `windows/src-tauri/nsis/hooks.nsh` with:

```nsis
; Uninstall hooks for the NSIS installer.
;
; The app stages mayak-hook.exe into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak\bin at launch, so the
; installer never recorded it and the default uninstaller leaves it behind. The
; inbox and the log live in the same place and are ours too.
;
; Tool configs are deliberately NOT touched here: ~/.codex/hooks.json and
; ~/.claude/settings.json belong to the user, they may hold hooks from other
; tools, and rewriting somebody's config from an uninstaller with no diff and no
; consent is exactly what the rest of this app goes out of its way not to do.
; When a Codex hooks.json exists, the uninstaller only reminds the user to remove
; the integration from Mayak's settings first (spec section 8). OK continues,
; Cancel stops the uninstall before anything is deleted (this hook runs before
; the template's CheckIfAppIsRunning, so Mayak may still be open to do it). An
; update (/UPDATE) or a passive run (/P, which a newer setup started with /P
; passes on when it removes this version) skips the reminder; $UpdateMode and
; $PassiveMode are the template's own globals, set in un.onInit. ASCII only:
; NSIS reads a .nsh without BOM in the ANSI code page.

!macro NSIS_HOOK_PREUNINSTALL
  ${If} $UpdateMode <> 1
  ${AndIf} $PassiveMode <> 1
    Push $0
    ReadEnvStr $0 CODEX_HOME
    StrCmp $0 "" 0 +2
      StrCpy $0 "$PROFILE\.codex"
    IfFileExists "$0\hooks.json" 0 mayak_codex_hint_done
      MessageBox MB_OKCANCEL|MB_ICONINFORMATION "If you installed Mayak's Codex integration, remove it first: Mayak > Settings > Codex > Remove. The uninstaller does not edit $0\hooks.json.$\r$\nOK continues, Cancel stops the uninstall." /SD IDOK IDOK mayak_codex_hint_done
      Pop $0
      Abort
    mayak_codex_hint_done:
    Pop $0
  ${EndIf}
  RMDir /r "$LOCALAPPDATA\Mayak\bin"
  RMDir /r "$LOCALAPPDATA\Mayak\inbox"
  Delete "$LOCALAPPDATA\Mayak\mayak.log"
!macroend
```

`/SD IDOK` makes a silent run (`/S`) continue. An interactive "uninstall the previous version first" from a newer setup.exe (the template's `PageLeaveReinstall`, run without `/UPDATE` and `/P`) still shows the reminder, because the running uninstaller cannot tell that run from a removal; there OK continues the upgrade.

`s2-prepare.ps1` — builds the debug relay, copies it to a path without spaces, records hashes of

```powershell
# Spike S2: builds the debug relay (it has --dump), copies it to a stable path
# without spaces, records the state of hooks.json and config.toml (hashes only)
# and writes the hooks.json snippet for the user to paste. Writes nothing in
# the Codex folder.
param(
    [string]$Repo = 'C:\Users\HP\Documents\claude\coucou\windows',
    [string]$Spike = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Mayak\spike'),
    [string]$CodexHome = $(if ($env:CODEX_HOME) { $env:CODEX_HOME } else { Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.codex' })
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
if (-not (Get-Command cargo -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    $env:Path = (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.cargo\bin') + ';' + $env:Path
}

Push-Location $Repo
try {
    # cargo reports progress on stderr; under 'Stop' PowerShell 5.1 would treat
    # that as a failure, so only the exit code decides here.
    $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
    cargo build -p mayak-hook 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
    if ($code -ne 0) { throw "cargo build -p mayak-hook failed ($code)" }
} finally {
    Pop-Location
}

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $Spike | Out-Null
$relay = Join-Path $Spike 'mayak-hook.exe'
Copy-Item (Join-Path $Repo 'target\debug\mayak-hook.exe') $relay -Force
if ($relay -match '\s') { throw "relay path contains whitespace: $relay" }

$hooks = Join-Path $CodexHome 'hooks.json'
$state = Join-Path $Spike 'state.txt'
$lines = @()
if (Test-Path $hooks) {
    Copy-Item $hooks (Join-Path $Spike 'hooks.json.s2-backup') -Force
    $lines += "hooks.json=present sha256=$((Get-FileHash $hooks -Algorithm SHA256).Hash)"
} else {
    $lines += 'hooks.json=absent'
}
$config = Join-Path $CodexHome 'config.toml'
if (Test-Path $config) {
    $lines += "config.toml sha256 before Trust=$((Get-FileHash $config -Algorithm SHA256).Hash)"
} else {
    $lines += 'config.toml=absent'
}
Set-Content -Path $state -Value $lines -Encoding ASCII

$command = ("$relay --agent codex --dump").Replace('\', '\\')
$snippet = @"
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [ { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "$command", "timeout": 10 } ] } ],
    "PermissionRequest": [ { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "$command", "timeout": 10 } ] } ],
    "Stop": [ { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "$command", "timeout": 10 } ] } ],
    "Interrupt": [ { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "$command", "timeout": 2 } ] } ],
    "SessionEnd": [ { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "$command", "timeout": 2 } ] } ]
  }
}
"@
$null = $snippet | ConvertFrom-Json   # throws if the snippet is not valid JSON
$snippetPath = Join-Path $Spike 'hooks.snippet.json'
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($snippetPath, $snippet, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding $false))

Get-Content $state
"snippet: $snippetPath"
$snippet
```

`s2-shell-timing.ps1` — wall time of one Codex hook run through each shell (sends `SessionEnd` for
an unknown session, which creates no session, D22):

```powershell
# Spike S2: wall time of one Codex hook run through each shell Codex may use.
# Sends a SessionEnd for an unknown session: the model creates nothing for it (D22).
param(
    [string]$Relay = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Mayak\bin\mayak-hook.exe'),
    [int]$Runs = 10
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
if (-not (Test-Path $Relay)) { throw "relay not found: $Relay" }
$payload = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes('{"hook_event_name":"SessionEnd","session_id":"s2-timing","cwd":"C:\\"}')

function Measure-Hook([string]$File, [string]$Arguments) {
    $times = foreach ($i in 1..$Runs) {
        $psi = New-Object Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo $File, $Arguments
        $psi.UseShellExecute = $false
        $psi.RedirectStandardInput = $true
        $psi.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
        $psi.CreateNoWindow = $true
        $sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
        $p = [Diagnostics.Process]::Start($psi)
        $p.StandardInput.BaseStream.Write($payload, 0, $payload.Length)
        $p.StandardInput.Close()
        $out = $p.StandardOutput.ReadToEnd()
        $p.WaitForExit()
        $sw.Stop()
        if ($p.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "$File exited with $($p.ExitCode)" }
        if ($out.Length -ne 0) { throw "$File printed $($out.Length) chars; a Codex run must print nothing" }
        $sw.ElapsedMilliseconds
    }
    $sorted = @($times | Sort-Object)
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Shell    = $File
        Runs     = $Runs
        MedianMs = $sorted[[int][math]::Floor($Runs / 2)]
        MaxMs    = $sorted[-1]
    }
}

# Same command line Codex builds: the hooks.json command passed as one argument.
# The first row (relay alone, no shell) shows what the shell adds.
$command = "$Relay --agent codex"
Measure-Hook $Relay '--agent codex'
Measure-Hook 'powershell.exe' "-NoProfile -Command `"$command`""
Measure-Hook 'cmd.exe' "/C `"$command`""
```

`s2-read-dumps.ps1` — prints every dump line with its local time, from the real `%LOCALAPPDATA%`
and from MSIX-virtualized package folders (a relay started by Codex Desktop may write there):

```powershell
# Spike S2: prints every dump.log line of the debug relay, prefixed with its
# local time (to match mayak.log). A relay started by MSIX Codex Desktop may
# write into the package's virtualized AppData, so both places are read.
# Lines hold only lengths, hashes, times and exe names.
param([string]$LocalAppData = $env:LOCALAPPDATA)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$candidates = @(Join-Path $LocalAppData 'Mayak\dump.log')
$packages = Join-Path $LocalAppData 'Packages'
if (Test-Path $packages) {
    $candidates += @(Get-ChildItem -Path $packages -Directory |
        ForEach-Object { Join-Path $_.FullName 'LocalCache\Local\Mayak\dump.log' })
}
$found = $false
foreach ($file in $candidates) {
    if (Test-Path $file) {
        $found = $true
        "== $file"
        Get-Content $file | ForEach-Object {
            $ms = ($_ -split ' ')[0] -as [int64]
            if ($null -eq $ms) { "?         $_" }
            else { '{0}  {1}' -f [DateTimeOffset]::FromUnixTimeMilliseconds($ms).ToLocalTime().ToString('HH:mm:ss'), $_ }
        }
    }
}
if (-not $found) { 'no dump.log found' }
```

`s2-codex-images.ps1` — image path and parent of every running `codex.exe` (command lines are
never read):

```powershell
# Spike S2: image path of every running codex.exe (and its parent), to check
# the host rules of codex::classify_host. Command lines are never read: they
# can carry tokens.
param([string]$Name = 'codex.exe')
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$all = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process)
$byPid = @{}
foreach ($p in $all) { $byPid[[int]$p.ProcessId] = $p }
$rows = foreach ($p in $all | Where-Object { $_.Name -ieq $Name }) {
    $parent = $byPid[[int]$p.ParentProcessId]
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Pid        = $p.ProcessId
        Path       = $p.ExecutablePath
        ParentName = $(if ($parent) { $parent.Name } else { '-' })
    }
}
if (-not $rows) { "no running $Name" } else { $rows | Format-List }
```

`s2-cleanup.ps1` — first checks that `hooks.json` holds nothing but its state before S2 plus the
snippet groups (otherwise it stops and changes nothing), then restores it byte for byte (or deletes
it if it did not exist), reports whether `config.toml` changed or was created, removes the spike
relay and every `dump.log`:

```powershell
# Spike S2-S5 cleanup: puts hooks.json back exactly as s2-prepare.ps1 found it
# and removes the spike relay and every dump.log. Run with Codex closed or idle.
# Changes nothing when hooks.json holds more than its state before S2 plus the
# snippet groups: an edit made meanwhile is never overwritten.
param(
    [string]$Spike = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Mayak\spike'),
    [string]$LocalAppData = $env:LOCALAPPDATA,
    [string]$CodexHome = $(if ($env:CODEX_HOME) { $env:CODEX_HOME } else { Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.codex' })
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$hooks = Join-Path $CodexHome 'hooks.json'
$state = Get-Content (Join-Path $Spike 'state.txt')
$backup = Join-Path $Spike 'hooks.json.s2-backup'
$wasAbsent = $state -contains 'hooks.json=absent'
$command = (Join-Path $Spike 'mayak-hook.exe') + ' --agent codex --dump'
$utf8 = New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding $false

# Compact JSON of a hooks.json text without the groups whose only hook runs
# $command. An event array emptied that way goes, unless $Keep names it.
function Get-WithoutSnippet([string]$Text, [string[]]$Keep) {
    $obj = $Text | ConvertFrom-Json
    if ($obj -and ($obj.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'hooks') -and $obj.hooks) {
        foreach ($p in @($obj.hooks.PSObject.Properties)) {
            $groups = @($p.Value)
            $kept = @($groups | Where-Object { -not ((@($_.hooks).Count -eq 1) -and ($_.hooks[0].command -eq $command)) })
            if ($kept.Count -eq $groups.Count) { continue }
            if ($kept.Count -eq 0 -and $Keep -notcontains $p.Name) { $obj.hooks.PSObject.Properties.Remove($p.Name) }
            else { $p.Value = $kept }
        }
    }
    $obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 64 -Compress
}

if (Test-Path $hooks) {
    $names = @()
    if ($wasAbsent) {
        $expected = '{"hooks":{}}'
    } else {
        $parsed = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($backup, $utf8) | ConvertFrom-Json
        if ($parsed -and ($parsed.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'hooks') -and $parsed.hooks) {
            $names = @($parsed.hooks.PSObject.Properties.Name)
        }
        $expected = $parsed | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 64 -Compress
    }
    $current = Get-WithoutSnippet ([IO.File]::ReadAllText($hooks, $utf8)) $names
    if ($current -ne $expected) {
        throw "hooks.json holds more than the S2 snippet - nothing was changed. Remove the snippet groups by hand (state before S2: $(if ($wasAbsent) { 'no file' } else { $backup }))."
    }
}

if ($wasAbsent) {
    if (Test-Path $hooks) { Remove-Item $hooks -Confirm:$false }
    if (Test-Path $hooks) { throw 'hooks.json still exists' }
    'hooks.json removed (it did not exist before S2)'
} else {
    $expectedHash = (($state | Where-Object { $_ -like 'hooks.json=present sha256=*' }) -split '=')[-1]
    Copy-Item $backup $hooks -Force
    $actual = (Get-FileHash $hooks -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    if ($actual -ne $expectedHash) { throw "restored hooks.json hash $actual differs from $expectedHash" }
    "hooks.json restored, sha256=$actual"
}

$config = Join-Path $CodexHome 'config.toml'
$before = (($state | Where-Object { $_ -like 'config.toml sha256 before Trust=*' }) -split '=')[-1]
if ($before -and (Test-Path $config)) {
    $now = (Get-FileHash $config -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    if ($now -eq $before) { 'config.toml unchanged since S2 started' }
    else { 'config.toml CHANGED since S2 started (Codex Trust state) - review it yourself before the next dotfiles push' }
} elseif (Test-Path $config) {
    'config.toml CREATED since S2 started (Codex Trust state) - review it yourself before the next dotfiles push'
} elseif ($before) {
    'config.toml DELETED since S2 started - review it yourself before the next dotfiles push'
} else {
    'config.toml still absent'
}

$dumps = @(Join-Path $LocalAppData 'Mayak\dump.log')
$packages = Join-Path $LocalAppData 'Packages'
if (Test-Path $packages) {
    $dumps += @(Get-ChildItem -Path $packages -Directory |
        ForEach-Object { Join-Path $_.FullName 'LocalCache\Local\Mayak' })
}
foreach ($d in $dumps) {
    if (Test-Path $d) { Remove-Item $d -Recurse -Force -Confirm:$false; "removed $d" }
}
Remove-Item $Spike -Recurse -Force -Confirm:$false
"removed $Spike"
```

`s3-rollout-keys.mjs` — rollout shape: keys, record type names and JSON type names only, plus the
`session_meta` labels `history_mode` / `originator` / `source` and `cli_version` (each printed only when
it looks like a short label or a version) and, for a subagent's `session_meta`, the key paths of
`parent_thread_id` / `agent_role` / `subagent` with their JSON types and whether T8 reads them (D67):

```javascript
// Spike S3: shape of Codex rollout files - keys and record types only.
// Never prints a value except: record type names (type / payload.type) that
// look like identifiers, JSON type names (string/object/...), and the
// session_meta labels history_mode / originator / source (only when they look
// like short labels) and cli_version (only when it looks like a version).
// For a subagent's session_meta it prints the key paths of parent_thread_id,
// agent_role and subagent with JSON type names, never their values (D67).
//
// Usage: node s3-rollout-keys.mjs [--root <sessions dir>] [--since <ISO time>] [--newest <n>]
//   --root    default: $CODEX_HOME\sessions, else %USERPROFILE%\.codex\sessions
//   --since   only files modified at or after this time (default: no limit)
//   --newest  how many of the most recently modified files to report (default 2)
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, basename } from "node:path";

// Top-level types T8's parse_rollout_line knows; any other one is Unknown there.
const KNOWN_TYPES = new Set(["session_meta", "event_msg", "response_item", "turn_context", "world_state", "compacted"]);
// Keys whose place in session_meta.payload the subagent check reports (D67).
const SUBAGENT_KEYS = new Set(["parent_thread_id", "agent_role", "subagent"]);

function arg(name, fallback) {
  const i = process.argv.indexOf(name);
  return i >= 0 && i + 1 < process.argv.length ? process.argv[i + 1] : fallback;
}

const home = process.env.CODEX_HOME || join(process.env.USERPROFILE || "", ".codex");
const root = arg("--root", join(home, "sessions"));
const since = arg("--since", null);
const sinceMs = since === null ? -Infinity : Date.parse(since);
if (Number.isNaN(sinceMs)) {
  console.error(`--since is not a date: ${since}`);
  process.exit(2);
}
const newest = Number(arg("--newest", "2"));

function walk(dir, out) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const p = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(p, out);
    else if (/^rollout-.*\.jsonl$/.test(entry.name)) out.push({ path: p, mtime: statSync(p).mtimeMs });
  }
  return out;
}

const jsonType = (v) => (v === null ? "null" : Array.isArray(v) ? "array" : typeof v);
const ident = (s) => (typeof s === "string" && /^[a-z_]{1,40}$/.test(s) ? s : "<not-an-identifier>");
const keysOf = (v) => (v && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v) ? Object.keys(v).sort() : []);
// A short label such as "legacy", "codex_vscode" or "Codex Desktop"; anything else shows its JSON type.
const label = (v) =>
  v === undefined ? "absent" : typeof v === "string" && /^[A-Za-z0-9_. -]{1,40}$/.test(v) ? JSON.stringify(v) : `<${jsonType(v)}>`;
const version = (v) => (v === undefined ? "absent" : typeof v === "string" && /^[0-9a-z.\-]+$/.test(v) ? v : `<${jsonType(v)}>`);
const sourceOf = (v) => (v && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v) ? `{${keysOf(v).map(ident).join(",")}}` : label(v));
const str = (p, k) => typeof p[k] === "string";
const keyName = (k) => (/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$/.test(k) ? k : "<not-a-key-name>");

// Key paths below session_meta.payload whose last key is in SUBAGENT_KEYS, each with the JSON
// type of its value, e.g. "source.subagent.thread_spawn.agent_role:string". Keys only.
function subagentPaths(v, prefix, out) {
  if (Array.isArray(v)) {
    v.forEach((x) => subagentPaths(x, `${prefix}[]`, out));
  } else if (v && typeof v === "object") {
    for (const k of Object.keys(v)) {
      const path = prefix ? `${prefix}.${keyName(k)}` : keyName(k);
      if (SUBAGENT_KEYS.has(k)) out.add(`${path}:${jsonType(v[k])}`);
      subagentPaths(v[k], path, out);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

// Mirrors T8's Meta extraction: a string at payload.<key>, else at
// payload.source.subagent.thread_spawn.<key>.
function t8Reads(p, key) {
  const spawn = p.source && p.source.subagent && p.source.subagent.thread_spawn;
  const nested = spawn !== null && typeof spawn === "object" && !Array.isArray(spawn) && str(spawn, key);
  return str(p, key) || nested ? "yes" : "no";
}

// Mirrors observe::codex::parse_rollout_line (T8): true when it returns RolloutRecord::Unknown.
function t8Unknown(v) {
  if (!v || typeof v !== "object" || Array.isArray(v) || typeof v.type !== "string") return true;
  if (!KNOWN_TYPES.has(v.type)) return true;
  if (v.type === "turn_context" || v.type === "world_state" || v.type === "compacted") return false;
  const p = v.payload;
  if (jsonType(p) !== "object") return true;
  if (v.type === "session_meta") return !str(p, "id");
  if (!str(p, "type")) return true;
  if (v.type === "response_item" && (p.type === "function_call" || p.type === "custom_tool_call")) return !str(p, "name");
  return false;
}

let subagentRecords = 0; // session_meta records with a subagent key, over all reported files

function report(file) {
  const lines = readFileSync(file.path, "utf8").split("\n").filter((l) => l.trim() !== "");
  const metas = new Map(); // "history_mode=... originator=... source=... cli_version=..." -> count
  const subagents = new Map(); // "paths=... t8=..." of session_meta records with subagent keys -> count
  const modes = new Set(); // label(history_mode) of every session_meta
  const shapes = new Map(); // top-level key set -> count
  const records = new Map(); // "type/payload.type" -> { count, keys:Set }
  const unknownTypes = new Map(); // ident(top-level type) of lines T8 reads as Unknown -> count
  let unparsable = 0;
  const turnId = { task_started: [0, 0], task_complete: [0, 0], turn_aborted: [0, 0] };
  const errorTypes = new Map();
  for (const line of lines) {
    let v;
    try {
      v = JSON.parse(line);
    } catch {
      unparsable++;
      continue;
    }
    const shape = keysOf(v).join(",") || `<${jsonType(v)}>`;
    shapes.set(shape, (shapes.get(shape) || 0) + 1);
    if (t8Unknown(v)) {
      const t = v && typeof v === "object" ? ident(v.type) : `<${jsonType(v)}>`;
      unknownTypes.set(t, (unknownTypes.get(t) || 0) + 1);
      continue;
    }
    if (v.type === "session_meta") {
      const p = v.payload;
      modes.add(label(p.history_mode));
      const m = `history_mode=${label(p.history_mode)} originator=${label(p.originator)} source=${sourceOf(p.source)} cli_version=${version(p.cli_version)}`;
      metas.set(m, (metas.get(m) || 0) + 1);
      const paths = [...subagentPaths(p, "", new Set())].sort();
      if (paths.length > 0) {
        const t8 = `parent_thread_id:${t8Reads(p, "parent_thread_id")},agent_role:${t8Reads(p, "agent_role")}`;
        const sa = `paths=${paths.join(",")} t8=${t8}`;
        subagents.set(sa, (subagents.get(sa) || 0) + 1);
      }
    }
    if (jsonType(v.payload) !== "object") continue; // turn_context / world_state / compacted without an object payload
    const sub = v.type === "event_msg" || v.type === "response_item" ? `/${ident(v.payload.type)}` : "";
    const name = `${v.type}${sub}`;
    const rec = records.get(name) || { count: 0, keys: new Set() };
    rec.count++;
    keysOf(v.payload).forEach((k) => rec.keys.add(k));
    records.set(name, rec);
    if (v.type === "event_msg" && v.payload.type in turnId) {
      const t = turnId[v.payload.type];
      t[1]++;
      if (v.payload.turn_id !== undefined && v.payload.turn_id !== null) t[0]++;
      if (v.payload.type === "task_complete" && "error" in v.payload) {
        const ty = jsonType(v.payload.error);
        errorTypes.set(ty, (errorTypes.get(ty) || 0) + 1);
      }
    }
  }
  console.log(`== ${basename(file.path)}  modified ${new Date(file.mtime).toISOString()}  lines=${lines.length}`);
  for (const [m, n] of metas) console.log(`meta: ${m} x${n}`);
  for (const [sa, n] of subagents) console.log(`subagent: ${sa} x${n}`);
  subagentRecords += [...subagents.values()].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  const mode =
    modes.size === 0
      ? "unknown - no session_meta record"
      : modes.size === 1 && modes.has('"legacy"')
        ? "legacy"
        : `NOT legacy - history_mode ${[...modes].join(", ")}`;
  console.log(`mode: ${mode}`);
  console.log("top-level key sets:");
  for (const [shape, n] of shapes) console.log(`  [${shape}] x${n}`);
  console.log("records (payload keys):");
  for (const [name, rec] of [...records].sort()) console.log(`  ${name} x${rec.count}  [${[...rec.keys].sort().join(", ")}]`);
  for (const [name, [withId, total]] of Object.entries(turnId)) {
    console.log(`  ${name}: ${total} record(s), ${withId} with turn_id`);
  }
  const errs = [...errorTypes].map(([t, n]) => `${t} x${n}`).join(", ");
  console.log(`  task_complete with an "error" key: ${errs || "none"}`);
  const unknown = [...unknownTypes].map(([t, n]) => `${t} x${n}`).join(", ");
  console.log(`  lines T8 reads as Unknown (Degraded expected): ${unknown || "none"}`);
  console.log(`  unparsable lines: ${unparsable}`);
  console.log("");
}

const files = walk(root, [])
  .filter((f) => f.mtime >= sinceMs)
  .sort((a, b) => b.mtime - a.mtime)
  .slice(0, newest);
if (files.length === 0) {
  console.log(`no rollout files under ${root}${since ? ` modified since ${since}` : ""}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
files.forEach(report);
console.log(
  subagentRecords === 0
    ? "subagent check: no session_meta with parent_thread_id, agent_role or subagent keys in these files"
    : `subagent check: ${subagentRecords} session_meta record(s) with subagent keys (see the subagent: lines)`,
);
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Start the dev app and open the snapshot console**

Run in a separate terminal: `cd windows && npm run tauri dev` (`npm run dev` alone starts only Vite).
Expected: the island appears; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak\mayak.log` ends with `--- Mayak <version> started ---`.

The island has no session rows before T16/T17, so sessions are read from the store: tray →
Settings…, right-click inside the Settings window → Inspect → Console (as in T14 Step 34), and run:

```js
window.mayakSnap = async () => {
  const s = await window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke("sessions_snapshot");
  return s.projects.flatMap((p) =>
    p.sessions
      .filter((x) => x.agent === "codex")
      .map((x) => ({ project: p.name, host: x.host, phase: x.phase.kind, wait: x.phase.wait ?? "", outcome: x.outcome ? x.outcome.kind : "" }))
  );
};
console.table(await window.mayakSnap());
```

Expected: an empty table (no Codex session yet). Later steps run `console.table(await window.mayakSnap())`
again; it prints only project names, hosts and phases (no titles, prompts or paths). After every
restart of the dev app, open the console again and re-run this block.

- [ ] **Step 4: Build the spike relay and produce the snippet**

Run in PowerShell: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-spike\s2-prepare.ps1"`

Expected output, in this order: cargo's ``Finished `dev` profile …``; `hooks.json=absent` (or
`hooks.json=present sha256=<64 hex>`); `config.toml sha256 before Trust=<64 hex>` (or
`config.toml=absent`); `snippet: C:\Users\HP\AppData\Local\Mayak\spike\hooks.snippet.json`; the
snippet, whose five groups all carry
`"command": "C:\\Users\\HP\\AppData\\Local\\Mayak\\spike\\mayak-hook.exe --agent codex --dump"`
(timeout 10 for `UserPromptSubmit`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`; 2 for `Interrupt`, `SessionEnd`).

- [ ] **Step 5: User — install the snippet by hand**

- If Step 4 printed `hooks.json=absent`, run in PowerShell:

```powershell
$codexHome = if ($env:CODEX_HOME) { $env:CODEX_HOME } else { Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.codex' }
Copy-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Mayak\spike\hooks.snippet.json" (Join-Path $codexHome 'hooks.json')
```

- If it printed `hooks.json=present …`: open `hooks.json` in an editor and, for each of the five
  event keys of the snippet, append the snippet's group object at the **end** of that event's
  array (create the key if it is missing). Do not move or edit existing groups: Codex trust keys
  are positional.

Then note the start time for S3: `$s3Since = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('o'); $s3Since`

- [ ] **Step 6: User — run the S2/S3 prompts on both surfaces**

Prepare a project whose name has Cyrillic letters (stdin integrity shows up as the session's project
name in `mayakSnap()`), in an interactive PowerShell console:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\mayak-проверка" | Out-Null
git -C "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\mayak-проверка" init
```

Then, first in **Cursor** (Codex extension) and afterwards in **Codex Desktop**, with that folder
open:
1. When Codex reports that hooks need review: Trust them, then "Reload hooks" or start a new
   thread (loaded threads do not re-read `hooks.json`). Note whether the second surface asks for
   Trust again (S2.8).
2. Switch Codex to the mode in which it asks before writing files (read-only / ask mode; the
   label differs per version) and send `Create a file named s2-check.txt containing the word ok.`
   — Codex shows its native approval request. Before approving, run
   `console.table(await window.mayakSnap())` in the Settings console (Step 3). Then approve it.
3. Send `Ответь одним словом: привет`. After the answer, run `console.table(await window.mayakSnap())`
   again.
4. Start one subagent (S3 subagent check, D67), send:
   `Start a subagent that lists the files in this folder, wait for it to finish, then reply with what it found.`
   Approve any request it shows. If Codex answers that it cannot start a subagent, note "no
   subagent tool" for S3.1.
5. Send `Count slowly from 1 to 300, one number per line.` and press Stop/Esc while it streams
   (the `Interrupt` hook exists only in 0.158, so only Desktop fires it; both may write
   `turn_aborted` to the rollout).
6. Close the thread (Cursor: close the window; Desktop: quit the app) — `SessionEnd` exists in
   0.146 and 0.158.
7. During all of this, watch for a console window flashing up on a hook (S2.4).

Expected in `mayakSnap()`, per surface: during item 2 a row with `project` `mayak-проверка`, `host`
`cursor` (Cursor) or `codexDesktop` (Desktop), `phase` `waiting`, `wait` `permission`; after item 3
the same row with `phase` `idle`, `outcome` `finished`. Fill S2.5 from the `project` column:
exactly `mayak-проверка` → that text; any other text in that row → "mangled" plus the text shown;
no row with that surface's `host` → "no session". (A row disappears after item 6's `SessionEnd`, so
read it at items 2 and 3.)

- [ ] **Step 7: Collect the S2 observations**

(a) `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-spike\s2-read-dumps.ps1"`
— Expected: lines `HH:mm:ss  <ms> len=<n> sha256=<hex> age_ms=<n> chain=<a>b>… shell=<exe>`; one per
hook run. Fill S2.1 (`shell=`) and S2.2 (`codex.exe` present in `chain=`; when it is missing, also
the number of `>`-separated entries in `chain=`, at most 6) per surface; lines in a
`…\Packages\…\LocalCache\Local\Mayak\dump.log` file come from a packaged (Desktop) relay.

(b) `Select-String -Path "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Mayak\mayak.log" -Pattern '^\S+ \S+ (hook codex|codex )' | Select-Object -Last 40`
(`Select-String` reads the UTF-8 log correctly in Windows PowerShell 5.1; `Get-Content` needs
`-Encoding UTF8`)
— Expected: for every dump line a `hook codex <Event> s=<8>` line at the same second and a
`codex <Event> s=<8> host=<host> proc=<yes|no>` line (`host` is `HostKind`'s Debug name). Fill
S2.6. Expected values: Cursor `host=Cursor proc=yes`; Desktop `host=CodexDesktop proc=yes`; a
surface the rules do not recognise logs `host=Unknown`.

(c) Start Codex Desktop again (Step 6 item 6 quit it; no prompt needed), then:
`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-spike\s2-codex-images.ps1"`
— Expected: one block per `codex.exe` with `Path` and `ParentName`. Fill S2.7 with the path of
the Desktop one.

(d) `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-spike\s2-shell-timing.ps1" | Format-List`
— runs the release relay `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak\bin\mayak-hook.exe` 10 times per row. Expected:
three records (relay alone — `Shell` is the relay's path —, `powershell.exe`, `cmd.exe`) with
`MedianMs`/`MaxMs`; the scratch run measured 89 / 424 / 133 ms. Fill S2.3 per surface with the
`MedianMs` of the row matching S2.1: `powershell.exe` → the `powershell.exe` row, `cmd.exe` → the
`cmd.exe` row, `codex.exe` (Codex started the relay without a shell) → the relay-alone row; any
other S2.1 value has no row — write "no row". These runs reach the running Mayak as `SessionEnd`
of an unknown session: no session is created (D22), but the in-memory Codex `receiving` status
lists an Unknown host until the app restarts (D24).

(e) Interpretation of a missing session: a dump line with no matching `hook codex` line means the
relay ran but its line never reached the router (JSON broken by the shell, or the same-user
check failed) — S2.5 = "no session".

- [ ] **Step 8: Run S3 on the same prompts**

Run: `node "$env:TEMP\mayak-spike\s3-rollout-keys.mjs" --since $s3Since --newest 8`
(`$s3Since` from Step 5; use the same console or paste the printed value; 8 leaves room for the
main thread and the subagent of Step 6 item 4 on each surface, plus a thread started for Trust).

Expected per file: `== rollout-….jsonl  modified <ISO>  lines=<n>`; one or more
`meta: history_mode="legacy" originator=<label> source=<label> cli_version=<version> x<n>` lines;
for a file whose `session_meta` carries a key named `parent_thread_id`, `agent_role` or `subagent`
at any depth (the subagent's rollout of Step 6 item 4) also one or more
`subagent: paths=<key path>:<JSON type>,… t8=parent_thread_id:<yes|no>,agent_role:<yes|no> x<n>`
lines (key paths below `session_meta.payload`, e.g. `source.subagent.thread_spawn.agent_role:string`;
`t8=` says whether T8's `parse_rollout_line` finds a string for that key: top level or under
`source.subagent.thread_spawn`); `mode: legacy` (decided from `session_meta.payload.history_mode`
alone: `legacy` in every `session_meta` of the file); the top-level key set
`[payload,timestamp,type]`; the record list (e.g. `event_msg/task_started x<n>  [ …keys… ]`); three
`…: <m> record(s), <n> with turn_id` lines; `task_complete with an "error" key: none` (or the JSON
type); `lines T8 reads as Unknown (Degraded expected): none`; `unparsable lines: 0`. After the last
file: `subagent check: <n> session_meta record(s) with subagent keys (see the subagent: lines)` or
`subagent check: no session_meta with parent_thread_id, agent_role or subagent keys in these files`.
The local rollouts read while writing this plan print
`meta: history_mode="legacy" originator="codex_vscode" source="vscode" cli_version=0.146.0-alpha.3`
(Codex in Cursor) and `meta: history_mode="legacy" originator="Codex Desktop" source="vscode"
cli_version=0.144.2` (Codex Desktop), no `subagent:` line, and the `subagent check: no …` line (no
subagent was ever started on this machine).

Assign each file to a surface by its `meta:` line: `originator="codex_vscode"` → Cursor,
`originator="Codex Desktop"` → Codex Desktop (`source` is `"vscode"` on both, so it does not
separate them). Any other `originator` → assign by `cli_version` (`0.146.*` → Cursor, `0.158.*` →
Codex Desktop) and write the originator into S3.1. A file that fits neither rule is left out;
write its `meta:` line into S3.1. Fill S3.1, S3.2, S3.4 (an interrupted turn from Step 6 item 5
shows as `event_msg/turn_aborted`).

Optional, for S3.3: disconnect the network, send any prompt on one surface, wait until Codex
reports the failure (retries can take about a minute), reconnect, run the script again with
`--newest 1`.

- [ ] **Step 9: Apply the S3 decision rules**

- **Mode (D70).** Every file `mode: legacy` → `parse_rollout_line` stays as T8 wrote it; skip
  Step 9a. Otherwise write the `mode:` line and the `top-level key sets:` of each non-legacy file
  into S3.1, then:
  - every non-legacy file prints `mode: NOT legacy - history_mode "paginated"`, and its top-level
    key sets are only `[ordinal,payload,timestamp,type]`, `[metadata,ordinal,payload,timestamp,type]`
    or `[payload,timestamp,type]` → Step 9a (spec §12 S3: «Если paginated — добавить разбор»);
  - anything else (another `history_mode` label or `absent`, `mode: unknown - no session_meta
    record`, or any other top-level key set) → the shape cannot be determined from keys alone: no
    code is written for it. T15 finishes Steps 10–23 (S2 decisions, S4 and S5 do not read

  "yes". S2.3 "no row" on a surface (S2.1 names a program Step 7d does not measure) → stop and
  decide with the user. If R1 says reduce but S3.2 shows `task_started` without `turn_id` on a
  surface, stop and decide with the user (without `UserPromptSubmit` that surface would never show
  `Working`). Otherwise: reduce → Step 12; keep → skip Step 12.
- **R2 (host).** A surface whose `codex …` lines say `host=Unknown` → Step 13 with its image path
  (S2.7 for Desktop; for Cursor run Step 7c while only Cursor runs Codex).
- **R3 (ancestor).** The dump walks at most `MAX_ANCESTOR_STEPS` = 6 ancestors, so a deeper
  `codex.exe` cannot show up in `chain=`. `proc=no` with no `codex.exe` in `chain=`:
  - fewer than 6 entries in `chain=` → the walk ended before the cap (no parent row, an unreadable
    creation time, or a parent younger than its child, see `win::ancestors`); record it together
    with the last exe name of `chain=` (rows then stay until `SessionEnd`/OK, spec §15);
  - exactly 6 entries → `codex.exe` may sit deeper than the walk looks: stop and ask the user (a
    deeper walk changes spec §5.2). For diagnosis only, the spike relay can dump a longer chain: in
    `windows/hook/src/main.rs` `fn dump`, replace `relay::MAX_ANCESTOR_STEPS)` with `16)`; in
    PowerShell run `$env:Path = (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.cargo\bin') + ';' + $env:Path; cd C:\Users\HP\Documents\claude\coucou\windows; cargo build -p mayak-hook; Copy-Item target\debug\mayak-hook.exe "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Mayak\spike\mayak-hook.exe" -Force`
    (do not rerun `s2-prepare.ps1`: it would overwrite the saved pre-S2 state); send one prompt and
    read the new dump line (Step 7a); then `git checkout -- windows/hook/src/main.rs`, rebuild and
    copy again the same way. Never commit it.

  `proc=no` although `codex.exe` is in the chain → record; it is a T12 proof failure to investigate
  before T15 continues.
- **R4 (stdin).** S2.5 "mangled" or "no session" while dump lines exist → stop and decide with the
  user (the relay cannot repair a shell's re-encoding; changing the command shape changes the
  Codex trust hash).

for the Desktop `{la}` form, the `%LOCALAPPDATA%` folder (`c:\users\<name>\appdata\local`) becomes
`{la}`; for a `const` pattern, the drive and, when present, the `users\<name>` segments become `**`.

```rust
/// The only place a pipe instance is created. `first` also means we refuse to
/// join a pipe somebody else already owns under our name.
pub fn create_instance(name: &str, first: bool) -> std::io::Result<NamedPipeServer> {

```

with

```rust
/// The only place a pipe instance is created. `first` also means we refuse to
/// join a pipe somebody else already owns under our name.
///
/// Every instance carries a protected DACL with a single entry: full access for
/// the current user's SID. The default DACL also lets other accounts read and
/// connect; with this one only our own account (the relay) can. Spike S4
/// confirmed that the relay started by MSIX Codex Desktop still connects.
pub fn create_instance(name: &str, first: bool) -> std::io::Result<NamedPipeServer> {
    let sid = crate::win_user::current_user_sid()
        .ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other("cannot read the current user SID"))?;
    let descriptor = SecurityDescriptor::from_sddl(&current_user_sddl(&sid))?;
    let mut attributes = SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES {
        nLength: std::mem::size_of::<SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES>() as u32,
        lpSecurityDescriptor: descriptor.0 .0,
        bInheritHandle: false.into(),
    };
    let mut options = ServerOptions::new();
    options.first_pipe_instance(first);
    // SAFETY: `attributes` and the descriptor it points to outlive the call.
    unsafe {
        options.create_with_security_attributes_raw(
            name,
            (&mut attributes as *mut SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES).cast(),
        )
    }
}

/// `D:P(A;;GA;;;<sid>)` — protected (nothing inherited), one allow entry.
fn current_user_sddl(sid: &str) -> String {
    format!("D:P(A;;GA;;;{sid})")
}

/// A security descriptor allocated by Windows, freed with LocalFree on drop.
struct SecurityDescriptor(PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR);

impl SecurityDescriptor {
    fn from_sddl(sddl: &str) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let mut descriptor = PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR::default();
        unsafe {
            ConvertStringSecurityDescriptorToSecurityDescriptorW(
                &HSTRING::from(sddl),
                SDDL_REVISION_1,
                &mut descriptor,
                None,
            )
        }
        .map_err(std::io::Error::from)?;
        Ok(Self(descriptor))
    }
}

impl Drop for SecurityDescriptor {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        unsafe {
            let _ = LocalFree(Some(HLOCAL(self.0 .0)));
        }
    }
}

```

```ts
export type Host = "claudeDesktop" | "cursor" | "vsCode" | "codexDesktop" | "unknown";
export type Phase =
  | { kind: "working" }
  | { kind: "waiting"; wait: "permission" | "input" | "other"; label: string }
  | { kind: "idle" }
  | { kind: "unknown"; label: string };
export type OutcomeView = null | { kind: "finished" | "error" | "interrupted"; summary: string; at: number };
export type AttentionKind = null | "permission" | "input" | "error" | "finished";
export type BotState = "approval" | "question" | "error" | "working" | "finished" | "idle";
export type Health = "ok" | "missing" | { error: string } | { degraded: { unreadable: number } };
export type CodexHooksState =
  | "not_installed" | "installed_unseen" | { receiving: { hosts: Host[]; since: number } };
export interface SessionView {
  key: string; agent: "claude" | "codex"; host: Host; title: string | null;
  phase: Phase; since: number; activity: string | null; detail: string | null;
  outcome: OutcomeView; attention: AttentionKind; acked: boolean;
}
export interface ProjectView { key: string; name: string; root: string; sessions: SessionView[] }
export interface SessionsSnapshot {
  rev: number; now: number; projects: ProjectView[]; attention: string[];
  counts: { waiting: number; error: number; finished: number; working: number };
  hold: boolean; aggregate: BotState;
  sources: { claude: Health; codex: Health; codexHooks: CodexHooksState };
}
export interface Alert {
  key: string; kind: "permission" | "input" | "error" | "finished"; rank: number;
  agent: "claude" | "codex"; host: Host; project: string; title: string | null;
  detail: string | null; text: string; since: number;
}
export type HookTarget = "claude" | "codex";
export interface HookStatus {
  target: HookTarget; installed: boolean; outdated: boolean; settingsPath: string;
  hookPath: string; hookReady: boolean; notes: string[];
}
export interface HookPreview {
  diff: string; backup: string; settingsPath: string; fingerprint: string; notes: string[];
  unchanged: boolean;   // D53
}
```

Replace the whole file with:

```ts
// Thin wrapper over the Tauri commands/events. Every call is a no-op when the
// page is opened in a plain browser, so the island can be iterated on with
// `npm run dev` alone.

import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";
import { listen } from "@tauri-apps/api/event";
import { getCurrentWebview } from "@tauri-apps/api/webview";
import type { Settings } from "./state";

export const IS_TAURI =
  typeof window !== "undefined" && "__TAURI_INTERNALS__" in window;

async function call<T>(cmd: string, args?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<T | null> {
  if (!IS_TAURI) return null;
  try {
    return await invoke<T>(cmd, args);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`[mayak] ${cmd} failed`, err);
    return null;
  }
}

export interface BootInfo {
  settings: Settings;
  /** Logical screen rect of the monitor the island lives on. */
  screen: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; scale: number };
  version: string;
  hookPath: string;
}

export const Bridge = {
  boot: () => call<BootInfo>("boot"),

  saveSettings: (settings: Settings) => call<void>("save_settings", { settings }),

  /** Shrink the window down to the invisible wake strip (hidden) or back to full. */
  setCollapsed: (collapsed: boolean) => call<void>("set_collapsed", { collapsed }),

  /**
   * Pushes the island shape in window coordinates. Rust flips click-through from
   * its own cursor poll, so the flag is never a frame behind a click.
   */
  setIslandRect: (x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number) =>
    call<void>("set_island_rect", { x, y, width, height }),

  /** Give the window keyboard focus (chat field) and take it away again. */
  focusWindow: (focused: boolean) => call<void>("focus_window", { focused }),

  reposition: () => call<void>("reposition"),

  openUrl: (url: string) => call<void>("open_url", { url }),

  /** "Open terminal" → opens the folder in VS Code when `code` is on PATH. */
  openInVSCode: (path: string | null) => call<boolean>("open_in_vscode", { path }),

  quit: () => call<void>("quit_app"),

  openSettingsWindow: () => call<void>("open_settings_window"),

  /** Writes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak\mayak.log, next to the Rust lines. */
  log: (message: string) => call<void>("log_line", { message }),

  // ── Agent sessions (observer) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  /** Latest published snapshot; the island also receives it as the `sessions` event. */
  sessionsSnapshot: () => call<SessionsSnapshot>("sessions_snapshot"),
  /** "Seen": hides the current episode of that row. Never changes its phase. */
  sessionAck: (key: string) => call<void>("session_ack", { key }),
  /** Opens the project root in the session's host editor; false → Explorer was used. */
  sessionOpen: (key: string) => call<boolean>("session_open", { key }),

  // ── Hook installers (Codex hooks.json, legacy Claude settings.json) ──────────
  hooksStatus: (target: HookTarget = "claude") => call<HookStatus>("hooks_status", { target }),
  /** Diff to show before anything is written. `install: false` previews removal. */
  hooksPreview: (install: boolean, target: HookTarget = "claude") =>
    callOrThrow<HookPreview>("hooks_preview", { target, install }),
  /**
   * Writes the target's config file — only ever after an explicit click, and only
   * when the file still matches the preview the user looked at.
   */
  hooksApply: (install: boolean, fingerprint: string, target: HookTarget = "claude") =>
    callOrThrow<string>("hooks_apply", { target, install, fingerprint }),

  approvalDecision: (requestId: string, decision: "allow" | "deny") =>
    call<void>("approval_decision", { requestId, decision }),
  /** "The card is up" — until this lands the relay only waits a moment. */
  approvalAck: (requestId: string) => call<void>("approval_ack", { requestId }),
  /** "Nobody can act on this" — Claude Code asks in the terminal right away. */
  approvalDecline: (requestId: string) => call<void>("approval_decline", { requestId }),

  // ── Chat, files, secrets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  /** One chat turn. The API key and any file bytes never leave Rust. */
  chatSend: (query: string, context: ChatContext | null) =>
    callOrThrow<{ text: string }>("chat_send", { query, context }),
  chatReset: () => call<void>("chat_reset"),
  /** Copies a dropped file into the inbox. */
  ingestFile: (path: string) => callOrThrow<DroppedFile>("ingest_file", { path }),
  /** Only ever tells you whether a key exists — never its value. */
  secretPresent: (key: string) => call<boolean>("secret_present", { key }),
  secretSet: (key: string, value: string) => callOrThrow<void>("secret_set", { key, value }),
  secretClear: (key: string) => callOrThrow<void>("secret_clear", { key }),

  // ── Integrations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  refreshIntegration: (id: string) => call<void>("refresh_integration", { id }),
  /** Opens the configured n8n instance in the browser. */
  openN8n: () => call<void>("open_n8n"),

  /** Tray → Pause. Stops the integration pollers, not just the island. */
  setPaused: (paused: boolean) => call<void>("set_paused", { paused }),
};

export interface IntegrationUpdate {
  id: string;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
  error: string | null;
  event: { success: boolean; label: string; detail: string | null } | null;
}

export type ChatContext =
  | { kind: "file"; name: string; path: string }
  | { kind: "window"; appName: string; title: string; url?: string };

export interface DroppedFile {
  name: string;
  path: string;
  size: number;
}

// ── Sessions snapshot — mirrors the Rust wire types (spec §10) ────────────────

export type Host = "claudeDesktop" | "cursor" | "vsCode" | "codexDesktop" | "unknown";
export type Phase =
  | { kind: "working" }
  | { kind: "waiting"; wait: "permission" | "input" | "other"; label: string }
  | { kind: "idle" }
  | { kind: "unknown"; label: string };
export type OutcomeView = null | { kind: "finished" | "error" | "interrupted"; summary: string; at: number };
export type AttentionKind = null | "permission" | "input" | "error" | "finished";
export type BotState = "approval" | "question" | "error" | "working" | "finished" | "idle";
export type Health = "ok" | "missing" | { error: string } | { degraded: { unreadable: number } };
export type CodexHooksState =
  | "not_installed" | "installed_unseen" | { receiving: { hosts: Host[]; since: number } };
export interface SessionView {
  key: string; agent: "claude" | "codex"; host: Host; title: string | null;
  phase: Phase; since: number; activity: string | null; detail: string | null;
  outcome: OutcomeView; attention: AttentionKind; acked: boolean;
}
export interface ProjectView { key: string; name: string; root: string; sessions: SessionView[] }
export interface SessionsSnapshot {
  rev: number; now: number; projects: ProjectView[]; attention: string[];
  counts: { waiting: number; error: number; finished: number; working: number };
  hold: boolean; aggregate: BotState;
  sources: { claude: Health; codex: Health; codexHooks: CodexHooksState };
}
export interface Alert {
  key: string; kind: "permission" | "input" | "error" | "finished"; rank: number;
  agent: "claude" | "codex"; host: Host; project: string; title: string | null;
  detail: string | null; text: string; since: number;
}

// ── Hook installers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export type HookTarget = "claude" | "codex";
export interface HookStatus {
  target: HookTarget; installed: boolean; outdated: boolean; settingsPath: string;
  hookPath: string; hookReady: boolean; notes: string[];
}
export interface HookPreview {
  /** Hand `fingerprint` back to hooksApply so only the reviewed diff is ever written. */
  diff: string; backup: string; settingsPath: string; fingerprint: string; notes: string[];
  /** Nothing would be written (the entry is already there): Apply stays disabled. */
  unchanged: boolean;
}

/** Same as `call`, but surfaces the error so the UI can show what went wrong. */
async function callOrThrow<T>(cmd: string, args?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<T> {
  if (!IS_TAURI) throw new Error("not running inside Mayak");
  return invoke<T>(cmd, args);
}

export type BridgeEvent =
  | { name: "cursor"; payload: { x: number; y: number } }
  | { name: "tray"; payload: string }
  | { name: "hook"; payload: Record<string, unknown> }
  | { name: "screen-changed"; payload: null }
  | { name: "sessions"; payload: SessionsSnapshot }
  | { name: "session-alert"; payload: Alert[] };

export interface DragDropPayload {
  type: "enter" | "over" | "drop" | "leave";
  paths?: string[];
}

/** Files dragged onto the island. Only reaches us when the window takes the mouse. */
export async function onDragDrop(handler: (e: DragDropPayload) => void) {
  if (!IS_TAURI) return () => {};
  return getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent((event) => {
    handler(event.payload as DragDropPayload);
  });
}

export async function onEvent<T>(name: string, handler: (payload: T) => void) {
  if (!IS_TAURI) return () => {};
  return listen<T>(name, (e) => handler(e.payload));
}

/** Every published sessions snapshot (emit_to "island"). */
export function onSessions(handler: (s: SessionsSnapshot) => void): Promise<() => void> {
  return onEvent<SessionsSnapshot>("sessions", handler);
}

/** One batch of model alerts, emitted just before the snapshot that contains them. */
export function onSessionAlert(handler: (alerts: Alert[]) => void): Promise<() => void> {
  return onEvent<Alert[]>("session-alert", handler);
}
```

```ts
// Sessions snapshot store — the island's copy of what the Rust observer
// publishes. No state logic lives here: ranks, attention, counts, hold and the
// aggregate are all computed in Rust (spec §10). This file only drops stale
// snapshots (rev guard) and counts the lines the sessions view will draw.

import type {
  Alert, AttentionKind, BotState, ProjectView, SessionView, SessionsSnapshot,
} from "./bridge";
import type { BotStateName, IslandViewName } from "./layout";
import type { SoundName } from "./sound";

/** Acked idle rows of one project beyond this many fold into one "+N idle" line. */
export const IDLE_FOLD_LIMIT = 3;

/**
 * The project's rows in display order: everything that is not an acked Idle row
 * keeps the snapshot order (Rust already ranks it); acked Idle rows go last.
 */
export function splitIdle(project: ProjectView): { live: SessionView[]; idle: SessionView[] } {
  const live: SessionView[] = [];
  const idle: SessionView[] = [];
  for (const s of project.sessions) {
    if (s.phase.kind === "idle" && s.acked) idle.push(s);
    else live.push(s);
  }
  return { live, idle };
}

export class SessionsStore {
  snapshot: SessionsSnapshot | null = null;
  /** Project keys whose "+N idle" fold is open. */
  readonly expandedIdle = new Set<string>();

  private lastRev = -1;
  private listeners = new Set<() => void>();

  /** False (ignored) when s.rev <= the last accepted rev; the first rev accepted is 0. */
  accept(s: SessionsSnapshot): boolean {
    if (s.rev <= this.lastRev) return false;
    this.lastRev = s.rev;
    this.snapshot = s;
    for (const fn of this.listeners) fn();
    return true;
  }

  /** Any project with at least one session. */
  get hasSessions(): boolean {
    return this.snapshot?.projects.some((p) => p.sessions.length > 0) ?? false;
  }

  find(key: string): { session: SessionView; project: ProjectView } | null {
    for (const project of this.snapshot?.projects ?? []) {
      const session = project.sessions.find((s) => s.key === key);
      if (session) return { session, project };
    }
    return null;
  }

  /** True when this project's acked Idle rows are drawn as one "+N idle" line. */
  folded(projectKey: string, ackedIdle: number): boolean {
    return ackedIdle > IDLE_FOLD_LIMIT && !this.expandedIdle.has(projectKey);
  }

  /**
   * 24 px lines the sessions view renders: project headers + visible rows +
   * "+N idle" rows. With no session at all the view draws one empty-state line.
   */
  rowCount(): number {
    let rows = 0;
    for (const project of this.snapshot?.projects ?? []) {
      if (project.sessions.length === 0) continue;
      const { live, idle } = splitIdle(project);
      rows += 1 + live.length + (this.folded(project.key, idle.length) ? 1 : idle.length);
    }
    return Math.max(1, rows);
  }

  subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void {
    this.listeners.add(fn);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(fn);
  }
}

export const Sessions = new SessionsStore();

/** The aggregate names are a subset of Mochi's states: identity mapping. */
export function botStateName(s: BotState): BotStateName {
  return s;
}

/** The card an attention item opens. */
export function viewForAttention(k: Exclude<AttentionKind, null>): IslandViewName {
  switch (k) {
    case "permission":
    case "input":
      return "waiting";
    case "error":
      return "error";
    case "finished":
      return "finished";
  }
}

/** Existing WAVs until the sound set is replaced (sub-project 3). */
export const ALERT_SOUND: Record<Alert["kind"], SoundName> = {
  permission: "approval",
  input: "approval",
  error: "error",
  finished: "finish",
};
```

- [ ] **Step 12: Create `windows/src/island/observer.ts`**

```ts
// Agent sessions → island. The snapshot listener is registered before the
// initial fetch, so a snapshot emitted in between is never lost; the rev guard
// in SessionsStore drops the duplicate.

import { Bridge, onSessions, type SessionsSnapshot } from "../core/bridge";
import { Sessions } from "../core/sessions";
import type { Island } from "./island";

export async function registerObserver(island: Island): Promise<void> {
  const take = (s: SessionsSnapshot) => {
    if (Sessions.accept(s)) island.onSnapshot(s);
  };
  await onSessions(take);
  const initial = await Bridge.sessionsSnapshot();
  if (initial) take(initial);
}
```
