```ts
// App state — mirror of AppState.swift (the parts the island needs).

import type { BotEmoteName, BotStateName, IslandMode, IslandViewName } from "./layout";
import type { EyeShape } from "../mochi/engine";
import { Sessions } from "./sessions";

export type AgentSource = "claudeCode" | "n8n";
export type PillBadge = "approval" | "finished" | "error";

export interface AgentTask {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  color: string;
  state: BotStateName;
  stepIndex: number;
  steps: string[];
  source: AgentSource;
  isIntegration: boolean;
  emote?: BotEmoteName | null;
  miniEye?: EyeShape | null;
  pillBadge?: PillBadge | null;
  sessionCwd?: string | null;
}

export interface ApprovalInfo {
  requestId: string;
  sessionId: string;
  tool: string;
  command: string;
  /** Observer key of the asking session (router annotation), null when unknown. */
  sessionKey: string | null;
  /** Caption of the card: project basename from the router, else the cwd basename. */
  projectName: string;
}

export interface ChatMessage {
  id: number;
  role: "user" | "assistant";
  content: string;
}

export type PromptContext =
  | { kind: "window"; appName: string; title: string; url?: string }
  | { kind: "file"; name: string; path?: string };

export interface ResultItem {
  label: string;
  detail: string;
  url?: string;
}

export interface SearchResult {
  title: string;
  items: ResultItem[];
  note?: string;
}

const task = (
  id: string, name: string, color: string, source: AgentSource,
): AgentTask => ({
  id, name, color, state: "idle", stepIndex: 0, steps: [], source, isIntegration: true,
});

/** AgentTask.integrationAgents — same ids, names and colours as macOS. */
export const INTEGRATION_AGENTS: AgentTask[] = [
  task("integration_resend", "Resend", "#22C55E", "n8n"),
  task("integration_n8n", "n8n", "#F29B38", "n8n"),
  task("integration_vercel", "Vercel", "#7C5CFF", "n8n"),
  task("integration_github", "GitHub", "#F4505E", "n8n"),
  task("integration_notion", "Notion", "#8C8C8C", "n8n"),
  task("integration_calcom", "Cal.com", "#C9956A", "n8n"),
  task("integration_stripe", "Stripe", "#0570DE", "n8n"),
];

export const TOGGLEABLE_INTEGRATION_IDS = [
  "integration_resend", "integration_n8n", "integration_vercel", "integration_github",
  "integration_notion", "integration_calcom", "integration_stripe",
];

/** What an integration poller last reported. */
export interface IntegrationInfo {
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
  error: string | null;
  loaded: boolean;
  configured: boolean;
}

export interface Settings {
  soundEnabled: boolean;
  soundVolume: number;
  autoCloseInterval: number;
  absenceInterval: number;
  activeIntegrations: string[];
  screen: "primary" | "cursor";
  autostart: boolean;
  /** Claude model used by the chat. */
  model: string;
  /** Alert kinds, switched separately; Rust defaults them to true for older files. */
  alertWaiting: boolean;
  alertFinished: boolean;
  alertError: boolean;
}

export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: Settings = {
  soundEnabled: true,
  soundVolume: 0.12,
  autoCloseInterval: 15,
  absenceInterval: 180,
  activeIntegrations: [
    "integration_resend", "integration_n8n", "integration_vercel", "integration_github",
  ],
  screen: "primary",
  autostart: false,
  model: "claude-opus-5",
  alertWaiting: true,
  alertFinished: true,
  alertError: true,
};

type Listener = () => void;

class AppState {
  mode: IslandMode = "hidden";
  view: IslandViewName = "overview";

  tasks: AgentTask[] = [];
  focusId: string | null = null;

  stateOverride: BotStateName | null = null;

  /** Cursor in logical screen pixels, origin top-left (like AppState.mousePosition). */
  mouse = { x: 0, y: 0 };
  /** Cursor relative to the island's top-left corner. */
  mouseInIsland = { x: 0, y: 0 };

  isPinned = false;
  paused = false;

  uploadProgress = 0;
  uploadDuration = 2.4;
  fileDragOver = false;

  promptContext: PromptContext | null = null;
  droppedFile: { name: string; path: string } | null = null;
  noteMessage: string | null = null;
  searchResult: SearchResult | null = null;
  chatHistory: ChatMessage[] = [];
  pendingApproval: ApprovalInfo | null = null;
  /** Session shown by the waiting / finished / error / session cards. */
  alertKey: string | null = null;

  integrations: Record<string, IntegrationInfo> = {};

  lastActivity = performance.now();

  settings: Settings = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS };

  private listeners = new Set<Listener>();

  subscribe(fn: Listener): () => void {
    this.listeners.add(fn);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(fn);
  }

  /** Marks the UI dirty; the island re-renders on the next frame. */
  notify() {
    for (const fn of this.listeners) fn();
  }

  get focusTask(): AgentTask | null {
    return this.tasks.find((t) => t.id === this.focusId) ?? this.tasks[0] ?? null;
  }

  get effectiveState(): BotStateName {
    return this.stateOverride ?? this.focusTask?.state ?? "idle";
  }

  get otherTasks(): AgentTask[] {
    return this.tasks.filter((t) => t.id !== this.focusId);
  }

  setFocus(id: string) {
    const t = this.tasks.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (!t) return;
    this.focusId = id;
    t.pillBadge = null;
    this.notify();
  }

  updateTask(id: string, state: BotStateName) {
    const t = this.tasks.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (!t) return;
    t.state = state;
    this.notify();
  }

  appendStep(id: string, step: string) {
    const t = this.tasks.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (!t) return;
    t.steps.push(step);
    if (t.steps.length > 20) t.steps.shift();
    t.stepIndex = t.steps.length - 1;
    this.notify();
  }

  setPillBadge(id: string, badge: PillBadge | null) {
    const t = this.tasks.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (!t) return;
    t.pillBadge = badge;
    this.notify();
  }

  /** loadIntegrationTasks() — opt-in integrations (max 4), in their declared order. */
  loadIntegrationTasks() {
    for (const proto of INTEGRATION_AGENTS) {
      const shouldLoad = this.settings.activeIntegrations.includes(proto.id);
      const idx = this.tasks.findIndex((t) => t.id === proto.id);
      if (shouldLoad && idx < 0) this.tasks.push({ ...proto, steps: [] });
      if (!shouldLoad && idx >= 0) this.tasks.splice(idx, 1);
    }
    // Keep the declared order so pills never shuffle.
    const order = INTEGRATION_AGENTS.map((t) => t.id);
    this.tasks.sort((a, b) => order.indexOf(a.id) - order.indexOf(b.id));
    // Focus falls back to the first pill, or to nothing when no pill is on.
    if (!this.tasks.some((t) => t.id === this.focusId)) this.focusId = this.tasks[0]?.id ?? null;
    this.notify();
  }

  toggleIntegration(id: string) {
    const active = this.settings.activeIntegrations;
    if (active.includes(id)) {
      this.settings.activeIntegrations = active.filter((x) => x !== id);
    } else {
      if (active.length >= 4) return;
      this.settings.activeIntegrations = [...active, id];
    }
    this.loadIntegrationTasks();
  }

  /** Agent sessions first (spec §10), then the integrations overview. */
  defaultView(): IslandViewName {
    if (Sessions.hasSessions) return "sessions";
    return this.tasks.length === 0 ? "empty" : "overview";
  }
}

export const State = new AppState();
```

```ts
function buildOverview(actions: ViewActions): ViewHost {
  const leftBody = h("div", { class: "left-body" });
  const jump = h(
    "button",
    { class: "icon-btn jump", title: "Open", onclick: () => actions.openTarget() },
    svg(ICONS.arrowUpRight, 8),
  );
  const left = card(null, leftBody, jump);
  const pills = h("div", { class: "pills" });
  const right = card(null, pills);

  const el = h("div", { class: "view overview" },
    h("div", { class: "left" }, left),
    h("div", { class: "right" }, right),
  );

  let pillIds = "";
  let detailOpen = false;
  let lastFocus: string | null = null;
  let cardKey = "";

  const hooks: IntegrationCardHooks = {
    get detailOpen() {
      return detailOpen;
    },
    openDetail() {
      detailOpen = true;
      cardKey = "";
      State.notify();
    },
    closeDetail() {
      detailOpen = false;
      cardKey = "";
      State.notify();
    },
    openSettings: () => actions.openSettingsWindow(),
  };

  return {
    el,
    sync() {
      const task = State.focusTask;
      if (task?.id !== lastFocus) {
        lastFocus = task?.id ?? null;
        detailOpen = false;
        cardKey = "";
      }

      // Every pill shows its own card, exactly like IntegrationCardView. Agent
      // sessions have their own view ("sessions").
      if (task) {
        const info = State.integrations[task.id];
        const key = [
          task.id, detailOpen, task.state, task.steps.join("|"),
          info?.loaded, info?.error, info?.configured,
          JSON.stringify(info?.data ?? {}),
        ].join("~");
        if (key !== cardKey) {
          cardKey = key;
          clear(leftBody);
          leftBody.append(renderIntegrationCard(task, hooks));
        }
      }

      jump.style.display = detailOpen ? "none" : "";

      const others = State.otherTasks.slice(0, 4);
      const pillKey = others.map((t) => `${t.id}:${t.pillBadge ?? ""}`).join("|");
      if (pillKey !== pillIds) {
        pillIds = pillKey;
        clear(pills);
        for (const t of others) pills.append(buildPill(t, actions));
        pruneMiniBots();
      }
    },
  };
}

Layout check (D35): Task 16 already added `"sessions" | "waiting" | "session"` to `IslandViewName` and their `VIEW_LAYOUTS` entries exactly as contract §4.4 lists them; this task does not add them again. Step 0 checks the three `VIEW_LAYOUTS` entries against contract §4.4 and changes nothing when they match; Step 1 only adds `sessionsHeight` and the `islandSize` parameter.

Contract amendment (contract §7 D63–D65; the spec wins over the contract):
- **D63** One alert sound per batch, played only when the batch opens or replaces a card or lands on the sessions list: hidden, compact or the launch greeting (D64) → sound, then `island.alert`; an expanded `waiting`/`finished`/`error` card outranked by the top alert → sound, then the card is replaced; expanded `"sessions"` → sound, the view stays. A card that is not outranked, `"approval"` and every other expanded view only call `State.notify()` (counters and pager), without a sound. Contract §4.4 says "At most one sound `ALERT_SOUND[top.kind]` per batch, played only when the batch opens or replaces a card or lands on the sessions list (D63)"; this reads spec §10, which names a sound for hidden/compact ("Один звук на пачку") and for `"sessions"` ("звучит звук"), while for another view "обновляются только счётчики" and for an open card that is not outranked "обновляется только счётчик листалки". A sound over the approval card would read as being about the request on screen.
- **D64** The launch greeting (`State.view === "greeting"`, FSM `coucou`) is neither a view the user chose nor a card, so `handleAlerts` treats it like hidden/compact: the top alert opens its card via `island.alert` (the legacy approval path already interrupts the greeting through `forceHome`). The `coucou → home` transition calls `greeting.interrupt()`, so the greeting's timed `greet`/`blip` sounds do not follow the alert's sound (and no longer follow an approval card or a file drop that cuts the greeting short).
- **D65** Alert cards fall back when the snapshot cannot show `State.alertKey`. `state.ts` gains `export type CardSubject = { alert: Alert } | { session: SessionView; project: ProjectView }` and `State.alertFallback: CardSubject | null = null`. `handleAlerts` stores `{ alert: top }` whenever it sets `alertKey`; `Island.onSnapshot` clears an alert fallback, because spec §9 emits a batch's `session-alert` just before the `sessions` snapshot that contains it (it is cleared by that next snapshot, not only once a snapshot shows the key in the alerted state: one batch can carry a session past that state — a Codex `PermissionRequest` and `Stop` in one batch leave it Idle/finished — and the card would then keep showing a wait that is over); `openSession` stores the clicked `{ session, project }` before `session_ack`, because spec §7 removes an Idle Codex session without a process on ack. `cardSubject()` (views/sessions.ts) returns the alert fallback for the key, else `Sessions.find(key)`, else the row fallback for the key; the waiting/finished/error cards render from it (`Alert.detail` is the alert body: detail for permission/input, summary for finished, error summary for error — contract §2.15, T9 `complete_alerts`), the session card from a row subject. An alert carries the project name but no project key, so its who-line has no project dot (as the approval card, D59). `cardRank` reads the same subject.

Contract §4.4 (the D63/D64 branches of `handleAlerts`; `CardSubject`, `State.alertFallback`, `cardSubject`, `subjectWho`, `outcomeSummary`) and the T17 entry of contract §6 already state these rules. No task step edits `contract.md`.

    const snap = Sessions.hasSessions ? Sessions.snapshot : null;
    return this.stateOverride ?? (snap ? botStateName(snap.aggregate) : this.focusTask?.state ?? "idle");
  }
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Create `windows/src/views/sessions.ts`**

```ts
// Agent sessions views: the project-grouped list ("sessions"), the read-only
// waiting card ("waiting") and the details card of any session ("session"),
// plus the pieces the finished / error cards share with them. Everything shown
// comes from the Rust snapshot (spec §10). The only value computed here is the
// elapsed time, rewritten once a second while a view is really on screen and
// never through State.notify(), so the frame loop stays asleep.

import { h, svg, clear, dot } from "./dom";
import { ICONS } from "./icons";
import { washRGBA, type Wash } from "../core/layout";
import { Sessions, splitIdle } from "../core/sessions";
import { State, type CardSubject } from "../core/state";
import type { Host, ProjectView, SessionView } from "../core/bridge";
import type { ViewActions, ViewHost } from "./views";

// ── Labels ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export const HOST_LABEL: Record<Host, string> = {
  claudeDesktop: "Desktop",
  cursor: "Cursor",
  vsCode: "VS Code",
  codexDesktop: "Codex app",
  unknown: "Other",
};

const AGENT_NAME = { claude: "Claude", codex: "Codex" } as const;
const AGENT_GLYPH = { claude: "C", codex: "X" } as const;

/** Spec §10 project dot (D60): FNV-1a 32 of the project key into a fixed palette. */
const PROJECT_PALETTE = [
  "#38BDF8", "#F29B38", "#7C5CFF", "#2EC4A0", "#EC4899", "#EAB308", "#FF5A4E", "#60A5FA",
];

export function colorForProject(projectKey: string): string {
  let hash = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (let i = 0; i < projectKey.length; i++) {
    hash ^= projectKey.charCodeAt(i);
    hash = Math.imul(hash, 0x01000193) >>> 0;
  }
  return PROJECT_PALETTE[hash % PROJECT_PALETTE.length];
}

/** "<60s" → "Ns"; "<60m" → "Nm"; else "Hh MMm". */
export function formatElapsed(ms: number): string {
  const s = Math.max(0, Math.floor(ms / 1000));
  if (s < 60) return `${s}s`;
  const m = Math.floor(s / 60);
  if (m < 60) return `${m}m`;
  return `${Math.floor(m / 60)}h ${String(m % 60).padStart(2, "0")}m`;
}

/** Short phase word of a row. */
export function phaseLabel(s: SessionView): string {
  switch (s.phase.kind) {
    case "working":
      return "working";
    case "waiting":
      if (s.phase.wait === "permission") return "needs permission";
      if (s.phase.wait === "input") return "asks";
      return s.phase.label || "waiting";
    case "idle":
      return s.outcome?.kind ?? "idle";
    case "unknown":
      return s.phase.label || "unknown";
  }
}

/** Colour family of the phase word. */
function tone(s: SessionView): "amber" | "red" | "green" | "blue" | "dim" {
  if (s.phase.kind === "waiting") return "amber";
  if (s.phase.kind === "working") return "blue";
  if (s.phase.kind === "idle" && s.outcome?.kind === "error") return "red";
  if (s.phase.kind === "idle" && s.outcome?.kind === "finished") return "green";
  return "dim";
}

/** What the row's detail column says. */
function rowDetail(s: SessionView): string {
  switch (s.phase.kind) {
    case "waiting":
      return s.detail ?? s.title ?? "";
    case "working":
      return s.activity ?? s.detail ?? s.title ?? "";
    case "idle":
      return s.outcome?.summary || s.title || "";
    case "unknown":
      return s.title ?? "";
  }
}

// ── Shared pieces ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** Elapsed-time text nodes of one view, rewritten by its 1 s clock. */
interface Clock {
  el: HTMLElement;
  since: number;
  prefix: string;
}

function tickClocks(clocks: Clock[]) {
  const now = Date.now();
  for (const c of clocks) c.el.textContent = `${c.prefix}${formatElapsed(now - c.since)}`;
}

/** One 1 s interval per view, alive only while the view is active (D57). */
function clockRunner(clocks: () => Clock[]): (on: boolean) => void {
  let timer: number | null = null;
  return (on) => {
    if (on && timer == null) {
      tickClocks(clocks());
      timer = window.setInterval(() => tickClocks(clocks()), 1000);
    } else if (!on && timer != null) {
      window.clearInterval(timer);
      timer = null;
    }
  };
}

function cardEl(wash: Wash, ...children: Node[]): HTMLElement {
  const el = h("div", { class: wash ? "card wash" : "card" }, ...children);
  if (wash) el.style.setProperty("--wash", washRGBA(wash));
  return el;
}

function stackEl(...children: Node[]): HTMLElement {
  const el = h("div", { class: "stack" }, ...children);
  el.style.padding = "4px 16px 4px 116px";
  return el;
}

function button(label: string, kind: "primary" | "secondary", onClick: () => void): HTMLElement {
  return h("button", { class: `btn ${kind}`, onclick: onClick }, h("span", { text: label }));
}

/** Coloured project dot, project name, "Agent · Host", then an optional verb. */
export function sessionWho(
  found: { session: SessionView; project: ProjectView },
  verb?: string,
): HTMLElement {
  const { session, project } = found;
  return h(
    "div",
    { class: "who-row" },
    dot(colorForProject(project.key), 8),
    h("span", { class: "n", text: project.name }),
    h("span", { text: `${AGENT_NAME[session.agent]} · ${HOST_LABEL[session.host]}` }),
    verb ? h("span", { class: "who-verb", text: verb }) : null,
  );
}

/**
 * What the card of State.alertKey shows: the alert that opened it until the next
 * snapshot is in (spec §9 sends the alert first), else the live row, else the
 * row that was clicked when its ack removed the session (spec §7).
 */
export function cardSubject(): CardSubject | null {
  const key = State.alertKey;
  if (!key) return null;
  const fallback = State.alertFallback;
  if (fallback && "alert" in fallback && fallback.alert.key === key) return fallback;
  const found = Sessions.find(key);
  if (found) return found;
  if (fallback && "session" in fallback && fallback.session.key === key) return fallback;
  return null;
}

/** sessionWho for a card subject. An alert names the project but has no project key: no dot. */
export function subjectWho(subject: CardSubject, verb?: string): HTMLElement {
  if (!("alert" in subject)) return sessionWho(subject, verb);
  const a = subject.alert;
  return h(
    "div",
    { class: "who-row" },
    h("span", { class: "n", text: a.project }),
    h("span", { text: `${AGENT_NAME[a.agent]} · ${HOST_LABEL[a.host]}` }),
    verb ? h("span", { class: "who-verb", text: verb }) : null,
  );
}

/**
 * Summary of a finished / error turn: the row's outcome, or the alert's body
 * (Alert.detail carries the summary / error summary for those kinds).
 */
export function outcomeSummary(subject: CardSubject | null, kind: "finished" | "error"): string {
  if (!subject) return "";
  if ("alert" in subject) return subject.alert.kind === kind ? subject.alert.detail ?? "" : "";
  const o = subject.session.outcome;
  return o?.kind === kind ? o.summary : "";
}

/** ‹ n/m › over snapshot.attention (unacked episodes only). */
export function buildPager(actions: ViewActions): { el: HTMLElement; sync(): void } {
  const label = h("span", { class: "pager-label" });
  const el = h(
    "div",
    { class: "pager" },
    h("button", { class: "pager-btn", title: "Previous", onclick: () => actions.pageAlert(-1) },
      svg(ICONS.chevronLeft, 9, { stroke: 2.4 })),
    label,
    h("button", { class: "pager-btn", title: "Next", onclick: () => actions.pageAlert(1) },
      svg(ICONS.chevronRight, 9, { stroke: 2.4 })),
  );
  return {
    el,
    sync() {
      const list = Sessions.snapshot?.attention ?? [];
      const idx = State.alertKey ? list.indexOf(State.alertKey) : -1;
      const others = idx >= 0 ? list.length - 1 : list.length;
      el.style.display = others > 0 ? "" : "none";
      label.textContent = idx >= 0 ? `${idx + 1}/${list.length}` : `${list.length} more`;
    },
  };
}

// ── Sessions list ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export function buildSessions(actions: ViewActions): ViewHost {
  const list = h("div", { class: "sess-list" });
  const el = h("div", { class: "view" }, h("div", { class: "card sess-card" }, list));
  let clocks: Clock[] = [];
  let renderedKey = "";
  const runClock = clockRunner(() => clocks);

  // Rows act on mousedown: a snapshot can rebuild the list between the press
  // and the release, which would swallow a click.
  const onPress = (fn: () => void) => (e: Event) => {
    if ((e as MouseEvent).button === 0) fn();
  };

  function row(s: SessionView, dim: boolean): HTMLElement {
    const time = h("span", { class: "sess-time", text: formatElapsed(Date.now() - s.since) });
    clocks.push({ el: time, since: s.since, prefix: "" });
    const cls = ["sess-row", `tone-${tone(s)}`, s.agent];
    if (dim) cls.push("dim");
    if (s.attention) cls.push("attn");
    return h(
      "div",
      { class: cls.join(" "), onmousedown: onPress(() => actions.openSession(s.key)) },
      h("span", { class: "sess-agent", title: AGENT_NAME[s.agent], text: AGENT_GLYPH[s.agent] }),
      h("span", { class: "sess-host", text: HOST_LABEL[s.host] }),
      h("span", { class: "sess-phase", text: phaseLabel(s) }),
      h("span", { class: "sess-detail", text: rowDetail(s) }),
      time,
    );
  }

  function projectHeader(project: ProjectView): HTMLElement {
    const hosts = [...new Set(project.sessions.map((s) => s.host))].filter((x) => x !== "unknown");
    return h(
      "div",
      { class: "sess-project", title: project.root },
      dot(colorForProject(project.key), 7),
      h("span", { class: "sess-pname", text: project.name }),
      ...hosts.map((x) => h("span", { class: "sess-hostlabel", text: HOST_LABEL[x] })),
      // Sub-project 2 puts the project's app windows here.
      h("span", { class: "sess-apps" }),
    );
  }

  function render() {
    clear(list);
    clocks = [];
    const projects = (Sessions.snapshot?.projects ?? []).filter((p) => p.sessions.length > 0);
    if (projects.length === 0) {
      list.append(h("div", { class: "sess-empty", text: "No agent sessions right now." }));
      return;
    }
    for (const project of projects) {
      list.append(projectHeader(project));
      const { live, idle } = splitIdle(project);
      for (const s of live) list.append(row(s, false));
      if (Sessions.folded(project.key, idle.length)) {
        list.append(h("div", {
          class: "sess-fold",
          text: `+${idle.length} idle`,
          onmousedown: onPress(() => actions.toggleIdleFold(project.key)),
        }));
      } else {
        for (const s of idle) list.append(row(s, true));
      }
    }
  }

  return {
    el,
    sync() {
      const key = `${Sessions.snapshot?.rev ?? -1}|${[...Sessions.expandedIdle].join("|")}`;
      if (key === renderedKey) return;
      renderedKey = key;
      render();
    },
    setActive(on: boolean) {
      runClock(on);
      // The "+N idle" folds close again once the list is left.
      if (!on && Sessions.expandedIdle.size > 0) Sessions.expandedIdle.clear();
    },
  };
}

// ── Waiting card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface WaitFacts {
  wait: "permission" | "input" | "other";
  text: string | null;
  since: number;
  verb: string;
}

/** The waiting card's content, from the row or from the alert; null when nothing waits. */
function waitFacts(subject: CardSubject): WaitFacts | null {
  if ("alert" in subject) {
    const a = subject.alert;
    if (a.kind !== "permission" && a.kind !== "input") return null;
    const verb = a.kind === "permission" ? "needs permission" : "asks";
    return { wait: a.kind, text: a.detail ?? a.title, since: a.since, verb };
  }
  const s = subject.session;
  if (s.phase.kind !== "waiting") return null;
  return { wait: s.phase.wait, text: s.detail ?? s.title, since: s.since, verb: phaseLabel(s) };
}

export function buildWaiting(actions: ViewActions): ViewHost {
  const who = h("div");
  const target = h("div", { class: "code" });
  const question = h("div", { class: "title sess-clamp" });
  const waited = h("span", { class: "sess-waited" });
  const pager = buildPager(actions);
  const row = h(
    "div",
    { class: "actions sess-actions" },
    button("OK", "primary", () => actions.ackAlert()),
    waited,
    h("div", { class: "grow" }),
    pager.el,
  );
  const el = h("div", { class: "view" }, cardEl("amber", stackEl(who, target, question, row)));
  let clocks: Clock[] = [];
  const runClock = clockRunner(() => clocks);

  return {
    el,
    sync() {
      const subject = cardSubject();
      const w = subject ? waitFacts(subject) : null;
      clear(who);
      clocks = [];
      waited.textContent = "";
      target.style.display = "none";
      question.style.display = "";
      if (!subject) {
        question.textContent = "…";
      } else if (!w) {
        who.append(subjectWho(subject));
        question.textContent = "Not waiting any more.";
      } else {
        who.append(subjectWho(subject, w.verb));
        if (w.wait === "permission") {
          // Read-only: the answer is given in the agent itself.
          target.style.display = "";
          target.textContent = w.text ?? "…";
          question.style.display = "none";
        } else {
          question.textContent = w.text ?? "Needs your input.";
        }
        clocks.push({ el: waited, since: w.since, prefix: "waiting " });
        tickClocks(clocks);
      }
      pager.sync();
    },
    setActive: runClock,
  };
}

// ── Session card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export function buildSession(actions: ViewActions): ViewHost {
  const who = h("div");
  const phase = h("div", { class: "title" });
  const activity = h("div", { class: "sub sess-line" });
  const outcome = h("div", { class: "sub sess-line" });
  const since = h("span", { class: "sess-waited" });
  const row = h(
    "div",
    { class: "actions sess-actions" },
    button("↗ Open", "primary", () => actions.openSessionTarget()),
    since,
  );
  const el = h("div", { class: "view" }, cardEl("soft", stackEl(who, phase, activity, outcome, row)));
  let clocks: Clock[] = [];
  const runClock = clockRunner(() => clocks);

  return {
    el,
    sync() {
      const subject = cardSubject();
      clear(who);
      clocks = [];
      since.textContent = "";
      // Opened from a row; an alert subject belongs to the waiting / finished / error cards.
      if (!subject || "alert" in subject) {
        phase.textContent = "…";
        activity.textContent = "";
        outcome.style.display = "none";
        return;
      }
      const s = subject.session;
      who.append(sessionWho(subject));
      const word = phaseLabel(s);
      phase.textContent = word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1);
      activity.textContent = s.activity ?? s.detail ?? s.title ?? "";
      const o = s.outcome;
      outcome.style.display = o ? "" : "none";
      if (o) {
        const head = o.kind === "finished" ? "Finished" : o.kind === "error" ? "Error" : "Interrupted";
        outcome.textContent = o.summary ? `${head}: ${o.summary}` : head;
      }
      clocks.push({ el: since, since: s.since, prefix: "for " });
      tickClocks(clocks);
    },
    setActive: runClock,
  };
}
```

        const next =
          idx < 0 ? (step === 1 ? 0 : list.length - 1) : (idx + step + list.length) % list.length;

- [ ] **Step 14: `onSnapshot`, `handleAlerts` and `cardRank` in `windows/src/island/island.ts` (D63–D65)**

Replace

```ts
  /** A sessions snapshot passed the rev guard (island/observer.ts). */
  onSnapshot(_s: SessionsSnapshot) {
    State.notify();
    if (State.mode === "expanded" && State.view === "sessions") this.animateGeometry(false);
  }
```

with

```ts
  /** A sessions snapshot passed the rev guard (island/observer.ts). */
  onSnapshot(s: SessionsSnapshot) {
    this.fsm.setHoldVisible(s.hold);
    // Spec §9 sends an alert batch just before the snapshot that contains it, so
    // from this snapshot on the cards read the session again, not the alert.
    if (State.alertFallback && "alert" in State.alertFallback) State.alertFallback = null;
    State.notify();
    if (State.mode === "expanded" && State.view === "sessions") this.animateGeometry(false);
  }

  /**
   * One batch of model alerts (spec §10). Kinds turned off in the settings never
   * reach here (Rust drops them); pause is applied here. One sound per batch,
   * only when it opens or replaces a card or lands on the sessions list.
   */
  handleAlerts(alerts: Alert[]) {
    if (State.paused) return;
    // A live legacy approval card already stands for that session's permission.
    const approvalKey = State.pendingApproval?.sessionKey ?? null;
    const batch = alerts.filter(
      (a) => !(a.kind === "permission" && approvalKey !== null && a.key === approvalKey),
    );
    if (batch.length === 0) return;
    // Most important = smallest rank; ties keep the batch order.
    const top = batch.reduce((best, a) => (a.rank < best.rank ? a : best));
    const view = State.view;

    // Hidden, compact, or the launch greeting: none of them is a view the user chose.
    if (State.mode !== "expanded" || view === "greeting") {
      Sound.play(ALERT_SOUND[top.kind]);
      State.alertKey = top.key;
      State.alertFallback = { alert: top };
      this.alert(viewForAttention(top.kind));
    } else if ((view === "waiting" || view === "finished" || view === "error") && top.rank < this.cardRank(view)) {
      Sound.play(ALERT_SOUND[top.kind]);
      State.alertKey = top.key;
      State.alertFallback = { alert: top };
      this.setView(viewForAttention(top.kind));
    } else if (view === "sessions") {
      // The rows re-sort from the snapshot that follows; the view stays.
      Sound.play(ALERT_SOUND[top.kind]);
      State.notify();
    } else {
      // A card that is not outranked, the approval card and every other view keep
      // the screen without a sound: only the counters and the pager move.
      State.notify();
    }
  }

  /** Rank of the alert card on screen, on the same 0..3 scale as Alert.rank. */
  private cardRank(view: "waiting" | "finished" | "error"): number {
    if (view === "error") return 2;
    if (view === "finished") return 3;
    const subject = cardSubject();
    if (subject && "alert" in subject) return subject.alert.rank;
    const phase = subject?.session.phase;
    return phase?.kind === "waiting" && phase.wait === "permission" ? 0 : 1;
  }
```

  /** `!n` `✕n` `✓n` `•n`, non-zero values only (D34). */
  private syncCounters() {
    const c = Sessions.snapshot?.counts;
    if (!c) return;
    const key = COUNTERS.map(([k]) => c[k]).join("|");
    if (this.counters.dataset.key === key) return;
    this.counters.dataset.key = key;
    this.counters.replaceChildren(
      ...COUNTERS.filter(([k]) => c[k] > 0).map(([k, glyph, tone]) =>
        h("span", { class: `cnt ${tone}`, text: `${glyph}${c[k]}` }),
      ),
    );
  }

  /** Applies settings coming from Rust at boot. */

```ts
// Legacy Claude Code Allow/Deny (Settings → Advanced, off by default).
// The router forwards to the island only Claude PermissionRequest payloads that
// carry a request_id (spec §5.3); every other Claude event is read by the
// observer, and Codex never gets an answer from the island.

import { Bridge, onEvent } from "../core/bridge";
import { Sound } from "../core/sound";
import { State } from "../core/state";
import type { Island } from "./island";

/** Clears the approval card if no decision was made before the hook gave up. */
let pendingTimeout: number | null = null;

interface HookPayload {
  hook_event_name?: string;
  request_id?: string;
  session_id?: string;
  cwd?: string;
  tool_name?: string;
  tool_input?: Record<string, unknown>;
  /** Router annotations (null when the observer has no match). */
  session_key?: string | null;
  project_name?: string | null;
}

const PROJECT_ALIASES: Record<string, string> = {
  "notch-buddy": "Notch Buddy",
  notchbuddy: "Notch Buddy",
  notch_buddy: "Notch Buddy",
};

function aliasProjectName(name: string): string {
  return PROJECT_ALIASES[name.toLowerCase()] ?? name;
}

function lastPathComponent(p: string): string {
  const cleaned = p.replace(/[\\/]+$/, "");
  const idx = Math.max(cleaned.lastIndexOf("\\"), cleaned.lastIndexOf("/"));
  return idx >= 0 ? cleaned.slice(idx + 1) : cleaned;
}

/**
 * What the Allow button actually authorises. Approving "Write" tells you nothing
 * — approving `Write · C:\…\.env` tells you everything, and the difference is
 * the whole point of approving from the island rather than blind.
 *
 * Ordered by how specific the field is, so an unfamiliar tool still shows
 * whatever identifying string it carries instead of falling back to its name.
 */
const APPROVAL_FIELDS = [
  "command", // Bash, PowerShell
  "file_path", // Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit
  "path", // Read, LS
  "url", // WebFetch
  "query", // WebSearch
  "pattern", // Glob, Grep
  "prompt", // Task
] as const;

function approvalTarget(tool: string, input: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  for (const field of APPROVAL_FIELDS) {
    const value = input[field];
    if (typeof value === "string" && value.trim()) {
      return `${tool} · ${value.trim()}`;
    }
  }
  return tool;
}

export function registerHookHandlers(island: Island) {
  void onEvent<HookPayload>("hook", (payload) => handleHook(island, payload));
}

function handleHook(island: Island, payload: HookPayload) {
  const requestId = payload.request_id ?? "";
  if (payload.hook_event_name !== "PermissionRequest" || !requestId) return;

  if (State.paused) {
    // Silence here used to cost Claude Code nearly two minutes: the relay waited
    // for a decision from an island that had already decided not to look. Say so,
    // and the terminal takes the question immediately.
    void Bridge.approvalDecline(requestId);
    return;
  }
  // One card, one request. A second one must never quietly replace the first
  // — that would leave a human staring at request B while request A waits for
  // a decision nobody can give. Hand it straight back to the terminal.
  if (State.pendingApproval && State.pendingApproval.requestId !== requestId) {
    void Bridge.approvalDecline(requestId);
    return;
  }

  if (pendingTimeout != null) window.clearTimeout(pendingTimeout);
  const tool = payload.tool_name ?? "Tool";
  const input = payload.tool_input ?? {};
  const cwdName = aliasProjectName(lastPathComponent(payload.cwd ?? "") || "Session");
  State.pendingApproval = {
    requestId,
    sessionId: payload.session_id ?? "",
    tool,
    command: approvalTarget(tool, input),
    sessionKey: payload.session_key ?? null,
    projectName: payload.project_name || cwdName,
  };
  // The relay's short ack window closes in 800 ms; everything below this
  // line is synchronous, so the card really is up by the time it lands.
  void Bridge.approvalAck(requestId);
  State.isPinned = true;
  Sound.play("approval");
  // Opens the card, or replaces a waiting card of the same session in place.
  island.alert("approval");
  // Mayak answers within 108 s or not at all; after that the terminal has
  // taken over and the card would be lying.
  pendingTimeout = window.setTimeout(() => {
    pendingTimeout = null;
    if (!State.pendingApproval) return;
    State.pendingApproval = null;
    State.isPinned = false;
    island.dropPin();
    if (State.view === "approval") island.setView(State.defaultView());
    State.notify();
  }, 110_000);
  State.notify();
}
```

The Claude API, Integrations and General sections are copied unchanged. Replace the whole file with:

```ts
// Settings window — the place where anything that writes to disk is confirmed.
// Agent sessions are observed with no setup at all. The Codex hooks and the
// legacy Claude Code Allow/Deny hook are optional, and both go through the same
// status → preview (exact diff) → apply flow.

import "./settings.css";
import {
  Bridge, onEvent, type Health, type HookPreview, type HookStatus, type HookTarget,
  type SessionsSnapshot,
} from "../core/bridge";
import { DEFAULT_SETTINGS, type Settings } from "../core/state";
import { HOST_LABEL } from "../views/sessions";
import { h, clear } from "../views/dom";

let settings: Settings = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS };
let version = "";
let snapshot: SessionsSnapshot | null = null;
/** Rev of `snapshot`: an older answer never replaces a newer one (spec §9). */
let lastRev = -1;
/** Parts of the page drawn from the sessions snapshot, redrawn on every refresh. */
const snapshotViews: ((s: SessionsSnapshot | null) => void)[] = [];
/** One status refresher per integrationSection, run on every window focus. */
const statusLoaders: (() => Promise<void>)[] = [];

const root = document.getElementById("settings-root")!;

async function save() {
  await Bridge.saveSettings(settings);
}

/** Takes `s` only when it is newer than the snapshot already shown (spec §9). */
function takeSnapshot(s: SessionsSnapshot | null): boolean {
  if (!s || s.rev <= lastRev) return false;
  lastRev = s.rev;
  snapshot = s;
  return true;
}

/** The snapshot is fetched at boot and again every time the window gets focus (D37). */
async function refreshSnapshot() {
  if (!takeSnapshot(await Bridge.sessionsSnapshot())) return;
  for (const draw of snapshotViews) draw(snapshot);
}

/** Every show of the window re-reads what it displays: the snapshot and the hook status. */
function refreshOnFocus() {
  void refreshSnapshot();
  for (const refresh of statusLoaders) void refresh();
}

// ── Reusable bits ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function toggle(on: boolean, onChange: (v: boolean) => void): HTMLElement {
  const el = h("button", { class: on ? "switch on" : "switch", "aria-pressed": on });
  el.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const next = !el.classList.contains("on");
    el.classList.toggle("on", next);
    onChange(next);
  });
  return el;
}

function colorDot(color: string): HTMLElement {
  return h("i", { class: "dot", style: `background:${color}` });
}

function statusDot(ok: boolean): HTMLElement {
  return colorDot(ok ? "#22c55e" : "#f4505e");
}

function renderDiff(text: string): HTMLElement {
  const box = h("div", { class: "diff" });
  for (const line of text.split("\n")) {
    const cls = line.startsWith("+") ? "add" : line.startsWith("-") ? "del" : "ctx";
    box.append(h("div", { class: cls, text: line }));
  }
  return box;
}

function healthView(health: Health): { color: string; text: string } {
  if (health === "ok") return { color: "#22c55e", text: "OK" };
  if (health === "missing") return { color: "#f5a524", text: "Folder not found" };
  if ("error" in health) return { color: "#f4505e", text: `Error: ${health.error}` };
  return { color: "#f5a524", text: `Degraded — ${health.degraded.unreadable} unreadable` };
}

// ── Hook installer (shared by Codex and the legacy Claude block) ──────────────

const TARGET_FILE: Record<HookTarget, string> = {
  claude: "settings.json",
  codex: "hooks.json",
};

function integrationSection(target: HookTarget): HTMLElement {
  const file = TARGET_FILE[target];
  const body = h("div", { class: "integration" });
  let status: HookStatus | null = null;
  /** True while the status rows are on screen (not a preview, an error or a result). */
  let showingStatus = false;

  async function load() {
    showingStatus = false;
    clear(body);
    body.append(h("div", { class: "hint", text: "Checking…" }));
    status = await Bridge.hooksStatus(target);
    clear(body);
    draw();
  }

  /** Window focus: the file may have been changed outside Mayak since it was read. */
  async function refresh() {
    // ~/.claude/settings.json is read only while the Advanced block is open (spec §8).
    const advanced = body.closest("details");
    if (!showingStatus || (advanced !== null && !advanced.open)) return;
    const next = await Bridge.hooksStatus(target);
    // A preview opened while the status was being read keeps the screen.
    if (!showingStatus) return;
    status = next;
    clear(body);
    draw();
  }

  function draw() {
    showingStatus = true;
    const st = status;
    if (!st) {
      body.append(h("div", { class: "notice err", text: `Could not read the status of ${file}.` }));
      return;
    }
    const state = st.installed ? (st.outdated ? "Installed — out of date" : "Installed") : "Not installed";
    body.append(
      h("div", { class: "row" }, h("label", { text: "Status" }), statusDot(st.installed && !st.outdated),
        h("span", { text: state })),
      h("div", { class: "row" }, h("label", { text: file }), h("span", { class: "path", text: st.settingsPath })),
      h("div", { class: "row" },
        h("label", { text: "Relay" }),
        h("span", { class: "path", text: st.hookPath }),
        statusDot(st.hookReady),
      ),
    );
    for (const note of st.notes) body.append(h("div", { class: "notice warn", text: note }));
    if (!st.hookReady) {
      body.append(h("div", {
        class: "notice warn",
        text: "mayak-hook.exe is not in place yet. Restart Mayak; if it still fails, build it with `cargo build -p mayak-hook`.",
      }));
    }

    const actions = h("div", { class: "row" });
    const install = h("button", {
      class: "primary",
      text: st.installed ? (st.outdated ? "Update…" : "Reinstall…") : "Install…",
      onclick: () => void showPreview(true),
    });
    // Writing hook commands that point at a relay which isn't there would give
    // every session a broken hook and nothing to show for it.
    if (!st.hookReady) {
      install.disabled = true;
      install.title = "The relay isn't installed yet.";
    }
    actions.append(install);
    if (st.installed) {
      actions.append(h("button", { class: "danger", text: "Remove…", onclick: () => void showPreview(false) }));
    }
    body.append(actions);
  }

  async function showPreview(install: boolean) {
    showingStatus = false;
    let preview: HookPreview;
    try {
      preview = await Bridge.hooksPreview(install, target);
    } catch (err) {
      // An unreadable or invalid file stops here rather than being treated as
      // empty and written over.
      clear(body);
      body.append(
        h("div", { class: "notice err", text: String(err).replace(/^Error:\s*/, "") }),
        h("div", { class: "row" }, h("button", { text: "Back", onclick: () => { clear(body); draw(); } })),
      );
      return;
    }
    clear(body);
    body.append(h("div", {
      class: "hint",
      text: install
        ? `This is exactly what will change in ${file}. Entries that are not Mayak's stay where they are.`
        : `This removes Mayak's entries only. Everything else in ${file} stays as it is.`,
    }));
    const confirm = h("button", {
      class: install ? "primary" : "danger",
      text: install ? "Back up and write" : "Back up and remove",
    });
    if (preview.unchanged) {
      // The entry is already exactly there: nothing would be written (D53).
      body.append(h("div", { class: "notice ok", text: "No change." }));
      confirm.disabled = true;
    } else {
      body.append(
        renderDiff(preview.diff),
        // hooks_apply backs up only a file that exists, and the preview cannot tell.
        h("div", { class: "row" }, h("span", {
          class: "path",
          text: `Backup (made only if the file already exists) → ${preview.backup}`,
        })),
      );
    }
    for (const note of preview.notes) body.append(h("div", { class: "notice warn", text: note }));
    confirm.addEventListener("click", async () => {
      confirm.disabled = true;
      try {
        const backup = await Bridge.hooksApply(install, preview.fingerprint, target);
        clear(body);
        body.append(h("div", {
          class: "notice ok",
          text: backup === ""
            ? "Done. There was no previous file, so there is no backup."
            : `Done. The previous file is saved as ${backup}.`,
        }));
        window.setTimeout(() => {
          void load();
          // The store has had time to apply CodexHooksInstalled by now.
          if (target === "codex") void refreshSnapshot();
        }, 2600);
      } catch (err) {
        confirm.disabled = false;
        body.append(h("div", { class: "notice err", text: `Could not write: ${String(err)}` }));
      }
    });
    body.append(h("div", { class: "row" }, confirm, h("button", {
      text: "Cancel",
      onclick: () => { clear(body); draw(); },
    })));
  }

  statusLoaders.push(refresh);
  void load();
  return body;
}

// ── Agent sessions: sources ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

function sourcesSection(snap: SessionsSnapshot | null): HTMLElement {
  const rows = h("div", { style: "display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px" });
  const draw = (s: SessionsSnapshot | null) => {
    clear(rows);
    if (!s) {
      rows.append(h("div", { class: "hint", text: "The observer has not published anything yet." }));
      return;
    }
    const line = (label: string, what: string, health: Health) => {
      const v = healthView(health);
      return h("div", { class: "row" },
        h("label", { text: label }), colorDot(v.color), h("span", { text: v.text }),
        h("span", { class: "hint", text: what }));
    };
    rows.append(
      line("Claude Code", "~/.claude/sessions and transcripts, read-only", s.sources.claude),
      line("Codex", "rollouts named by Codex hooks, read-only", s.sources.codex),
    );
  };
  draw(snap);
  snapshotViews.push(draw);
  return h(
    "section",
    {},
    h("h2", {}, h("span", { text: "Agent sessions" })),
    h("div", {
      class: "hint",
      text: "Claude Code sessions (Desktop, Cursor, VS Code) are read from the files Claude Code keeps for itself. Nothing is written to their configuration.",
    }),
    rows,
  );
}

// ── Codex ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function receivingText(s: SessionsSnapshot | null): string {
  if (!s) return "Unknown.";
  const hooks = s.sources.codexHooks;
  if (hooks === "not_installed") return "Not installed.";
  if (hooks === "installed_unseen") {
    return "Installed. No Codex event since Mayak started — trust the hooks in Codex, then reload them or start a new thread.";
  }
  const hosts = hooks.receiving.hosts.map((x) => HOST_LABEL[x]).join(", ") || "Codex";
  const since = new Date(hooks.receiving.since).toLocaleTimeString(undefined, { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit" });
  return `Receiving from ${hosts} since ${since}.`;
}

function trustSteps(): HTMLElement {
  return h(
    "div",
    { class: "steps" },
    h("div", { class: "hint", text: "Codex runs new hooks only after you trust them:" }),
    h("ol", {},
      h("li", { text: "In Codex, open the “hooks need review” notice." }),
      h("li", { text: "Choose Trust." }),
      h("li", { text: "Choose “Reload hooks”, or start a new thread: threads that are already open keep the hooks they loaded." }),
    ),
    h("div", {
      class: "hint",
      text: "Mayak never marks hooks as trusted for you. Reordering hooks.json by hand asks for Trust again.",
    }),
  );
}

function codexSection(snap: SessionsSnapshot | null): HTMLElement {
  const receiving = h("span", {});
  const draw = (s: SessionsSnapshot | null) => {
    receiving.textContent = receivingText(s);
  };
  draw(snap);
  snapshotViews.push(draw);
  return h(
    "section",
    {},
    h("h2", {}, h("span", { text: "Codex" })),
    h("div", {
      class: "hint",
      text: "Optional. Mayak appends one hook group per event to ~/.codex/hooks.json, so Codex turns — working, waiting for permission, finished — show up in the island. The island only watches: it never answers Codex.",
    }),
    integrationSection("codex"),
    trustSteps(),
    h("div", { class: "row" }, h("label", { text: "Events" }), receiving),
  );
}

// ── Alerts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function alertsSection(): HTMLElement {
  const item = (label: string, what: string, on: boolean, set: (v: boolean) => void) =>
    h("div", { class: "row" },
      h("label", { text: label }),
      toggle(on, (v) => { set(v); void save(); }),
      h("span", { class: "hint", text: what }),
    );
  return h(
    "section",
    {},
    h("h2", {}, h("span", { text: "Alerts" })),
    h("div", {
      class: "hint",
      text: "A card and a sound when an agent needs you. A type that is off neither sounds nor opens a card; its row and the counters still update.",
    }),
    item("Waiting", "permission requests and questions", settings.alertWaiting, (v) => { settings.alertWaiting = v; }),
    item("Finished", "a turn ended", settings.alertFinished, (v) => { settings.alertFinished = v; }),
    item("Error", "a turn ended on an error", settings.alertError, (v) => { settings.alertError = v; }),
  );
}

// ── Advanced: legacy Claude Code Allow/Deny ───────────────────────────────────

function advancedSection(): HTMLElement {
  const body = h("div", { class: "advanced-body" });
  const details = h(
    "details",
    { class: "advanced" },
    h("summary", { text: "Advanced — Claude Code Allow/Deny in the island (legacy)" }),
    body,
  );
  let built = false;
  // ~/.claude/settings.json is read only once this block is opened (spec §8).
  details.addEventListener("toggle", () => {
    if (!details.open || built) return;
    built = true;
    body.append(
      h("div", {
        class: "hint",
        text: "Not needed to see Claude Code sessions. This optional hook adds Allow / Deny buttons to the island for Claude Code permission requests by writing a PermissionRequest hook into ~/.claude/settings.json.",
      }),
      h("div", {
        class: "notice warn",
        text: "If ~/.claude/settings.json comes from your dotfiles: sync.ps1 pull will erase this entry, and sync.ps1 push will commit this machine's path into the dotfiles repository.",
      }),
      integrationSection("claude"),
    );
  });
  return h("section", {}, details);
}

// ── Claude API section ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const MODELS: [string, string][] = [
  ["claude-opus-5", "Claude Opus 5"],
  ["claude-sonnet-5", "Claude Sonnet 5"],
  ["claude-haiku-4-5", "Claude Haiku 4.5"],
];

function apiSection(hasKey: boolean): HTMLElement {
  const dot = statusDot(hasKey);
  const state = h("span", { class: "hint", text: hasKey ? "Key saved in the Windows Credential Manager." : "No key yet — the chat needs one." });

  const field = h("input", {
    type: "password",
    placeholder: hasKey ? "••••••••••••  (stored)" : "sk-ant-...",
    style: "flex:1 1 auto;min-width:0",
    autocomplete: "off",
    spellcheck: "false",
  }) as HTMLInputElement;

  const saveBtn = h("button", { class: "primary", text: "Save key" });
  const clearBtn = h("button", { class: "danger", text: "Remove" });
  const feedback = h("div", {});

  async function refresh() {
    const present = (await Bridge.secretPresent("anthropic-api-key")) ?? false;
    dot.style.background = present ? "#22c55e" : "#f4505e";
    state.textContent = present
      ? "Key saved in the Windows Credential Manager."
      : "No key yet — the chat needs one.";
    field.placeholder = present ? "••••••••••••  (stored)" : "sk-ant-...";
    clearBtn.style.display = present ? "" : "none";
  }

  saveBtn.addEventListener("click", async () => {
    const value = field.value.trim();
    if (!value) return;
    clear(feedback);
    try {
      await Bridge.secretSet("anthropic-api-key", value);
      field.value = "";
      feedback.append(h("div", { class: "notice ok", text: "Saved. It never touches disk." }));
      await refresh();
    } catch (err) {
      feedback.append(h("div", { class: "notice err", text: `Could not save: ${String(err)}` }));
    }
  });

  clearBtn.addEventListener("click", async () => {
    clear(feedback);
    try {
      await Bridge.secretClear("anthropic-api-key");
      feedback.append(h("div", { class: "notice ok", text: "Key removed." }));
      await refresh();
    } catch (err) {
      feedback.append(h("div", { class: "notice err", text: `Could not remove: ${String(err)}` }));
    }
  });

  const model = h("select", {}) as HTMLSelectElement;
  for (const [id, label] of MODELS) model.append(h("option", { value: id, text: label }));
  if (!MODELS.some(([id]) => id === settings.model)) {
    model.append(h("option", { value: settings.model, text: settings.model }));
  }
  model.value = settings.model;
  model.addEventListener("change", () => {
    settings.model = model.value;
    void save();
  });

  clearBtn.style.display = hasKey ? "" : "none";

  return h(
    "section",
    {},
    h("h2", {}, dot, h("span", { text: "Claude" })),
    state,
    h("div", { class: "row" }, h("label", { text: "API key" }), field, saveBtn, clearBtn),
    h("div", { class: "row" }, h("label", { text: "Model" }), model),
    feedback,
  );
}

// ── Integrations section ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface IntegrationDef {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  color: string;
  /** Credential Manager keys, in the order they are shown. */
  fields: { key: string; label: string; placeholder: string; secret: boolean }[];
}

const INTEGRATIONS: IntegrationDef[] = [
  { id: "integration_stripe", name: "Stripe", color: "#0570DE",
    fields: [{ key: "stripe-api-key", label: "Secret key", placeholder: "sk_live_…", secret: true }] },
  { id: "integration_github", name: "GitHub", color: "#F4505E",
    fields: [{ key: "github-token", label: "Token", placeholder: "ghp_…", secret: true }] },
  { id: "integration_vercel", name: "Vercel", color: "#7C5CFF",
    fields: [{ key: "vercel-token", label: "Token", placeholder: "…", secret: true }] },
  { id: "integration_n8n", name: "n8n", color: "#F29B38",
    fields: [
      { key: "n8n-url", label: "Instance URL", placeholder: "https://n8n.example.com", secret: false },
      { key: "n8n-api-key", label: "API key", placeholder: "…", secret: true },
    ] },
  { id: "integration_resend", name: "Resend", color: "#22C55E",
    fields: [{ key: "resend-api-key", label: "API key", placeholder: "re_…", secret: true }] },
  { id: "integration_notion", name: "Notion", color: "#8C8C8C",
    fields: [{ key: "notion-api-key", label: "Integration token", placeholder: "ntn_…", secret: true }] },
  { id: "integration_calcom", name: "Cal.com", color: "#C9956A",
    fields: [{ key: "calcom-api-key", label: "API key", placeholder: "cal_…", secret: true }] },
];

const MAX_ACTIVE = 4;

function integrationsSection(present: Record<string, boolean>): HTMLElement {
  const note = h("div", { class: "hint" });
  const list = h("div", { style: "display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:14px" });

  function updateNote() {
    const used = settings.activeIntegrations.length;
    note.textContent = `Pick up to ${MAX_ACTIVE} pills to show next to Mochi — ${used}/${MAX_ACTIVE} in use. Keys are stored in the Windows Credential Manager, never on disk.`;
  }

  for (const def of INTEGRATIONS) {
    const active = settings.activeIntegrations.includes(def.id);
    const sw = h("button", { class: active ? "switch on" : "switch" });
    sw.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const on = settings.activeIntegrations.includes(def.id);
      if (on) {
        settings.activeIntegrations = settings.activeIntegrations.filter((x) => x !== def.id);
      } else {
        if (settings.activeIntegrations.length >= MAX_ACTIVE) return;
        settings.activeIntegrations = [...settings.activeIntegrations, def.id];
      }
      sw.classList.toggle("on", !on);
      updateNote();
      void save();
    });

    const rows = h("div", { style: "display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;flex:1 1 auto;min-width:0" });
    for (const field of def.fields) {
      const input = h("input", {
        type: field.secret ? "password" : "text",
        placeholder: present[field.key] ? "••••••••  (stored)" : field.placeholder,
        autocomplete: "off",
        spellcheck: "false",
        style: "flex:1 1 auto;min-width:0",
      }) as HTMLInputElement;
      const saveBtn = h("button", { text: "Save" });
      const dotEl = statusDot(present[field.key] ?? false);
      saveBtn.addEventListener("click", async () => {
        const value = input.value.trim();
        try {
          await Bridge.secretSet(field.key, value);
          present[field.key] = value.length > 0;
          input.value = "";
          input.placeholder = value ? "••••••••  (stored)" : field.placeholder;
          dotEl.style.background = value ? "#22c55e" : "#f4505e";
        } catch {
          dotEl.style.background = "#f5a524";
        }
      });
      rows.append(
        h("div", { class: "row" },
          h("label", { style: "min-width:104px", text: field.label }),
          input, saveBtn, dotEl,
        ),
      );
    }

    list.append(
      h("div", { style: "display:flex;gap:12px;align-items:flex-start" },
        h("div", { style: "display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;min-width:132px;padding-top:4px" },
          sw,
          h("i", { class: "dot", style: `background:${def.color}` }),
          h("span", { style: "font-size:12.5px", text: def.name }),
        ),
        rows,
      ),
    );
  }

  updateNote();
  return h("section", {}, h("h2", {}, h("span", { text: "Integrations" })), note, list);
}

// ── General section ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function generalSection(): HTMLElement {
  const volume = h("input", {
    type: "range", min: "0", max: "0.2", step: "0.005",
    value: String(settings.soundVolume),
  }) as HTMLInputElement;
  volume.addEventListener("input", () => {
    settings.soundVolume = Number(volume.value);
    void save();
  });

  const autoClose = h("input", {
    type: "number", min: "5", max: "120", step: "1",
    value: String(Math.round(settings.autoCloseInterval)),
    style: "width:72px",
  }) as HTMLInputElement;
  autoClose.addEventListener("change", () => {
    settings.autoCloseInterval = Math.max(5, Math.min(120, Number(autoClose.value) || 15));
    autoClose.value = String(settings.autoCloseInterval);
    void save();
  });

  const screen = h("select", {}) as HTMLSelectElement;
  screen.append(
    h("option", { value: "primary", text: "Main display" }),
    h("option", { value: "cursor", text: "Display under the cursor" }),
  );
  screen.value = settings.screen;
  screen.addEventListener("change", () => {
    settings.screen = screen.value as Settings["screen"];
    void save();
  });

  return h(
    "section",
    {},
    h("h2", {}, h("span", { text: "General" })),
    h("div", { class: "row" },
      h("label", { text: "Sound" }),
      toggle(settings.soundEnabled, (v) => { settings.soundEnabled = v; void save(); }),
      volume,
    ),
    h("div", { class: "row" },
      h("label", { text: "Auto-close" }),
      autoClose,
      h("span", { class: "hint", text: "seconds after you leave the island" }),
    ),
    h("div", { class: "row" },
      h("label", { text: "Island lives on" }),
      screen,
    ),
    h("div", { class: "row" },
      h("label", { text: "Launch at startup" }),
      toggle(settings.autostart, (v) => { settings.autostart = v; void save(); }),
    ),
  );
}

// ── Boot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function main() {
  // The window is created hidden at launch and shown later; registered before
  // anything is awaited, so a show during the awaits below is never missed.
  window.addEventListener("focus", refreshOnFocus);

  const boot = await Bridge.boot();
  if (boot) {
    settings = { ...settings, ...boot.settings };
    version = boot.version;
  }
  takeSnapshot(await Bridge.sessionsSnapshot());

  const hasKey = (await Bridge.secretPresent("anthropic-api-key")) ?? false;

  const keys = [
    "stripe-api-key", "github-token", "vercel-token",
    "n8n-url", "n8n-api-key", "resend-api-key", "notion-api-key", "calcom-api-key",
  ];
  const present: Record<string, boolean> = {};
  for (const k of keys) present[k] = (await Bridge.secretPresent(k)) ?? false;

  clear(root);
  root.append(
    h("h1", {}, h("span", { text: "Mayak" }), h("span", { class: "version", text: version })),
    sourcesSection(snapshot),
    codexSection(snapshot),
    alertsSection(),
    apiSection(hasKey),
    integrationsSection(present),
    generalSection(),
    advancedSection(),
    h("div", {
      class: "hint",
      text: "No telemetry. Network requests only go to the services you configure yourself.",
    }),
  );

  void onEvent<Settings>("settings-changed", (s) => {
    settings = { ...settings, ...s };
  });
}

void main();
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Point the files test at an explicit inbox (failing test)**

In `windows/src-tauri/src/files.rs` replace the whole `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` block (lines 85–131) with:
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testutil::TempDir;

    #[test]
    fn ingest_copies_and_never_overwrites() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("files");
        let inbox = tmp.path.join("inbox");
        let source = tmp.path.join("note.txt");
        std::fs::write(&source, b"hello").unwrap();

        let first = ingest_into(source.to_str().unwrap(), &inbox).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(first.name, "note.txt");
        assert!(
            Path::new(&first.path).starts_with(&inbox),
            "the copy must land in the inbox it was given, got {}",
            first.path
        );
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&first.path).unwrap(), b"hello");

        // A second drop of the same name must not clobber the first copy.
        std::fs::write(&source, b"second").unwrap();
        let second = ingest_into(source.to_str().unwrap(), &inbox).unwrap();
        assert_ne!(first.path, second.path);
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&first.path).unwrap(), b"hello");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&second.path).unwrap(), b"second");

        // Folders are refused rather than silently ignored.
        assert!(ingest_into(tmp.path.to_str().unwrap(), &inbox).is_err());

        // An ancient source must not arrive already older than the sweep window.
        let old_source = tmp.path.join("ancient.txt");
        std::fs::write(&old_source, b"old").unwrap();
        let long_ago = SystemTime::now() - KEEP_FOR - Duration::from_secs(60 * 60);
        std::fs::File::options()
            .write(true)
            .open(&old_source)
            .unwrap()
            .set_modified(long_ago)
            .unwrap();
        let aged = ingest_into(old_source.to_str().unwrap(), &inbox).unwrap();
        assert!(
            Path::new(&aged.path).exists(),
            "a file copied just now was swept as if it were a week old"
        );
        // `tmp` removes the source files and the inbox when it is dropped.
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Add `ingest_into`; `ingest` delegates to it**

In `windows/src-tauri/src/files.rs` replace
```rust
pub fn ingest(source: &str) -> Result<DroppedFile, String> {
    let src = Path::new(source);
    let meta = std::fs::metadata(src).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {source}: {e}"))?;
    if meta.is_dir() {
        return Err("Folders can't be dropped yet.".into());
    }

    let dir = inbox_dir();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
```
with
```rust
pub fn ingest(source: &str) -> Result<DroppedFile, String> {
    ingest_into(source, &inbox_dir())
}

/// `ingest` with the inbox passed in, so tests never touch the real one.
pub fn ingest_into(source: &str, inbox: &Path) -> Result<DroppedFile, String> {
    let src = Path::new(source);
    let meta = std::fs::metadata(src).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {source}: {e}"))?;
    if meta.is_dir() {
        return Err("Folders can't be dropped yet.".into());
    }

    let dir = inbox.to_path_buf();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
```
(The rest of the function body is unchanged; it already works on `dir`.)

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `.github/workflows/windows-test.yml`**

```yaml
name: Windows tests

# Type-checks and builds the Windows front end and runs every Rust test of the
# Windows workspace (app + relay). Runs on pull requests and by hand; it builds
# no installer and publishes nothing. The tag-driven release build stays in
# windows.yml.

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: windows-test-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: windows

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: windows/package-lock.json

      # Its own key: test builds are debug artifacts and must not evict the
      # release cache of windows.yml.
      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            windows/target
          key: windows-test-cargo-${{ hashFiles('windows/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: windows-test-cargo-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # `npm run build` first runs `prebuild` (cargo build --release -p mayak-hook),
      # then `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build`. The order matters for the next step:
      # tauri-build refuses to compile the app while the bundle resource
      # ../target/release/mayak-hook.exe does not exist.
      - name: Build relay, type-check and build front end
        run: npm run build

      - name: Rust tests
        run: cargo test --workspace
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Item 5 — hidden island CPU**

Create `%TEMP%\mayak-accept\sample-cpu.ps1`:
```powershell
<#
  Mayak acceptance item 5 (spec section 12): CPU of a hidden island.
  Samples, once per second, the CPU cycles used by the mayak process
  (QueryProcessCycleTime: exact accounting, catches wakeups far shorter than a
  clock tick) and, over the whole window, the CPU time of mayak plus its
  msedgewebview2.exe descendants (editors started by "Open" are not counted).
  Read-only; prints numbers only.
#>
param(
    [string]$Name = 'mayak',
    [int]$Seconds = 60,
    [string]$OutPath = (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'mayak-accept\cpu.log'),
    [UInt64]$QuietCycles = 1000000
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$outDir = Split-Path -Parent $OutPath
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $outDir | Out-Null }

Add-Type -TypeDefinition @"
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public static class MayakCycles {
    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError = true)]
    public static extern IntPtr OpenProcess(uint access, bool inherit, uint pid);
    [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError = true)]
    public static extern bool QueryProcessCycleTime(IntPtr process, out ulong cycles);
    [DllImport("kernel32.dll")]
    public static extern bool CloseHandle(IntPtr handle);
}
"@

function Write-Line([string]$Text) {
    Write-Host $Text
    Add-Content -LiteralPath $OutPath -Value $Text -Encoding UTF8
}

function Get-TreeIds([int]$Root) {
    $all = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Select-Object ProcessId, ParentProcessId, Name)
    $ids = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[int]
    $ids.Add($Root)
    $i = 0
    while ($i -lt $ids.Count) {
        foreach ($p in $all) {
            if ($p.ParentProcessId -eq $ids[$i] -and $p.Name -eq 'msedgewebview2.exe' -and -not $ids.Contains([int]$p.ProcessId)) { $ids.Add([int]$p.ProcessId) }
        }
        $i++
    }
    return $ids
}

function Get-TreeCpuSeconds($Ids) {
    $sum = 0.0
    foreach ($id in $Ids) {
        $p = Get-Process -Id $id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if ($p) { $sum += $p.TotalProcessorTime.TotalSeconds }
    }
    return $sum
}

$proc = Get-Process -Name $Name | Select-Object -First 1
$handle = [MayakCycles]::OpenProcess(0x1000, $false, [uint32]$proc.Id)   # PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
if ($handle -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) { throw "OpenProcess($($proc.Id)) failed" }
try {
    $ids = Get-TreeIds $proc.Id
    $cpuStart = Get-TreeCpuSeconds $ids
    [UInt64]$prev = 0
    if (-not [MayakCycles]::QueryProcessCycleTime($handle, [ref]$prev)) { throw 'QueryProcessCycleTime failed' }
    Write-Line ('{0:HH:mm:ss.fff} START pid={1} tree={2} seconds={3} quiet_below={4}' -f (Get-Date), $proc.Id, $ids.Count, $Seconds, $QuietCycles)
    $quiet = 0
    for ($i = 1; $i -le $Seconds; $i++) {
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
        [UInt64]$now = 0
        if (-not [MayakCycles]::QueryProcessCycleTime($handle, [ref]$now)) { throw 'QueryProcessCycleTime failed' }
        $delta = $now - $prev
        $prev = $now
        if ($delta -lt $QuietCycles) { $quiet++ }
        Write-Line ('{0:HH:mm:ss.fff} cycles={1}' -f (Get-Date), $delta)
    }
    $cpu = (Get-TreeCpuSeconds $ids) - $cpuStart
    $percent = $cpu / ($Seconds * [Environment]::ProcessorCount) * 100
    # Invariant culture: '.' as the decimal point and no group separator, whatever the
    # user's regional settings, so RESULT compares directly with the 5a limit 0.100.
    $inv = [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture
    Write-Line ('{0:HH:mm:ss.fff} RESULT quiet_seconds={1}/{2} tree_cpu_seconds={3} tree_avg_percent_of_machine={4}' -f `
        (Get-Date), $quiet, $Seconds, $cpu.ToString('0.000', $inv), $percent.ToString('0.000', $inv))
} finally {
    [void][MayakCycles]::CloseHandle($handle)
}
```
(Smoke-tested against `explorer.exe`: START, one `cycles=` line per second, RESULT.)

5a — agents idle: ask the user to let every agent go idle and to hide the island (Esc, then move the
mouse away until it retracts), then run
`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\sample-cpu.ps1" -OutPath "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\cpu-idle.log"`
and ask the user to watch Task Manager → Details (mayak.exe, its msedgewebview2.exe) meanwhile.
Pass: `RESULT … tree_avg_percent_of_machine` below `0.100` (the sampler prints both RESULT numbers with
the invariant culture, three decimals after a `.`, e.g. `0.016`) and the user saw CPU `00`/`0%` for those
processes.

5b — an agent working. Create `%TEMP%\mayak-accept\check-5b.ps1`:
```powershell
<#
  Mayak acceptance item 5b (spec section 12): every sampled CPU burst of mayak must
  follow a file notification. Reads the two logs written by sample-cpu.ps1 and
  watch-s1.ps1 -AnyFile; prints counts and the unexplained cycles= lines only.
#>
param(
    [string]$CpuLog = (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'mayak-accept\cpu-working.log'),
    [string]$EventsLog = (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'mayak-accept\events.log'),
    [UInt64]$QuietCycles = 1000000,
    [int]$WindowMs = 2000
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$inv = [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture
function Get-At([string]$Line) { [TimeSpan]::ParseExact($Line.Substring(0, 12), 'hh\:mm\:ss\.fff', $inv) }

$cpu = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $CpuLog -Encoding UTF8)
$events = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $EventsLog -Encoding UTF8)
$t0 = Get-At @($cpu | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\S+ START ' })[0]
$t1 = Get-At @($cpu | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\S+ RESULT ' })[0]
$acts = @($events | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\S+ (EVENT|TX|FILE) ' } | ForEach-Object { Get-At $_ })
$stops = @($events | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\S+ POLL .* status=(waiting|idle) ' } |
    Where-Object { $t = Get-At $_; $t -ge $t0 -and $t -le $t1 })
$bursts = @($cpu | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\S+ cycles=(\d+)$' -and [UInt64]$Matches[1] -ge $QuietCycles })
$bad = @($bursts | Where-Object {
    $t = Get-At $_
    @($acts | Where-Object { $_ -le $t -and ($t - $_).TotalMilliseconds -le $WindowMs }).Count -eq 0
})
'window {0} .. {1}' -f $t0, $t1
'turn ended or waited in the window (POLL waiting/idle): {0}' -f $stops.Count
'bursts >= {0} cycles: {1}' -f $QuietCycles, $bursts.Count
'unexplained bursts: {0}' -f $bad.Count
$bad
```
(Tested on synthetic logs and on real `sample-cpu.ps1`/`watch-s1.ps1` output: a burst 0.5 s and 1.1 s
after a `TX`/`FILE` line counts as explained, one 3.1 s after the last one is listed; the UTF-8 BOM of
both logs is handled.)

Run it as follows; a run that is not valid is repeated and is neither PASS nor FAIL:
1. Preconditions: the island is hidden as in 5a and the mouse stays away from the top edge of the
   screen; no Codex turn runs (Codex hooks reach Mayak over the pipe, which the observer does not see).
   Remove the logs of an earlier run (both scripts append):
   `foreach ($f in "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\cpu-working.log", "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\events.log") { if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $f) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f } }`.
2. Start the observer for **all** sessions and **all** files under `sessions` and `projects` in the
   background (Mayak's `projects` watcher also wakes for tool-result files, memory `.md` files and so on,
   which have no `EVENT`/`TX` line):
   `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-s1\watch-s1.ps1" -Entrypoint '*' -AnyFile -LogPath "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\events.log" -DurationSec 300`
3. Ask the user to start, in the Cursor session on repo B (or another repository with at least ~50
   source files), a read-only turn that runs for at least 3 minutes:
   `Read every source file of this repository one at a time with the Read tool. Do not run shell commands and do not edit files. After each file, write one line about it.`
   and to tell you once the first files are being read.
4. Only then run the sampler:
   `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\sample-cpu.ps1" -OutPath "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\cpu-working.log"`
5. When it prints `RESULT`, ask the user whether the island stayed hidden and no card opened during that
   minute, then run `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\mayak-accept\check-5b.ps1"`.

Valid run: the user confirms that the island stayed hidden and no card opened between the sampler's
`START` and `RESULT`, and the checker prints `turn ended or waited in the window (POLL waiting/idle): 0`.
A finished turn or a permission prompt reveals the island (card, then `autoCloseInterval`, then about
60 s compact), and a visible island runs the ~60 Hz cursor poll (`island.rs` `PollGate`), so such a
window says nothing about the hidden island. Repeat an invalid run with a longer turn.
Pass (valid run): `unexplained bursts: 0`: every `cycles=` line `≥ 1000000` has an `EVENT`, `TX` or
`FILE` line at most 2 s before it (the sample's own second or the one before it, because a reaction can
straddle one sample boundary). Mayak only reacts to file events and never wakes up periodically.
Fail: any listed `cycles=` line; record the lines.
If 5a or 5b fails and integration keys are configured, repeat it with tray → Pause on (pollers stop;
session tracking continues, spec §10) and record both runs; the item passes only if the paused run passes.
Record row 5 with the RESULT lines.

```markdown
## Mayak — sub-project 1: multi-session core (Windows)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-01-mayak-multi-session-core-design.md`

Mayak (fork of Coucou) shows every local Claude Code and Codex session, grouped by project, and tells
who is waiting: permission requests, questions, finished turns and errors.

### What changes
- Rename to Mayak: crates `mayak`/`mayak_lib`/`mayak-hook`, bundle id `io.github.mahach666.mayak`, pipe `\\.\pipe\mayak-<SID>`, folders `%APPDATA%\Mayak` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak`; one-time copy of the Coucou `settings.json` (§11, §8).
- Relay `mayak-hook.exe` with `--agent claude|codex`; Codex events never wait and never print (§5.2).
- Pipe router: Codex → observer, Claude `PermissionRequest` → legacy approval, the rest ignored (§5.3).
- Passive Claude observer of `~/.claude/sessions` and transcripts; Codex observer of hooks and rollouts (§5.5, §5.6).
- One pure state model with table tests; store thread publishing snapshots and alerts (§5.4, §6, §7, §9).
- Opt-in Codex hook installer with exact-bytes diff, backup and fingerprint; legacy Claude Allow/Deny moved to Advanced (§8).
- Island: sessions view, waiting/session cards, compact counters, per-type alerts; settings window sections (§10).
- CI: `.github/workflows/windows-test.yml` on pull requests (§12).

### Verification
- `cargo test --workspace`: {{total passed from Task 20 Step 1}} passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit` + vite): OK.
- CI "Windows tests" (`.github/workflows/windows-test.yml`): see the Checks tab of this PR.

### Spikes (§12)
| # | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | {{S1 verdict}} | {{S1 C1/C2/C3 lines from mayak-pr-notes.md}} |
| S2 | {{S2 outcome: default hook set and host rules chosen}} | {{rows S2.1–S2.9 of the Task 15 sheet}} |
| S3 | {{S3 outcome: rollout mode and fields}} | {{rows S3.1–S3.4 of the Task 15 sheet}} |
| S4 | {{S4 outcome: DACL commit or default DACL with reason}} | {{row S4 of the Task 15 sheet}} |
| S5 | {{S5 outcome}} | {{rows S5.1–S5.2 of the Task 15 sheet}} |

### Manual acceptance (§12)
{{the acceptance table from mayak-pr-notes.md, rows 1–8}}

### Platform observations
{{the lines under "## Platform observations" in mayak-pr-notes.md: the two open-handle diagnostic lines and the NSIS bundle line}}

### Declared limits (§15)
- A Codex wait stays until the next hook of that session (usually `Stop`) or "OK".
- A failed Codex turn shows its error only once the rollout is read (island visible or next hook).
- Codex questions to the user are not covered; after a Mayak restart Codex sessions reappear with their next hook.

### Known migration effects
- API keys that Coucou stored under the keyring service `fr.louisraille.coucou` are not visible to Mayak (`io.github.mahach666.mayak`): enter them again in Settings.
- A copied Coucou `settings.json` with `autostart: true` shows "Launch at startup" on, but Mayak is not registered to start until that toggle is switched off and on.
- New bundle id means a new WebView2 profile and single-instance key: Coucou and Mayak can run side by side; quit Coucou.

### Not in this PR
- Window binding and VS 2022 (sub-project 2); visual rebrand (sub-project 3). Mochi, the sounds and the icons are still Coucou assets (`LICENSE-ASSETS.md`), so no Mayak build is published.
```

### Notes from section F

#### Section F — I/O threads and Tauri wiring (T11, T12, T13)

**Conventions for this section**

- Paths are relative to the repository root `C:\Users\HP\Documents\claude\coucou`. Shell steps use Git Bash; Rust needs `export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"` once per shell. Test commands run from `windows/` (`cd windows && …`), git commands from the repository root.
- Prerequisites: T1–T10 are merged with the names of the interface contract (`mayak` / `mayak_lib`, `observe::{keys, paths, tail, win, claude, claude_transcript, text, codex, model}`, `crate::testutil::TempDir`, T4's `AppSink` in `lib.rs`).
- The I/O part of `observe/claude.rs` (T11) and `observe/codex.rs` (T12) is appended to the file written by T7/T8 as a private child module `mod io_thread { … }` whose public items are re-exported (`pub use io_thread::{…}`) in the cycle that adds `spawn`. Its own `use` lines therefore never collide with the parsing part's imports, and the contract paths (`observe::claude::spawn`, `observe::codex::CodexInput`, …) are unchanged. Tests live in `io_thread::tests`.
- Every task is a sequence of red/green cycles: add the tests of one behaviour group, run them and see them fail, add the code, run them and see them pass, commit.
- "Insert … directly above the `    #[cfg(test)]` line of `mod io_thread`" means the `#[cfg(test)]` indented by four spaces that opens `io_thread::tests` (not the unindented one of the parsing part's tests). Inserting each chunk above that line keeps the chunks in step order.
- "Insert … at the end of `io_thread::tests`" means directly above the last two lines of the file, `    }` (closes `mod tests`) and `}` (closes `mod io_thread`).
- "Replace the `use` block of `mod io_thread`" means every `    use …;` line between `mod io_thread {` and the first item below them (blank lines between those `use` lines included); the blank line before the first item stays.
- Process proof in tests uses the test process itself (`proc::identify(std::process::id())`); one T11 test and one T12 test start `cmd /c ping -n 3 127.0.0.1 >nul` to watch a real exit. No test sets environment variables.
- Unit tests never write `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Mayak\mayak.log`: T11 Step 1 sends `crate::log::line` to the running test's stderr under `cfg(test)`.
- Threads: `std::thread` + `std::sync::mpsc` only. Nothing in this section runs on, or blocks, the tokio runtime; the router's only call into the observer (`observe` / `approval_context`) is a non-blocking channel send or already runs on `spawn_blocking` (T4, D46).
- Logs carry file names, keys, event names, counts, error kinds and health — never payload text.
- Until T13 wires them, `cargo build` warns that some new items are never used (`spawn`, `ClaudeConfig`, `CodexConfig`, …), and the non-test build of an intermediate cycle warns about imports only its tests use yet. Those warnings are expected; there must be no errors.
- The three Review Focus tests of T11 Step 17 (claude-io driven together with a real `model::Store`) were verified in `scratchpad/plan/focus/crate`, a stand-in crate with the T5–T13 code of sections C–F: Step 18 state (Steps 19, 20, 23, 25 undone) `20 passed; 10 failed` with the quoted messages, Steps 21/26 green (30/31), the whole stand-in `cargo test --offline --lib` 201 passed and `cargo build --offline --lib` without warnings, eight repeated runs stable. Each catches a mutation that the 28 older claude-io tests miss: `status_changed` without its `statusUpdatedAt` half, the model not emitting Untrack/Track on a `sessionId` change, a first sight of a waiting session raising an alert.
